# Working with shopping cart and checkout
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/accelerators/react-accelerator/working-with-shopping-cart-and-checkout

This page will introduce you to how to work with shopping cart and checkout page.

## Working with shopping cart

Every visitors visiting a site should have their own shopping cart. A shopping cart is created if Cart context is not available in Cookies. The check and creation of Cart is done in [middleware.ts](/accelerators/react-accelerator/routing-fundamentals). React accelerator queries and mutates Cart, processes checkout flow by consuming the Storefront API. For more information regarding how to work with cart and checkout in Storefront API, click [here](/platform/guides/how-to-work-with-cart-and-checkout-using-the-storefront-api).

A cart object, together with website settings, are loaded when visitor visits the site, by using CartContext and WebsiteContext in app/layout.tsx. Because the root layout app/layout.tsx is a [Server component](https://nextjs.org/docs/getting-started/react-essentials#server-components), these data are loaded at the server. Client components use these data by using [useContext](https://react.dev/reference/react/useContext) hook. For example, to access the Cart:

```tsx theme={null}
const cartContext = useContext(CartContext);
```

To add a product to shopping cart, components/BuyButton.tsx component should be used. Here is an example:

```tsx theme={null}
<BuyButton
  label="Add to cart"
  successLabel="Added to cart"
  articleNumber={articleNumber}
></BuyButton>
```

## Checkout page

After adding products to shopping cart, visitor can click on a button in Cart to navigate to Checkout page to place an order. components/checkout/CheckoutWizard.tsx is the component which handles the checkout process, which is divided into three steps:

1. Enter delivery address
2. Choose delivery option
3. Payment

CheckoutWizard access Cart via CartContext and maintain the Checkout state as its own state. After every step, a request is sent to the server to save information, by using checkoutService.client. At the Payment step, depending on what payment and delivery methods are configured, different components are shown because only a set of providers can be combined. Below is the list of methods that can be combined, but let's take a look at the terms being used first:

Payment methods

* Inline - solution implementation form, for example, DirectPay.
* Iframe checkout - iframe with customer information form such as Klarna, Qliro and Svea.
* Payment checkout - iframe with only payment, no customer information form, for example, Adyen.

Delivery methods

* Inline - solution implementation form, for example, DirectShipment.
* Payment checkout - contains customer information forms and delivery option selection, as part of the iframe checkout in the "payment method" (example Klarna with KSA)
* Delivery checkout - example Ingrid, contain delivery option selection and maybe delivery information form

Combination

* If multiple iframe checkouts are configured for a channel, only the first one will be used in the checkout.
* An iframe checkout cannot be combined with an inline or a payment checkout. The system should render the iframe checkout and ignore the inline and payment checkout.
* An inline or a payment checkout can be combined.

## Render payment widget for Iframe and Payment checkouts

Iframe and Payment checkouts have their own payment widgets, which are a set of HTML and Javascript. This is returned by the server as paymentHtmlSnippet. By giving the paymentHtmlSnippet to PaymentWdiget component, we can render payment widget by adding HTML and Javascript into the DOM and execute them. The payment is then handled by the payment widget.

## Show order confirmation

After an order is placed, visitor is redirected to Order confirmation page, which is handled by app/(StickyHeader)/OrderConfirmationPage/\[\[...slug]]/page.tsx. Depending on what payment method was used, different content is displayed.

If the payment method was used support sending back a receipt, we can display it just like we display payment widget. Otherwise, a message will be displayed to inform the order has been placed. This will be changed in the future to show the order detail.

## See also

* [How to work with cart and checkout using the Storefront API](/platform/guides/how-to-work-with-cart-and-checkout-using-the-storefront-api)


# Working with wishlists
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/accelerators/react-accelerator/working-with-wishlists

Understand how to implement and use wishlist functionality in the Litium React accelerator.

## Overview

Wishlists allow authenticated users to save products for later purchase or reference. The React accelerator provides wishlist functionality through the Storefront API, enabling customers to create, manage, and share both personal and organizational product collections.

<Note>
  Wishlist functionality requires user authentication. Users must be logged in to create and manage wishlists.
</Note>

## Working with wishlists

**Wishlist context**

Similar to the shopping cart, wishlists are managed through a context provider. The wishlist data is loaded for authenticated users and made available through the `WishlistContext`:

```tsx theme={null}
import { useContext } from 'react';
import { WishlistContext } from '@/contexts/WishlistContext';

const WishlistComponent = () => {
  const wishlistContext = useContext(WishlistContext);
  const { wishlists, activeWishlist } = wishlistContext;
  
  return (
    <div>
      {wishlists.map(wishlist => (
        <div key={wishlist.id}>{wishlist.name}</div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};
```

**Add to wishlist button**

To add a product to a wishlist, use the `WishlistButton` component:

```tsx theme={null}
<WishlistButton
  label="Add to wishlist"
  successLabel="Added to wishlist"
  articleNumber={articleNumber}
  wishlistId={activeWishlistId}
/>
```

The `WishlistButton` component automatically handles authentication checks and displays appropriate messaging for unauthenticated users.

**Create a new wishlist**

Users can create multiple wishlists for different purposes. Use the wishlistService to create a personal or organizational wishlist:

```tsx theme={null}
import { wishlistService } from '@/services/wishlistService.client';

// Create a personal wishlist
const createPersonalWishlist = async (name: string, category?: string) => {
  try {
    const result = await wishlistService.createPersonalWishlist({
      name: name,
      category: category
    });
    
    if (result.wishlist) {
      // Update UI or context with new wishlist
      console.log('Wishlist created:', result.wishlist);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to create wishlist:', error);
  }
};

// Creating organizational wishlists
const createOrganizationalWishlist = async (name: string, isShared: boolean) => {
  try {
    const result = await wishlistService.createOrganizationalWishlist({
      name: name,
      category: "Team",
      isShared: isShared
    });
    
    if (result.wishlist) {
      console.log('Organizational wishlist created:', result.wishlist);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to create wishlist:', error);
  }
};
```

**Display wishlist items**

The `WishlistView` component displays wishlist items with product details, images, and pricing:

```tsx theme={null}
import { WishlistView } from '@/components/wishlist/WishlistView';

<WishlistView 
  wishlistId={activeWishlistId}
  showAddToCart={true}
  showRemove={true}
/>
```

**Update wishlist products**

Add or update products in an existing wishlist using the `updateWishlist` mutation:

```tsx theme={null}
import { wishlistService } from '@/services/wishlistService.client';

const updateWishlistProducts = async (wishlistId: string, products: Array<{articleNumber: string, quantity: number}>) => {
  try {
    const result = await wishlistService.updateWishlist({
      wishlistId: wishlistId,
      products: products
    });
    
    if (result.wishlist) {
      // Refresh wishlist context
      console.log('Wishlist updated:', result.wishlist);
    } else if (result.errors) {
      console.error('Errors:', result.errors);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to update wishlist:', error);
  }
};

// Remove a product by setting quantity to 0
const removeProductFromWishlist = async (wishlistId: string, articleNumber: string) => {
  try {
    const result = await wishlistService.updateWishlist({
      wishlistId: wishlistId,
      products: [
        {
          articleNumber: articleNumber,
          quantity: 0  // Setting to 0 removes the product
        }
      ]
    });
    
    if (result.wishlist) {
      console.log('Product removed from wishlist');
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to remove product:', error);
  }
};
```

To remove a product from a wishlist, update it with quantity: 0. This will remove the product entirely.

## Wishlist page

The wishlist page is typically found in the user's account section. The page component is located at *app/(StickyHeader)/AccountPage/wishlists/page.tsx* and displays:

* All wishlists for the current user
* Options to create, edit, or delete wishlists
* Product items within each wishlist
* Actions to add items to cart or remove from wishlist

```tsx theme={null}
// Example wishlist page structure
const WishlistsPage = () => {
  const { wishlists, activeWishlist, setActiveWishlist } = useContext(WishlistContext);
  
  return (
    <div className="wishlists-container">
      <WishlistSelector 
        wishlists={wishlists}
        activeId={activeWishlist?.id}
        onSelect={setActiveWishlist}
      />
      
      {activeWishlist && (
        <WishlistView 
          wishlistId={activeWishlist.id}
          showAddToCart={true}
          showRemove={true}
        />
      )}
      
      <CreateWishlistButton />
    </div>
  );
};
```

## Wishlist features

**Multiple wishlists**

Users can organize products into different types of wishlists:

```tsx theme={null}
// Creating personal wishlists
await wishlistService.createPersonalWishlist({ 
  name: "Gift Ideas",
  category: "Gifts"
});
await wishlistService.createPersonalWishlist({ 
  name: "Compare Later",
  category: "Research"
});

// Creating organizational wishlists
await wishlistService.createOrganizationalWishlist({ 
  name: "Team Equipment",
  category: "Office",
  isShared: true
});
```

**Share organizational wishlists**

Enable sharing for organizational wishlists with team members:

```tsx theme={null}
const toggleWishlistSharing = async (wishlistId: string, isShared: boolean) => {
  const result = await wishlistService.updateWishlist({
    wishlistId: wishlistId,
    isShared: isShared
  });
  
  if (result.wishlist) {
    console.log(`Wishlist sharing ${isShared ? 'enabled' : 'disabled'}`);
  }
};
```

<Note>
  Only organizational wishlists can be shared. Personal wishlists remain private to the individual user.
</Note>

**Stock status indicators**

Display stock availability for wishlist products:

```tsx theme={null}
<div className="wishlist-item">
  <ProductImage src={item.productItem?.images[0]?.url} />
  <ProductName>{item.productItem?.name}</ProductName>
  
  {item.productItem?.inStock ? (
    <span className="in-stock">In stock</span>
  ) : (
    <span className="out-of-stock">Out of stock</span>
  )}
  
  <Price amount={item.productItem?.price?.includingVat} />
</div>
```

**Query wishlists with filters**

Retrieve wishlists with filtering and sorting options:

```tsx theme={null}
const loadWishlists = async (type: 'PersonalOnly' | 'OrganizationOnly' | 'Both') => {
  try {
    const result = await wishlistService.getWishlists({
      wishlistType: type,
      sortBy: 'ModifiedAt',
      sortOrder: 'Descending'
    });
    
    if (result.wishlists) {
      console.log('Wishlists loaded:', result.wishlists);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to load wishlists:', error);
  }
};
```

**Delete a wishlist**

Remove a wishlist and all its products:

```tsx theme={null}
const deleteWishlist = async (wishlistId: string) => {
  try {
    const result = await wishlistService.deleteWishlist({
      wishlistId: wishlistId
    });
    
    if (!result.errors || result.errors.length === 0) {
      console.log('Wishlist deleted successfully');
      // Refresh wishlist context
    } else {
      console.error('Errors:', result.errors);
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to delete wishlist:', error);
  }
};
```

<Warning>
  Deleting a wishlist is permanent. Confirm with the user before performing this action.
</Warning>

## Component structure

**Key components**

* *WishlistButton.tsx* - Add to wishlist button component
* *WishlistView\.tsx* - Displays wishlist items with details
* *WishlistSelector.tsx* - Dropdown or list to switch between wishlists
* *CreateWishlistButton.tsx* - Creates new wishlists
* *WishlistItem.tsx* - Individual product item in wishlist

**Services**

* *wishlistService.client.ts* - Client-side service for wishlist API calls
* *wishlistService.server.ts* - Server-side service for SSR wishlist operations

## Best practices

**Performance optimization**

* Load wishlist data only for authenticated users
* Cache wishlist data on the client side
* Implement optimistic UI updates for better user experience
* Use pagination for wishlists with many items

**User experience**

* Provide visual feedback when adding items to wishlist
* Show item count badge on wishlist icon in navigation
* Allow bulk actions (add all to cart, remove all)
* Display stock status and price changes prominently
* Enable quick switching between multiple wishlists

**Mobile considerations**

* Ensure wishlist buttons are touch-friendly
* Optimize wishlist view for small screens
* Implement swipe gestures for item removal
* Use bottom sheets or modals for wishlist selection

**Accessibility**

* Include proper ARIA labels on wishlist buttons
* Ensure keyboard navigation works for all wishlist actions
* Provide screen reader announcements for wishlist updates
* Use semantic HTML for wishlist structure

## Related

[How to work with wishlists using the Storefront API](/platform/guides/how-to-work-with-wishlists-using-the-storefront-api)


# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/lipscore-connector/configure

This section explains how to configure the Lipscore connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge> <Badge>Litium 8</Badge>

After installing the Lipscore add-on you can restart the site and open Backoffice. For each channel the following options are available:

| Field name                | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Activate Lipscore         | Enable Lipscore on the channel by setting to "Yes"                                                                                                                          |
| Lipscore API key          | Enter the API key from the Lipscore account at [https://members.lipscore.com/](https://members.lipscore.com/widgets)                                                        |
| Lipscore secret           | Enter the API secret from the Lipscore account at [https://members.lipscore.com/](https://members.lipscore.com/)                                                            |
| Color of rating stars     | Enter a valid CSS value to override the default gold color                                                                                                                  |
| Use SEO data for products | Enable this only if Lipscore's Google Shopping Feed will be used. When enabled data for PriceWithVat, Currency, Category, and GTIN will be included in the Lipscore widgets |

The language setting under "Market, language and website" on the channel will be used to display widgets and translated to the Lipscore language codes.

* [Sending invitations task](#sending-invitations-task)
* [Product data mapping](#product-data-mapping)
* [Lipscore widgets](#lipscore-widgets)
* [Lipscore product review widgets](#lipscore-product-review-widgets)
* [Lipscore Service Review Widgets](#lipscore-service-review-widgets)

## Sending invitations task

The review request emails that Lipscore sends on your behalf after purchase are the single most important feature to get customers to write reviews. You can configure how the email looks in your Lipscore account.

The Invitations task is executed every 15 minutes. When Lipscore is activated in the channel settings all new orders are marked as not sent. When these orders reach the status Completed the Lipscore Invitations API is used by the task to trigger sending out invites for reviews.

## Product data mapping

It is possible to override what data is used for Brand and GTIN in Products/Google shopping.

<Note>
  GTIN is only included if you enable "Use SEO data for products".
</Note>

## Lipscore widgets

You are now ready to place the Lipscore Widgets on your views. It is done through html-helpers available by placing the directive `@using Litium.Addons.Lipscore` at the top of the `.cshtml` file.

You will see all the widgets available when you start typing the name of the Lipscore helper.

## Lipscore product review widgets

You can find a full reference for what the helpers listed below will create at [lipscore.com/widgets](https://members.lipscore.com/widgets).

<Note>
  The Id parameter to product widgets can be either for the BaseProduct or the Variant. But the Id used in the created div/span will always be for the BaseProduct. Only the product Id is required for product widgets. The CssClass parameter is optional, and use it if you wish to introduce your own styling more easily.
</Note>

`@Html.LipscoreRating(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass, _readonly)`

Lipscore rating widget. It can only be one per page. The default widget used in product details pages has two different main layouts and several colors and styles to choose from. The size of this widget is fixed. It can optionally be made read-only by giving true for the `_readonly` parameter.

`@Html.LipscoreRatingSmall(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass)`

Lipscore small rating widget. Note! It is invisible if there are no ratings for the product.

It is most commonly used in "category pages" and lists where multiple products are listed together. It has two layouts.

`@Html.LipscoreReviewList(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass)`

Lipscore review list widget. This widget lists all the reviews you have gotten for a given product and should be placed on the product details page, usually inside a Reviews-tab or something similar. The widget displays five reviews at a time with a paging control at the bottom.

`@Html.LipscoreReviewCount(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass)`

Lipscore review count widget. This widget displays the number of reviews for a given product, without any attributes or styling whatsoever. It is a plain number and most commonly used in a Reviews-tab indicating the number of reviews of a product before the customer clicks the tab to read the actual reviews.

`@Html.LipscoreTestimonial(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass)`

Lipscore testimonial widget. The testimonial widget displays product reviews that have been marked as testimonials, either manually in the Reviews page in the backend, or by automatically marking all 5-star reviews as testimonials. The widget will display one single random review from the ten latest reviews marked as testimonials for the given product.

`@Html.LipscoreNewQuestionPost(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass)`

Lipscore question post/form widget. This is the form where users write their questions about the product. Users must log in using one of the social logins before being allowed to submit the question.

`@Html.LipscoreQuestionsList(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass, PageSize)`

Lipscore questions list widget. This widget lists all the questions you have gotten for a given product and should be placed on the product details page, usually inside a Questions-tab or something similar. The widget by default displays five questions at a time with a paging control at the bottom. You can change page size using the optional parameter `PageSize`.

`@Html.LipscoreQuestionsCount(Model.ProductItem.Id, CssClass)`

Lipscore questions count widget. This widget displays the number of questions for a given product, without any attributes or styling whatsoever. It is a plain number and most commonly used in a Questions-tab indicating the number of questions of a product before the customer clicks the tab to read the actual questions.

## Lipscore Service Review Widgets

To use these helpers your Lipscore account must be enabled for Service Reviews. They are not related to products and can be used on any kind of page. Parameters for height and width are optional and given in px or %.

`@Html.LipscoreServiceReviewBadgeStarred(height, width, CssClass)`

Lipscore service review widget. The service reviews badge shows the average rating your business/service has received. When the badge is clicked a modal window opens where all the service reviews are displayed.

`@Html.LipscoreServiceReviewTestimonialBanner(height, width, CssClass)`

Lipscore service review testimonial banner widget. Displays service reviews that have been marked as testimonials, either manually in the Reviews page in the backend, or by automatically marking all 5-star reviews as testimonials.

`@Html.LipscoreServiceReviewTestimonial(height, width, CssClass)`

Lipscore service review testimonial widget. The testimonial widget displays service reviews that have been marked as testimonials, either manually in the Reviews page in the backend, or by automatically marking all 5-star reviews as testimonials.


# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/lipscore-connector/develop

This section contains instructions for further customization of the Lipscore connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge> <Badge>Litium 8</Badge>

## React quirk

When a partial update of a page is dispatched in the React code there is a need to refresh the Lipscore widgets. It can be done by using the Lipscore function `reInitWidgets`. Suggested is to place this after the dispatch causing the partial update:

```js theme={null}
dispatch(receive(result));

lipscore && lipscore.reInitWidgets();
```

<Note>
  For the Litium accelerators faceted search there is a script injected on the page that checks if this field is changed: `window.__litium.cache.PRODUCT_VIEW_CACHED.productsViewCachedId`
</Note>

This script is injected by `GetBodyEndScript` in `LipscoreScriptGenerator` and could be overridden if you rather want to do this in the React code. If you do that then you must change the file `FacetedSearch.action.js` as shown above.

# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-c3-print-connector/develop_1

Tips on how to customise the features of the add-on.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Modifying the XML output structure

The default format of the exported XML file looks like this:

```xml theme={null}
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<litium>
  <category>
    <displayName></displayName>
    <displayImage href="" />
    <properties>
      <property name="">value</property>
      <property name="">value</property>
    </properties>

    <categories>
      <category>
        <displayName></displayName>
        <displayImage href="" />
        <products>
          <!-- products in this category -->
        </products>
        <categories>
          <Category>
            <displayName></displayName>
            <displayImage href="" />
            <products>
              <!-- products in this category -->
            </products>
          </Category>
        </categories>
      </category>
    </categories>

    <products>
      <product>
        <articleNumber></articleNumber>
        <!-- article number for the product-->
        <displayName></displayName>
        <!-- product name-->
        <displayImage href="" />
        <!-- product display image-->
        <properties>
          <property name="">value</property>
          <property name="">value</property>
        </properties>
        <variants>
          <variant>
            <articleNumber></articleNumber>
            <!-- article number for the variant-->
            <displayName></displayName>
            <!-- variant display name-->
            <displayImage href="" />
            <!-- variant display image-->
            <priceItem price="80" vatPercentage=".25" vat="20" priceInclVat="100" />
            <properties>
              <property name="">value</property>
              <property name="">value</property>
            </properties>
          </variant>
        </variants>
      </product>
    </products>

  </category>
</litium>
```

You can modify the XML output by creating an XSLT file and upload it to the server by clicking **Add new XSLT** on the C3 Print connector panel. The customised XSLT file is stored in the `\Files` folder of your site. Example:

```xml theme={null}
<xsl:stylesheet version="2.0" exclude-result-prefixes="xs xdt err fn" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform" xmlns:xs="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:fn="http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions" xmlns:xdt="http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-datatypes" xmlns:err="http://www.w3.org/2005/xqt-errors">
        <xsl:template match="/">
                <c3>
                        <xsl:for-each select="//category">
                        <Category>
                                <Name>
                                        <xsl:value-of select="displayName"/>
                                </Name>
                                <Products>
                                        <xsl:for-each select="child::products//product">
                                                <Product>
                                                        <Name>
                                                                <xsl:value-of select="displayName"/>
                                                        </Name>
                                                        <ArticleNumber>
                                                                <xsl:value-of select="articleNumber"/>
                                                        </ArticleNumber>
                                                </Product>
                                        </xsl:for-each>
                                </Products>
                        </Category>
                        </xsl:for-each>
                </c3>
        </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>
```

The above sample XSLT file results in the following XML file format:

```xml theme={null}
<c3>
        <Category>
                <Name>Byxor</Name>
                <Products>
                        <Product>
                                <Name>Alabama</Name>
                                <ArticleNumber>636632015562230451</ArticleNumber>
                        </Product>
                        <Product>
                                <Name>Sidney</Name>
                                <ArticleNumber>636632015562230452</ArticleNumber>
                        </Product>
                        <Product>
                                <Name>Melbourne</Name>
                                <ArticleNumber>636632015562230453</ArticleNumber>
                        </Product>
                        <Product>
                                <Name>Denver Manchester</Name>
                                <ArticleNumber>636632015562230454</ArticleNumber>
                        </Product>
                </Products>
        </Category>
</c3>
```

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-channelengine/configure

This section explains how to configure the Litium ChannelEngine Connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

There are two kinds of configuration sources for the `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine` package. First is the configuration defined for Litium channels. The second one is defined in `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.dll.config` file.

## Channel configuration

Channel configuration related to Channel Engine may be defined in ChannelEngine field group. The following fields are available:

| Field Name              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| API URL                 | Defines URL of the ChannelEngine endpoint responsible for handling integration requests related to this Litium channel.                                                                                |
| Merchant API Key        | API Key is used to authenticate integration in ChannelEngine Merchant API service.                                                                                                                     |
| Carrier Name            | Name of the delivery service that will be sent to ChannelEngine upon creation of order delivery in Litium.                                                                                             |
| Monitored Inventory     | The ID of the inventory in which stock changes shall be monitored and forwarded to ChannelEngine.                                                                                                      |
| Monitored Price List    | The ID of the price list which changes shall be monitored and forwarded to ChannelEngine. NOTE! This price list must be including VAT in the same currency as the base currency used in ChannelEngine. |
| Default Delivery Method | Name of the Delivery method that shall be selected for orders imported from ChannelEngine.                                                                                                             |
| Default Payment Method  | Name of the Payment method that shall be selected for orders imported from ChannelEngine.                                                                                                              |
| Default currency        | Currency is configured as a base currency on the ChannelEngine portal. Orders will be created in this currency using the currency converted amounts from ChannelEngine.                                |

## Global settings

Global package settings that affect all configured channels are stored in `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.dll.config` file which is automatically created when referencing `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine` NuGet package. The following table contains all configuration entries defined in this file:

| Attribute Name                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| enableIntegration                  | Determines whether the integration shall be enabled on the currently running system.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| stockUpdateInterval                | The time interval between successive executions of a task that updates ChannelEngine stock by checking all the items in the Inventory configured for each of the Litium channels.                                                                                                                                       |
| priceUpdateInterval                | The time interval between successive executions of a task that updates ChannelEngine prices by checking all the items in the Price List configured for each of the Litium channels. NOTE! This should be set according to how often you update your prices, to avoid ChannelEngine orders being placed with old prices. |
| ordersImportInterval               | The time interval between successive executions of a task that imports new orders from each of the Litium channels that have correct ChannelEngine configuration assigned.                                                                                                                                              |
| ordersSynchronizationRetryInterval | The time interval between successive executions of a task that checks each Channel Engine order for an unsuccessfully acknowledgement or shipment creation and retries the attempt.                                                                                                                                     |
| defaultOrderStatus                 | An integer representing an order status that the new order imported from Channel Engine shall be assigned with.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| defaultDeliveryStatus              | An integer representing a delivery status that the new order imported from Channel Engine shall be assigned with.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| orderAcknowledgementStatus         | An integer representing an order status for which each of the orders imported from Channel Engine shall be acknowledged in Channel Engine when entering this state.                                                                                                                                                     |
| orderShipmentStatus                | An integer representing an order status for which shipment of each of the orders imported from Channel Engine shall be created in Channel Engine when entering this state.                                                                                                                                              |

Note that the order and delivery statuses you configure has to comply with the order fulfilment process and states in your solution.

## About the product feed

Different marketplaces have different requirements for the structure of product information. ChannelEngine documentation contains a guide for each marketplace on how to make sure your product information is correct. Please make sure that your feed contains information for both the base product (parent in ChannelEngine) and variant (child in ChannelEngine).

## About orders

The following data are added to orders created from ChannelEngine:

| Litium OrderCarrier property                 | ChannelEngine property  | Description                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEExtraData"]          | ExtraData               |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEOrderKey"]           | Id + "\_" + ChannelName |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEChannelOrderID"]     | Id                      |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEChannelName"]        | ChannelName             |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEChannelID"]          | ChannelId               |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEChannelOrderNumber"] | ChannelOrderNo          |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEChannelCreatedAt"]   | CreatedAt               |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEChannelOrderDate"]   | OrderDate               |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEIsBusinessOrder"]    | IsBusinessOrder         |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEVatNo"]              | VatNo                   |                                                                                                                                                                          |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEOrderAcknowledged"]  |                         | True if an order has been successfully acknowledged to CE. False if acknowledgement has been tried and failed. Missing if acknowledgement has not been attempted yet.    |
| AdditionalOrderInfo\["CEShipmentCreated"]    |                         | True if the shipment has been successfully created in CE. False if shipment creation has been tried and failed. Missing if shipment creation has not been attempted yet. |

Note that no changes can be done on orders created from ChannelEngine. Order cancellation is not currently supported by the connector. If you cancel an order in Litium, the order needs to be manually cancelled from the ChannelEngine dashboard.

By default, a new customer and/or organisation will be created for each order from ChannelEngine. The connector will not try to match any existing customers or organisations in Litium.

ChannelEngine does not support pro-rata calculations for VAT on shipment fees. The VAT amount received from ChannelEngine will be used to calculate the VAT percentage of the shipment fee in Litium.


# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-channelengine/develop



<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Order shipment tracking creation

ChannelEngine shipment tracking is using tracking number object which is not present in the Litium system.

Because of that tracking information is not available as an out-of-box experience via `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine` package. A custom integration has to be created with the usage of `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.Services.ChannelEngineService.UpdateShipmentTracking` method.

<Note>
  Adding tracking information to shipment may result in shipment closure in ChannelEngine. Once a shipment is closed it may no longer be edited.
</Note>


# Getting started
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-channelengine/get-started

Get started with ChannelEngine.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

1. Start by requesting a merchant account from [ChannelEngine](http://www.channelengine.com) in order to receive an API key and API URL.

   Use these credentials when configuring the add-on.

2. Set up a feed with product data that ChannelEngine can access.

   This can be done in many different ways depending on your solution's needs. Please see the page below for an example implementation of this using the price agent feed built into Litium. Details on the required format of the feed can be found in [ChannelEngine documentation](https://support.channelengine.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409484576925-ChannelEngine-product-feeds).

The feed is used to create and update products and product information in ChannelEngine while stock and price are updated via API calls when the watched pricelist or inventory is updated.

Orders created from ChannelEngine will by default be in the "Init" state. The connector will automatically create the order, a payment, and a delivery. You will need to adapt your solution to handle these orders and move them to the "Confirmed" state. This includes reducing stock in Litium to trigger a stock update to ChannelEngine.

For most marketplace channels, a tracking number is required to accept the delivery by the marketplace. More information about how to send this information can be found on the Develop page. Partial deliveries and orders fulfilled by the marketplace are currently not supported by the connector.


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-channelengine/install

Installation instructions for ChannelEngine.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Read the [system requirements](https://docs.litium.com/documentation/previous-versions/litium-6/get-started/system-requirements) for the development environment before installing the add-on. The ChannelEngine Connector is installed via NuGet:

* Open Visual Studio and your solution.
* Install the `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine` package from Litium NuGet feed
* Build the solution. The add-on automatically creates a number of tasks when the Litium application starts, see details below.
* Change `Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.dll.config` file with your solution's values if they differ from what already existing in the file.
* Configure one Channel to be used for ChannelEngine.
* Setup a product feed for ChannelEngine. This can be done using the price agent framework in Litium.
* You will need to adapt the order flow to have a complete order integration, more information can be found in the Develop section.

## Startup tasks

Following list describes tasks that are registered by the package to be executed on Litium startup:

**`Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.Setup.ChannelTemplatesSetupTask`**

Creates field definitions and extends field templates to provide Litium Back Office configuration for Channel Engine integration. To get more [information about the configuration available for the package, please see Configure](configure).

**`Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.Setup.InventoryEventsSetupTask`**

Registers handlers for inventory update events. This tasks monitors inventories configured for any of the Litium channels via ChannelEngineInventory channel field. Any changes in the stock number for any of the products in the inventory are passed to Channel Engine via ChannelEngineService.

**`Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.Setup.OrderEventsSetupTask`**

Registers handlers for order update events. This tasks monitor orders for any changes and informs the ChannelEngine endpoint associated with the Litium channel to which the order belongs.

**`Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.Setup.PriceListEventsSetupTask`**

Registers handlers for price list update events. This task monitors the price list configured for any of the Litium channels via the ChannelEnginePriceList channel field. Any changes in the price for any of the products in the price list are passed to Channel Engine via ChannelEngineService.

**`Litium.AddOns.ChannelEngine.Setup.SchedulerSetupTask`**

Registers tasks that shall be executed periodically using configurable time intervals.

# Security
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/configure/security

Secure the web api endpoints with a Litium service account or cookie authentication.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Using service account

Certain endpoints are secured to use Litium Service Account so that only a remote server that knows the service account credentials can access them.

Read about [other methods of securing here](https://docs.litium.com/platform/previous-versions/litium-6/architecture/web-api).

To use the service account, mark the endpoints with `Litium.Web.WebApi.OnlyServiceAccountAuthorization` attribute.

## Configure service account

In Litium backoffice, **Control panel > System settings > service accounts**, add a service account and associate it with an existing user. The associated existing users' user groups will ultimately control the amount of access this service account user would have.

The endpoint that needs to be secured has to be marked with `OnlyServiceAccountAuthorization` attribute. For example, the Get method in `OrderController`.

To access the endpoint, an appropriate authorization header should be sent. One way to test is to copy the ServiceAccount `<passwordhash>` as an Authorization header and use the Postman client to send in a request.

<img alt="service account auth.jpg" />

In practice when calling from a client, you can send in the `access_token` instead of the authorization header. The access token should be fetched from `/Litium/Oauth/Token` endpoint. The resulting `access_token` should be sent in as the bearer token in the Authorization header.

<img alt="bearer token.png" />


# Add a basic endpoint
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/develop/add-an-endpoint

This article walks through an example on adding an endpoint which just displays a simple string.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

To create an endpoint, create a class that derives from `HeadlessApiControllerBase` class. Apply the `RoutePrefix` attribute to the class level, that define the url to this endpoint.

## Basic endpoint

For this example, we create a `TestPage` controller, that would have the url `<your domain name>/headlessapi/Test`

```csharp theme={null}
[RoutePrefix(Routes.RootUri + "/TestPage")]
public class TestPageController:HeadlessApiControllerBase
{

}
```

Add a HTTP GET method that would simply return a string "This is a test page"

```csharp theme={null}
[RoutePrefix(Routes.RootUri + "/TestPage")]
public class TestPageController:HeadlessApiControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    [Route("", Name = "TestPage")]
    public IHttpActionResult Get()
    {           
        return Ok("This is a test page");
    }
}
```

If the Litium instance running is on `server.localtest.me`, the url to the test page would be `http://server.localtest.me/headlessApi/TestPage`

Open Postman and send a GET request to this page, which would produce the following output.

<img alt="TestPage_Get.png" />


# Exception handling
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/develop/exception-handling

The exceptions are globally handled in the ErrorFilterAttribute class.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Continuing the previous example, if we post a height = 0 into our `http://server.localtest.me/headlessApi/TestPage` endpoint, and then try to get the TestPage, we would get an invalid operation exception.

However, instead of a Internal Server Error, the HTTP status returned is a Invalid Operation.

The reason is, the exception is intercepted in the `src\Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi\Attributes\ErrorFilterAttribute.cs` class, and re-wired as a BadRequest.

You should consider doing the same thing for known errors, as they are not server errors, rather unexpected data.

```csharp theme={null}
switch(actionExecutedContext.Exception)
{
    //Here we treat known exceptions as BadRequests. 
    //these exceptions are not bugs in code, just that the original request is bad.
    //TODO: handle other known exceptions.
    case DoesNotExistException doesNotExistsException:
    case InvalidOperationException invalidOperationException:
        actionExecutedContext.Response = actionExecutedContext.Request.CreateErrorResponse(HttpStatusCode.BadRequest, new HttpError(actionExecutedContext.Exception, true));
        return;
}
```


# Model builders
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/develop/model-builders

We continue the previous example by adding more content, this time in the form of a model.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

The content is placed in a separate class `TestPageModel`, and it is built using a `TestPageModelBuilder` class.

Separating out the content data into a "model" class is part of the MVC design pattern.

In the example model, we just add two numbers weight and height. We create it under `Models\Site` and add the `TestPageModel.cs`, inherit from `PageModel` to give common base class functionality.

```csharp theme={null}
public class TestPageModel : PageModel
{
    public int Height { get; set; }
    public decimal Weight { get; set; }
}
```

We use a model builder class to separate out the model building. We apply the service attribute to the class, so it can be injected into the `TestPageController` constructor.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection;

namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site.Builders
{
    [Service(Lifetime = DependencyLifetime.Singleton, ServiceType = typeof(TestPageModelBuilder))]
    public class TestPageModelBuilder
    {
        private const int initialHeight = 181;
        private const decimal initialWeight = 50;

        public TestPageModel Build()
        {
            return new TestPageModel()
            {
                Weight = initialWeight,
                Height = initialHeight
            };
        }
    }
}
```

We modify the `TestPageController`, with the model builder injected into the constructor. We use the `ModelBuilder` to build the test page model.

For the web API swagger documentation, we apply the `ResponseType` Attribute, so the response type is generated documentation is correct.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site;
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site.Builders;
using System.Web.Http;
using System.Web.Http.Description;

namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Controllers.Site
{
    [RoutePrefix(Routes.RootUri + "/TestPage")]
    public class TestPageController:HeadlessApiControllerBase
    {
        private readonly TestPageModelBuilder _testPageModelBuilder;

        public TestPageController(TestPageModelBuilder testPageModelBuilder)
        {
            _testPageModelBuilder = testPageModelBuilder;
        }

        [HttpGet]
        [Route("", Name = "TestPage")]
        [ResponseType(typeof(TestPageModel))]
        public IHttpActionResult Get()
        {
            var model = _testPageModelBuilder.Build();
            if (model == null)
            {
                return NotFound();
            }
            return Ok(model);
        }
    }
}
```

# Services
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/develop/services

The business logic should be separated out into Service classes so that controllers are decoupled from them.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

This makes it easier to reuse business logic and results in more readable elegant design. We continue the previous example to add business logic to test page, by calculating the Body-mass index.

## Model change

Our model should change to store the Body mass index.

```csharp theme={null}
namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site
{
    public class TestPageModel : PageModel
    {
        public int Height { get; set; }
        public decimal Weight { get; set; }

        public decimal BodyMassIndex { get; set; }
    }
}
```

## Service to separate business logic

The actual calculation is business logic, we separate it out into a `BodyMassIndexService` class, which is put under the `TestServices` folder. We apply the service attribute, so it can be constructor injected to the model builder.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection;
using System;

namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Services.TestServices
{
    [Service(Lifetime = DependencyLifetime.Singleton, ServiceType = typeof(BodyMassIndexService))]
    public class BodyMassIndexService
    {
        public decimal Calculate(int height, decimal weight)
        {
            if (height <= 0)
                throw new InvalidOperationException("Height should be greater than zero");

            //bodymass index = weight / (height square)
            return decimal.Divide(weight, height * height);
        }
    }
}
```

Then we inject the `BodyMassIndexService` into the model builder, so it can use it to calculate the Body mass index.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Services.TestServices;
using Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection;

namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site.Builders
{
    [Service(Lifetime = DependencyLifetime.Singleton, ServiceType = typeof(TestPageModelBuilder))]
    public class TestPageModelBuilder
    {
        private const int initialHeight = 181;
        private const decimal initialWeight = 50;
        private readonly BodyMassIndexService _bodyMassIndexService;

        public TestPageModelBuilder(BodyMassIndexService bodyMassIndexService)
        {
            _bodyMassIndexService = bodyMassIndexService;
        }

        public TestPageModel Build()
        {
            return new TestPageModel()
            {
                Weight = initialWeight,
                Height = initialHeight,
                BodyMassIndex = _bodyMassIndexService.Calculate(initialHeight, initialWeight)
            };
        }
    }
}
```

When the endpoint is accessed, it produces the following output.

<img alt="using service output.png" />


# Tools for development
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/develop/tools

Fiddler and Postman are two tools that would help in development, together with Swagger docs.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Fiddler

Fiddler is a debugging proxy that allows viewing the network communication between programs. You can read and install it from [Telerik fiddler official site](https://www.telerik.com/fiddler).

When using Fiddler, communication between the browser and the webserver is directly visible in Fiddler. However, the following configuration is needed to observe the background traffic such as server to server communication.

In the `web.config` that calls the web api, add the following code:

```xml theme={null}
<system.net>
   <defaultProxy enabled="true" useDefaultCredentials="true">
     <proxy autoDetect="False" bypassonlocal="False" proxyaddress="http://127.0.0.1:8888" usesystemdefault="False"/>
   </defaultProxy>
</system.net>
```

## Postman

Postman makes it easy to test the endpoints by sending web API requests. It can debug and save the requests for easy development and testing.

You can download Postman from [getpostman.com](https://www.getpostman.com/) site.

## Testing secure endpoints

When the headless api endpoints are marked with `Litium.Web.WebApi.OnlyServiceAccountAuthorization` attribute the bearer token need to be sent with the requests. Not having the bearer token or incorrect token results in an unauthorized error.

First, configure a service account in the Litium backoffice as described [here](../configure/security).

Then you need to acquire the auth token from Litium using the account configured above.

Send a HTTP POST request to the endpoint `http://server.localtest.me/Litium/Oauth/Token`, with the following form elements in the body:

* `grant_type` → `client_credentials`
* `client_id` → User Id of the service account
* `client_secret` → password specified in the service account

<img alt="bearer_token_request.png" />

As the response, you would receive the `access_token`.

Use this `access_token` as "bearer token" value in Authorization header when requesting a secure endpoint.

<img alt="send secure request.png" />


# User session
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/develop/user-session

Users' information about the current session is kept in the WebApiContext.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

We extend the previous example to store the user height and weight in the user session.

## Basic modifications to store data

The `TestPageModel` contains the height and the weight, but that is a display page. The actual user's height and weight belong to the user and therefore are separate from the data we render in the page.

We add a `UserInfo` class to keep the user's data:

```csharp theme={null}
namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.UserSessions
{
    public class UserInfo
    {
        public int Height { get; set; }
        public decimal Weight { get; set; }
    }
}
```

and add this class into `UserSession`, so it can be maintained across multiple requests.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Foundation.Modules.ECommerce.Carriers;
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.UserSessions.Builders;
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.UserSessions
{
    /// <summary>
    /// Info about current user. Use <see cref="UserSessionBuilder"/> to build.
    /// </summary>
    public class UserSession
    {
        public KeyValuePair<string, Guid> Currency { get; set; }
        public KeyValuePair<string, Guid> Culture { get; set; }
        public string Id { get; set; }
        public OrderCarrier OrderCarrier { get; set; }       
        public UserInfo UserInfo { get; set; }
    }
}
```

The user session builder should ideally use a `UserInfo` builder to build the user info. To keep the code simple, we build the user info also inside the userSession builder, we modify its `\src\Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi\Models\UserSessions\Builders\UserSessionBuilder.cs` `Build()` method.

```csharp theme={null}
public virtual UserSession Build(string id = null)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(id))
        id = Guid.NewGuid().ToString();           

    var orderCarrier = _orderFactory.Create(null, ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);
    orderCarrier.WebSiteID = Guid.Empty;

    var websiteSettings = _webSiteSettingsBuilder.Build();
    orderCarrier.CurrencyID = websiteSettings.CurrencyCodes.FirstOrDefault().Value;

    var result = new UserSession()
    {
        Id = id,
        OrderCarrier = orderCarrier,
        Culture = websiteSettings.DefaultLanguage,
        Currency = websiteSettings.DefaultCurrency,
        UserInfo = new UserInfo()
    };

    return result;
}
```

## POST information to user session

To save the information to the user session, we add a new endpoint, that can capture the user session. We pass in the user info as a parameter also.

When the `Route("{sessionId}"` attribute is set, it automatically finds and populates the `WebApiContext` parameter in the `SetUserInfo()` method below. This parameter binding is done in the `WebApiContextModelBinder` class (`src\Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi\Models\WebApiContextModelBinder.cs`).

We also modify the `Get` method, so that it will return the `TestPageModel` based on the current user session.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models;
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site;
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site.Builders;
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.UserSessions;
using System.Web.Http;
using System.Web.Http.Description;

namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Controllers.Site
{
    [RoutePrefix(Routes.RootUri + "/TestPage")]
    public class TestPageController:HeadlessApiControllerBase
    {
        private readonly TestPageModelBuilder _testPageModelBuilder;

        public TestPageController(TestPageModelBuilder testPageModelBuilder)
        {
            _testPageModelBuilder = testPageModelBuilder;
        }

        [HttpGet]
        [Route("{sessionId}", Name = "TestPage")]
        [ResponseType(typeof(TestPageModel))]
        public IHttpActionResult Get(WebApiContext webApiContext)
        {
            var model = _testPageModelBuilder.Build(webApiContext.UserSession.UserInfo);
            if (model == null)
            {
                return NotFound();
            }
            return Ok(model);
        }

        [HttpPost]
        [Route("{sessionId}", Name = "SetUserInfo")]
        [ResponseType(typeof(UserInfo))]
        public IHttpActionResult SetUserInfo(WebApiContext webApiContext, [FromBody] UserInfo userInfo)
        {           
            webApiContext.UserSession.UserInfo = userInfo;
            return Ok(webApiContext.UserSession.UserInfo);
        }
    }
}
```

The test page model builder should be changed, so that the model building accepts a `userInfo`, and builds the model from it.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.UserSessions;
using Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Services.TestServices;
using Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection;

namespace Litium.AddOns.HeadlessApi.Models.Site.Builders
{
    [Service(Lifetime = DependencyLifetime.Singleton, ServiceType = typeof(TestPageModelBuilder))]
    public class TestPageModelBuilder
    {
        private const int initialHeight = 181;
        private const decimal initialWeight = 50;
        private readonly BodyMassIndexService _bodyMassIndexService;

        public TestPageModelBuilder(BodyMassIndexService bodyMassIndexService)
        {
            _bodyMassIndexService = bodyMassIndexService;
        }

        public TestPageModel Build(UserInfo userInfo)
        {
            return new TestPageModel()
            {
                Weight = userInfo.Weight,
                Height = userInfo.Height,
                BodyMassIndex = _bodyMassIndexService.Calculate(userInfo.Height, userInfo.Weight)
            };
        }
    }
}
```

Then we send a POST request, with a body containing `UserInfo` json, and a `Content-Type` header with `application/json` as content type.

<img alt="Post userInfo.png" />

Now a Get request to the TestPage endpoint with same session would give our results back, together with bodymass index.

<img alt="GetPostedFromSession.png" />


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/install

To install HeadlessAPI simply add the Litium.AddOns.HeadlessAPI project to your existing Litium solution and build.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

* The download package contains the `Litium.AddOns.HeadlessAPI` project.
* Add the project into your existing Litium solution, reference the project from your MVC project (to copy the dlls to bin folder) and build.
* Update the payment providers in the headless API project to their latest released version (The Payment provider addons may have a newer version than the version shipped with the headless API src zip)

<Note>
  Headless API Addon may use a different version of Litium and other package references than your solution. In which case fix any warnings in the build that shows incompatibility of Litium dlls you have in your project vs Litium version used by the headless api addon. You may add binding redirects (recomended) or choose to upgrade/downgrade headless API addon references.
</Note>

After a successful build, you can browse the documentation from `http://your-domain/HeadlessApi-docs/index`


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-headless-api/overview

A WebAPI kit that can be the starting point for Litium in headless scenarios.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

This add-on will get you started with web APIs for headless e-commerce with Litium. It can also be used as a starting point to write SPA clients in such scenarios, as well as server-to-server integrations.


# Features
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-inriver-connector/features

inRiver comes with a number of functionalities.

<Badge>Litium 4.6.2</Badge> <Badge>Litium 4.7</Badge> <Badge>Litium 4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

* **Streamlined**: For Litium Accelerator B2C.
* **Model**: Creates Litium Products property fields and field templates based on the inRiver model.
* **Product Content**: Creates Litium Base Products, Variants, Assortments, Categories, using the inRiver entity types Item, Product, ChannelNode and Specification.
* **Relations**: Creates Litium Product relationships based on specified inRiver LinkTypes.
* **Images**: Transfers inRiver Resource entities as Litium Media image files, and links them to products and Categories.
* **Quasi-realtime updates**: Allows updates of entities in a published InRiver channel to be visible in Litium in near real time. Time depends mostly on actual file transfer time from the inRiver server to the Litium server.
* **Batch updates**: Updates can be scheduled to be executed at a given time of the day.
* **Architecture**: Based on inRiver Connect API and Litium Integration Kit.
