where T is specific item that should be imported.

## Methods that are mandatory to implement

```csharp theme={null}
protected override IEnumerable<Item> Transform(FileInfo importFile)
```

This method is responsible for transforming data from file into the Item class collection. The Item class can be POCO object which is responsible for carrying data into the Import method. Note that the Transform method returns a collection of Item objects.

```csharp theme={null}
protected override void ProcessItem(Item item)
```

This method is used to implement the main logic of importing data from the Item object into the Litium Studio structure.

## Methods that are optional to implement

```csharp theme={null}
protected override bool PrepareProcess(FileInfo importFile)
```

This method is used to implement preparation process logic such as read files, fetch Litium Studio related data or entity.

```csharp theme={null}
protected virtual void PostProcess(FileInfo importFile)
```

This method is used for post-processing logic.

## Processing workflow for integrations

Assuming the process described above the whole process of importing data into Litium Studio is as follows:

1. Prepare file, reading from disk and etc. (PrepareProcess)
2. Transform data from file into Item object (Transform)
3. Process data, importing data into Litium Studio (ProcessItem)
4. Final post-import procedures, deleting import file, move to another folder etc.


# Setup the standard file transfer service
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-integration-kit/previous-versions/version-7-to-7-3-x/setup-the-standard-file-transfer-service

How to set up the standard file transfer service.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Install the file transfer service

Follow these four steps to install the file transfer zip:

1. Make sure you have configuration to use [Litium NuGet](https://docs.litium.com/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-integration-kit/previous-versions/version-7-to-7-3-x) and other pre-requisites to develop.
2. Extract all files to optional folder on your local machine.
3. Open and compile `Litium.Integration.File.Transfer.sln` file.

## Integration import files

The `DefaultFileImportBase.cs` file is Litium Studio specific and should not be altered in order to avoid future upgrade problems. If you want to add methods common for all import cs-files they should be added in the `FileImportBase.cs` which all Import cs-files inherit from.

General:

* Corresponding folders are automatically generated in Litium when importing Variants, Price lists etc.
* Folders "Error", "Archive" and "Ignore" are created automatically as needed.
* All import files are imported in chronological order.
* All successfully imported files are saved in the Archive folder (except for media files which are saved in Litium Studio Media Archive)
* All incomplete files are sent to the "Error" folder
* All unknown files (for instance price list files that does not have the same name as the price list) are sent to the "Ignore" folder

## Example files are included in the package

<img alt="Sample files included in the package" />

## Product Data Import

The standard product data xml file has a structured format to handle the base products & variants, price and inventory information. All information is in a single structure to correctly handle the import and that the price list integration is not run before the variant integration has been executed. That could cause the information to mis-match between the systems, for example if trying to import prices before the variant has been created.

If you add or delete any element in this file you also need to update the corresponding validation file: `ProductDataImport.xsd`. The XSD file validates that the xml file is correct when importing. If a file cannot be validated it is sent to the "Error" folder. See examples in the `ProductData.xml` file in the package.

## Pricelist import

The first step, prior to importing pricelists, is to set them up in Litium Studio. If a pricelist has not been created in Litium Studio before importing files it will NOT be created automatically.

Note! The pricelist Id must be the same as the filename (excluding extension).

Pricelists are imported as tab-separated text files: Article number (tab) Price (tab) minQuantity

The example file `PriceListId.txt` is found in the package.

## Stock balance import

The first step, prior to importing stock balance, is to set it up in Litium Studio. If a warehouse has not been created in Litium Studio before importing files it will NOT be created automatically and the files will be sent to the "Ignore" folder.

Note! The Inventory Id must be the same as the stock balance filename (excluding extension).

Pricelists are imported as tab-separated text files: Article number (tab) Quantity(tab)

The example file `InventoryId.txt` is found in the package.

## App.Config file settings

Check all of below settings in the `App.Config` file and make the changes needed.

In AppSettings\value, set the path to the Litium studio Integration Kit folder on your server:

```xml theme={null}
<appSettings>
  <add key="IntegrationDirectory" value="[YourRootPath]\Src\Files\Integration" />
```

The ConnectionString should be the same as for your Litium Studio installation:

```xml theme={null}
<connectionStrings>
  <add name="FoundationConnectionString" connectionString="Pooling=;User Id=;Password=;Database=;Server=" />
```

The Integration service covers four default important tasks:

* Product data import - `Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.ProductDataImport`
* MediaArchive import - `Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.MediaImport`
* Price list import - `Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.PriceListImport`
* Stock balance import - `Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.StockBalanceImport`

Where:

* `type` – full type name for the task responsible for the integration process
* `parameters` – not mandatory, can be used to transfer additional data into the task
* `startTime` - time to start executing the integration task from service start
* `interval` – interval between executing the task

All default integration values can be changed:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.ProductDataImport, Litium.Integration.Implementation" parameters="" startTime="04:00" interval="10m" />
<scheduledTask type="Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.MediaImport, Litium.Integration.Implementation" parameters="" startTime="04:00" interval="10m" />
<scheduledTask type="Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.PriceListImport, Litium.Integration.Implementation" parameters="" startTime="04:00" interval="10m" />
<scheduledTask type="Litium.Integration.Implementation.Imports.StockBalanceImport, Litium.Integration.Implementation" parameters="" startTime="04:00" interval="10m" />
```

## Build the integration service

By right-clicking the `Litium.Integration.Service` you build the file transfer service. Correct any errors and if necessary rebuild.

The integration service is now installed.

## How to install as a Windows service

If you want to you can set it up as a [Windows service](./install-as-a-windows-service) running in the background on your server.

## How to build custom implementation tasks

The windows service integration kit allows integration process to run for custom import implementation.


# Features
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-nosto-connector/litium-version-4-8-and-5/features

Features and functionality in Nosto connector for Litium 5.

<Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

### Features

Nosto analyzes your customers' behavior, learning their likes and dislikes, and enables you to deliver automated, personalized recommendations in real-time.

* Facebook Ads
* Product Recommendations
* Behavioral Pop-ups
* Triggered Emails

### Litium Nosto Connector functionality

The connector updates products and connects to Nosto.

* Products are updated in Nosto if there are changes in one of the fields: `articleNumber`, `price`, `categories`, `name`, `URL`, `imageurl`, or `status`.
* The `ArticleNumber` is used as a unique key to connect products to Nosto.
* If the price is `0`, or `url` or `description` is empty, the product is disconnected from Nosto.
* If the product doesn't exist in the stock, the product is marked as "OutOfStock" in Nosto.

### Products in Nosto

A product in Nosto has one URL. If a product exists in more than one category in Litium it has more than one URL. The URL from the category where the product has the "MainCategory" flag as true is sent to Nosto.

Conditions and data sent to Nosto:

1. The Article number, name, description, imageUrl, and brand are taken from the BaseProduct.
2. Price and stock status are taken from the first published variant.
3. URL — if the template for the product has the flag "show as product" in the settings, the BaseProduct's URL will be used; otherwise the URL will be taken from the first published variant.
4. If some of the fields (name, description, imageUrl, and brand) are empty in the BaseProduct, those fields will be used from the first published variant.

The "Categories" field contains all Categories where the product is published. For the product with variants, it additionally has categories where variants are published.

### Prices sent to Nosto

If there are two prices on a product detail page (list price and price), the list price for both is sent (not the campaign price). If there is a campaign price, it will be sent to Nosto from the shopping cart and order confirmation page.


# Install and Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-nosto-connector/litium-version-4-8-and-5/install-and-configure

How to install the Litium Nosto Connector and update templates to work with it.

<Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

### Install

1. [Download](http://kc.litiumstudio.se/add-ons) the add-on package.
2. Copy the contents of the `Source\Src\Litium.AddOns.Nosto.UI\Site` folder in the installation package to your `wwwroot\Site` folder.
3. Add the `Source\Src\Litium.AddOns.Nosto\Litium.AddOns.Nosto.xproj` project to your solution.
4. The WebSite must have a pre-selected Assortment and AssortmentLanguage.
5. Add the following Scheduled task to your `web.config`:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.Nosto.NostoScheduler, Litium.AddOns.Nosto"
  startTime="00:00" interval="1D"
  parameters="ResendFailedProductsIntervalInMinutes=10, CountOfResendFailedProductsAttempt=1" />
```

### Notes for NostoScheduler settings

* `ResendFailedProductsIntervalInMinutes` — Sets the interval in minutes when it tries to resend updated products to Nosto (in case some errors occur during the first sending attempt).
* `CountOfResendFailedProductsAttempt` — Sets the number of attempts for resending data to Nosto.

### Update templates

1. Add the following settings fields to "StartPage" and fill them in with the corresponding data from Nosto:
   * `NostoApiKey` (Text short) — API key from Nosto.
   * `NostoEmbedScript` (Text middle) — Add the embed script with Nosto account ID. See [http://my.nosto.com/tagging](http://my.nosto.com/tagging).

2. `EmbedScript.ascx` must be added to the `Base.master` file.

   Registration at the top of the file:

   ```aspx theme={null}
   <%@ Register TagPrefix="nosto" TagName="NostoEmbedScript"
     Src="~/Site/CMS/Templates/UserControls/Nosto/EmbedScript.ascx" %>
   ```

   Inside the `<head>` tag:

   ```aspx theme={null}
   <head>
       <site:Head runat="server" />
       <asp:ContentPlaceHolder ID="Head" runat="server" />
       <nosto:NostoEmbedScript runat="server" />
   </head>
   ```

3. `Tagging.ascx` must be added to the `Default.master`.

   Registration at the top of the file:

   ```aspx theme={null}
   <%@ Register TagPrefix="nosto" TagName="NostoTagging"
     Src="~/Site/CMS/Templates/UserControls/Nosto/Tagging.ascx" %>
   ```

   Tagging after the `<asp:ContentPlaceHolder ID="Content" runat="server" />` tag:

   ```aspx theme={null}
   <asp:ContentPlaceHolder ID="Content" runat="server" />
   <nosto:NostoTagging runat="server" />
   ```

4. `ShoppingCartTags.ascx` must be added to the `MiniCart.ascx` control (User Controls).

   Registration at the top of the file:

   ```aspx theme={null}
   <%@ Register TagPrefix="nosto" TagName="ShoppingCartTags"
     Src="~/Site/CMS/Templates/UserControls/Nosto/ShoppingCartTags.ascx" %>
   ```

   Tag inside the cart:

   ```aspx theme={null}
   <div class="cart-container">
       <%--Tag the shopping cart content--%>
       <nosto:ShoppingCartTags runat="server" />
   </div>
   ```

If more tagging is needed, it is up to the customer and project team to decide what has to be implemented additionally. See more in [Nosto's documentation](https://support.nosto.com/get-started/categories/api-documentation/).

### Quick verification

For quick verification of whether the Nosto connector works, add `?nostodebug=true` to the URL:

```
http://yourdomain/?nostodebug=true
```

### If sending to Nosto failed

If sending information to Nosto fails, the file with products is stored in the `FailedProducts` folder. Later the failed products will be resent in the background.

# Configuration
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-nosto-connector/litium-version-7-x/configuration

How to configure the Litium Nosto Connector add-on.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Configuration

In file `Litium.AddOns.Nosto.dll.config`:

**PageTypes:**

* `nostoPageType` — The type of the supported Nosto recommendations. Do not alter.
* `recommendationsFieldId` — The Id of the created field on Litium Channel. Do not alter.
* `litiumPageType` — The type of Litium page. The values in the config file are the currently supported types of Litium pages.

**Fields (Product & Variant):**

* `name` attribute is for system use when picking up the element and **must** be unique; otherwise only the first match will be picked by the system.
* `nodeId` attribute will be shown as class id/name for Nosto field elements.
* `litiumId` attribute is the Id of the field in Litium from which the value will be read.

When choosing a multifield from Litium, the Nosto class name will be the Id of the Litium field and the value will be the field value, so `nostoId` will not be printed as a class name on those elements.

If you need to override the values from system fields, use the Litium Decorator approach on `INostoProductService`. Read more on [how to decorate a service](https://docs.litium.com/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/architecture/dependency-injection/service-decorator).

**Products synchronization**

Add the following `ScheduledTask` to the solution's `web.config`:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.Nosto.ProductSynchronizationScheduler, Litium.AddOns.Nosto"
  startTime="00:00" interval="1h"/>
```

Sending updates to Nosto through REST API occurs when:

* BaseProduct/Variant information is updated
* BaseProduct/Variant Category relations changed
* BaseProduct/Variant ProductList relations changed
* BaseProduct/Variant Channel relations changed
* Variant `PriceListItemUpdated`
* Campaign Activated/Deactivated on Actions: `ReducePriceByPercentageAction` and `ArticleCampaignPriceAction` when no conditions are included
* Inventory quantity changed

**Channel settings in Litium Back Office**

<img alt="Nosto channel settings" />

Settings you need to fill in:

* Enable/disable the Nosto addon.
* Nosto Account number, EmailToken, and ProductToken — found in your Nosto Back Office.
* `NostoRecommendations` — The Id of the Nosto recommendation block, found in Nosto Back Office on the Recommendations page. This is only needed for pages that have no landing page in the Litium Websites module (such as the Product page). Some code needs to be added in the `.cshtml` page to fill it with the Nosto recommendations block. On pages with a landing page, you can use the Litium Recommendations Block created automatically on installation; you only need to fill it with the Id of the Nosto Recommendations Placement.

<img alt="Nosto recommendations block" />

## Quick verification

On product, category, brand, and search pages click F12 and check the Nosto tags under `div id="Globalnotification"` / `div class="nosto_product"`.

Nosto recommendations will appear at the end of the main body of the page above the footer, also inside `div id="Globalnotification"`. Styling of the recommendations block should occur in Nosto Back Office. For more information on how to create recommendations, refer to your Nosto account dashboard.

For quick verification of whether the Nosto connector works, add `?nostodebug=true` to the URL:

```
http://yourdomain/?nostodebug=true
```

You can also expose your local environment to the outside by using [Ngrok](https://ngrok.com/).

Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-nosto-connector/litium-version-7-x/develop

Develop the Nosto connector.

### Adding code in existing files

**In `Litium.Accelerator\ViewModels\Framework\CartViewModel.cs`**

Add this property:

```csharp theme={null}
public string NostoCartHtmlTagging { get; set; }
```

**In `Litium.Accelerator\Builders\Framework\CartViewModelBuilder.cs`**

Insert this in the `Build` method:

```csharp theme={null}
public CartViewModel Build(Cart cart)
{
    // other code

    return new CartViewModel
    {
        // other code
        NostoCartHtmlTagging = NostoHelper.GenerateCartHtmlTagging(cart)
    };
}
```

**In `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc\Definitions\FieldTemplateSetupDecorator.cs`**

Add this line to the end of the `_controllerMapping` dictionary:

```csharp theme={null}
[(typeof(Blocks.BlockArea), "Nosto")] = (typeof(NostoBlockController), nameof(NostoBlockController.Index))
```

**In `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc\Client\Scripts\index.js` at row 24**

Apply `cartMiddleware` to the end of the parameter. It would look like this example:

```js theme={null}
const store = window.__litium.store = window.__litium.store || (window.parent.__litium && window.parent.__litium.store)
    || createStore(app, preloadState, composeWithDevTools(applyMiddleware(thunk, historyMiddleware, cartMiddleware)));
```

For Nosto recommendations that have landing pages on the Website, you can use the Nosto Recommendation Block to visualize the Nosto Recommendation Products. Otherwise you will need to add code in the page views directly.

**Add code in `.cshtml` pages that do not have landing pages for Nosto recommendations**

You need these namespaces:

```csharp theme={null}
@using Litium;
@using Litium.Web.Routing;
@using Litium.FieldFramework;
```

Then add this code wherever you want to visualize the Nosto recommendations on the page (example of Product page):

```csharp theme={null}
var pageType = "Product-page";
var fields = IoC.Resolve<RouteRequestLookupInfoAccessor>().RouteRequestLookupInfo.Channel?.Fields?.GetValue<IEnumerable<MultiFieldItem>>(pageType);
if (fields != null)
{
    foreach (var field in fields)
    {
        var id = field.Fields?.GetValue<string>($"{pageType}-nosto-Id");
        @Html.Raw($"<div class=\"nosto_element\" id=\"{id}\"></div>")
    }
}
```

Alternatively, you can add the logic in the `ViewModelBuilder` instead and run the `foreach` method on a newly created property, e.g. `List<string> NostoRecommendationIds`, on the ViewModel.

### Toggle marketing permission

A customer field named `NostoMarketingPermission` will be added automatically to handle customer marketing permission in Customers/Persons/Person properties.

Use `INostoCustomerService` to handle and send permission to Nosto.

**Insert these lines of code in `Litium.Accelerator/ViewModels/MyPages/MyDetailsViewModel.cs`:**

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.AddOns.Nosto.Constants;

public bool MarketingPermission { get; set; }

[UsedImplicitly]
void IAutoMapperConfiguration.Configure(IMapperConfigurationExpression cfg)
{
   cfg.CreateMap<PageModel, MyDetailsViewModel>();
   cfg.CreateMap<Person, MyDetailsViewModel>()
      .ForMember(x => x.CustomerNumber, m => m.MapFrom(person => person.Id))

      // Insert this line of code
      .ForMember(x => x.MarketingPermission, m => m.MapFrom(person => person.Fields.GetValue<bool>(NostoConstants.CustomerField.MarketingPermissionId)))

      .ForMember(x => x.DeliveryAddress, m => m.MapFrom<AddressViewModelResolver>())
      .ForMember(x => x.AlternativeDeliveryAddress, m => m.MapFrom<AlternativeAddressViewModelResolver>())
      .ReverseMap()
      .ForMember(x => x.Addresses, m => m.MapFrom<AddressModelResolver>());
}
```

**Insert these lines of code in `Litium.Accelerator/Services/MyPagesViewModelService.cs`**

Inject `INostoCustomerService` in the constructor, then:

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.AddOns.Nosto.Services;

public virtual void SaveMyDetails(IViewModel viewModel)
{
    var person = _personService.Get(_securityContextService.GetIdentityUserSystemId().GetValueOrDefault())?.MakeWritableClone();
    if (person == null) return;

    person.MapFrom(viewModel);

    using (_securityContextService.ActAsSystem())
    {
        _personService.Update(person);
    }

    // Insert this section of code
    if(viewModel is MyDetailsViewModel detailsViewModel)
    {
        if (detailsViewModel.MarketingPermission)
        {
            _nostoCustomerService.GrantConsent(person);
        }
        else
        {
            _nostoCustomerService.RevokeConsent(person);
        }
    }
    CheckoutState.ClearState();
}
```

**Insert these lines of code in `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Views/MyPages/_MyDetailsPanel.cshtml`** wherever you want the checkbox to appear:

```html theme={null}
<div class="row">
    <div class="columns small-12 medium-4">
        @Html.CheckBoxFor(x => x.MarketingPermission)
        @Html.LabelFor(x => x.MarketingPermission, @Html.WebSiteString("marketing.permission"))
    </div>
</div>
```

Finally, build the solution and client scripts.

# Features
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-nosto-connector/litium-version-7-x/features

Functionality included in the Nosto connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Features

Nosto analyzes your customers' behavior, learning their likes and dislikes, and enables you to deliver automated, personalized recommendations in real-time.

* Product Tagging
* Category and Brands Tagging
* Search Tagging
* Cart Tagging
* Customer Tagging
* Order Tagging
* PageType tagging
* Product Recommendations
* Data synchronization

The connector updates products and connects to Nosto.

* Products are updated in Nosto if there are changes in one of the fields: `articleNumber`, `price`, `categories`, `name`, `url`, `imageurl`, or `status`.
* The `ArticleNumber` is used as a unique key to connect products to Nosto.
* If `price`, `url`, or `imageUrl` are empty, the product is disconnected from Nosto.
* If the product doesn't exist in the stock, the product is marked as "OutOfStock" in Nosto.
* If the product is removed, the product is discontinued from Nosto.

The connector sends GDPR requests to Nosto. These requests are hooked to Litium GDPR.

The connector also sends the blacklisting/unblacklisting emails and customers' Marketing Permission to Nosto.

**Unsupported features:**

* Support for multi-currency
* Support for customer group pricing

### Products in Nosto

[Product schema](https://github.com/Nosto/techdocs/wiki/Basic:-Default-Product-Tagging)

[Variant schema](https://github.com/Nosto/techdocs/wiki/Extending-tagging-with-SKUs)

A product in Nosto has one url. If a product exists in more than one category in Litium it has more than one url. The url from the category where the product has the "MainCategory" flag as true is sent to Nosto.

Conditions and data are sent to Nosto:

**If the product page is Product-based:**

The price of the Nosto product will contain the cheapest price from all its variants, and if it exists in any variant stock then it will show "InStock" in the Nosto product.

**If the product page is Variant-based:**

The product will contain only one variant and the property values on both product and its variant will match.

The "Categories" field contains all Categories where the product is published. For the product with variants, it additionally has categories where variants are published.

### Prices sent to Nosto

List-price and Campaign-Price are sent to Nosto, and if no campaign-price exists then both prices will be list-price value.

### Category, Brand, and Search Tagging

Category/Brands Id/Name and Search-query will be tagged on the page for Nosto to crawl. (Not visible on-page but in Html.)

### Recommendations tagging

Based on Nosto's own algorithms similar products will be shown/visible at the end of the main body of the site page depending on what type of Nosto Recommendations is chosen to be shown.

# Get started
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/get-started

Get started with Voyado by requesting a merchant account.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Request a merchant account from [www.voyado.com](http://www.voyado.com/). You will receive the API key and API server URLs from Voyado. The API key and API server URLs are used to configure the Litium Voyado add-on.

You also need to give Voyado information on how to set up a tenant. The following is required:

* List of channels (or website names in Litium 5) — these will be used as stores in Voyado.
* List of order states, at least Confirmed and Completed.
* List of payment states, at least Reserved and Paid.

Voyado tenant setup may be a process running together with project development, since it is a marketing automation system you will need to set the automation flows. Contact Voyado support for configuration.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/overview

The Litium Voyado Connector adds marketing automation to Litium through Voyado.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

The Litium Voyado Connector adds marketing automation to Litium through Voyado.

* [Voyado connector v7](/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v7/overview) requires Litium 7.x, where x is the latest service release.
* [Voyado connector v6](/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v6/overview) requires Litium 6.x, where x is the latest service release.
* [Voyado connector v5](/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v5/overview) requires Litium 5.x, where x is the latest service release.

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v5/configure

How to configure the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

### app.config

`src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\app.config` contains the configuration. If you are making a new installation, rename `app.config.sample` to `app.config`.

The config file will be copied to the accelerator MVC project bin (`wwwroot/bin`) as `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector.config`. Rebuild the project after configuration changes so a new copy with the latest saved information is created in the bin folder.

### Product feeds

Generation of product feeds needs to be enabled as a scheduled task from `web.config`:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Setup.FeedTask, Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation"
  startTime="00:00" interval="1d" parameters="maxAgeInDays=30" />
```

### Order stores

The list of stores configured at Voyado must have exactly the same names as your website names. Otherwise, the orders API may fail with 404 not found errors.

### Audit log cleanup

A scheduled task should clean up the `MarketingAutomation.AuditLog` table. Add this task as a scheduled task to `web.config`. The following example runs every day and cleans up log entries older than 30 days:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Setup.AuditLogCleanupTask, Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation"
  startTime="00:00" interval="1d" parameters="maxAgeInDays=30" />
```

### Going live

You may need to change the server URLs from staging to live URLs, and change the API keys. Contact Voyado regarding the going-live process.


# App building
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v5/develop/app-building

How to build the application.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

During Litium application startup, the marketing automation addons are registered using the `IConnectorInstaller` class. In Voyado the implementation is at `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Installer.cs`.

## Setup

The setup classes described in the previous section are added first. They will run during application startup.

```csharp theme={null}
public void Install(IAppBuilder appBuilder)
{
    appBuilder
        .AddConnector(Constants.ConnectorName, (connectorRegistration) =>
        {
            connectorRegistration
                .AddSetup<InstallConsents>()
                .AddSetup<InstallStore>();
        });
}
```

## Customer sync service

This service will sync Litium customers into Voyado contacts. ContactType in Voyado is "Member".

```csharp theme={null}
public void Install(IAppBuilder appBuilder)
{
    appBuilder
        .AddConnector(Constants.ConnectorName, (connectorRegistration) =>
        {
            connectorRegistration
                .AddCustomerSyncService((customerSyncServiceRegistration) =>
                {
                    customerSyncServiceRegistration
                        .UseSyncService<CustomerSyncService>()
                        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpClientExceptionCondition>()
                        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpRequestExceptionCondition>()
                        .AddExceptionHandler<MappingExceptionCondition>();
                })
        });
}
```

Marketing automation will not automatically trigger events when customers are created or updated. When a user is created, call the following method from your accelerator code to register the customer with Voyado:

```csharp theme={null}
//customerSystemId is the systemId of Litium person
IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterUserCreated(customerSystemId);
```

## Order sync service

Voyado needs to be notified when order states are changing. The following information is sent:

* User who created the order.
* Voyado receipt API
* Voyado orders API

The implementation is in `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\SyncServices\OrderSyncService.cs`.

This service is registered in `install.cs`:

```csharp theme={null}
.AddOrderSyncService((orderSyncServiceRegistration) =>
{
    orderSyncServiceRegistration
        .UseSyncService<OrderSyncService>()
        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpClientExceptionCondition>()
        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpRequestExceptionCondition>()
        .AddExceptionHandler<MappingExceptionCondition>();
})
```

As described in the install section, the order state change needs to be triggered from the accelerator state transitions in `\src\Litium.Accelerator\StateTransition\OrderStateBuilder.cs`:

```csharp theme={null}
//Order Confirmed
var confirmed = new State<OrderCarrier>((short)OrderState.Confirmed, OrderState.Confirmed.ToString(),
    (orderCarrier, currentState, token) =>
    {
        //Order confirmed entry action.
        //now the order is confirmed, reduce the stock balances.
        OrderUtilities.ReduceStockBalance(ModuleECommerce.Instance.Orders[orderCarrier.ID, token], ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //notify campaigns engine to take order confirmation actions.
        ModuleECommerce.Instance.CampaignCalculator.HandleOrderConfirmation(orderCarrier, ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //Send order confirmation email.
        IoC.Resolve<IMailService>().SendEmail(new OrderConfirmationEmail(orderCarrier.ID, orderCarrier.CustomerInfo.Address.Email, orderCarrier.WebSiteID), false);

        //Marketing automation integration code to execute when an order is confirmed.
        IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterOrderStateChanged(orderCarrier.ID);
    },
    null);
```

## Product feeds

Product feeds are configured from the following code in `Installer.cs`:

```csharp theme={null}
.AddProductFeedService<ProductFeedItem>("Common", "common", (productFeedServiceRegistration) =>
{
    productFeedServiceRegistration
        .UseConverter<VariantToProductFeedConverter>()
        .UseSerializer<ProductFeedSerializer>()
        .SetFeedPickupFolder($"{PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.FeedPickupFolder}")
        .SetScheduler(PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.WebsiteFeeds.DefaultDueTime,
                      PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.WebsiteFeeds.DefaultInterval,
                      PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.WebsiteFeeds.Enabled)
        .SetForceDownload(true);
})
.AddMarketFeedService(_converterFactory);
```

The common product feed exports all the variants. It uses `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.ProductFetcher` to query the Litium database to get the total list of variants. This fetcher is set by default and is not configured above.

You can add your own fetcher by using `.UseFecther<class that implements IFeedFetcher>()`.

`AddMarketFeedService` is the extension method that adds a feed for each website.

The list of feeds configured can be accessed through `http://<your domain>/marketingAutomationApi/Voyado/feeds`.

Note: This is a web-API endpoint. If the endpoint fails to work, this can be due to a version mismatch of underlying assemblies. Add `Litium.Web.WebApi.Abstractions` to your `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc` project and add the necessary assembly redirections. A warning of the mismatch will usually be displayed.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v5/develop/overview

How to develop the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

### Trace mode and audit log

Set the `traceMode` flag to `true` in the `app.config` in `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector` to get additional trace log messages to the Litium event log.

The communication between Litium and Voyado is also recorded in the `MarketingAutomation.AuditLog` table. Entries in the table that are older than 30 days are automatically cleared by an internal scheduled task.


# Setup
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v5/develop/setup

How to set up the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

When Litium starts, `IConnectorSetup` classes will run to set up the necessary infrastructure for marketing automation add-ons. They are configured during App building, which is described in the next article.

In the Voyado connector, this interface is implemented in:

* `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Setups\InstallStore.cs`
* `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Setups\InstallConsents.cs`, through base class `ConsentsInstallerBase<string, Consent>`

## Install store

`InstallStore.cs` implements the Voyado store API, calling Voyado to update or create the store.

## Install consents

User consents are end-user agreements to accept newsletters and other communication, as well as general terms and conditions. The list is related to GDPR agreements between end customers and merchants. The list of consents is set up by Voyado during tenant setup.

During Litium start-up, this list of consents is fetched and the Litium customer field template is updated by creating new boolean fields to store these consents. The list of consents should either be presented to end customers for explicit agreement as checkboxes, or end customers should be made aware of the implicit agreement to these consents, depending on business and legal requirements.

## Default behavior

When a logged-in user in Litium is synced to Voyado, the default behavior is to get consent from the user's Litium fields. See `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\PersonConverter.cs`.

```csharp theme={null}
var consents = _consentService.GetAllFromCache();
foreach (var item in consents)
{
    var fieldName = $"{Constants.Customer.Fields.CustomerConsentPrefix}{item.Id}";
    var field = person.CustomFields.GetField(fieldName) as BooleanField;
    if (field != null)
    {
        if (contact.Consents == null)
        {
            contact.Consents = new List<ContactConsent>();
        }
        contact.Consents.Add(new ContactConsent()
        {
            Id = item.Id,
            Value = (bool)field.Value,
            Date = DateTime.Now,
            Source = "Litium",
            Comment = string.Empty
        });
    }
}
```

When an anonymous user is synced to Voyado as a guest (for order processing), the default behavior is to set all consents to false. See `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\EcomPersonInfoConverter.cs`.

```csharp theme={null}
var consents = _consentService.GetAllFromCache();
foreach (var item in consents)
{
    if (contact.Consents == null)
    {
        contact.Consents = new List<ContactConsent>();
    }
    contact.Consents.Add(new ContactConsent()
    {
        Id = item.Id,
        Value = false,
        //TODO: we set as user has not consented to anything. The default consents would be in merchant terms of use agreement.
        Date = DateTime.Now,
        Source = "Litium",
        Comment = string.Empty
    });
}
```


# Upgrade
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v5/develop/upgrade

Upgrade instructions for the Voyado addon.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

### Upgrading to v5.6.107

#### Remove this line from CheckoutB2BController.cs and CheckoutB2CController.cs

```csharp theme={null}
private void UpdatePersonInformation(Person person, CustomerDetailsB2CViewModel customerDetailsViewModel)
{
    //...

    if (isUpdated)
    {
        person.SetValuesByCarrier(personCarrier, Solution.Instance.SystemToken);
        IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterUserUpdated(person.ID);
    }
}
```

#### Breaking change

This public method in `ContactService.cs` in the `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector` project has an extra parameter which is the Voyado Contact type — see `ContactType.cs`:

```csharp theme={null}
public Task<Contact> GetContactByEmailAsync(ContactType contactType, string email)
{
    if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(email))
    {
        throw new ArgumentException("Invalid email");
    }

    return Client.GetAsync<Contact>($"{BaseUrl}/{contactType.ToString()}/bykey/{email}");
}
```

Upgraded code in files:

* `OrderSyncService.cs`
* `CustomerSyncService.cs`
* `ContactType.cs`
* `ContactService.cs`

### Upgrading to v5.6.106

1. There are no configuration file changes.
2. Xslt transformation was found to be redundant and is removed. Xslt files are no longer needed to generate feed.
3. The following files in the Voyado project are changed:
   * `/Src/Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector/Converters/VariantToProductFeedConverter.cs` — `IFeedConverter` interface has changed, and code updated accordingly.
   * `/Src/Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector/Extensions/ObjectExtensions.cs` — Try-catch protection around generating logging information.
   * `/Src/Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector/Feeds/MarketFeedFilter.cs` — The implementing interface `IFeedFilter<T>` has changed, and code updated accordingly. Critical change: the lifetime dependency of the service is marked as `Transient` now.
   * `/Src/Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector/Serializers/ProductFeedSerializer.cs`

### Upgrading to v5.6.105

1. There are no configuration file changes.
2. In `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\VariantToProductFeedConverter.cs`, the `public bool CanConvert(Type type)` method is changed to return `typeof(Variant)`:

```csharp theme={null}
public bool CanConvert(Type type)
{
    return type == typeof(Variant);
}
```


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v5/install

Installation instructions for the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge>

### Prerequisites

Litium 5.x, where x is the latest service release.

### Set up a Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector project

1. Download the zip package from [Litium AddOns](https://docs.litium.com/resources/download-add-ons/connectors).
2. Unzip and copy the `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector` folder into your solutions folder.
3. Rename `app.config.sample` to `app.config`.
4. Add the `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector` project into your solution, and add a project reference from it to the `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` project.
5. Add NuGet packages `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation` to your `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` project. This will also add `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Abstractions`.
6. Add NuGet packages `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Abstractions` to your `Litium.Accelerator` project.

### Configure feed folder

In the files folder (or common files folder if you do not have one), create a sub-folder called `Voyado`.

### Configure accelerator state transitions

In `src\Litium.Accelerator\StateTransition\OrderStateBuilder.cs`, register `MarketingAutomation.RegisterOrderStateChanged` when an order is Confirmed and Completed. Add to any other states set up in your Voyado tenant.

You will need the following using statement: `using Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Abstractions;`

Order Confirmed state:

```csharp theme={null}
var confirmed = new State<OrderCarrier>((short)OrderState.Confirmed, OrderState.Confirmed.ToString(),
    (orderCarrier, currentState, token) =>
    {
        //Order confirmed entry action.
        //now the order is confirmed, reduce the stock balances.
        OrderUtilities.ReduceStockBalance(ModuleECommerce.Instance.Orders[orderCarrier.ID, token], ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //notify campaigns engine to take order confirmation actions.
        ModuleECommerce.Instance.CampaignCalculator.HandleOrderConfirmation(orderCarrier, ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //Send order confirmation email.
        IoC.Resolve<IMailService>().SendEmail(new OrderConfirmationEmail(orderCarrier.ID, orderCarrier.CustomerInfo.Address.Email, orderCarrier.WebSiteID), false);

        //Marketing automation integration code to execute when an order is confirmed.
        IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterOrderStateChanged(orderCarrier.ID);
    },
    null);
```

Add to the Order Completed event as well, and to any other states you want marketing automation flows on:

```csharp theme={null}
//Order Completed: All tasks relating to order is completed.
var completed = new State<OrderCarrier>((short)OrderState.Completed, OrderState.Completed.ToString(),
    (orderCarrier, currentState, token) =>
    {
        IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterOrderStateChanged(orderCarrier.ID);
    }, null);
```

### Build

Build the solution.

# Configure

How to configure the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

### app.config

<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Setup.FeedTask, Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation"

The list of stores configured at Voyado must have **exactly the same names as your website names**. Otherwise the orders API may fail with 404 not found errors.

# App building
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v6/develop/app-building

How to build the application.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

During Litium application startup, the marketing automation addons are registered using the `IConnectorInstaller` class. In Voyado the implementation is at `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Installer.cs`.

## Setup

                .AddCustomerSyncService((customerSyncServiceRegistration) =>

# Setup
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v6/develop/setup

How to set up the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

When Litium starts, `IConnectorSetup` classes will run to set up the necessary infrastructure for marketing automation add-ons. They are configured during App building, which is described in the next article.

In the Voyado connector, this interface is implemented in:

* `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Setups\InstallStore.cs`
* `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Setups\InstallConsents.cs`, through base class `ConsentsInstallerBase<string, Consent>`

## Install store

`InstallStore.cs` implements the Voyado store API, calling Voyado to update or create the store.

## Install consents

## Default behavior

When a logged-in user in Litium is synced to Voyado, the default behavior is to get consent from the user's Litium fields. See `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\PersonConverter.cs`.

```csharp theme={null}
var consents = _consentService.GetAllFromCache();
foreach (var item in consents)
{
    var fieldName = $"{Constants.Customer.Fields.CustomerConsentPrefix}{item.Id}";
    var field = person.CustomFields.GetField(fieldName) as BooleanField;
    if (field != null)
    {
        if (contact.Consents == null)
        {
            contact.Consents = new List<ContactConsent>();
        }
        contact.Consents.Add(new ContactConsent()
        {
            Id = item.Id,
            Value = (bool)field.Value,
            Date = DateTime.Now,
            Source = "Litium",
            Comment = string.Empty
        });
    }
}
```

When an anonymous user is synced to Voyado as a guest (for order processing), the default behavior is to set all consents to false. See `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\EcomPersonInfoConverter.cs`.

```csharp theme={null}
var consents = _consentService.GetAllFromCache();
foreach (var item in consents)
{
    if (contact.Consents == null)
    {
        contact.Consents = new List<ContactConsent>();
    }
    contact.Consents.Add(new ContactConsent()
    {
        Id = item.Id,
        Value = false,
        //TODO: we set as user has not consented to anything. The default consents would be in merchant terms of use agreement.
        Date = DateTime.Now,
        Source = "Litium",
        Comment = string.Empty
    });
}
```

Upgrade instructions for the Voyado addon.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

### Upgrading to v5.4.106

1. There are no configuration file changes.

   * `/Src/Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector/Extensions/ObjectExtensions.cs` — Try-catch protection around generating logging information.
   * `/Src/Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector/Feeds/MarketFeedFilter.cs` — The implementing interface `IFeedFilter<T>` has changed, and code updated accordingly. Critical change: the lifetime dependency of the service is marked as `Transient` now.
   * `/Src/Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector/Serializers/ProductFeedSerializer.cs`

### Upgrading to v5.4.105

1. There are no configuration file changes.
2. In `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\VariantToProductFeedConverter.cs`, the `public bool CanConvert(Type type)` method is changed to return `typeof(Variant)`:

```csharp theme={null}
public bool CanConvert(Type type)
{

}
```


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v6/install

Installation instructions for the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

### Prerequisites

Litium 6.x, where x is the latest service release.

### Set up a Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector project

1. Download the zip package from [Litium AddOns](https://docs.litium.com/resources/download-add-ons/connectors).
2. Unzip and copy the `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector` folder into your solutions folder.
3. Rename `app.config.sample` to `app.config`.
4. Add the `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector` project into your solution, and add a project reference from it to the `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` project.
5. Add NuGet packages `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation` to your `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` project. This will also add `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Abstractions`.
6. Add NuGet packages `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Abstractions` to your `Litium.Accelerator` project.

### Configure feed folder

In the files folder (or common files folder if you do not have one), create a sub-folder called `Voyado`.

### Configure accelerator state transitions

In `src\Litium.Accelerator\StateTransition\OrderStateBuilder.cs`, register `MarketingAutomation.RegisterOrderStateChanged` when an order is Confirmed and Completed. Add to any other states set up in your Voyado tenant.

You will need the following using statement: `using Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Abstractions;`

Order Confirmed state:

```csharp theme={null}
var confirmed = new State<OrderCarrier>((short)OrderState.Confirmed, OrderState.Confirmed.ToString(),
    (orderCarrier, currentState, token) =>
    {
        //Order confirmed entry action.
        //now the order is confirmed, reduce the stock balances.
        OrderUtilities.ReduceStockBalance(ModuleECommerce.Instance.Orders[orderCarrier.ID, token], ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //notify campaigns engine to take order confirmation actions.
        ModuleECommerce.Instance.CampaignCalculator.HandleOrderConfirmation(orderCarrier, ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //Send order confirmation email.
        IoC.Resolve<IMailService>().SendEmail(new OrderConfirmationEmail(orderCarrier.ID, orderCarrier.CustomerInfo.Address.Email, orderCarrier.WebSiteID), false);

        //Marketing automation integration code to execute when an order is confirmed.
        IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterOrderStateChanged(orderCarrier.ID);
    },
    null);
```

Add to the Order Completed event as well, and to any other states you want marketing automation flows on:

```csharp theme={null}
//Order Completed: All tasks relating to order is completed.
var completed = new State<OrderCarrier>((short)OrderState.Completed, OrderState.Completed.ToString(),
    (orderCarrier, currentState, token) =>
    {
        IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterOrderStateChanged(orderCarrier.ID);
    }, null);
```

### Build

Build the solution.

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v7/configure

How to configure the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## app.config

`src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\app.config` contains the configuration, with instructions in the file itself. If you are making a new installation, rename `app.config.sample` to `app.config`.

`Src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\app.config` will be copied to the accelerator MVC project bin (`wwwroot/bin`) as `Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector.config`.

New changes in the config file in v7.4.0 are the attributes in the `channelstoreMapping` node:

* `channelId` — Litium channel Id (check not null)
* `merchant` — Voyado merchant/store name
* `externalId` — Voyado merchant/store ExternalId

**Important:** Rebuild the project after configuration changes so a new copy with the latest saved information will be created in the bin folder.

## Product feeds

Generation of product feeds needs to be enabled as a scheduled task from `web.config`:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Setup.FeedTask, Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation"
  startTime="00:00" interval="1d" parameters="maxAgeInDays=30" />
```

You can see the list of product feeds at `http://<Your domain name>/marketingAutomationApi/Voyado/feeds`.

Send this list of feeds to Voyado in order to configure the tenant to download feeds.

## Order stores

This needs to be configured at Voyado tenant setup. The list of stores configured at Voyado must exactly match the ids of your channels — this can be done in the Voyado config file. Otherwise the orders API may fail with 404 not found errors.

If you have created the channels from the back office their programmatic id can be null; in this case, add code to initialize your channels with desired ids. You may use a start-up task for that.

## Audit log cleanup

A scheduled task should clean up the `MarketingAutomation.AuditLog` table. Add this task to `web.config`. The following example runs every day and cleans up log entries older than 30 days:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.Setup.AuditLogCleanupTask, Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation"
  startTime="00:00" interval="1d" parameters="maxAgeInDays=30" />
```

## Going live

You may need to change the server URLs from staging to live URLs, and change the API keys. Contact Voyado regarding the going-live process.


# App building
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v7/develop/app-building

How to build the application.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

During Litium application startup, the marketing automation addons are registered using the `IConnectorInstaller` class. In Voyado the implementation is at `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Installer.cs`.

## Setup

The setup classes described in the previous section are added first. They will run during application startup.

```csharp theme={null}
public void Install(IAppBuilder appBuilder)
{
    appBuilder
        .AddConnector(Constants.ConnectorName, (connectorRegistration) =>
        {
            connectorRegistration
                .AddSetup<InstallConsents>()
                .AddSetup<InstallStore>();
        });
}
```

## Customer sync service

This service will sync Litium customers into Voyado contacts. ContactType in Voyado is "Member".

```csharp theme={null}
public void Install(IAppBuilder appBuilder)
{
    appBuilder
        .AddConnector(Constants.ConnectorName, (connectorRegistration) =>
        {
            connectorRegistration
                .AddCustomerSyncService((customerSyncServiceRegistration) =>
                {
                    customerSyncServiceRegistration
                        .UseSyncService<CustomerSyncService>()
                        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpClientExceptionCondition>()
                        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpRequestExceptionCondition>()
                        .AddExceptionHandler<MappingExceptionCondition>();
                })
        });
}
```

Marketing automation will not automatically trigger events when customers are created or updated. When a user is created, call the following method from your accelerator code to register the customer with Voyado:

```csharp theme={null}
//customerSystemId is the systemId of Litium person
IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterUserCreated(customerSystemId);
```

## Order sync service

Voyado needs to be notified when order states are changing. The following information is sent:

* User who created the order.
* Voyado receipt API
* Voyado orders API

The implementation is in `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\SyncServices\OrderSyncService.cs`.

This service is registered in `install.cs`:

```csharp theme={null}
.AddOrderSyncService((orderSyncServiceRegistration) =>
{
    orderSyncServiceRegistration
        .UseSyncService<OrderSyncService>()
        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpClientExceptionCondition>()
        .AddExceptionHandler<HttpRequestExceptionCondition>()
        .AddExceptionHandler<MappingExceptionCondition>();
})
```

As described in the install section, the order state change needs to be triggered from the accelerator state transitions in `\src\Litium.Accelerator\StateTransition\OrderStateBuilder.cs`:

```csharp theme={null}
//Order Confirmed
var confirmed = new State<OrderCarrier>((short)OrderState.Confirmed, OrderState.Confirmed.ToString(),
    (orderCarrier, currentState, token) =>
    {
        //now the order is confirmed, reduce the stock balances.
        OrderUtilities.ReduceStockBalance(ModuleECommerce.Instance.Orders[orderCarrier.ID, token], ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //notify campaigns engine to take order confirmation actions.
        ModuleECommerce.Instance.CampaignCalculator.HandleOrderConfirmation(orderCarrier, ModuleECommerce.Instance.AdminToken);

        //Send order confirmation email.
        IoC.Resolve<IMailService>().SendEmail(new OrderConfirmationEmail(orderCarrier.ID, orderCarrier.CustomerInfo.Address.Email, orderCarrier.WebSiteID), false);

        //Marketing automation integration code to execute when an order is confirmed.
        IoC.Resolve<MarketingAutomationService>().RegisterOrderStateChanged(orderCarrier.ID);
    },
    null);
```

## Product feeds

Product feeds are configured from the following code in `Installer.cs`:

```csharp theme={null}
.AddProductFeedService<ProductFeedItem>("Common", "common", (productFeedServiceRegistration) =>
{
    productFeedServiceRegistration
        .UseConverter<VariantToProductFeedConverter>()
        .UseSerializer<ProductFeedSerializer>()
        .SetFeedPickupFolder($"{PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.FeedPickupFolder}")
        .SetScheduler(PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.WebsiteFeeds.DefaultDueTime,
                      PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.WebsiteFeeds.DefaultInterval,
                      PluginSettings.Instance.Configuration.WebsiteFeeds.Enabled)
        .SetForceDownload(true);
})
.AddMarketFeedService(_converterFactory);
```

The common product feed exports all the variants. It uses `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.ProductFetcher` to query the Litium database to get the total list of variants. This fetcher is set by default and is not configured above.

You can add your own fetcher by using `.UseFecther<class that implements IFeedFetcher>()`.

`AddMarketFeedService` is the extension method that adds a feed for each website.

The list of feeds configured can be accessed through `http://<your domain>/marketingAutomationApi/Voyado/feeds`.

Note: This is a web-API endpoint. If the endpoint fails to work, this can be due to a version mismatch of underlying assemblies. Add `Litium.Web.WebApi.Abstractions` to your `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc` project and add the necessary assembly redirections. A warning of the mismatch will usually be displayed.

The common product feed exports all the variants. It uses `Litium.AddOns.MarketingAutomation.ProductFetcher` to query the Litium database to get the total list of variants. This fetcher is set by default.

You can add your own fetcher by using `.UseFetcher<class that implements IFeedFetcher>()`.

`AddMarketFeedService` is the extension method that adds a feed for each website.

The list of feeds configured can be accessed through `http://<your domain>/marketingAutomationApi/Voyado/feeds`.

# Setup
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v7/develop/setup

How to set up the Litium Voyado Connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

When Litium starts, `IConnectorSetup` classes will run to set up the necessary infrastructure for marketing automation add-ons. They are configured during App building, which is described in the next article.

In the Voyado connector, this interface is implemented in:

* `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Setups\InstallStore.cs`
* `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Setups\InstallConsents.cs`, through base class `ConsentsInstallerBase<string, Consent>`

## Install store

`InstallStore.cs` implements the Voyado store API, calling Voyado to update or create the store.

## Install consents

User consents are end-user agreements to accept newsletters and other communication, as well as general terms and conditions. The list is related to GDPR agreements between end customers and merchants. The list of consents is set up by Voyado during tenant setup.

During Litium start-up, this list of consents is fetched and the Litium customer field template is updated by creating new boolean fields to store these consents. The list of consents should either be presented to end customers for explicit agreement as checkboxes, or end customers should be made aware of the implicit agreement to these consents, depending on business and legal requirements.

## Default behaviour

When a logged-in user in Litium is synced to Voyado, the default behaviour is to get the consents from the user's Litium fields. See `\src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\PersonConverter.cs`.

```csharp theme={null}
var consents = _consentService.GetAllFromCache();
foreach (var item in consents)
{
    var fieldName = $"{Constants.Customer.Fields.CustomerConsentPrefix}{item.Id}";
    var field = person.CustomFields.GetField(fieldName) as BooleanField;
    if (field != null)
    {
        if (contact.Consents == null)
        {
            contact.Consents = new List<ContactConsent>();
        }
        contact.Consents.Add(new ContactConsent()
        {
            Id = item.Id,
            Value = (bool)field.Value,
            Date = DateTime.Now,
            Source = "Litium",
            Comment = string.Empty
        });
    }
}
```

When an anonymous user is synced to Voyado as a guest (for order processing), the default behaviour is to set all consents to false. See `src\Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector\Converters\EcomPersonInfoConverter.cs`.

```csharp theme={null}
var consents = _consentService.GetAllFromCache();
foreach (var item in consents)
{
    if (contact.Consents == null)
    {
        contact.Consents = new List<ContactConsent>();
    }
    contact.Consents.Add(new ContactConsent()
    {
        Id = item.Id,
        Value = false,
        //TODO: we set as user has not consented to anything. The default consents would be in merchant terms of use agreement.
        Date = DateTime.Now,
        Source = "Litium",
        Comment = string.Empty
    });
}
```

Installation instructions for the Litium Voyado Connector 7.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Prerequisites

Litium 7.x, where x is the latest service release.

## Set up a Litium.AddOns.VoyadoConnector project

# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/litium-voyado-connector/voyado-connector-v7/voyado-promotion/overview

Voyado promotion is connected to Litium's campaigns through a chosen campaign condition.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Voyado promotion is connected to Litium's campaigns through a chosen campaign condition.

### The Promotion module

The Promotion module is connected to Multi-channel promotions in Voyado.

The module is dynamic and shows each customer's available offers. The multi-channel promotions must meet the following criteria to be displayed:

* The promotion needs to be active.
* The promotion needs to be assigned to the customer.
* The promotion needs to be valid (validity period has started but not yet ended).
* The promotion needs to have content (a presentation), at least a title.

Promotions that have already expired, have a validity date in the future, or lack a title in the presentation will not display in the module.

You can read [more about Personal offers in emails at Voyado here](https://explore.voyado.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360013296840-Personal-offers-in-emails).

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/loop54/loop54-old-api/configure

How to configure Litium Loop54 connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

There are two projects in the add-on: `Litium.AddOns.Loop54` and `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search`.

### Litium.AddOns.Loop54

This is a standalone library to create feeds, send event updates to Loop54 and search using the Loop54 API. It has the following parts:

**1. Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search.Filtering.Loop54IndexingProviderPreProcessor**

Saves all the product information on the disc under the `Search\_loop54` folder. Each product is saved as a separate file containing the product information in JSON format. When a product is updated in Litium, its file is updated with the new information.

**2. Litium.AddOns.Loop54.FeedHandler**

Handles the data feed that Loop54 fetches from Litium. Loop54 calls the feed handler for each website separately. The request header has to contain the attribute `X-Loop54-Api-Key` with the value that you have determined in the app settings of your `web.config` with the key `Loop54ApiKey`.

Example: `http://yourdomain/loop54.axd?channelSystemId=059becee-21fc-43b3-8cfc-923edfeb7d7a&minutes=60`

The request parameter `channelSystemId` is used to determine the channel. The parameter `minutes` is used to determine how far back in time the feed should include product changes. If the request does not contain a `minutes` parameter, the feed will contain all the products published on the channel.

You can test your feed with a post call, using your API key and channelSystemId via Postman.

**3. Litium.AddOns.Loop54.PushProcessor**

Handles the information that will be sent to Loop54 following different events:

* Place order
* Add product to shopping cart
* Remove product from shopping cart (Not handled as standard. The method exists in the source code but doesn't do anything unless you add a behavior.)
* Show a product

### Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search

This project is dependent on Litium Accelerator 7.0.2. It is an override of `ProductSearchService` in order to use Loop54 instead of the standard search that is included.

In order to use `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search`, you have to make some changes in Litium Accelerator. In coming versions, these changes will already have been added, so the following part is only applicable for version 7.0.2.

**Version 7.0.2:**

We need an abstract class in Litium Accelerator to decorate it from the Loop54 add-on. Since `ProductSearchService` injects other classes in Accelerator, we have to use the existing name (`ProductSearchService`) for the abstract class, and `ProductSearchServiceImpl` for the old one.

```csharp theme={null}
[Service(ServiceType = typeof(ProductSearchService), Lifetime = DependencyLifetime.Singleton)]
public abstract class ProductSearchService
{
    public abstract SearchResponse Search(
        SearchQuery searchQuery,
        IDictionary<string, ISet<string>> tags = null,
        bool addPriceFilterTags = false,
        bool addNewsFilterTags = false,
        bool addCategoryFilterTags = false,
        int? searchSize = null);
}
```

The current `ProductSearchService` will be renamed `ProductSearchServiceImpl`, and remove `SortableSearchHit` from `ProductSearchServiceImpl`.


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/loop54/loop54-old-api/install

How to install Litium Loop54 connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Please note that this add-on is compatible with Litium Accelerator 7.x.

To compile the add-on, unzip the add-on zip file and open the `src` folder. Then you add the projects to your Litium solution.

Copy `Loop54.dll` to the bin folder of your website that is located in the `SharedLibs` folder coming with the zip file. When necessary, correct the references of the add-on projects so that they refer to the correct packages.

Update your `web.config` file as follows:

1. Under app settings add the following:

```xml theme={null}
<add key="Loop54ApiKey" value="A key you decide and communicate to Loop54"/>
<add key="Loop54ScriptTimeout" value="1800"/>
```

2. Add references to the add-on projects from the website in your solution.
3. Compile your solution.
4. Log in to back office and add Loop54 settings in the channel page.
5. Set Use V25 url to Yes if your Loop54 search engine is version 2.5 or older. Contact Loop54 to check which version you have. If Use Loop54 is set to Yes, the system will use Loop54. Otherwise, it will use Litium's built-in search engine.

<img alt="Loop54 channel settings" />

6. Rebuild the product catalog indices in back office. Then Loop54 can get data from your feed and construct its own indices.

Loop54 does not support dynamic filtering (faceting). You have to let Loop54 know which fields you are going to use as filter (faceting) fields in your solution.

Loop54 does not support different price intervals, only max and min prices, and it is not working as real faceting. If there are no products in the given interval, all other faceting returns null. Price filters are implemented as price intervals in Litium Accelerator. If you want to use price faceting with Loop54, you have to change this to a slider or similar.

Loop54 does not support different time intervals, only one interval is used, and it is not working as a real faceting. If there are no products in the given interval, all other faceting returns null.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/loop54/loop54-old-api/overview

Documentation for the Loop54 Old API connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

This is documentation for Loop54 addon for a depricated version of Loop 54 API.

Litium Loop54 Connector is a source-code add-on that you can easily adjust or develop further. It contains both the add-on project and an implementation project. The latter implements the product-related parts of `ProductSearchService` in Litium Accelerator 7.x, using the Loop54 add-on.


# General
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/loop54/loop54-old-api/previous-versions/loop54-for-litium-4-8/general

General information about Litium Loop54 Connector for Litium 4.8.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Shoppers expect the same level of relevance and personalisation online as they experience in-store. Loop54 deliver on those expectations by turning search into a helpful sales associate.

## Features

* **Related results**: Loop54 learns the relationships between products in your product catalog and presents related search results.
* **Search insights & analytics**: Full visibility into how shoppers are engaging with search; what they search for and what they convert on.
* **Language agnostic**: Loop54 doesn't need language models, dictionaries, or thesauruses. It learns from human behavior instead.
* **Automatically learns new words & synonyms**: Loop54 continuously monitors your visitor's language and learns new words and synonyms automatically.
* **Any device or UI**: Loop54's open API can be implemented with any UI or device.
* **Faceted navigation & autocomplete**: Built-in support for facets and autocomplete.

## Litium Loop54 Connector functionality

The connector updates product information and connects to Loop54. Product information is sent to Loop54. Information about product visits, products added to basket and products purchased is sent to Loop54.

There are two projects in the add-on.

### Litium.Studio.AddOns.Loop54

This is a standalone library to create feeds, send event updates to Loop54 and search using the Loop54 API. It has the following parts:

**1. Loop54IndexingProviderPreProcessor**

Saves all the product information on the disc under the `Search\_loop54` folder. Each product is saved as a separate file containing the product information in JSON format. When a product is updated in Litium, its file is updated with the new information.

**2. FeedHandler**

Handles the data feed that Loop54 fetches from Litium. Loop54 calls the feed handler for each website separately. The request header has to contain the attribute `X-Loop54-Api-Key` with the value that you have determined in `web.config`.

Example: `http://yourdomain/loop54.axd?webId=1&minutes=60`

The request parameter `webId` is used to determine the website. The parameter `minutes` is used to determine how far back in time the feed should include product changes. If the request does not contain a `minutes` parameter, the feed will contain all the products published on the website.

**3. PushProcessor**

Handles the information that will be sent to Loop54 following different events:

* Place order (Litium: `OrderEvent`, Loop54: `PurchaseEvent`)
* Add product to shopping cart (Litium: `ItemAddedToCartEvent`, Loop54: `AddToCartEvent`)
* Remove product from shopping cart (Litium: `ItemRemovedFromCartEvent`, Loop54: Not Supported)
* Show a product (Litium: `PageEvent`, Loop54: `ClickEvent`)

### Litium.Studio.AddOns.Loop54.ContentProviders

This project is dependent on `Litium.Studio.Accelerator 4.1`. It is an override of the `ContentProvider` of the Litium.Studio.Accelerator in order to use Loop54 instead of the standard search delivered with Litium Studio.


# Install and Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/loop54/loop54-old-api/previous-versions/loop54-for-litium-4-8/install-and-configure

How to install and configure Litium Loop54 Connector for Litium 4.8.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

1. Download the add-on package.

2. Copy the contents of the `Src\Templates` folder to the `wwwroot\Site\Cms\Templates` folder.

3. Add the two projects to your solution, correct the references, and refer to the projects from your website project.

4. Update your `web.config` file by adding the following under app settings:

   ```xml theme={null}
   <add key="Loop54ApiKey" value="A key you decide and communicate to Loop54"/>
   <add key="Loop54ScriptTimeout" value="1800"/>
   ```

5. Compile your solution.

6. Log in to back office and create a page of the type `Loop54Settings`. Edit and publish the page.

   <img alt="Loop54 settings" />

7. Rebuild the product catalog indices in back office. Then Loop54 can get data from your feed and construct its own indices.

Set **Use V25 url** to Yes if your Loop54 search engine is version 2.5 or older. Contact Loop54 to check which version you have.

Loop54 does not support dynamic filtering (faceting). You have to let Loop54 know which fields you are going to use as filter (faceting) fields in your solution.

Loop54 does not support different price intervals, only max and min prices, and it is not working as real faceting. If there are no products in the given interval, all other faceting returns null.

Loop54 does not support different time intervals, only one interval is used, and it is not working as a real faceting. If there are no products in the given interval, all other faceting returns null.

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/loop54/loop54-v3-api_1/configure

How to configure Litium Loop54 connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

### Litium Back Office configuration

<img alt="Loop54 Back Office settings" />

### Settings description

* **Use Loop54**: Switcher to turn Loop54 search On or Off.
* **Use AutoComplete search**: Option to show quick search as regular search or Loop54 AutoComplete search.
* **Cache the call to Loop54 in seconds**: Amount of seconds to store Loop54 response in cache.
* **Maximum number AutoComplete hits**: How many options to show on an AutoComplete search.
* **Maximum number Similar-Products hits**: How many similar products option to show.
* **Maximum number of Similar-Query-Text hits**: How many similar query text options to show.
* **Brand field-id for products**: The Id of your solutions products Brand field Id.
* **News field-id for products**: The Id of your solutions products News field Id.
* **Text for (Categories)**: Translation or the text for "Categories" in AutoComplete Search result.
* **Text for (Products)**: Translation or the text for "Products" in AutoComplete Search result.
* **Text for (In)**: Translation or the text for "In" in AutoComplete Search result.

## There are two projects in the add-on

### Litium.AddOns.Loop54

This is a standalone library to create feeds, send event updates to Loop54 and search using the Loop54 API. It has the following parts:

**1. Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search.Filtering.Loop54IndexingProviderPreProcessor**

Saves all the product information on the disc under the `Search\_loop54` folder. Each product or product group is saved as a separate file containing the product information in JSON format. When a product is updated in Litium, its file is updated with the new information.

**2. Litium.AddOns.Loop54.FeedHandler**

Handles the data feed that Loop54 fetches from Litium. Loop54 calls the feed handler for each Channel separately. The request header must contain the attribute `X-Loop54-Api-Key` with the value that you have determined in `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.dll.config` file.

Example: `http://yourdomain/loop54.axd?channelSystemId=059becee-21fc-43b3-8cfc-923edfeb7d7a&minutes=60`

The request parameter `channelSystemId` is used to determine the channel. The parameter `minutes` is used to determine how far back in time the feed should include product changes published on the website. If the request does not contain a `minutes` parameter, the feed will contain all the products published on the channel.

You can test your feed with a post-call, using your API\_key and channelSystemId via Postman.

**3. Litium.AddOns.Loop54.PushProcessor**

Handles the information that will be sent to Loop54 following different events:

* Place order (Litium: `OrderEvent`, Loop54: `PurchaseEvent`)
* Add product to shopping cart (Litium: `ItemAddedToCartEvent`, Loop54: `AddToCartEvent`)
* Remove the product from the shopping cart (Litium: `ItemRemovedFromCartEvent`, Loop54: Not Supported)
* Show a product (Litium: `PageEvent`, Loop54: `ClickEvent`)

### Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search

This project is dependent on Litium Accelerator 7.x. It is an override of `ProductSearchService` in order to use Loop54 instead of the standard search that is included.

In order to use `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search`, you have to make some changes in Litium Accelerator. The changed files are placed in the downloaded zip file `Src/Litium/Litium-Accelerator-Files` folder.

On category pages (`GetEntitiesByAttributeRequest` search) the `CategoryPageViewModelBuilder` should set the property `searchQuery.CategoryShowRecursively` to `true` in order to fetch a correct number of products from Loop54 and since we cache the first call and reuse the response for upcoming requests in the same scope then it needs to fetch all information.

Caching the response in seconds you can set in backoffice Channel settings. The cache keys are unique for every session.

All Loop54 features are not implemented in the Litium Accelerator but the `OriginalResponse` is added to the `Litium.Framework.Search.SearchResponse` since `OriginalResponse` inherits from it, so for example in order to make related products visible it is needed to get the `RecommendedHits` from the `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search.Response` which needs to be cast to `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.Search.Response` objects and implements the logic to make the recommended products visible.

That applies for `RelatedQueries`, `SpellingSuggestions`, `CustomData` and similar.
