# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/loop54/loop54-v3-api_1/install

How to install Litium Loop54 connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Please note that this add-on is compatible with Litium Accelerator 7 from Litium Accelerator version 7.4.

### Get started

1. Unzip the AddOn zip file and copy `Litium.AddOns.Loop54` project in the `src` folder to your solution.
2. Copy file `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.dll.config` from `Litium-Accelerator-Files` folder to your website (MVC) root folder.
3. Add reference `Loop54.dll` from `SharedLibs` folder into your `Litium.Accelerator` and `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` projects.
4. (If necessary) Correct the references of the add-on projects so that they refer to the correct packages.
5. Add reference `Litium.AddOns.Loop54` into your `Litium.Accelerator` and `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` projects.
6. Add and replace or alter your files in Litium projects with new codes/files from `Litium-Accelerator-Files` folder under `Src` folder in zip file (description on changes below).
7. Fix any compile errors and compile your solution, also rebuild frontend code.
8. Add your Loop54 account credentials to the copied config file and start your website. (Loop54 custom fields should be created now on all Litium channels.)
9. Rebuild the product catalog indices in back office. Then Loop54 can get data from your feed and construct its own indices.

Loop54 uses client chosen filters such as size, color, price as facets, and non-client choosable product tags as filters.

Loop54 does not support different price intervals since it is not returning a number of items in different price ranges, only max and min prices (RangeFacet), and it is not working as a real faceting. If there are no products in the given interval then returned products will be null or zero. Price filters are implemented as price intervals in Litium Accelerator. If you want to use price filtering with Loop54, you have to change price filter options to a slider or similar instead of single or multi chosen checkboxes.

The same logic applies for News faceting since it also is a RangeFacet. There is hard-coded logic on 1 and 3 months on the News field and you choose your News field in backoffice in the Loop54 channel settings. Apply a slider for presenting News in a satisfactory option on the page.

On the sorting option, "Recommended" is not used by Loop54.

### Litium-Accelerator-Files description

In `Litium.Accelerator` project:

* `CampaignIndexingProviderPreProcessor.cs` — Almost whole file is altered so most of the code are replaced for supporting indexing new format on campaign tags.
* `CategoryPageViewModelBuilder.cs` — Private method `BuildProducts` is altered to set `CategoryShowRecursively` to true.
* `PriceFilterService.cs` — Adding new campaign readtags with and without vat.
* `SearchQuery.cs` — Property `IsAutoCompleteType` added to `SearchQuery` class.
* `QuickSearchResultViewModelBuilder.cs` — Logic to support boolean property `IsAutoCompleteType` in `SearchRequest` object implemented.
* `SearchQueryBuilder.cs` — Altering pagesize for Loop54 and built-in Lucene. (In Loop54 set as number of products presented by page.)
* `VariantIndexDocumentMerger.cs` — Class is made public instead of internal.

New files to insert:

* `Loop54FilterAggregatorDecorator.cs`
* `Loop54ProductSearchServiceDecorator.cs`
* `Loop54SearchService.cs`
* `SortableSearchHit.cs`

In `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` project:

* `QuickSearch.container.js` — Altering the code to wait on at least 3 characters in QuickSearch before calling the server.
* `Litium.AddOns.Loop54.dll.config` — The account credentials to Loop54 must be filled in this file.

# Import Configuration
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/microsoft-dynamics-365-fo-connector/import-configuration

Import configurations for the Microsoft Dynamics 365 FO Connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Import configurations for the Microsoft Dynamics connector. Configuration is defined in `connectorImportConfiguration.json`.

## Catalog (Products)

Catalog/Product configuration aggregating both base product and variants mapping configuration.

```json theme={null}
"Catalog": {
       "catalogStructure": {
           "subCatalog": "",
           "filePrefix": "Litium Export-Released products",
           "exportId": ""
       },
 
       "mapping": {
           "product": {
               "root": "ECORESRELEASEDPRODUCTV2ENTITY",
               "productArticleNumberSuffix": "-P",
               "fieldTemplateId": "ProductWithVariants",
               "taxClassId": "TaxClassId",
               "articleNumberNodeName": "ITEMNUMBER",
               "fields": [
                   {
                       "fieldDefinitionId": "_name",
                       "fieldDataNodeName": "SEARCHNAME",
                       "culture": "en-US",
                       "type": "string"
                   }
               ]
           },
           "variant": {
               "root": "ECORESRELEASEDPRODUCTV2ENTITY",
               "unitOfMeasurement": "UOM",
               "articleNumberNodeName": "ITEMNUMBER",
               "fields": [
                   {
                       "fieldDefinitionId": "_name",
                       "fieldDataNodeName": "SEARCHNAME",
                       "culture": "en-US",
                       "type": "string"
                   }
               ]
           }
       },
       "importBatchSize": 500,
       "defaultVariantFieldTemplate": "ProductWithVariants_default",
       "defaultBaseProductFieldTemplate": "ProductWithVariants_base_default",
       "defaultTaxClassId": "TaxClassId_default",
       "defaultUnitOfMeasurement": "UOM_default",
       "autoGenerateBaseProduct": false,
       "generateUrl": false,
       "urlFieldList": [],
       "importBehavior": "proceedWithErrors"
   },
```

* `defaultBaseProductFieldTemplate`: string — default Litium product template.
* `defaultVariantFieldTemplate`: string — default Litium variant field template.
* `defaultTaxClassId`: string — default tax class id.
* `defaultUnitOfMeasurement`: string — default unit of measurement.
* `importBatchSize`: integer — number of products imported in one batch.
* `autoGenerateBaseProduct`: bool — catalog import setting. See Litium ERP reference.
* `generateUrl`: bool — catalog import setting. See Litium ERP reference.
* `urlFieldList`: string\[] — fields used for generating URLs.
* `importBehavior`: string — `stopOnAnyError` or `proceedWithErrors`.

### catalogStructure

Containing information of product import structure.

* `subCatalog`: string — product import sub catalog. If set, the file prefix check will not be checked and all files will be treated as product files.
* `filePrefix`: string — file prefix for recognizing catalog import files. Only used when sub catalog is not set.
* `exportId`: guid — D365 export Id containing catalog files (Export-Released products).

### mapping

Mapping configuration for both Litium variants and base products.

#### product

* `root`: string — root node of base product entity in catalog export file.
* `productArticleNumberSuffix`: string — suffix to differentiate base product from variant ID in case of 1 to 1 relation.
* `fieldTemplateId`: string — Litium product template id.
* `taxClassId`: string — Litium tax class id.
* `articleNumberNodeName`: string — article number node name.
* `articleNameNodeName`: string — article name node.
* `fields`: array — fields mapping containing Litium FieldId, corresponding node in entity, culture, and type. See Litium ERP 1.1 for reference.

#### variant

* `root`: string — root node of variant entity in catalog export file.
* `unitOfMeasurement`: string — node name for variant unit of measurement.
* `articleNumberNodeName`: string — article number node name.
* `articleNameNodeName`: string — article name node.
* `fields`: array — fields mapping containing Litium FieldId, corresponding node in entity, culture, and type. See Litium ERP 1.1 for reference.

***

* `defaultPersonFiledTemplate`: string — default person field template.

### catalogStructure

Containing information of customer import structure.

* `subCatalog`: string — customer import sub catalog. If set, the file prefix check will not be checked and all files will be treated as customer files.
* `filePrefix`: string — file prefix for recognizing catalog import files. Only used when sub catalog is not set.
* `exportId`: guid — D365 export Id containing customer files (Customer V3).

### mapping

Mapping configuration for both Litium Persons and Organizations.

* `customerTypeNodeName`: string — root node for customer mapping.
* `discountPriceGroupIdNodeName`: string — mapping for customer price list (for organizations) and price group id (for persons).

#### Organization

* `vatRegistrationNumberNodeName`: string — VAT node name.
* `legalRegistrationNumberMappingNode`: string — legal registration node number.
* `customerTypes`: string\[] — customer types mapped to organizations: `"Organization"`, `"LegalEntity"`.
* `idNodeName`: string — organization id node.
* `nameNodeName`: string — organization name node id.
* `fieldTemplateId`: string — organization template id in Litium.
* `defaultAddressType`: string — default address import type in Litium.
* `fields`: array — fields mapping containing Litium FieldId, corresponding node in entity, culture, and type. See Litium ERP 1.1 for reference.

#### person

* `customerTypes`: string\[] — customer types mapped to persons: `"Person"`.
* `idNodeName`: string — person id node.
* `fieldTemplateId`: string — person template id in Litium.
* `fields`: array — fields mapping containing Litium FieldId, corresponding node in entity, culture, and type. See Litium ERP 1.1 for reference.

##### addressFields

Array of address mappings.

* `addressTypeId`: string — Litium address type for mapping, e.g. `"Delivery"`.
* `addressFields`: array — array of fields corresponding to the Litium address model.

```json theme={null}
"addressFields": [
  {

    "type": "string"
  }
]
```

## Price import

* `importBatchSize`: integer — number of price items imported in one batch.
* `importBehavior`: string — `stopOnAnyError` or `proceedWithErrors`.

```json theme={null}
"Price": {
    "catalogStructure": {
        "subCatalog": "",
        "filePrefix": "Sales price agreements",
        "exportId": ""
    },
    "importBatchSize": 500,
    "importBehavior": "proceedWithErrors",
    "mapping": {
        "rootNode": "SALESPRICEAGREEMENTENTITY",
        "vatIncluded": false,
        "basePriceListId": "usdPriceList",
        "defaultCurrency": "USD",
        "currencyNodeName": "PRICECURRENCYCODE",
        "customerIdNodeName": "CUSTOMERACCOUNTNUMBER",
        "minQuantityNodeName": "SALESPRICEQUANTITY",
        "articleNumberNodeName": "ITEMNUMBER",
        "priceNodeName": "PRICE",
        "priceCustomerGroupCode": "PRICECUSTOMERGROUPCODE"
    }
},
```

### mapping

* `rootNode`: string — root node of the price entity in the export file.
* `vatIncluded`: bool — indicates whether the import file contains prices with VAT or not.
* `basePriceListId`: string — default Litium accelerator price list if not present in the export file.
* `defaultCurrency`: string — default Litium accelerator currency if not present in the export file.
* `currencyNodeName`: string — node name for extracting currency.
* `customerIdNodeName`: string — node name for extracting customer id for customer-specific price lists.
* `minQuantityNodeName`: string — node name for extracting minimum quantity.
* `articleNumberNodeName`: string — node name for extracting item id.
* `priceNodeName`: string — node name for extracting price.
* `priceCustomerGroupCode`: string — node name for extracting price list name.

### catalogStructure

Containing information of price import structure.

* `subCatalog`: string — price import sub catalog. If set, the file prefix check will not be checked and all files will be treated as product files.
* `filePrefix`: string — file prefix for recognizing catalog import files. Only used when sub catalog is not set.
* `exportId`: guid — D365 export Id containing price files.

# Features
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/product-media-mapper/features

Product media mapper connects the Media area and the Product area.

<Badge>4.6.1</Badge> <Badge>4.6.2</Badge> <Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge> <Badge>Litium 8</Badge>

* Automatically connects images and files uploaded in the Media area to products and their variants in the Products area.
* Pattern recognition functionality passes the file names through a set of rules defined in the settings file of the Litium application to determine what products/variants the files should be connected to. Up to 5 sets of rules are included in the add-on, and more can be configured.
* Files connected to a product/variant can be directed to a specific, language-handled property or a group of properties.
* All uploaded files connected to a product/variant will be organised in a catalog structure that makes it easy to manage large amounts of files.
* When updating a file in the Media area the products it is connected to are automatically updated.

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/product-media-mapper/product-media-mapper-v7-and-before/configure

Configuration settings, options in the config file and a configuration example.

<Badge>4.6.1</Badge> <Badge>4.6.2</Badge> <Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

All settings are configured in the `Litium.AddOns.ProductMediaMapper.dll.config` file located in the wwwroot folder. Note that the files you want to map need to contain the article numbers in the file names. The article numbers can be found in the Products area in the backoffice.

The following options are available in the config file:

* **mediaarchiverootfolder**: Defines the root folder of where folders will be created, to which the files that are mapped will be moved. The default folder is `ArticleFiles`.
* **articlenumbercharacterlengthmatch**: Defines how many characters the name of the subfolder that holds the mapped files will contain. This makes it possible to group the files according to article number in different ways. The default is 1 character.
* **AllowedFileTypes**: Defines the file types that are valid for automatic mapping.
* **FieldFileMappings**: Defines what custom product image fields the files should be mapped to. One file per field is supported.
* **DisplayImagesMappings**: Defines what default product display image fields the files should be mapped to. Mapping of multiple files is supported.

Note: The `prefix` and `suffix` attributes can be used to define the sort order for files and language dependency if several files are mapped to the same product image field. The `templatefieldname` attribute is the ID of the field, not the field name.

Example of a configuration:

```xml theme={null}
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<Configuration xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="Site/ProductMediaMapper/ProductMediaMapping.xsd"
  mediaarchiverootfolder="ArticleFiles" articlenumbercharacterlengthmatch="1">
  <AllowedFileTypes>
    <AllowedFileType filetype="gif" />
    <AllowedFileType filetype="jpg" />
    <AllowedFileType filetype="png" />
  </AllowedFileTypes>
  <FieldFileMappings>
    <FieldFileMapping prefix="" suffix="" templatefieldname="File01"/>
    <!-- Example match 654765.jpg matches article with number 654765-->
    <FieldFileMapping prefix="" suffix="_1" templatefieldname="File02"/>
    <!-- Example match 654765_1.jpg matches article with number 654765-->
    <FieldFileMapping prefix="" suffix="_2" templatefieldname="File03"/>
    <!-- Example match 654765_2.jpg matches article with number 654765-->
  </FieldFileMappings>
  <DisplayImagesMappings>
    <DisplayImagesMapping prefix="" suffix="" templatefieldname="Image01"/>
    <!-- Example match 654765.jpg matches article with number 654765-->
    <DisplayImagesMapping prefix="" suffix="_1" templatefieldname="Image02"/>
    <!-- Example match 654765_1.jpg matches article with number 654765-->
    <DisplayImagesMapping prefix="" suffix="_2" templatefieldname="Image03"/>
    <!-- Example match 654765_2.jpg matches article with number 654765-->
  </DisplayImagesMappings>
</Configuration>
```

By adding a `language` attribute you can use the `FieldFileMapping` setting to map language-dependent files.

```xml theme={null}
<FieldFileMapping prefix="" suffix="_SV" language="sv_SE" templatefieldname="File1"/>
<!-- Example match A0001_SV.jpg matches article with number A0001-->
<FieldFileMapping prefix="" suffix="_1_SV" language="sv_SE" templatefieldname="File2"/>
<!-- Example match A0001_1_SV.jpg matches article with number A0001-->
<FieldFileMapping prefix="" suffix="_GB" language="en-GB" templatefieldname="File1"/>
<!-- Example match A0001_GB.jpg matches article with number A0001-->
<FieldFileMapping prefix="" suffix="_1_GB" language="en-GB" templatefieldname="File2"/>
<!-- Example match A0001_1_GB.jpg matches article with number A0001-->
```

# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/rate-and-review/develop

Further customisation of the Rate and Review add-on.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

Further customisation of the Rate and Review add-on.

## Architecture

### Data access layer

The `Repository` class contains all the methods to persist and manipulate data in the database. It does not contain business logic.

### Business logic layer

Business logic is implemented with the `RateAndReviewService` class and implementations of `IUserContext`.

* **`UserContext`** — used to handle anonymous users and logged-in users. It uses `CurrentState` in order to return user, website and language. It also handles caching of the reviewed item ids in the session. It ensures that the id of reviewed items are cached in the session so that the user cannot rate and review the same item more than once during that session.
* **`AdminUserContext`** — used to handle all rate and reviews. It is possible to pass language and token information to the `AdminUserContext`. There is no caching in the session for the `AdminUserContext`, since the admin user cannot create rate and reviews.

### Data carriers

Rate and Review classes are data carriers. They have no logic implemented and are used to carry data between data, business logic and representation layer.

***

## Code examples

All code examples are based on Litium Accelerator implementation.

### Adding Rate and Review

```csharp theme={null}
var rateAndReviewService = new RateAndReviewService(new UserContext());
if (CurrentState.Current.Token.IsAnonymousUser)
{
   rateAndReviewService.AddAnonymousely(variant.SystemId, model.Review, model.Rate, true);
}
else
{
   rateAndReviewService.Add(variant.SystemId, model.Review, model.Rate, $"{CurrentState.Current.Token.Person.FirstName} {CurrentState.Current.Token.Person.LastName}", CurrentState.Current.Token.Person.Email, true);
}
```

Assuming that your input model contains Rate and Review and the variant is not null.

### Showing reviews on the product page

#### 1. Create a view model for rate and review

```csharp theme={null}
namespace Litium.Accelerator.Mvc.ViewModels.Product
{
    public class RateAndReviewViewModel
    {

        public string Rate { get; set; }
        public string Reviewer { get; set; }
        public string ArticleNumber { get; set; }
        public long Id { get; set; }
        public DateTime Date { get; set; }
        public bool IsArticle { get; set; }
        public bool IsApproved { get; set; }
    }
}
```

#### 2. Add a collection of rate and review model to the ProductPageViewModel

```csharp theme={null}
public List<RateAndReviewViewModel> RateAndReviews { get; set; }
```

#### 3. Change Build method of the ProductPageViewModelBuilder

This code changes the `Build` method of the `ProductPageViewModelBuilder`, so that it adds the rate and review collection to the `ProductPageViewModel`:

```csharp theme={null}
var rateAndReviewViewService = new RateAndReviewService(new UserContext());
var rateAndReviews = rateAndReviewViewService.Get(baseProduct.SystemId, true, false, OrderBy.CreatedDate, false, 1, 10);
if (variant != null)

    rateAndReviews.AddRange(rateAndReviewViewService.Get(variant.SystemId, true, false, OrderBy.CreatedDate, false, 1, 10));
}
productPageModel.RateAndReviews = rateAndReviews.Select(x => new RateAndReviewViewModel() { Date = x.CreatedDate, Rate = x.Rate.HasValue ? x.Rate.ToString() : string.Empty, ArticleNumber = x.ArticleNumber, Review = x.Comment, Reviewer = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(x.Email) ? "anonymous" : x.Email }).ToList();
// Use website string instead of "anonymous"
```

#### 5. Attach the event to your SaveInfoButton in JavaScript

```javascript theme={null}
events: function (scope) {
        this.log('events');
        var self = this;

       $(scope)
              .off('.' + this.name)
             .on('click' + '.accelerator.' + this.name, '#SaveInfoButton', function(e) {
                    e.preventDefault();
                    var sender = $(this);
                    var form = $('#RateAndReviewPanelForm');

                    $('.loader').show();
                    $.ajax({
                        url: form.attr('action'),
                        data: form.serializeArray(),
                        type: 'POST',
                        success: function(data) {
                            sender.trigger('show-notification');
                        },
                        error: function(data) {
                            for (var property in data.responseJSON.ModelState) {
                                if (data.responseJSON.ModelState.hasOwnProperty(property)) {
                                    var msg = data.responseJSON.ModelState[property][0];
                                    var element = $('input[name="' + property + '"]');
                                    self.addError(element, msg);
                                }
                            }
                        },
                        complete: function() {
                            $('.loader').hide();
                        }
                    });
                });
}
```

#### 6. Update the rate and reviews by the changes of the administrator

```csharp theme={null}
[HttpPost]
public JsonResult UpdateInfo(YourAdministrationPageType currentPageTypeDefinition, Page page, FormCollection formCollection)
{
   if (ModelState.IsValid && SaveRateAndReviews(formCollection))
   {
      return Json(true);
   }
 
   Response.StatusCode = 400;
   return Json(new
   {
      Message = "The request is invalid.", // Use website string
      ModelState = ModelState.GetErrors()
   });
}
private bool SaveRateAndReviews(FormCollection formCollection)
{
  try
  {
    var languageService = IoC.Resolve<LanguageService>();
    var rateAndReviewService = new RateAndReviewService(new AdminUserContext(languageService.Get(CurrentState.Current.Culture), CurrentState.Current.Token));
    var rateAndReviews = rateAndReviewService.Get(false, false, OrderBy.CreatedDate, false, 1, 10);
    for (var i = 0; i < rateAndReviews.Count; i++)
    {
      var rate = formCollection[$"rate_{i}"];
      var idInput = formCollection[$"id_{i}"];
      var id = long.Parse(idInput);
      var reviewText = formCollection[$"review_{i}"];
      var action = formCollection[$"action_{i}"];
      var review = rateAndReviewService.Get(id);
      if (review != null)
      {
        switch (action)
        {
          case "u":
            review.Comment = reviewText;
            review.Rate = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(rate) ? null : short.Parse(rate);
            rateAndReviewService.Update(review);
            break;
          case "di":
            rateAndReviewService.Disapprove(id);
            break;
          case "de":
            rateAndReviewService.Delete(id);
            break;
          case "a":
            rateAndReviewService.Approve(id);
            break;
        }
      }
    }
    return true;
  }
  catch (Exception exc)
  {
    // Log the error
  }
  return false;
}
```

***

## Implementation example

### Show the rate and review count and sort the search result

This is an implementation example of how to show the rate and review count, and how to sort the search result by the rate of a product in Litium Accelerator. The same approach can be used to sort the search result by the review count.

#### 1. Add Rate constant to SearchQueryParser

Add the following using statement:


#### 6. Change CreateProductModels in your ProductSearch to handle a new CustomProductModel class

Add the following code as shown in the screenshot below:

```csharp theme={null}
private List<CustomProductModel> CreateProductModels(Collection<Hit> hits)
{
    var productModels = new List<CustomProductModel>();
    if (hits.Count == 0)
    {
        return productModels;
    }
 
    foreach (var hit in hits)
    {
        var systemId = new Guid(hit.Id);
        var baseProduct = _baseProductService.Get(systemId);
 
        ProductModel model;
        if (baseProduct != null)
        {
            model = CreateProductModel(baseProduct);
        }
        else
        {
            if (hit.Tags.Any(x => x.Name == VariantIndexDocumentMerger.MergeTagName))
            {
                model = CreateProductModel(hit.Tags.Where(x => x.Name == TagNames.ArticleNumber).Select(x => _variantService.Get(x.Value)));
            }
            else
            {
                var variant = _variantService.Get(systemId);
                model = _productModelBuilder.BuildFromVariant(variant);
            }
        }
 
        if (model != null)
        {
            productModels.Add(new CustomProductModel() { ProductModel = model, Rate = hit.Tags.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Name.Equals(RateAndReviewService.RateTag, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))?.Value, ReviewCount = hit.Tags.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Name.Equals(RateAndReviewService.ReviewCountTag, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))?.Value });
        }
    }
 
    return productModels;
}
```

# Features
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/rate-and-review/features

Rate and Review provides a standalone solution that contains both the add-on project and a test project.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

The purpose of Rate and Review is to allow customers to rate and review the products.

It is compiled with Litium version 6.x. You can use the add-on project in your Litium solution by changing the references to the NuGet packages of your solution.

This add-on consists of an API and database functionality to persist data. No UI is included. UI for customers and for administrators has to be implemented in your solution.

<Note>
  Rate and Review can only be used with Litium 6.x.
</Note>

## Features

* Both logged-in and anonymous customers can rate and review a base product or variant.
* Rate is a point between 1 and 5 (validation in the API but can be changed in your solution). Review is a text that the customers write. A customer can rate or review, or both, for a base product or variant.
* Rate and review are connected and cannot be added on different occasions during the same customer session. When they have been saved, they cannot be changed.
* Rate and review can be saved for a variant or for a base product. It is possible to save only rate, only review, or both.
* Rate and review are saved with the current date, current language, name and e-mail of the currently logged in customer. A logged-in customer can always save the rate and review anonymously. No customer-specific information will be saved with the rate and review in that case.
* An anonymous customer (not logged in) can save the rate and review with user information, by providing name (not mandatory) and e-mail (not mandatory).
* Reviews have to be approved by an administrator before they are published on the site (approval procedure can be changed in your solution). If rate and review contain only rate, no approval is required. If rate and review contain only review, or both rate and review, approval is required. The rate given with a review will not affect the rate of the product before the review is approved.
* Rate and review can be edited and changed by an administrator.
* When a variant or base product is deleted all the rate and reviews of them are deleted permanently from the database.
* When a customer is deleted all his/her rate and reviews will be unaffected and left in the database.
* The API has support to sort the products on their rating or their number of reviews. It is very simple to add this sorting option in all the product listing pages, like category, product list or search result page.


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/rate-and-review/install

Installation instructions for the Rate and Review add-on.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

To install, unzip the add-on and copy the `Litium.Studio.AddOns.RateAndReview` folder located in the `Src` folder to your project folder. Add a reference to the `Litium.Studio.AddOns.RateAndReview` project from your web project. Ensure `Litium.Studio.AddOns.RateAndReview` project references are using your packages. Add the following startup task in your `web.config`:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.RateAndReview.Search.RateEventListener, Litium.AddOns.RateAndReview"/>
```

Install the add-on database tables by running the script file `RateAndReview_Install.sql` located at the `DB` folder of the add-on on your project database.

## Tests

To compile the add-on, unzip it and open the solution `RateAndReview.sln` located in the `Src` folder.

In order to run the tests, change the references to the NuGet packages of your solution. Use the database located in the `tools/dB` folder of your `Litium.Setup.Core.X.X.X` package.

Then create an `app.config` file, which is a copy of `Source/Configurations/app.config.build`. Change the database connection string to point to the newly restored database:

```xml theme={null}
<add name="FoundationConnectionString" connectionString="Pooling=true;User Id=;Password=;Database=;Server=(local)" providerName="System.Data.SqlClient" />
```

Change the files folder path to the appropriate one:

```xml theme={null}
<filesDirectory value="" />
```

Copy `license.xml` of your solution to the root folder of the test project in order to be able to run the tests. Install the add-on database tables by running the script file `RateAndReview_Install.sql` located at the `DB` folder of the add-on.

# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/shopspray-punchout/develop

How to implement the required interfaces and adjust checkout for the Shopspray Punchout Connector.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge> <Badge>Litium 8</Badge>

## Implement interfaces

The Shopspray plugin needs instructions on how to do certain things within your application. These include:

* How to get a Person/User based on username in your solution
* Get an Organization that a Person/User belongs to
* Where to get certain pieces of information from your solution's OrderCarrier model
* How to login a user

To give the plugin these instructions you need to implement certain interfaces that are exposed by the plugin under the `Shopspray.PunchOut.Core.External` namespace. These include the following interfaces:

* **`IUserContextService`** — Responsible for giving the plugin information on how to identify users and their organizations, however your solution's customer model may look like.
* **`IOrderContextService`** — Responsible for mapping your relevant Order data to a generic structure that the plugin uses.
* **`IPunchoutServiceHandler`** — Responsible for common actions that the plugin performs but can't assume how they should be done in your solution, such as log in and logout.
* **`IOrderRequestService`** *(Optional)* — If you intend to use the plugin as a way to give your customers the option to place orders directly through the cXML Order Requests specification, then this provides you the ability to work with the data they pass in that request to create proper orders according to your solution's needs.

See [Sample Implementations](https://shopspray.freshdesk.com/a/solutions/articles/79000124815) for examples implemented for the default [Litium Accelerator](https://www.litium.com/product/accelerator). Feel free to use them as a baseline for your implementation and make adjustments as needed.

## Adjust Checkout

The end goal for a punchout user session is not to place an order but rather to Post Back cart line item data to their procurement system. This means that many features that you might have on your checkout page bear little relevance to your punchout users. The bare minimum you need is to ensure that they have some mechanism to return to their procurement system, but it's a good idea to remove as much from the checkout as possible for punchout users to reduce confusion.

Changes:

* Your "Place Order" button needs to be removed and replaced with a button that returns the punchout user to their procurement system. This is technically done by calling the endpoint: `/shopspray-route/punchout-service/postbackmessage`
* Remove payment selection
* Remove delivery method selection
* Remove address inputs
* Remove any other checkout elements that require user input but won't affect the final data being posted back to the user's procurement system
* If your checkout normally consists of several steps, consider bypassing steps to let punchout users "Post back" during their first checkout step, assuming that you can adjust that step to give a good overview of the cart

### Setting up the dev environment

1. Install a default Litium Accelerator MVC project, without any custom modifications.

   * From a command prompt, go to the directory of the `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc` project and execute: `yarn run build`
   * If any errors occur, execute `npm rebuild node-sass` and run `yarn run build` again.

# WebControls
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/web-controls

A source-code add-on that allows you to work with the old WebForm project in Litium 7.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

`Litium.AddOns.WebControls` is a source-code add-on that allows you to work with the old WebForm project in Litium 7. Since the old WebControls have been marked as obsolete, new ones must be used. In most cases you will need to replace the old namespaces with the new ones, according to the following table.

| Old namespace                                          | New namespace                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `Litium.Foundation.Modules.CMS.WebControls`            | `Litium.Foundation.Modules.Websites.WebControls`  |
| `Litium.Foundation.Modules.Relations.WebControls`      | `Litium.Foundation.Modules.Customers.WebControls` |
| `Litium.Foundation.Modules.ProductCatalog.WebControls` | `Litium.Foundation.Modules.Products.WebControls`  |

## How to install

1. Download the add-on package.
2. Build the `Litium.Studio.WebControls` project.
3. Copy `Litium.Studio.WebControls.dll` to the `bin` folder of your project.
4. Replace the old namespaces with the new ones.
5. Compile your solution.

The WebForm templates will now work on the public site. Web forms should also appear as a radio button in the Display template section.

<img alt="Display template" />

## Troubleshooting

If the web-form templates don't work on the public site, or if the radio button isn't visible, check that `Litium.AddOns.WebControls` and your project have the same version of Litium 7 (`Litium.Web.Application`).

# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/wishlist/develop_1

How to customize the Wish List add-on further, including code examples.

<Badge>Litium 8</Badge>

## Architecture

### Data access layer

The Repository class contains all the methods to persist and manipulate data in the database. It does not contain any business logic except selecting lists, sorting list items, and adding existing list items in the database.

### Business logic layer

Business logic is implemented with the injection of the `WishListFactoryService` class and implementation of `IUserContext`. For example, it ensures that the WishList products of a logged-in user has a user ID but no cookie ID. The WishList products of an anonymous user has a cookie ID but not a user ID.

**UserContext** handles anonymous users' and logged-in users' own WishList products. It returns user ID, channel, market, website, and shopping cart information. It also handles cookie generation, looks out for anonymous users without cookies, and ensures that lists and their items are cached in the session.

**AdminUserContext** is used by administrators to handle customers' WishList products. It is possible to pass user ID, channel, and shopping cart information to the `AdminUserContext`. It processes the data directly through the repository. There is no caching in the session for `AdminUserContext`. It does not handle cookies or shopping carts.

<Warning>Modifying a wish list while the user has an ongoing session may result in unexpected data loss for the user.</Warning>

### Data carriers

`List` and `ListItem` classes are data carriers. They have no logic implemented. They are used to carry data between the data, business logic, and representation layers.

## Code examples

All code examples are based on that Litium Accelerator has been implemented.

### 1. Creating WishListService

For the administrator:

```csharp theme={null}
var wishListService = _wishListServiceFactory.CreateAdminContext(_adminUserId, _Channel.SystemId);
```

For anonymous or logged-in customers:

```csharp theme={null}
var wishListService = _wishListServiceFactory.CreateUserContext(_channel.SystemId);
```

### 2. Adding an item to the wish list

Assuming that your input model contains `VariantSystemId` and `Quantity`, and that the variant is not null. If the wish list does not exist it will be created.

```csharp theme={null}
var variant = _variantService.Get(model.VariantSystemId);
if (variant != null)
{
    if (model.Quantity > 0)
    {
        wishListService.AddListItem("test", "test", variant, model.Quantity, true);
    }
}
```

### 3. Implementing wish list features in Litium Accelerator

The code below shows:

* How to add an item to a wish list.
* How to display and update all items in the wish list, and add them to the shopping cart.

#### 3.1 Before you start

Please read the article about [Setting up a front end development environment](/accelerators/mvc-accelerator/develop/setting-up-the-development-environment).

#### 3.2 Add Litium.AddOns.WishList reference to Litium.Accelerator.Mvc and Litium.Accelerator

#### 3.3 Add ViewModel files to Litium.Accelerator project

**3.3.1** Add `WishListItemViewModel.cs` to `Litium.Accelerator.ViewModels.Framework`:

```csharp theme={null}
using AutoMapper;
using JetBrains.Annotations;
using Litium.Runtime.AutoMapper;
using System;
using Litium.FieldFramework;
using Litium.Products;
using Litium.Web.Models;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Drawing;
using System.Linq;
using Litium.ComponentModel;
using Litium.AddOns.WishList;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.ViewModels.Framework
{
    public class WishListItemViewModel : IAutoMapperConfiguration
    {
        public WishListItemViewModel()
        {
            Id = Guid.NewGuid();
        }

        public Guid Id { get; }
        public Guid ListId { get; set; }
        public decimal Quantity { get; set; }
        public string ArticleNumber { get; set; }
        public string Image { get; set; }
        public string Name { get; set; }
        public Guid VariantId { get; set; }
        public long SortIndex { get; set; }

        [UsedImplicitly]
        public void Configure(IMapperConfigurationExpression cfg)
        {
            cfg.CreateMap<WishListItem, WishListItemViewModel>()
                .ConvertUsing<WishListItemConverter>();
        }

        [UsedImplicitly]
        private class WishListItemConverter : ITypeConverter<WishListItem, WishListItemViewModel>
        {
            private readonly VariantService _variantService;
            private readonly BaseProductService _baseProductService;

            public WishListItemConverter(VariantService variantService, BaseProductService baseProductService)
            {
                _variantService = variantService;
                _baseProductService = baseProductService;
            }

            public WishListItemViewModel Convert(WishListItem source, WishListItemViewModel destination, ResolutionContext context)
            {
                var variant = _variantService.Get(source.ArticleId);
                if (variant == null)
                {
                    return new WishListItemViewModel();
                }

                var baseProduct = _baseProductService.Get(variant?.BaseProductSystemId ?? Guid.Empty);
                var image = (variant?.Fields.GetValue<IList<Guid>>(SystemFieldDefinitionConstants.Images)?.FirstOrDefault()
                             ?? baseProduct?.Fields.GetValue<IList<Guid>>(SystemFieldDefinitionConstants.Images)?.FirstOrDefault())
                    .MapTo<ImageModel>();

                var viewModel = new WishListItemViewModel
                {
                    ListId = source.ListId,
                    ArticleNumber = variant.Id,
                    VariantId = variant.SystemId,
                    Image = image.GetUrlToImage(Size.Empty, new Size(200, 120)).Url,
                    Name = variant?.Localizations.CurrentCulture.Name.NullIfWhiteSpace() ?? baseProduct?.Localizations.CurrentCulture.Name.NullIfWhiteSpace() ?? variant.Id,
                    Quantity = source.Quantity,
                    SortIndex = source.SortIndex
                };

                return viewModel;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**3.3.2** Add `WishListViewModel.cs` to `Litium.Accelerator.ViewModels.Framework`:

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Accelerator.Builders;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.ViewModels.Framework
{
    public class WishListViewModel : IViewModel
    {
        public const string DefaultListName = "Default";
        public const string DefaultListType = "Default";

        public Guid Id { get; set; }
        public string Name { get; set; }
        public string Type { get; set; }
        public IList<WishListItemViewModel> Items { get; set; }
```

#### 3.4 Add or update files in Litium.Accelerator.Mvc project

**3.4.1** Add `WishListController.cs` to `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Controllers/Api`:

```csharp theme={null}
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Litium.Accelerator.Routing;
using Litium.Accelerator.ViewModels.Framework;
using Litium.AddOns.WishList;
using Litium.Products;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.Mvc.Controllers.Api
{
    [Route("api/wishlist")]
    public class WishListController : ApiControllerBase
    {
        private readonly VariantService _variantService;
        private readonly RequestModelAccessor _requestModelAccessor;
        private readonly WishListServiceFactory _wishListServiceFactory;

        public WishListController(VariantService variantService, WishListServiceFactory wishListServiceFactory, RequestModelAccessor requestModelAccessor)
        {
            _variantService = variantService;
            _wishListServiceFactory = wishListServiceFactory;
            _requestModelAccessor = requestModelAccessor;
        }

        [HttpPost]
        [Route("add")]
        [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
        public async Task<IActionResult> Add(AddToWishListViewModel model)
        {
            var wishListService = _wishListServiceFactory.CreateUserContext(_requestModelAccessor.RequestModel.ChannelModel.Channel);
            var variant = _variantService.Get(model.ArticleNumber);

            IList<WishListItem> wishListItems = new List<WishListItem>();

            if (variant != null && model?.Quantity >= 0)
            {
                wishListItems = wishListService.AddListItem(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType, variant, model.Quantity, true);
            }
            return Ok(wishListItems);
        }

        [HttpPost]
        [Route("update")]
        [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
        public async Task<IActionResult> Update(WishListViewModel model)
        {
            var wishListService = _wishListServiceFactory.CreateUserContext(_requestModelAccessor.RequestModel.ChannelModel.Channel);
            var wishListItems = wishListService.GetListItems(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType, true);

            foreach (var item in model.Items)
            {
                var existing = wishListItems.FirstOrDefault(w => w.ArticleId == item.VariantId);
                var quantity = existing != null ? item.Quantity - existing.Quantity : item.Quantity;
                wishListService.AddListItem(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType, _variantService.Get(item.VariantId), quantity, true);
            }
            return Ok(true);
        }

        [HttpPost]
        [Route("addtocart")]
        [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
        public async Task<IActionResult> AddToCart()
        {
            var wishListService = _wishListServiceFactory.CreateUserContext(_requestModelAccessor.RequestModel.ChannelModel.Channel);
            wishListService.AddToShoppingCart(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType);
            return Ok(true);
        }
    }
}
```

```csharp theme={null}
public static IHtmlContent WishListButton<TModel>(this IHtmlHelper<TModel> htmlHelper, Expression<Func<TModel, ProductItemViewModel>> expression, string cssClass = null)
        {
            var expressionMetadataProvider = htmlHelper.ViewContext.HttpContext.RequestServices.GetService<ModelExpressionProvider>();
            var metadata = expressionMetadataProvider.CreateModelExpression(htmlHelper.ViewData, expression);
            return htmlHelper.WishListButton((ProductItemViewModel)metadata.Model, cssClass);
        }
        public static IHtmlContent WishListButton(this IHtmlHelper<ProductItemViewModel> htmlHelper, string cssClass = null)
        {
            return htmlHelper.WishListButton(htmlHelper.ViewData.Model, cssClass);
        }

       [System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessage("Style", "IDE0060:Remove unused parameter", Justification = "<Pending>")]
       private static IHtmlContent WishListButton(this IHtmlHelper htmlHelper, ProductItemViewModel model, string cssClass)
        {
            var tag = new TagBuilder("wishlist-button");

            var quantityFieldId = model.ShowQuantityField ? $"{model.QuantityFieldId}" : string.Empty;
            tag.Attributes.Add("data-article-number", model.Id);
            tag.Attributes.Add("data-quantity-field-id", quantityFieldId);
            cssClass = $"button wishlist-button {cssClass ?? string.Empty}".Trim();

            if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(cssClass))
            {
                tag.Attributes.Add("data-css-class", cssClass);
            }

            var label = "product.wishlist".AsWebsiteText();
            tag.InnerHtml.AppendHtml($"<span><a class='{cssClass}'>{label}</a></span>");
            tag.Attributes.Add("data-label", label);
            return tag;
        }
```

**3.5.4** Add `WishList.reducer.js` to `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Client/Scripts/Reducers`:

```javascript theme={null}
import {
    WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY,
    WISHLIST_UPDATE,
    WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART,
} from '../Services/WishList.service';

export const wishList = (state = {}, action) => {
    switch (action.type) {
        case WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY:
            return {
                ...state,
                items: state.items.map((wish) =>
                    wish.articleNumber === action.articleNumber
                        ? { ...wish, quantity: action.quantity }
                        : wish
                ),
            };
        case WISHLIST_UPDATE:
        case WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART:
            return {
                ...state,
                payload: action.payload,
            };
        default:
            return state;
    }
};
```

**3.5.5** Add `WishList.service.js` to `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Client/Scripts/Services`:

```javascript theme={null}
import { post } from './http';

export const WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY = 'WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY';
export const WISHLIST_UPDATE = 'WISHLIST_UPDATE';
export const WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART = 'WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART';

export const add = async ({ articleNumber, quantity = 1 }) => {
    if (!quantity || isNaN(quantity) || parseInt(quantity) <= 0) {
        throw 'Invalid quantity';
    }

    const response = await post('/api/wishlist/add', {
        articleNumber,
        quantity: parseInt(quantity),
    });
    return response.json();
};

export const changeQuantity = (articleNumber, quantity) => {
    return {
        type: WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY,
        articleNumber,
        quantity,
    };
};

export const updateWishList = () => (dispatch, getState) => {
    return post('/api/wishlist/update', getState().wishList)
        .then((response) => response.json())
        .then((result) => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_UPDATE,
                payload: {
                    success: true,
                    message: 'Wishlist was updated successfully',
                },
            });
        })
        .catch((ex) => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_UPDATE,
                payload: {
                    success: false,
                    message: 'There was an error',
                },
            });
        });
};

export const addToCart = () => (dispatch) => {
    return post('/api/wishlist/addtocart')
        .then((response) => response.json())
        .then((result) => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART,
                payload: {
                    success: true,
                    message: 'Wishlist items were added to cart successfully',
                },
            });
        })
        .catch((ex) => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART,
                payload: {
                    success: false,
                    message: 'There was an error',
                },
            });
        });
};
```

# Features
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/wishlist/features

Wish List is a source-code add-on that allows customers on an e-commerce site to put products on a wish list.

<Badge>Litium 8</Badge>

**Wish List is a source-code add-on that allows customers on an e-commerce site to put products on a wish list.**

The add-on provides a stand-alone solution including both the add-on project and one for testing. It is compiled with Litium version 8.x and can easily be adjusted or developed further. You can use the add-on project in your Litium solution by changing the references to the NuGet packages of the solution.

The add-on consists of an API and database functionality to persist data. No UI is included, so the UI for customers and administrators must be implemented in your solution.

The functionality is as follows:

* Wish lists may be created by both logged-in and anonymous customers.
* A wish list contains a sorted list of products and their quantities.
* Wish lists can have a name and a type.
* Customers may have different wish lists for different channels. A wish list belongs to a specific channel and can only contain products published on that specific channel.
* Customers must log in to access wish lists saved on their account (logged-in user wish list). An anonymous wish list is not one of the logged-in user's wish lists.
* A wish list can be created, edited, and deleted via integration (not included).
* Both logged-in and anonymous customers can edit their respective wish lists. It is possible to change the order of the products, add and remove products, delete or clear the list.
* Both logged-in and anonymous customers can copy the content of the shopping cart to a wish list.
* Both logged-in and anonymous customers can copy the content of a wish list to the shopping cart.
* A wish list only shows published product variants. Unpublished ones remain on the list but will not be shown, not even when it is edited by the customer.
* A wish list can be created, edited, and deleted by a user with the required access rights.
* A logged-in user wish list will never be cleared automatically.
* An anonymous wish list that has not been used for a certain number of days will be deleted automatically. The number of days can be set. By default 180 days is set.
* Wish lists with outdated channels are deleted automatically.
* A new product variant will be added at the top of the list.


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/wishlist/install

Installation instructions for Wish List for Litium 8.

<Badge>Litium 8</Badge>

Read the [system requirements](https://docs.litium.com/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/get-started/system-requirements) for the development environment before installing.

To install the add-on, unzip it and copy the `Litium.AddOns.WishList` folder to your project folder. Add a reference to the `Litium.AddOns.WishList` project to your web project. Ensure that the `Litium.AddOns.WishList` project references are using your packages. Add the following scheduled task to your `appsettings.json`:

```json theme={null}
"Litium.AddOns.WishList.CleanupScheduler": { "CronExpression": "0 0 0 1/1 * ? *", "Parameter": "Days=180" }
```

Install the add-on database tables by running the script file `WishList_Install.sql` located in the `DB` folder of the add-on on your project database.

## Run unit tests

2. Change the references to the NuGet packages of your solution to the same that the website project has.

# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/wishlist/wish-list-for-litium-7/develop

How to customize the Wish List add-on further for Litium 7, including code examples.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Architecture

### Data access layer

The Repository class contains all the methods to persist and manipulate data in the database. It does not contain any business logic except selecting lists, sorting list items, and adding existing list items in the database.

### Business logic layer

Business logic is implemented with the injection of the `WishListFactoryService` class and implementation of `IUserContext`. For example, it ensures that the WishList products of a logged-in user has a user ID but no cookie ID. The WishList products of an anonymous user has a cookie ID but not a user ID.

**UserContext** handles anonymous users' and logged-in users' own WishList products. It returns user ID, channel, market, website, and shopping cart information. It also handles cookie generation, looks out for anonymous users without cookies, and ensures that lists and their items are cached in the session.

**AdminUserContext** is used by administrators to handle customers' WishList products. It is possible to pass user ID, channel, and shopping cart information to the `AdminUserContext`. It processes the data directly through the repository. There is no caching in the session for `AdminUserContext`. It does not handle cookies or shopping carts.

<Warning>Modifying a wish list while the user has an ongoing session may result in unexpected data loss for the user.</Warning>

### Data carriers

`List` and `ListItem` classes are data carriers. They have no logic implemented. They are used to carry data between the data, business logic, and representation layers.

## Code examples

All code examples are based on that Litium Accelerator has been implemented.

### 1. Creating WishListService

For the administrator:

```csharp theme={null}
var wishListService = _wishListServiceFactory.CreateAdminContext(_adminUserId, _Channel.SystemId);
```

For anonymous or logged-in customers:

```csharp theme={null}
var wishListService = _wishListServiceFactory.CreateUserContext(_channel.SystemId);
```

### 2. Adding an item to the wish list

Assuming that your input model contains `VariantSystemId` and `Quantity`, and that the variant is not null. If the wish list does not exist it will be created.

```csharp theme={null}
var variant = _variantService.Get(model.VariantSystemId);
if (variant != null)
{
    if (model.Quantity > 0)
    {
        wishListService.AddListItem("test", "test", variant, model.Quantity, true);
    }
}
```

### 3. Implementing wish list features in Litium Accelerator

The code below shows:

* How to add an item to a wish list.
* How to display and update all items in the wish list, and add them to the shopping cart.

#### 3.1 Before you start

Please read the article about [Setting up a front end development environment](https://docs.litium.com/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/litium-accelerators/develop/setting-up-the-development-environment).

#### 3.2 Prepare web APIs for the wish list

Create an API controller with 3 actions: Add, Update, and AddToCart:

```csharp theme={null}
[RoutePrefix("api/wishlist")]
public class WishListController : ApiControllerBase
```

The Add action:

```csharp theme={null}
[HttpPost]
[Route("add")]
[ApiValidateAntiForgeryToken]
public IHttpActionResult Add(AddToWishListViewModel model)
{
    var variant = _variantService.Get(model.ArticleNumber);

    IList<WishListItem> wishListItems = new List<WishListItem>();

    if (variant!=null && model?.Quantity >= 0)
    {
        wishListItems = _wishListService.AddListItem(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType, variant, model.Quantity, true);
    }

    return Ok(wishListItems);
}
```

The Update action:

```csharp theme={null}
[HttpPost]
[Route("update")]
[ApiValidateAntiForgeryToken]
public IHttpActionResult Update(WishListViewModel model)
{
    var wishListItems = _wishListService
.GetListItems(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType, true);

    foreach (var item in model.Items)
    {
        var existing = wishListItems.FirstOrDefault(w => w.ArticleId == item.VariantId);
        var quantity = existing != null ? item.Quantity - existing.Quantity : item.Quantity;

        _wishListService.AddListItem(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType,
    _variantService.Get(item.VariantId), quantity, true);
    }

    return Ok(true);
}
```

The AddToCart action:

```csharp theme={null}
[HttpPost]
[Route("addtocart")]
[ApiValidateAntiForgeryToken]
public IHttpActionResult AddToCart()
{
    _wishListService.AddToShoppingCart(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType);

    return Ok(true);
}
```

#### 3.3 How to add an item to the wish list — server side

```csharp theme={null}
public static MvcHtmlString WishListButton<TModel>(this HtmlHelper<TModel> htmlHelper, Expression<Func<TModel, ProductItemViewModel>> expression, string cssClass = null)
{
    var modelMetadata = ModelMetadata.FromLambdaExpression(expression, htmlHelper.ViewData);
    return WishListButton(htmlHelper, (ProductItemViewModel)modelMetadata.Model, cssClass);
}

public static MvcHtmlString WishListButton(this HtmlHelper<ProductItemViewModel> htmlHelper, string cssClass = null)
{
    return WishListButton(htmlHelper, htmlHelper.ViewData.Model, cssClass);
}

private static MvcHtmlString WishListButton(this HtmlHelper htmlHelper, ProductItemViewModel model, string cssClass)
{
    var tag = new TagBuilder("a")
    {
InnerHtml = "product.wishlist".AsWebSiteString()
    };

    var quantityFieldId = model.ShowQuantityField ? $"'{model.QuantityFieldId}'" : "null";
    tag.Attributes.Add("onclick", $"window.__litium.events.onAddToWishListButtonClick(this,'{model.Id}', {quantityFieldId})");

    cssClass = $"button wishlist-button {cssClass ?? string.Empty}".Trim();

    if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(cssClass))
    {
tag.Attributes.Add("class", cssClass);
    }

    return MvcHtmlString.Create(tag.ToString(TagRenderMode.Normal));
}
```

#### 3.4 How to add an item to the wish list — client side

Create `Wishlist.action.js` and add the add action:

```javascript theme={null}
export const add = ({ articleNumber, quantity = 1, nodeIdToShowNotification = null, notificationMessage = null, hash = '' }) => {
    return (dispatch) => {
        if (!quantity || isNaN(quantity) || parseInt(quantity) <= 0) {
            return;
        }

        return post('/api/wishlist/add', { articleNumber, quantity: parseInt(quantity) })
            .then(response => response.json())
            .then((items) => {
                nodeIdToShowNotification && dispatch(showNotification(nodeIdToShowNotification, notificationMessage, hash));
            })
            .catch(ex => dispatch(catchError(ex, error => ({
                type: WISHLIST_LOAD_ERROR,
                payload: {
                    error,
                }
            }))));
    }
}
```

Declare this action in `index.js`:

```javascript theme={null}
import { add as addToWishList } from './Actions/WishList.action';
```

#### 3.5 How to display and update all items in the wish list, and add them to the shopping cart — server side

Create a view model for the wish list and wish-list items:

```csharp theme={null}
public class WishListViewModel : IViewModel
{
    public const string DefaultListName = "Default";
    public const string DefaultListType = "Default";

    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public string Name { get; set; }
    public string Type { get; set; }
    public IList<WishListItemViewModel> Items { get; set; }
}

public class WishListItemViewModel : IAutoMapperConfiguration
{
    public WishListItemViewModel()
    {
        Id = Guid.NewGuid();
    }

    public Guid Id { get; }
    public Guid ListId { get; set; }
    public decimal Quantity { get; set; }
    public string ArticleNumber { get; set; }
    public string Image { get; set; }
    public string Name { get; set; }
    public Guid VariantId { get; set; }
    public long SortIndex { get; set; }

    [UsedImplicitly]
    public void Configure(IMapperConfigurationExpression cfg)
    {
        cfg.CreateMap<WishListItem, WishListItemViewModel>()
            .ConvertUsing<WishListItemConverter>();
    }
}
```

Create a converter to convert `WishListItem` to `WishListItemViewModel`:

```csharp theme={null}
[UsedImplicitly]
private class WishListItemConverter : ITypeConverter<WishListItem, WishListItemViewModel>
{
    private readonly VariantService _variantService;
    private readonly BaseProductService _baseProductService;

    public WishListItemConverter(VariantService variantService, BaseProductService baseProductService)
    {
        _variantService = variantService;
        _baseProductService = baseProductService;
    }

    public WishListItemViewModel Convert(WishListItem source, WishListItemViewModel destination, ResolutionContext context)
    {
        var variant = _variantService.Get(source.ArticleId);
        if (variant == null)
        {
            return new WishListItemViewModel();
        }

        var baseProduct = _baseProductService.Get(variant?.BaseProductSystemId ?? Guid.Empty);
        var image = (variant?.Fields.GetValue<IList<Guid>>(SystemFieldDefinitionConstants.Images)?.FirstOrDefault()
                     ?? baseProduct?.Fields.GetValue<IList<Guid>>(SystemFieldDefinitionConstants.Images)?.FirstOrDefault())
            .MapTo<ImageModel>();

        var viewModel = new WishListItemViewModel
        {
            ListId = source.ListId,
            ArticleNumber = variant.Id,
            VariantId = variant.SystemId,
            Image = image.GetUrlToImage(Size.Empty, new Size(200, 120)).Url,
            Name = variant?.Localizations.CurrentCulture.Name.NullIfWhiteSpace() ?? baseProduct?.Localizations.CurrentCulture.Name.NullIfWhiteSpace() ?? variant.Id,
            Quantity = source.Quantity,
            SortIndex = source.SortIndex
        };

        return viewModel;
    }
}
```

Create a builder to build the view model:

```csharp theme={null}
public class WishListViewModelBuilder : IViewModelBuilder<WishListViewModel>
{
    private readonly WishListService _wishListService;

    public WishListViewModelBuilder(WishListServiceFactory wishListServiceFactory, RouteRequestLookupInfoAccessor routeRequestLookupInfoAccessor)
    {
        _wishListService =
            wishListServiceFactory.CreateUserContext(routeRequestLookupInfoAccessor.RouteRequestLookupInfo.Channel);
    }

    public virtual WishListViewModel Build(PageModel pageModel)
    {
        var wishListItems = _wishListService
            .GetListItems(WishListViewModel.DefaultListName, WishListViewModel.DefaultListType, true)
            .MapTo<IEnumerable<WishListItemViewModel>>();

        return new WishListViewModel()
        {
            Name = WishListViewModel.DefaultListName,
            Type = WishListViewModel.DefaultListType,
            Items = wishListItems.ToList()
        };
    }
}
```

Create a controller:

```csharp theme={null}
public class WishListController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly WishListViewModelBuilder _builder;
    public WishListController(WishListViewModelBuilder builder)
    {
        _builder = builder;
    }
    [HttpGet]
    public ActionResult Index(PageModel currentPageModel)
    {
        var model = _builder.Build(currentPageModel);

        return View(model);
    }
}
```

#### 3.6 How to display and update all items in the wish list, and add them to the shopping cart — client side

Create a wish-list component `WishList.js`:

```javascript theme={null}
import React, { Component, Fragment } from 'react';

class WishList extends Component {
    constructor(props) {
        super(props);
    }

    handleQuantityChange(articleNumber, quantity) {
        this.props.onQuantityChange(articleNumber, quantity)
    }

    render() {
        const productContentClass = "columns small-12 medium-4 large-6" + " checkout-cart__image-container";
        const quantityInputClass = "columns small-2 medium-2 large-1";
        return (
            <div>
                <div className="row checkout__container">
                    <div className="small-12 simple-table">
                        <div className="row small-unstack no-margin">
                            <div className="columns small-12 medium-4 large-6"></div>
                            <div className="columns small-4 medium-3 large-2">Quantity</div>
                        </div>
                        {this.props.wishList && this.props.wishList.items.map((item, index, array) => (
                            <div key={index} className="row small-unstack no-margin">

                                <div className={productContentClass}>
                                    <div className="checkout-cart__image-wrapper">
                                        <img className="checkout-cart__image" src={item.image} alt={item.name} />
                                    </div>
                                    <div className="checkout-cart__image-info">
                                        {item.name}
                                    </div>
                                </div>
                                <div className={quantityInputClass}>
                                    <input className="checkout-cart__input" type="number" min="1" maxLength={3}
                                        value={item.quantity}
                                        onChange={event => this.handleQuantityChange(item.articleNumber, event.target.value)} />

                                </div>
                            </div>
                        ))}
                    </div>
                </div>
            </div>
        )
    }
}


export default WishList;
```

Add the actions `changeQuantity`, `updateWishList`, and `addToCart` to `WishList.action.js`:

```javascript theme={null}
export const changeQuantity = (articleNumber, quantity) => {
    return {
        type: WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY,
        articleNumber,
        quantity
    }
}

export const updateWishList = () => (dispatch, getState) => {
    return post('/api/wishlist/update', getState().wishlist)
        .then(response => response.json())
        .then(result => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_UPDATE,
                payload: {
                    success: true,
                    message: 'Wishlist was updated successfully'
                }
            });
        })
        .catch(ex => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_UPDATE,
                payload: {
                    success: false,
                    message: 'There was an error'
                }
            });
        });
}

export const addToCart = () => (dispatch) => {
    return post('/api/wishlist/addtocart')
        .then(response => response.json())
        .then(result => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART,
                payload: {
                    success: true,
                    message: 'Wishlist items were added to cart successfully'
                }
            })
        })
        .catch(ex => {
            dispatch({
                type: WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART,
                payload: {
                    success: false,
                    message: 'There was an error'
                }
            });
        });
}
```

Create `WishList.reducer.js`:

```javascript theme={null}
import { WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY, WISHLIST_UPDATE, WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART } from '../Actions/WishList.action';

export const wishlist = (state = {}, action) => {
    switch (action.type) {
        case WISHLIST_CHANGE_QUANTITY:
            return {
                ...state,
                items: state.items.map(
                    (wish) =>
                        (wish.articleNumber === action.articleNumber) ? { ...wish, quantity: action.quantity } : wish),

            };
        case WISHLIST_UPDATE :
        case WISHLIST_ADD_TO_CART:
            return {
                ...state,
                payload: action.payload
            };
        default:
            return state;
    }
}
```

Create `Wishlist.container.js` and combine them:

```javascript theme={null}
import React, { Component, Fragment } from 'react';
import { connect } from 'react-redux';
import WishList from '../Components/WishList'
import { changeQuantity, updateWishList, addToCart } from '../Actions/WishList.action'

class WishListContainer extends Component {
    constructor(props) {
        super(props);
    }

    render() {
        const { wishlist } = this.props;
        if (!wishlist || !wishlist.items || wishlist.items.length < 1) {
            return (
                <div className="row">
                    <div className="small-12">
                        <h2 className="checkout__title">Your wish list is empty</h2>
                    </div>
                </div>
            );
        }

        const { payload } = wishlist;
        return (
            <Fragment>
                {
                    payload && (<div>{payload.message}</div>)
                }
                <div class="row"><div class="small-12"><h2 class="checkout__title">Wish list</h2></div></div>

                <WishList wishList={wishlist} onQuantityChange={(articleNumber, quantity) => this.props.changeQuantity(articleNumber, quantity)} />
                <div className="row">
                    <div className="small-12 medium-6 columns">
                        <button type="submit" className="checkout__submit-button" onClick={() => this.props.update()} >Update</button>
                    </div>
                    <div className="small-12 medium-6 columns">
                        <button type="submit" className="checkout__submit-button" onClick={() => this.props.addToCart()} >Add to Cart</button>
                    </div>
                </div>
            </Fragment>
        )
    }
}

const mapStateToProps = state => {
    return {
        wishlist: state.wishlist,
    }
}

const mapDispatchToProps = dispatch => {
    return {
        changeQuantity: (articleNumber, quantity) => dispatch(changeQuantity(articleNumber, quantity)),
        update: () => dispatch(updateWishList()),
        addToCart: () => dispatch(addToCart())
    }
}

export default connect(mapStateToProps, mapDispatchToProps)(WishListContainer)
```

Go to Litium back office and create a new field template. Set `WishlistController` as Controller and `Index` as Action to the display template. Finally, create a new page in the website against the new template.

# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/wishlist/wish-list-for-litium-7/overview

Wish List source-code add-on for Litium 7 that allows customers to put products on a wish list.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Wish List is a source-code add-on that allows customers on an e-commerce site to put products on a wish list.

The add-on provides a stand-alone solution including both the add-on project and one for testing. It is compiled with Litium version 7.x and can easily be adjusted or developed further. You can use the add-on project in your Litium solution by changing the references to the NuGet packages of the solution.

The add-on consists of an API and database functionality to persist data. No UI is included, so the UI for customers and administrators must be implemented in your solution.

The functionality is as follows:

* Wish lists may be created by both logged-in and anonymous customers.
* A wish list contains a sorted list of products and their quantities.
* Anonymous customers can only have one wish list (anonymous wish list) per channel.
* Customers may have different wish lists for different channels. A wish list belongs to a specific channel and can only contain products published on that specific channel.
* Customers must log in to access wish lists saved on their account (account wish list). An anonymous wish list is not one of the account wish lists.
* A wish list can be created, edited, and deleted via integration (not included).
* An account wish list can have a name and a type.
* Both logged-in and anonymous customers can edit their respective wish lists. It is possible to change the order of the products, add and remove products, or clear the list.
* Both logged-in and anonymous customers can copy the content of the shopping cart to a wish list.
* Both logged-in and anonymous customers can copy the content of a wish list to the shopping cart.
* A wish list can contain both products and variants.
* A wish list only shows published products. Unpublished ones remain on the list but will not be shown, not even when it is edited by the customer.
* A wish list can be created, edited, and deleted by a user with the required access rights.
* An account wish list will never be cleared automatically.
* An anonymous wish list that has not been used for a certain number of days will be deleted automatically. The number of days can be set.
* A product will be added at the top of the list.
* A customer cannot have more than 100 wish lists.


# Configure

## Scheduled task deleting old wish lists

Wish lists of anonymous users should be deleted after a certain amount of time, for example a few months. This is achieved by using a scheduled task that can be configured in the `scheduledTasks` section of the `web.config` file of your solution.

Version 1:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.Studio.AddOns.WishList.CleanupScheduler, Litium.Studio.AddOns.WishList" startTime="00:00" interval="1d" parameters="Days=180" />
```

Version 2 and 3:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.WishList.CleanupScheduler, Litium.AddOns.WishList" startTime="00:00" interval="1d" parameters="Days=180" />
```

## Running xUnit tests

Pre-requisites: [xUnit](https://xunit.net/)

1. Copy the `Litium.Studio.AddOns.WishList.Test` project and the `\Src\Configurations` folder to your solution `src` location.
2. Fix the references. Make sure the reference to `Litium.Studio.AddOns.WishList` is correct as well.
3. Rename `\Src\Configurations\app.config.build` to `app.config` and configure the connection string and files folder to your solution test database and files folder. Alternatively, copy your `web.config`, rename it to `app.config` and place it in the `\Src\Configurations\` folder.

<Note>The test articles and test websites will be added to the database used in test cases.</Note>

You can now run the xUnit tests.


# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/connectors-product-extensions/wishlist/wishlist-for-litium-6/develop

Customise the Wish List add-on further for Litium 5 and 6.

<Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge>

## Architecture

### Data access layer

The Repository class contains all the methods to persist and manipulate data in the database. It does not contain business logic except sorting of the list items, selecting lists, and adding existing list items.

### Business logic layer

Business logic is implemented with the Service class (`WishListService` class from version 2) and implementations of `IUserContext`. It ensures that the wish list products of a logged-in user has a user ID but no cookie ID. Wish list products of an anonymous user has a cookie ID but not a user ID. It also handles cookie generation and ensures that the lists and their items are cached in the session.

**UserContext** handles anonymous users' and logged-in users' own wish list products. It uses `CurrentState` to return user, website, and shopping cart information. It also handles cookie generation and look-up for anonymous users and caching in the session.

**AdminUserContext** is used for administrators to handle other persons' wish list products. It is possible to pass user, website, and token information to the `AdminUserContext`. It processes the data directly through the repository. There is no caching in the session for the `AdminUserContext`. It does not handle cookies or shopping carts.

<Warning>Modifying a user's wish list while the user has an ongoing session may result in unexpected data loss to the user.</Warning>

### Data carriers

The `List` and `ListItem` classes are data carriers. They have no logic implemented. They are used to carry data between the data, business logic, and representation layer.
