# Upgrade to V3
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/klarna/upgrade/upgrade-to-v3

This article shows steps to upgrade to Klarna V3.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

You can run Klarna V3 side by side with Klarna V2 and KPM (legacy). Also, do not uninstall your previous Klarna V2 (or KPM - legacy), because there can be old orders that will need refund, capture and cancel for some time.

## From Klarna V2

All you need to do is to [Install Klarna addon](/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/klarna/install-v3). You can run Klarna V3 side by side with Klarna V2.

Do not uninstall the Klarna V2 version after going live with Klarna V3, only remove it from the checkout page. The V2 should be available in the backoffice to support cancel, capture and refund of old orders for some time.

## From Legacy Klarna KPM (Kreditor)

Klarna V3 is an iframe based checkout, therefore may need programmatic changes in your checkout page to render it. All information is available in install sections, and you may need to take a look at how it is done in Litium Accelerator.

## Alternative

It is easy to switch from KPM to Klarna HPP (Hosted Payment Pages). Simply install Klarna addon, and use the Klarna HPP.

Do not uninstall the Klarna KPM after going live with Klarna V3, only remove it from the checkout page. The Klarna KPM should be available in the backoffice to support cancel, capture, and refund of old orders for some time.

## ERP integration

If your ERP system does not support Klarna V3, consider an integration towards Litium from ERP using Litium Connect (Requires Litium 7.4 or later).

Your ERP system does not need to connect to Klarna V3 then, instead will talk to Litium, which will in turn talk to Klarna.


# Upgrade to v4.7.106
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/klarna/upgrade/upgrade-to-v4-7-106

This section contains instructions for upgrading the Klarna add-on to v4.7.106.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

An upgrade to the Klarna add-on requires that both `Litium.AddOns.Klarna` and `Litium.Studio.AddOns.Klarna` are upgraded to 4.7.106 using NuGet.

The Klarna KCO V3 in add-on version v4.7.106 is upgraded to use the Klarna API library `Klarna.Rest.Core` 3.1.9 version. This version is significantly different from the `Klarna.Rest` library, which results in breaking changes in the Litium Accelerator code. They are handled as follows:

1. Uninstall the package `Klarna.Rest` from the `Accelerator.MVC` project.
2. Remove statements that are using `Klarna.Rest`.
3. Use the `CheckoutOrder` object from the `Klarna.Rest.Core` library, instead of `CheckoutOrderData` from the old `Klarna.Rest` library.
4. Use `CheckoutOptions` from the `Klarna.Rest.Core` library, instead of `Options` from the old `Klarna.Rest` library.
5. `LitiumKcoOrder` no longer has the `CheckoutOrderData` object from `Klarna.Rest` library, but the `CheckoutOrder` object from the `Klarna.Rest.Core` library.
6. Note that the settings file has changed in `Litium.AddOns.Klarna.config`, where the new attribute `isKlarnaPaymentsHppEnabled` has been added.

## Code example for Litium 7

Changes in class `KlarnaPaymentConfigV3`:

1. Replace the method `UpdateDataSentToKlarna`:

```csharp theme={null}
public void UpdateDataSentToKlarna(UrlHelper urlHelper, OrderCarrier orderCarrier, KlarnaPaymentArgs paymentArgs, CheckoutOrder klarnaCheckoutOrder)
{
    //if the project has specific data to be sent to Klarna, outside the order carrier,
    //or has them as additional order info, and is not handled by the Klarna addOn, modify the klarnaCheckoutOrder parameter.
    //it is the klarnaCheckoutOrder object that will be sent to Klarna checkout api at Klarna.
    //the format of klarnaCheckoutOrder parameter is described in Klarna API documentation https://developers.klarna.com.
    //Set the checkout options here.
    klarnaCheckoutOrder.CheckoutOptions = new CheckoutOptions
    {
        AllowSeparateShippingAddress = true,
        ColorButton = "#ff69b4",
        DateOfBirthMandatory = true
    };

    //External payment methods should be configured for each Merchant account by Klarna before they are used.
    AddCashOnDeliveryExternalPaymentMethod(urlHelper, orderCarrier, klarnaCheckoutOrder);
}
```

2. Replace the method `AddCashOnDeliveryExternalPaymentMethod`:

```csharp theme={null}
private void AddCashOnDeliveryExternalPaymentMethod(UrlHelper urlHelper, OrderCarrier orderCarrier, CheckoutOrder klarnaCheckoutOrder)
{
    var checkoutPage = _websiteService.Get(orderCarrier.WebSiteID)?.Fields.GetValue<PointerPageItem>(AcceleratorWebsiteFieldNameConstants.CheckoutPage)?.EntitySystemId.MapTo<Page>();
    var channel = _channelService.Get(orderCarrier.ChannelID);
    if (checkoutPage == null || channel == null)
    {
        return;
    }

    var redirectUrl = urlHelper.Action(checkoutPage, routeValues: new { action = nameof(CheckoutController.PlaceOrderDirect) }, channel: channel);

    var routeValues = new
    {
        PaymentProvider = "DirectPay",
        PaymentMethod = "DirectPayment",
        RedirectUrl = redirectUrl
    };
    // ...
}
```

3. Replace method `ValidateCheckoutOrder`:

```csharp theme={null}
public ValidationResult ValidateCheckoutOrder(ILitiumKcoOrder order)
{
    var kcoOrder = order as LitiumKcoOrder;
    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(kcoOrder?.CheckoutOrder?.CheckoutCustomer?.DateOfBirth))
    {
        AddOrUpdateAdditionalOrderInfo(order.OrderCarrier, "DateOfBirth", kcoOrder.CheckoutOrder.CheckoutCustomer.DateOfBirth);
    }

    var channel = _channelService.Get(order.OrderCarrier.ChannelID);
    var language = channel.WebsiteLanguageSystemId.HasValue ? _languageService.Get(channel.WebsiteLanguageSystemId.Value) : null;
    CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture = language != null ? language.CultureInfo : CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture;
    var routeRequestLookupInfo = new RouteRequestLookupInfo()
    {
        Channel = channel,
        IsSecureConnection = true,
    };
    _errorPageResolver.TryGet(routeRequestLookupInfo, out var routeRequestInfo);

    // following result is used by Klarna AddOn to send the validation result back to Klarna.
    // ReSharper disable once ConvertToLambdaExpression
    return new ValidationResult
    {
        IsOrderValid = true,
        RedirectToUrlOnValidationFailure = routeRequestInfo.DataPath,
    };
}
```


# Upgrade to v4.7.111
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/klarna/upgrade/upgrade-to-v4-7-111

Upgrade instructions to v4.7.111.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Step 1: Update NuGet packages and isKlarnaShippingServiceEnabled attribute

Update your Klarna addon NuGet packages, `Litium.AddOns.Klarna.*` to v4.7.111.

<Note>
  If your accelerator code refers to the old Klarna V2 addon, `Litium.Studio.AddOns.Klarna` from code, you must upgrade `Litium.Studio.AddOns.Klarna` also to v4.7.111. This is because new methods are added to its common .NET interfaces.
</Note>

When you upgrade to Litium v4.7.111, there is a new attribute `isKlarnaShippingServiceEnabled` in the `Litium.AddOns.Klarna.dll.config`.

Add the attribute `isKlarnaShippingServiceEnabled` to your `Litium.AddOns.Klarna.dll.config` file if you chose not to replace it.

## Step 2: Uninstall Klarna.Rest.Core nuget package

Klarna has deprecated this package, and the Litium derived version of it, `Litium.Klarna.Rest.Core.dll` is included with the Litium Klarna AddOn v4.7.111. Therefore, to avoid conflicts, this package from Klarna should be uninstalled.

## Step 3: If you use Klarna Shipping Services

To use Klarna Shipping services, see install instructions [here](/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/klarna/develop/klarna-shipping-service/install-kss).

## Important note

When you develop locally, your website should be accessible to Klarna for background notifications. Follow [steps here](/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/klarna/develop/developing-and-testing-klarna-behind-firewalls).


# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/nets/nets-easy/configure

Instructions on NetsEasy configuration.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Start filling you NetsEasy account information in the `Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy.dll.config` file:

* Applies to all accounts
  * `paymentProviderName` - Do not change!
  * `webHookToken` - Choose your own string to be compared on webhook callbacks.
  * `orderCarrierDiscCacheCleanTime` - Time in minutes when OrderCarrier folder gets cleaned of unnecessary stored OrderCarriers. Default 5 hours (300 min). This depends on how many orders the merchant has per day and sometimes for assurence one would like to keep the OrderCarriers quite longer but if too many OrderCarriers in the same folder then performance could be affected.
  * `webHookDiscCacheCleanTime` - Time in minutes when stored callback webhooks folder gets cleaned of unnecessary stored webhooks. Default is five minutes.
* Individual accounts
  * `accountId` - Should not contain spaces and should be Unique. Identifier to select the account. This value will be prefixed to the payment method name. The first word of the payment method will be paymentaccount identifier.
  * `merchantNumber` - Account number received from Nets which indicates the merchants account with Nets.
  * `defaultConsumerType` - We separate the B2B or B2C accounts in Litium implementation.
  * `supportedConsumerTypes` - We separate the B2B or B2C accounts in Litium implementation.
  * `prefillCompanyConsumerInfo` - When true company stored addresses will appear in Checkout page and we prefill the address information on the widget.
  * `merchantHandlesShippingCost` - If free shipping cost for consumer.
  * `shippingCountryCodes` - Supported shipping countries, comma separated list of countries in (ISO) three letter country codes, if no countries added then all available countries will be listed in checkout widget.
  * `useTestMode` - Set to true when testing the application.
  * `secretKey` - Encryption API key or CRUD operations acquired from Nets portal.
  * `checkoutKey` - Encryption checkout widget API key acquired from Nets portal.
  * `secretKeyTest` - Test environment Encryption API key or CRUD operations acquired from Nets portal.
  * `checkoutKeyTest` - Test environment Encryption checkout widget API key acquired from Nets portal.

## Web.Config

Add these two lines of codes inside `scheduledTasks`:

```xml theme={null}
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy.Tasks.WebHookTask, Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy" startTime="00:00" interval="5m" />
<scheduledTask type="Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy.Tasks.OrderCarrierTask, Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy" startTime="00:00" interval="6h" />
```

These lines will clear the WebHookPayment and OrderCarrier files inside the `..Files/NetsEasyCheckout` folder with background tasks.

WebHookTask is set to every five minutes and it clears all files older than two minutes. This functionality is just an extra check on that payment has been received successfully and placed in Litium by PaymentCompletedConfirmation method, otherwise it will be re-tried.

OrderCarrierTask is set to every six hours and it deletes files older than five hours (default), since the last received WebHook call is set to 2+5+10+15+20+25+30+40+50+60 = 257 minutes by Nets (Info from Nets support team).

## Next step

Choose the NetsEasy PaymentProvider in Litium backoffice/Settings/Channels and chosen Litium channel and add both B2B and B2C to the channel.


# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/nets/nets-easy/develop

Development instructions, hints, and samples.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

* Most of the modified code on the existing accelerator files are made for pre-filling the company information when a user is logged in and connected to a company that has addresses stored in Litium back office.
* Most of the business logics in Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy is made in NetsCheckoutService which inherits from INetsCheckoutService and you can use Litium [Service Decorator](https://docs.litium.com/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/architecture/dependency-injection/service-decorator) approach to override if needed in your solution.
* We only merge consumer information when payment object received from NetsEasy on OrderConfirmation before placing the order. If the user is connected to a company with stored addresses then we prefill that information in advance and no merging occurs afterward.
* All available WebHooks are implemented, you can comment out the ones not needed in NetsEasyWidgetV1.cs method CreateNotification(Uri channelUri).
* You can change a payment status from Litium back office or NetsEasy portal, either way states should synchronize and if that would fail by some unexpected issue then we can synchronize the status of the payment manually in Litium back office by clicking Synchronize Status button.
* Payment states are set by WebHooks so timing will differ between statuses.

## WebHook call try intervalls

```json theme={null}
{"intervalInMinutes":[2,5,10,15,20,25,30,40,50,60,70,80,90,120,250],"maxCount":10}
```

According to Nets support team this means that last webhook is sent by 2+5+10+15+20+25+30+40+50+60 = 257 minutes.

More information on NetsEasy

* [Nets Easy Documentation](https://tech.dibspayment.com/easy)
* [Nets Easy Swagger](https://dev-api.dibspayment.eu/docs/index.html)
* [Nets Easy Customer Portal](https://portal.dibspayment.eu/dashboard)

# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/nets/nets-easy/install

Installation instructions. Requires at minimum Litium 6.3.9 but Litium 7.x is preffered.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

Requires at minimum Litium 6.3.9 but Litium 7.x is preffered.

Read the [system requirements](https://docs.litium.com/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/get-started/system-requirements) for the development environment before installing.

## Installation

1. If you already have NetsEasy installed, back up the `Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy.dll.config` file from `wwwroot`.
2. Open Visual Studio and your solution.
3. Open **Package Manager Console** on the **Tools > NuGet Package Manager** menu. If you have multiple projects in the solution, ensure that the web application project is selected as **Default project** in Package Manager Console.
4. Install the nuget-packages with the following commands in Package Manager Console: (If you are running Litium Accelerator, both packages should be installed to the `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc` project and `Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy` is required in `Litium.Accelerator` project.)

```
Install-Package Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy
Install-Package Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy.UI
```

5. Update the `Litium.AddOns.NetsEasy.dll.config` found in `wwwroot` and enter your configuration options.

## Adding to Litium Accelerator checkout page

Follow following steps to add Nets iframe to accelerator checkout page. We recommend to use Chrome for the download.

1. Download zip package from below links:
   * [Accelerator 7.6.2 files for NetsEasy Checkout](https://docs.litium.com/storage/ma/685ad167d8124da5bfbc9d1d577c09d9/255f16cdfb244217bdab674396b20607/zip/7832C3457DA2BBCB476322133DE9BFC104F63AFD/AcceleratorFiles_L7_Nets_6_3_103.zip)
2. Unzip and place new files inside in `Litium.Accelerator.MVC` project.
3. Insert and alter codes inside related modified files in respective projects.
4. Build your solution.

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/nets/nets-netaxept/configure

Instructions for configuration of Nets.

<Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Configure Litium.Studio.AddOns.Nets.dll.config

To configure Nets, edit the file `Litium.Studio.AddOns.Nets.dll.config` in your `web\bin` directory.

If the file does not exist, then rename the file to a similar name as above, but end it with "dll.config.tmpl.exclude".

Necessary configuration instructions are at the begining of this file.

## Configuring transaction callback

Nets can call Litium Studio to notify changes to the transaction status. This notification call back is important in bank direct payments.

To setup, login to nets admin backoffice, and go to **Options > Callback**

Enter following url as the callback url.

```
https://<your site domain name>/PaymentProviderResult.axd/Report/Nets?paymentAccIdentifier=<Your payment account identifier in config file>
```

e.g.:

```
https://paymentproviders-7.site.nu/PaymentProviderResult.axd/Report/Nets?paymentAccIdentifier=SE
```

In the example above, the site domain name is "paymentproviders-7.product.workplace.nu", and the `Litium.Studio.AddOns.Nets.dll.config` contains the `paymentAccIdentifier` as "SE" for the Nets account.

## Testing Nets

If you do not have a test account to exclusively test Nets, you should request a seperate test account to be used from your staging environments.

Test information is at: [https://shop.nets.eu/web/partners/test-cards](https://shop.nets.eu/web/partners/test-cards)


# Develop
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/nets/nets-netaxept/develop

Development instructions, hints and samples.

<Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Nets mobile package

Nets payment user interface can be adopted to mobile devices, but it requires Nets to configure the merchant account with "MobilePackage". In the project one can set to use the mobile package always by setting the `useMobilePackage` attribute in the addons config file to true. This will make even desktop users go to mobile payment page which might not be appropriate.

To have a more adaptive behaviour, set the `useMobilePackage` parameter to `false` in the `Litium.Studio.AddOns.Nets.dll.config` and then change the CheckoutFlow page type template to detect the users browser and determine whether it is a mobile device or not. If it is a mobile device, set the checkoutflowInfo setting key `NetsExecutePaymentArgs.CheckoutFlowInfoKeyMobileDevice` to true.

Following code fragment shows how it will look if you change the accelerator checkout template.

```csharp theme={null}
var ismobileDevice = false;

//TODO: implement the method DetectMobileDevice() to determine whether the users browser is a mobile device or not., and uncomment the line below.
//ismobileDevice = DetectMobileDevice();

var checkoutFlowInfo = _cartAccessor.Cart.CheckoutFlowInfo;
// ...
checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue(NetsExecutePaymentArgs.CheckoutFlowInfoKeyMobileDevice, ismobileDevice);

ExecutePaymentResult result = paymentInfo.ExecutePayment(checkoutFlowInfo, _securityToken);
if (result != null)
{
    HandlePaymentResult(result.Success, result.ErrorMessage);
}
```

## Testing Nets

If you do not have a test account to exclusively test Nets, you should request a seperate test account to be used from your staging environments.

Test information is at: [https://shop.nets.eu/web/partners/test-cards](https://shop.nets.eu/web/partners/test-cards)

## Creating account

Contact Nets at [www.nets.eu](http://www.nets.eu/) and obtain the test account. Your merchant should apply for production accounts separately.

You will get the following information

* User Id and password to their Admin site
  * [https://epayment-test.bbs.no/admin/Default.aspx](https://epayment-test.bbs.no/admin/Default.aspx) (test)
  * [https://epayment.bbs.no/admin/Default.aspx](https://epayment.bbs.no/admin/Default.aspx) (production)
* Merchant Id
* API token

# Features
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/paypal/features



<Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

PayPal is an international payment provider and also acts as an acquirer. When paying through a PayPal account, the customer does not enter the credit card details, but uses the PayPal account, which stores credit/debit card information internally.

## Features

* Express checkout: Payments through Paypal account. Any payment methods added to the user's Paypal account can be used to make payments.
* Multimarket support: multiple PayPal accounts in the same Litium installation.
* Supports payment through Litium as a headless checkout.

For more information, go to the PayPal website.


# Get started
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/paypal/get-started

Before you begin, contact Paypal at www.paypal.com and obtain the test account information.

<Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

When using PayPal for development and testing, keep in mind you are working with three different account types.

* Your developer account accessed from developer.paypal.com. You must have a "real" e-mail account to log in here.
* After logging in you will create two more accounts, one is called the business account, to represent your merchant site, and another to simulate an end customer. Both contains "fake" email accounts.

# Customize createOrder
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/qliro/develop/customize-createorder

When the Qliro iframe is initialized, the Create order method is called in the Qliro API.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

`CreateOrderRequestArgs` parameters used in this call can be customized by the project.

In the released accelerator sample (see installation), see the file `\Src\Litium.Accelerator.Mvc\App_Start\QliroPaymentWidgetConfig.cs` to see how the data sent to Qliro is customized in the `UpdateDataSentToQliro` method. Project need to modify the `requestArgs` parameter passed in as shown below.

```csharp theme={null}
public void UpdateDataSentToQliro(OrderCarrier orderCarrier, QliroPaymentArgs paymentArgs, CreateOrderRequestArgs requestArgs)
{
    //if the project has specific data to be sent to Qliro, outside the order carrier,
    //or has them as additional order info, and is not handled by the Qliro addOn, modify the CreateOrderRequest parameter.
    //it is the CreateOrderRequestArgs object that will be sent to Qliro checkout api at Qliro.
    //the format of CreateOrderRequestArgs parameter is described in Qliro API documentation https://developers.qliro.com/merchant#createOrder-request.

    //Set the checkout options here.
    requestArgs.CallToActionColor = "#ff69b4";

    //to allow unrestricted shipping
}
```


# Multi-market support
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/qliro/develop/multi-market-support

To use the Qliro addon with multiple markets you need to send in the country code from checkout flow info.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

If the country is not sent in checkout flow info, the default country is determined by the currency of the order where possible.

To send the country code of the current order, send it as below:

in `\Src\Litium.Accelerator\Payments\Widgets\QliroWidget.cs`

```csharp theme={null}
private ExecutePaymentArgs CreatePaymentArgs(OrderCarrier order, string paymentAccountId)
{
    if (!_routeRequestLookupInfoAccessor.RouteRequestLookupInfo.IsSecureConnection)
    {
        this.Log().Trace("Qliro Checkout Validation is disabled. To enable the validate you need to use https on the checkout page.");
    }

    var checkoutFlowInfo = Cart.CheckoutFlowInfo;
    //...other code..
    var country = _countryService.Get(order.CountryID)?.Id.ToUpper() ?? "SE";
    checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue(ConstantsAndKeys.CountryCodeKey, country);

    //...other code..

    return new QliroPaymentArgsCreator().CreatePaymentArgs(checkoutFlowInfo);
}
```


# Order validation
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/qliro/develop/order-validation

How to implement order validation in Qliro One.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

When a user clicks the Slutför köpet button in the Qliro iframe, a callback will be executed and validate the order.

If the order is accepted, the response status code is 200.

If it is declined, the status code is 400 together with a reason.

Depending on the reason, Qliro One will present a message to the iframe.

Here is a code example for the implementation of order validation.

1. Create the public action in the controller that will receive the request from Qliro, in `\Src\Litium.Accelerator.Mvc\Controllers\Checkout\QliroPaymentController.cs`

```csharp theme={null}
[HttpPost]
public ActionResult Validate(string accountId, string transactionNumber)
{
    var checkoutApi = _qliroPaymentService.CreateQliroApi(accountId);
    checkoutApi.ValidateQliroOneOrder(order => _paymentWidgetConfig.ValidateCheckoutOrder(order), Request, Response);
    return Content("OK");
}
```

2. Set this URL when you get the Qliro widget:

```csharp theme={null}
private ExecutePaymentArgs CreatePaymentArgs(OrderCarrier order, string paymentAccountId)
{
    // … other code …
    var channelUri = new Uri(_urlService.GetUrl(_requestModelAccessor.RequestModel.ChannelModel.Channel, new ChannelUrlArgs() { AbsoluteUrl = true }));
    var validationUrl = new Uri(urlHelper.Action("Validate", "QliroPayment", null, Uri.UriSchemeHttps, channelUri.Host));

    checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue(ConstantsAndKeys.ValidationUrlKey, validationUrl.AbsoluteUri);

    // … other code …

    return new QliroPaymentArgsCreator().CreatePaymentArgs(checkoutFlowInfo);
}
```

3. Put your validation logic in this method:

```csharp theme={null}
public ValidationResult ValidateCheckoutOrder(ILitiumQliroOneOrder order)
{
    var calculatorItemArgs = order.OrderCarrier.OrderRows
        .Where(x => !x.CarrierState.IsMarkedForDeleting)
        .Select(x => new StockStatusCalculatorItemArgs
        {
            Quantity = x.Quantity,
            VariantSystemId = x.ProductID
        })
        .ToArray();

    var stockStatusResult = _stockStatusCalculator.GetStockStatuses(new StockStatusCalculatorArgs
        {
            CountrySystemId = order.OrderCarrier.CountryID,
            Date = DateTime.Now,
            UserSystemId = order.OrderCarrier.CustomerInfo.PersonID,
            WebSiteSystemId = order.OrderCarrier.WebSiteID
        },
        calculatorItemArgs);

    foreach (var row in order.OrderCarrier.OrderRows.Where(x => !x.CarrierState.IsMarkedForDeleting))
    {
        if (!stockStatusResult.TryGetValue(row.ProductID, out var status)
            || status.InStockQuantity < row.Quantity)
        {
            return new ValidationResult
            {
                IsOrderValid = false,
                DeclineReason = "OutOfStock"
            };
        }
    }
    // following result is used by Qliro AddOn to send the validation result back to Qliro.
    // ReSharper disable once ConvertToLambdaExpression
    return new ValidationResult
    {
        IsOrderValid = true,
        DeclineReason = string.Empty
    };
}
```

# Show shipping methods
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/qliro/develop/show-shipping-methods

Show the shipping options inside the Qliro iframe by following these instructions.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

<Note>
  Your Qliro site should be publicly visible to Qliro for Shipping methods to work. See below for setting up localhost when developer testing.
</Note>

* In the Qliro config file, enable set the `enableShippingMethods` attribute to `"true"`
* You need to override the default shipping method implementation to send the list of shipping options to Qliro. Qliro calls the Litium Qliro Addon, which in tern calls the `Build()` method and `GetDeliveryMethods()`. Following is an example code for Accelerator 7.1 to override it.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.AddOns.Qliro.Api.Models;
using Litium.AddOns.Qliro.Abstractions;
using Litium.Foundation.Modules.ECommerce;
using Litium.Foundation.Modules.ECommerce.Deliveries;
using Litium.Foundation.Security;
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using Litium.AddOns.Qliro.Builders;
using Litium.Globalization;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.Payments.Handlers
{
    public class CustomQliroShippingMethodsBuilder : QliroShippingMethodsBuilder
    {
        private readonly ChannelService _channelService;

        public CustomQliroShippingMethodsBuilder(ChannelService channelService)
        {
            _channelService = channelService;
        }

        public override List<ShippingMethod> Build(ShippingMethodBuildArgs args)
        {
            return base.Build(args);
        }

        protected override List<DeliveryMethod> GetDeliveryMethods(ShippingMethodBuildArgs args)
        {
            var channel = _channelService.Get(args.OrderCarrier.ChannelID);
            if (channel == null)
                return new List<DeliveryMethod>();

            var deliveryMethodIds = channel.CountryLinks?.FirstOrDefault()?.DeliveryMethodSystemIds ?? Enumerable.Empty<Guid>();
            return deliveryMethodIds.Select(deliveryMethodId => ModuleECommerce.Instance.DeliveryMethods.Get(deliveryMethodId, SecurityToken.CurrentSecurityToken)).ToList();
        }
    }
}
```

* If you are testing locally, you need publicly visible urls for server to server Qliro callbacks.
* You can set the `backgroundCallsDomainName` attribute in the Qliro addon config, to point the domain to a publicly visible domain.
* Alternatively, specify the full url for `AvailableShippingMethodsUrl` in the `checkoutFlowInfo` in `Src\Litium.Accelerator\Payments\Widgets\QliroWidget.cs`

```csharp theme={null}
private ExecutePaymentArgs CreatePaymentArgs(OrderCarrier order, string paymentAccountId)
{
    //....
    checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue(ConstantsAndKeys.AvailableShippingMethodsUrlKey, "https://somePublicDomain/");
    
    //....
}
```

* The default URL sent (if nothing is specified) is similar to:

```
"MerchantOrderAvailableShippingMethodsUrl": "http://sampleDomain.com/PaymentProviderResult.axd/Report/Qliro?QliroNotificationType=AvailableShippingMethods&accountId=Qliro"
```

## Customize shipping options sent to Qliro

You can customize the shipping options sent to Qliro by changing the return value of the `Build()` method in the above example.

```csharp theme={null}
public override List<ShippingMethod> Build(ShippingMethodBuildArgs args) 
{
    var result = base.Build(args);
    //TODO: Customize the result values, for example you can change descriptions, etc.
    return result;
}
```


# Troubleshoot tips and FAQs
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/qliro/develop/troubleshoot-tips

This section contains common troubleshooting tips and FAQs.

<Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## Shipping methods do not show up inside Qliro iframe

Check following:

* `enableShippingMethods` in the Qliro config file is enabled
* Website should be publicly visible to Qliro for background calls to succeed. If website is not publicly visible (behind a firewall) then shipping methods will not be displayed inside Qliro iframe.

## Shipping method change in Qliro iframe does not work properly

When showing shipping methods inside the Qliro iframe (`enableShippingMethods` is set to `true` in the config file) and then changing the shipping method in the Qliro iframe is dependent on the correct calculation of the shopping cart. If the background call does not succeed, the cart re-calculation fails and will result in an order that gets automatically canceled in Qliro.

To check, do the following:

If the shipping method is selected in the Qliro One Iframe, it also is updated in the litium cart.

`onShippingMethodChanged` event is registered on the client-side to call accelerator built-in `setDelivery` method. This method will call `SetDeliveryProvider` action of `CheckoutController`.

In order to know whether it works or not, you can open the network tabs of the chrome develop window and see that the `setDeliveryProvider` request is successful or not. Alternatively, attach a debugger and put a breakpoint to `setdeliveryprovider` method in the checkout controller.

# Configure
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/svea-checkout/configure

Configuration guide.

<Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

* Configure the Svea account information in the `Litium.AddOns.Svea.dll.config` file
  * `paymentAccIdentifier`: Mandatory. Must be unique for each payment account. Identifier to select the account.
  * `merchantId`: Mandatory. Svea merchant id. This value is assigned by Svea.
  * `sharedSecret`: Mandatory. Svea secret word. This value is assigned by Svea.
  * `isTestAccount`: If true, uses Svea test environment, if false uses Svea production. All test accounts should have this attribute true.
  * `isCompany`: true if site is B2B, otherwise false
  * `isSveaCheckoutEnabled`: Enable or disable SveaCheckout as a Payment method in Litium.
  * `useValidation`: If true, Svea validates the order before the processing the purchase.
  * `salesCountry`: ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code of selling country. If you are selling in multiple countries with same account, duplicate the entire payment account section with unique paymentAccountIdentifiers to each country, and specify correct sales country to this parameter.
* Choose and add Svea pay on the desired website/channel (depending on Litium version) in the Litium backoffice.

<Note>
  The Accelerator implementation for this add-on is developed for Litium 7.4.2 and might need to be adjusted if your project is using another version.
</Note>

# Configure SwedbankPay
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/swedbankpay/configure

How to configure the SwedbankPay extension.

<Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

When the SwedbankPay account is setup, you can get the Merchant ID (a guid) and a resource token can be generated there.

* Enter the merchant id and the resource token into the `Litium.AddOns.SwedbankPay.dll.config` in the wwwroot.
* Enter the `serverCommunicationDelayInMinutes = "2"`
  * This is the delay required to avoid race conditions, if background server communication receives at the same time a redirect occurs.
* Enter the `serverCommunicationUrl="Https://<YourDomainName>`
  * This is the url that will receive background calls from SwedbankPay. If you are in a developer machine behind a firewall, specify a publicly accessible address here.

## Terms Page

Make sure you have the following links on your terms page when you are using SwedbankPay invoice.

Sweden: [https://www.swedbankpay.se/villkor/faktura](https://www.swedbankpay.se/villkor/faktura)

Norway: [https://www.swedbankpay.no/vilkaar/faktura](https://www.swedbankpay.no/vilkaar/faktura)

# Install SwedbankPay
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/swedbankpay/install

Installation instructions and more.

<Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

* If you already have SwedbankPay installed, back up the `Litium.AddOns.SwedbankPay.dll.config` file from wwwroot.
* Open Visual Studio and your solution.
* Open **Package Manager Console** on the **Tools > NuGet Package Manager** menu. If you have multiple projects in the solution, ensure that the web application project (e.g. `Litium.Accelerator.Mvc`) is selected as **Default project** in Package Manager Console.
* Install the nuget-packages with the following commands in Package Manager Console:

```
Install-Package Litium.AddOns.SwedbankPay
Install-Package Litium.AddOns.SwedbankPay.UI
```

* Update the `Litium.AddOns.SwedbankPay.dll.config` found in wwwroot and enter your configuration options.
* It is mandatory to use TLS security (HTTPS). (If you are using Accelerator 7, enable this by setting a HSTS max age value in the domain url to be a value more than zero.)

## Checkout page code changes

Following checkout page code changes are required for the SwedbankPay payments to work.

Constants used in below code such as "TermsUrl", "LogoUrl" are defined in the `Litium.AddOns.SwedbankPay.dll` assembly in `Litium.AddOns.SwedbankPay.ConstantsAndKeys` class.

## Terms URL

The terms page is mandatory and its URL is mandatory when creating the payments, and should be an absolute Url. This page should specify the merchant's terms and conditions. It needs to be sent as part of CheckoutFlow info when placing the order.

In the Accelerator, you may obtain the terms URL as follows.

```csharp theme={null}
var checkoutPage = _requestModelAccessor.RequestModel.WebsiteModel.Fields.GetValue<PointerPageItem>(AcceleratorWebsiteFieldNameConstants.CheckouPage);
var checkoutPageUrl = GetAbsolutePageUrl(checkoutPage);
var checkoutPageEntity = checkoutPage.EntitySystemId.MapTo<Web.Models.Websites.PageModel>();
var termsAndConditionPage = checkoutPageEntity.GetValue<PointerPageItem>(CheckoutPageFieldNameConstants.TermsAndConditionsPage);
var termsAndConditionPageUrl = GetAbsolutePageUrl(termsAndConditionPage);
```

Then, the url should be sent using the CheckFlowInfo, in PlaceOrder method.

```csharp theme={null}
//Method signature is modified to pass in the absolute Urls
public override ExecutePaymentResult PlaceOrder(CheckoutViewModel model, string responseUrl, string cancelUrl, string termsUrl, string logoUrl, out string redirectUrl)
{
     //Other code...
     
    checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue("TermsUrl", termsUrl);
    checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue("LogoUrl", logoUrl);

    //Other code...

    _cartService.PlaceOrder(out PaymentInfo[] paymentInfos);

   //Other code...
}
```

## Logo Url

Logo Url is not mandatory, but can be used to show the merchants website logo in the SwedbankPay site.

Url should be an absolute Url.

```csharp theme={null}
checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue("LogoUrl", logoUrl);
```

## Description

A text description (maximum 40 charactors) can be shown in the page where buyer is entering payment details in SwedbankPay.

```csharp theme={null}
checkoutFlowInfo.SetValue("Description", "your description to show to buyer");
```


# Migrating from PayEx
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/swedbankpay/migrating-from-payex

This article has specific instructions on how to migrate from PayEx.

<Badge>4.7</Badge> <Badge>4.8</Badge> <Badge>Litium 5</Badge> <Badge>Litium 6</Badge> <Badge>Litium 7</Badge>

## General rule

* Do not uninstall PayEx, you may have old orders where PayEx is needed to refund, cancel, or capture.
* [Install SwedbankPay](install).
* Configure your checkout pages to use SwedbankPay, and remove PayEx payment methods from the checkout page.

## Compatibility

* Contact SwedbankPay support, if you are not sure whether a particular PayEx feature is not available in SwedbankPay. [Please see SwedbankPay documentation](https://developer.swedbankpay.com/payments/).
* Litium AddOn implements the "Swedbank Pay Payments" and the following are the supported methods in "Swedbank Pay Payments" as at June 2020. SwedbankPay may add more features in the future. If you are interested in additional functionality added to the SwedbankPay AddOn, contact Litium support.
  * Credit/Debit cards
  * SwedbankPay Invoice
  * MobilePay
  * Swish
  * Vipps

## Upgrading in Litium 4.x versions

In Litium 4.x versions, the checkout page may have hardcoded the Payment method names. In this case, you might see an error in the SwedbankPay addon, saying "Can't create component", and typically the error looks as follows.

<img alt="Can't create component error" />

This can be because the checkout page is still sending the old PaymentMethodName, that it used to send to PayEx addon. For example, for card payments, it typically used to be "SE CardPayment" in PayEx. In SwedbankPay, it should be "SE CartPayments\_redirect"

Remove all the payEx methods from your checkout page. Save and publish the checkout page. Then, add the SwedbankPay payment methods again.

If that does not solve the issue, it may be that your checkout page has hardcoded the value. A developer should replace the hardcoded value and send in the correct values.

## Debugging SwedbankPay

If you wish to debug the payment addon to understand and isolate the issues you are facing, contact Litium support.

# App concept
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/get-started/app-development-guide/app-concept

A Litium app allows you to extend the functionality of the Litium platform. A typical use-case for an app is to integrate a Litium solution with a third-party system that provide a specialized service within the e-commerce ecosystem, like payment service providers, transport management systems or the company's ERP system.

The Litium apps are designed to be decoupled from the Litium platform itself. Apps are running as separate applications in the Litium Commerce Cloud and are communicating with Litium using the platform's APIs. This has several important advantages:

1. **Less dependency on Litium** — To develop an extension (an add-on that is installed into the Litium solution) you would need extensive knowledge of the inner working of the platform. When implementing the same solution as an app you only need knowledge of the interface between your app and Litium. That is one or more of the Litium Connect APIs.
2. **Freedom of choice** — Litium is built using Microsoft .NET, but an app can be built using the programming language and framework that you prefer.
3. **Cloud compatible** — The app architecture of Litium supports the advantages of the Litium Commerce Cloud, such as autoscaling and ability for partners to manage the deployment of environments.

<Note>
  Litium apps works with Litium 8. For Litium 7 and earlier versions add-ons can be implemented by building an extension.
</Note>

## Communication between an app and Litium

Litium will communicate with an app via HTTP. Litium will notify the app of any events happening inside the platform for which the app has registered for the corresponding webhook. You can find all available events in the API Reference.

When processing these events, the app can request additional information using the Litium Connect APIs. These APIs can also be used to send data and requests to Litium.

A Litium service account is used to secure the communication between the app and Litium. More information about authentication and authorization for apps is in the app development guide.

## Public and private apps

Litium apps can be divided into two groups: public and private.

A public app is available to all Litium customers. Public apps can be installed to any customer environment in Litium Commerce Cloud through the [Litium Cloud CLI](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli). Public apps can be developed and maintained by Litium, eg the [Klarna payment app](/add-ons/litium-apps/klarna-payment) and the [Direct shipment app](/add-ons/litium-apps/direct-shipment), but can also be owned by a Technology Partner, eg the [Briqpay payment app](/add-ons/litium-apps/briqpay-payment). Before a public app built by a Technology Partner can be released, a Public app agreement must be signed between Litium and the partner. If you are interested in building a public app, please [contact Litium](mailto:support@litium.com).

A private app is on the other hand an app that is developed for a specific Litium customer and installed only in that customer's environment. These apps are, unlike the public apps, not available in the central Litium registry. They are commonly developed and maintained by the Solution Partner as part of a customer's Litium solution.

Both private and public apps run in Litium's cloud and can be managed using the Litium Cloud CLI. More information about considerations to keep in mind regarding the cloud environment when developing your app can be found in this guide. Detailed information about services available to private apps can be found in the [Litium Commerce Cloud documentation](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps).

## Communication between an app and Litium

Litium communicates with an app via HTTP. Litium notifies the app of any events happening inside the platform for which the app has registered the corresponding webhook. You can find all available events in the API reference.

When processing these events, the app can request additional information using the Litium Connect APIs. These APIs can also be used to send data and requests to Litium.

A Litium service account is used to secure the communication between the app and Litium. More information about authentication and authorization for apps is in the app development guide.

## Public and private apps

Litium apps can be divided into two groups: public and private.

**Public apps** are available to all Litium customers. They can be installed to any customer environment in Litium Commerce Cloud through the [Litium Cloud CLI](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli). Public apps can be developed and maintained by Litium, such as the Klarna payment app and the Direct shipment app, but can also be owned by a Technology Partner. Before a public app built by a Technology Partner can be released, a Public app agreement must be signed between Litium and the partner. If you are interested in building a public app, please [contact Litium](mailto:support@litium.com).

**Private apps** are developed for a specific Litium customer and installed only in that customer's environment. Unlike public apps, they are not available in the central Litium registry. They are commonly developed and maintained by a Solution Partner as part of a customer's Litium solution.

Both private and public apps run in Litium's cloud and can be managed using the Litium Cloud CLI. Detailed information about services available to private apps can be found in the [Litium Commerce Cloud documentation](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps).


# App installation and registration
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/get-started/app-development-guide/app-installation

A Litium app needs to register with the Litium instance that it will be connected to. The app will then be available on the apps page in Settings in Litium backoffice. On the apps page the user can install and uninstall apps and upload configuration files to installed apps.

The app registration and installation flow looks like this:

<Frame>
  <img alt="Litium app registration and installation flow" />
</Frame>

The installation flow is initiated by directing the user to an endpoint in the App Management API. The URL to this endpoint looks like this:

```
https://<Litium URL>/Litium/api/app-management/install?url=<App metadata URL>
```

The app metadata URL should be an endpoint in the app where the app will return the metadata needed for Litium to create and install the app. Litium will call the metadata endpoint and once the data is returned Litium will create an entry for the app in Litium's database and load the App Detail page of the Litium Backoffice.

On the App Detail page, the user clicks the Install button. Litium will then create a service account with the permissions that the app has requested and call the configuration endpoint of the app (defined in the metadata) with the token for the service account. This token will be used to secure the communication between Litium and the app.

Once the app has been installed, the app detail page of the Litium backoffice provides a UI to upload configuration files to the app. Litum currently supports configuration files in JSON format. When a user uploads a file, Litium will call the configuration file endpoint of the app with the uploaded data, see App configuration section below for more details.

## App metadata definition

The definition of the metadata Litium expects to be returned from the app looks like this:

```json theme={null}
{
    "id": "app-id",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "displayName": "Display name for the app",
    "requestedPermissions": [
        "Function/Products/Content",
        "Permissions/in/Litium/defined/way"
    ],
    "configurationUrl": "absolute url for the configuration endpoint",
    "metadataUrl": "absolute url for the metadata endpoint",
    "appUrl": "absolute domain for the app including scheme"
}
```

The endpoint for the metadata needs to be accessible by everyone when the application isn't yet installed in an Litium instance.

<Note>
  The metadata endpoint must be publicly accessible before the app is installed.
</Note>

## App configuration

The configuration endpoint defined in the above metadata needs to accept three different operations. In the following example `/configuration` is the endpoint defined in the `configurationUrl` metadata property.

**POST /configuration**

This endpoint will receive the "installation" request from Litium. This request contains the following payload:

```json theme={null}
{
    "clientSecret": "secret for the registered client",
    "clientId": "client identification"
}
```

The information in the payload needs to be stored with the application. The `clientId` and `clientSecret` should be used when creating the token for communication with Litium as well as validating incoming requests from Litium to the application.

**POST /configuration/files**

An admin user can upload configuration files to the app from the Litium back office. The configuration files are sent to this endpoint as a file upload request. The filename on the request will correspond to the `id` from the metadata configuration section `configFiles`.

The endpoint should respond with either `200 OK` if the configuration is accepted, or `400 BadRequest` with the following data if there is an error:

```json theme={null}
{
    "isError": true,
    "message": "Value for property X in the file has an unsupported value."
}
```

**GET /configuration/files/**

This endpoint should return the data of the corresponding configuration file, in raw format. The `{id}` will be the `id` from the metadata configuration section `configFiles`.

## Supported operations

The `SupportedOperations` metadata property lets Litium know which actions this app can perform. The possible values for the supported operations property is defined in the Connect APIs. See for example the supported operations of the [Connect Payments API](https://docs.litium.com/api-reference/api?product=Litium.Connect.Payments\&version=1.1\&xref=Payments.).

## Security

To secure the app, Litium will act as an OpenIdConnect provider, so after the initialization where the client information is provided we can start validating the authentication of the request with the regular OpenIdConnect protocol.

When the app has been installed, Litium will include an Authentication header with a bearer token that represents the Litium application The token contains the claim "[http://schemas.litium.com/identity/claims/application](http://schemas.litium.com/identity/claims/application)" that contains the value that previously was sent as `clientId` in the app installation.

## Uninstalling an app

The user can uninstall an installed app by clicking the Uninstall button on the app details page of the Litium backoffice. This will start the app uninstallation flow that looks like this:

<Frame>
  <img alt="Litium app uninstallation flow" />
</Frame>

Litium will call the configuration endpoint of the app with a null value for the service account. If the app responds to the request with something other than a 200 OK, Litium will throw an exception. If the app response with 200 OK, Litium deletes the app's service account and removes the app information from the database. The user can delete the app from the Apps page of the backoffice.

If the app has responded with an error on the request to the configuration endpoint, the user can select to force-delete the app. Litium will then delete the app's service account and remove the app from the database without sending a request to the configuration endpoint of the app.

If the app is forced delete, the file "LitiumApi.json" need to be removed also because it still contains connection information for Litium. The app can't be reinstalled until the "LitiumApi.json" file is removed.

<Warning>
  If the app is force-deleted, you must also manually remove the "LitiumApi.json" file. The app cannot be reinstalled until it is removed.
</Warning>

A Litium service account is used to secure the communication between the app and Litium. This info will help to ensure that the correct Litium instance is calling the app.

## Security

To secure the app, Litium will act as an OpenID Connect provider, so after the initialization where the client information is provided we can start validating the authentication of the request with the regular OpenID Connect protocol.

When the app has been installed, Litium will include an `Authorization` header with a bearer token that represents the Litium application. The token contains the claim `http://schemas.litium.com/identity/claims/application` that contains the value that previously was sent as `clientId` in the app installation.

## Uninstalling an app

The user can uninstall an installed app by clicking the **Uninstall** button on the app details page of the Litium back office. Litium will call the configuration endpoint of the app with a null value for the service account.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Litium app uninstallation flow diagram" />
</Frame>

If the app responds to the request with something other than a `200 OK`, Litium will throw an exception. If the app responds with `200 OK`, Litium deletes the app's service account and removes the app information from the database. The user can delete the app from the Apps page of the back office.

If the app has responded with an error on the request to the configuration endpoint, the user can select to force-delete the app. Litium will then delete the app's service account and remove the app from the database without sending a request to the configuration endpoint of the app.

If the app is force-deleted, the file *LitiumApi.json* needs to be removed also because it still contains connection information for Litium. The app can't be reinstalled until the *LitiumApi.json* file is removed.

<Warning>
  If the app is force-deleted, *LitiumApi.json* must also be removed manually. The app cannot be reinstalled until it is removed.
</Warning>


# Deployment in LCC
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/get-started/app-development-guide/deployment-in-lcc

When you have finished developing and testing your app in your development environment, you need to deploy it to Litium Commerce Cloud (LCC) to make it available to others. LCC currently only supports apps built on .NET.

To be able to deploy your app, you need to [contact Litium](mailto:support@litium.com) to obtain an AppName that will be used to identify your app. You should also provide us with the Litium developer account that should have access to upload your app to our NuGet.

## Upload your app to Litium

<Steps>
  <Step title="Install Octopus CLI">
    [Download Octopus CLI](https://octopus.com/downloads/octopuscli), if it is not already available. Install Octopus CLI as a .NET Core tool (this is only needed once per machine):

    ```bash theme={null}
    dotnet tool install --global Octopus.DotNet.Cli
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Publish the app and set a version number">
    ```bash theme={null}
    dotnet publish -c Release .\path\ProjectName.csproj -o publish -p:version=1.0.0
    ```

    <Warning>
      You cannot overwrite a previously published version. You must increase the version number for each new release.
    </Warning>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Create a NuGet package using octo-pack">
    ```bash theme={null}
    dotnet octo pack --basePath=publish --outFolder=builds --id=AppName --version="1.0.0"
    ```

    Replace `AppName` with the app name that you received from Litium.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Verify the app runs as an IIS website">
    Configuration should be run in the folder `..\AppConfig` relative to the path where the application is run. This is to be able to separate the application and user configuration. Please make sure to verify that this works before uploading the package to Litium NuGet.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Upload the package to Litium NuGet">
    Upload using the Litium account that was given upload access. The package can only be downloaded by the same user account that uploaded it, and Litium.

    ```bash theme={null}
    nuget push .\builds\AppName.1.0.0.nupkg -Source https://nuget.litium.com/nuget
    ```
  </Step>

  <Step title="Notify Litium">
    Notify Litium about the new version (including the version number) and we will start the process to make the app available to other users.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  Prereleases and test versions of your app need to be designated as `beta` in your version number. Example: `1.0.0-beta-01`.
</Note>


# Setup a development environment
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/get-started/app-development-guide/development-environment

To be able to develop a Litium app you need a number of things in your development environment.

You will need a Litium environment that your app can connect to. This can be an environment in Litium Commerce Cloud, or a local environment. Find out more about setting up a local environment in the [Get started section of the Platform documentation](/platform/get-started).

The requirements on your local development environment for a Litium app:

<Steps>
  <Step title="Docker Desktop">
    When deployed to LCC all Litium apps will be running in a Docker container. Install Docker Desktop to be able to run containers on your local machine.
  </Step>

  <Step title="DNS Resolver">
    When running Litium apps in containers the localhost domain will always point to the container itself and can't be used in the communication between the app and Litium. To solve the communication between the app and Litium, we will use a custom domain that resolves to the host of the container.

    For more information, please see the section on [shared dependencies](/platform/get-started/shared-dependencies) under Getting started for the platform.
  </Step>

  <Step title="A custom developer certificate">
    To be able to use custom domain names with .NET Core's inbuilt webserver Kestrel, you must generate your own certificate. More information can be found in the section on [custom developer certificate](/platform/get-started/custom-developer-certificate) under Getting started for the platform.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Litium NuGet">
    Litium provides a pre-built module to handle common tasks in the Litium app framework (like registering an app to the corresponding Litium instance) as a NuGet package. Information on how to access the Litium NuGet feed can be found on the [Litium packages](/platform/get-started/litium-packages) section under Getting started for the platform.
  </Step>
</Steps>

# Using the app management package
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/get-started/app-development-guide/using-the-app-management-package

Litium provides a pre-built package that handles the app management API functions that is required to install, configure and uninstall an app.

This package, Litium.AppManagement is distributed via Litium NuGet, to install Litium.AppManagement, we can find it in Litium Nuget source :

<Frame>
  <img alt="Litium.AppManagement NuGet package in the Litium NuGet source" />
</Frame>

Adding config files :

## AppSetting.json

The AppSetting.json contains various info on the app, including metata section which is used to provide the information about your app that Litium requires to be able to install your app in Litium. A sample file looks like this:

```json theme={null}
{
  "Logging": {
    "LogLevel": {
      "Default": "Information",
      "Microsoft": "Warning",
      "Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime": "Information"
    }
  },

  "ConnectionStrings": {
    // "Database": "" // Need to be commented out to avoid problem in production
  },

  "AllowedHosts": "*",

  "AppMetadata": {
    "Id": "SampleApp",
    "DisplayName": "Sample Litium app",
    "RequestedPermissions": [
      "Function/Connect/"
    ],
    "Subscribers": [
      {
        "Url": "/api/webhook/capturetransaction",
        "Event": "Litium.Connect.Payments.Events.CaptureTransaction"
      },
      {
        "Url": "/api/webhook/canceltransaction",
        "Event": "Litium.Connect.Payments.Events.CancelTransaction"
      },
      {
        "Url": "/api/webhook/refundtransaction",
        "Event": "Litium.Connect.Payments.Events.RefundTransaction"
      }
    ],
    "ConfigFiles": [
      {
        "Id": "AppConfiguration.json",
        "DisplayName": "Configuration file",
        "Description": "configuration for the Sample app."
      }
    ]
  },

  "SampleAppConfig": {
    "SampleAppShippingOptions": [
    ]
  }
}
```

Id: a machine readable id for your app. The id shoult not contain any spaces.

DisplayName: the human readable name of your app.

RequestedPermissions: an array of the Litium permissions that your app requires to function.

Subscribers: an array of Litium events that your app wants to subscribe to as part of the installation of the app. The Url property defines the endpoint in your app that Litium will call every time the event specified in the Event property is fired in Litium. All Litium events that you can subscribe to are available in the [API reference](https://docs.litium.com/api-reference/net-api).

ConfigFiles: an array of configuration files that your app supports. Each file defined here will generate a file upload field in the app detail page of the Litium backoffice where the user can upload the file to your app. The Id property defines the filename to be used and must be unique. The DisplayName property will be used as the label for the file upload field and the Description property will be displayed as a tooltip.

The SampleAppConfig section is the json schema definition for AppConfiguration.json file. In the example above the "SampleConfig" is the key to find the config section, and the SampleAppShippingOptions is a list of SampleAppShippingOption that we'll define in the actual config file. Please note that this only the structure for the config file and not the real section to define the config values.

Adding SampleApp Config File definition :

## SampleAppConfig.cs

```csharp theme={null}
namespace SampleApp.Configuration
{
    public class SampleAppConfig
    {
        public const string Key = "SampleAppConfig";
        public List<ShippingOption> SampleAppShippingOptions { get; set; }
    }
}
```

The Key "SampleAppConfig" here is the value of the root note of the config section defined in AppConfiguration.json. The list of SampleAppShippingOptions is also declared to have the base type of ConnectShipments.ShippingOption in the next line. The definition in this config file definition will help to deserialize the json config file into strong type and help to map the values into the correct C# model.

This is the sample of the AppConfiguration.json file to be uploaded to Litium back office :

```json theme={null}
{
  "SampleAppConfig": {
    "SampleAppShippingOptions": [
      {
        "Id": "standardPackage",
        "MerchantAccountId": "",
        "DeliveryCountries": null,
        "DeliveryTimeInDays": 0,
        "ShippingMethod": "NormalPost",
        "IntegrationType": "DeliveryCheckout",
        "FeeType": "Calculated",
        "AdditionalProperties": null
      },
      {
        "Id": "expressPackage",
        "MerchantAccountId": "",
        "DeliveryCountries": null,
        "DeliveryTimeInDays": 0,
        "ShippingMethod": "NormalPost",
        "IntegrationType": "DeliveryCheckout",
        "FeeType": "Calculated",
        "AdditionalProperties": null
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Hosting.json

The Hosting.json is used to provide information that your app needs about the hosting environment where the app is running. A sample file looks like this:

```json theme={null}
{
  "LitiumApi": {
    "ApiUrl": "https://litium.localtest.me/"
  },
  "AppMetadata": {
    "AppUrl": "https://my-sample-app.localtest.me/"
  }
}
```

LitiumApi: The ApiUrl property is the absolute URL to the Litium installation that the app should connect to.

AppMetadata: The AppUrl property is the absolute URL of the app itself.

In the app startup , we can add something like this :

```csharp theme={null}
public void ConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)
        {
            services.Configure<SampleAppConfig>(Configuration.GetSection(SampleAppConfig.Key));
        }
```

## Define Config\_Path environment variable

We need to define the evironmentVariable for Config path - it looks like this :

```xml theme={null}
<environmentVariable name="CONFIG_PATH" value="..\AppConfig" />
```

## LitiumApi.json

This file is created when the app is installed successfully to litium and will be removed during uninstall.

<Warning>
  In case the connection between litium is lost and the app is forced delete, the file "LitiumApi.json" need to be removed manually also. The app can't be reinstalled until the old "LitiumApi.json" file is removed.
</Warning>
