# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/litium-apps/rule/overview

The Rule app is used to integrate Litium with Rule marketing automation platform. Use your customer and order data from Litium to create personalised email and SMS communication, segment audiences, and automate messaging across the customer journey.

## Version dependencies

* **Rule app 1.0.0**
  * Requires Litium 8.27.0 or later

## Environments

The Rule app can be run in Litium Serverless Cloud, use the Cloud CLI to install it. The app requires a separate app agreement.

A [Docker Compose template](/add-ons/litium-apps/rule/docker-template) is available for local installation.

## App configuration file

The configuration file must have JSON format and UTF-8 encoding.

```json theme={null}
{
    "RuleAppConfig": {
        "ApiKey": "",
        "NewsletterOptInField": "",
        "RuleAppOptions": [
            {
                "ChannelId": "channel-1",
                "EnableRuleTracking": true,
                "ProductVariationProperty": "Color"
            },
            {
                "ChannelId": "channel-2",
                "EnableRuleTracking": true,
                "ProductVariationProperty": "Size"
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

* **ApiKey**: Rule API key for the customer (available in Rule portal).
* **NewsletterOptInField** (optional): Specifies a custom field name for if customer opted in. Needs to be a bool type placed in `Order.AdditionalInfo`. If not provided the app fallbacks to `"NewsletterOptIn"`.
* **RuleAppOptions**: Settings for Rule on channel level. Every channel where Rule should be enabled needs a separate object.
  * **ChannelId**: The Litium string Id for channel. This is not natively unique in Litium but make sure it is unique in your site.
  * **EnableRuleTracking**: Specify if data should be sent to Rule for the channel.
  * **ProductVariationProperty** (optional): The variant grouping field. Eg. Size, Color etc.

## Events sent to Rule

All Rule events are reliant on being able to identify a customer by email. No events can be sent to Rule if the Litium cart does not have an email set in `CustomerInfo`. Make sure the cart gets updated with this at log in or checkout for the app to work correctly.

## CartUpdated

Sent by Litium when a cart is updated with information (e.g. product added, removed, info added etc). Adds cart related fields data and CartInProgress tag in Rule. This can be used for handling abandoned carts.

<Note>
  Litium fires this event only for carts that has been persisted in the database. Carts are persisted when the cart has initialized a payment, normally when the customer goes to the checkout. You can create a checkout session by using the `createCheckoutSession` mutation in the Storefront API.
</Note>

## CheckoutUpdated

Custom event that needs to be implemented in the merchant's solution. Updates the cart entity in Rule with a `CheckoutUrl` pointing to the checkout page in the storefront.

The event needs to be named `Litium.Sales.Events.CheckoutUpdated` and provide the following data model:

```csharp theme={null}
public class CheckoutUpdatedItem
{
    public Litium.Sales.Cart Cart { get; set; }
    public string CheckoutUrl { get; set; }
}
```

## OrderConfirmed

Sent by Litium when cart is confirmed. Updates a subscriber with a new order entry with order data and OrderCompleted tag in Rule.

## Product url

To be able to send product URL:s to Rule, a custom filter condition needs to be added to the merchant's solution. Use the exact code provided below.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Data.Queryable.Conditions;
using Litium.Data.Queryable.ExpressionInfos;
using Litium.Data.Queryable.Internal;
using Litium.Data.Queryable;
using System;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.Conditions
{
    public class CategoryLinkedToBaseProductFilterCondition : FilterCondition
    {
        private Guid _value;

        /// <summary>
        /// Gets or sets the value.
        /// </summary>
        /// <value>The value.</value>
        public virtual Guid Value
        {
            get { return _value; }
            set
            {
                ThrowIfReadOnly();
                _value = value;
            }
        }
    }

    internal class CategoryLinkedToBaseProductQueryFilterCondition : QueryFilterCondition<CategoryLinkedToBaseProductFilterCondition>
    {
        private CategoryLinkedToBaseProductFilterCondition _filterCondition;

        protected override void InitCondition(CategoryLinkedToBaseProductFilterCondition filterCondition)
        {
            _filterCondition = filterCondition;
        }

        public override void ApplyFilter<T>(FilterDescriptor<T> filterDescriptor)
        {
            ((IFilterDescriptorExpression)filterDescriptor).AddExpression(new CategoryLinkedToBaseProductLinkQueryExpression
            {
                BaseProductSytemId = _filterCondition.Value,
            });
        }
    }
}
```

## OrderShipped

Sent by Litium when a DeliveryOrder is shipped. Updates a subscriber with a new orderupdate entry with shippingdata and OrderShipped tag in Rule.

## Historical order data

To start using Rule with existing data from Litium, the app provides a trigger for running a full historical order sync against Rule. The sync panel is available under Sales menu, under the Panels section – "Historical Sync". There you can run a job that syncs all orders to Rule and monitor the progress. The job can be paused and resumed as well as reset. However, it does not remove already synced data in Rule if reset so if you run orders already synced there will be duplicates in Rule.

# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/add-ons/litium-apps/svea-payment/overview

The Svea payment app integrates with Svea to handle payments in your e-commerce solution. It is developed and maintained by Litium.

The Svea payment app supports Svea Checkout. The app supports capture, cancel and refund transactions.

## Installation

* **Litium serverless cloud** — Use the [Cloud CLI](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-payment-and-delivery-apps) to install the app.
* **Litium legacy cloud** — Contact [support](mailto:support@litium.com) to install the app in your test and/or production environment.
* **Local environment** — A [Docker Compose template](/add-ons/litium-apps/svea-payment/docker-template) is available for local installation.

## Configuration file

The configuration file must have JSON format and UTF-8 encoding.

```json theme={null}
{
  "Svea": {
    "PaymentAccounts": [
      {
        "PaymentAccountId": "SE",
        "MerchantId": "123",
        "SharedSecret": "...",
        "Environment": "Test",
        "Country": "Sweden",
        "IsCompany": false,
        "UseValidation": false,
        "PaymentOptions": [
          "Checkout"
        ]
      },
      {
        "PaymentAccountId": "DK",
        "MerchantId": "123",
        "SharedSecret": "...",
        "Environment": "Test",
        "Country": "Denmark",
        "IsCompany": false,
        "UseValidation": false,
        "PaymentOptions": [
          "Checkout"
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

* **PaymentAccountId**: Identifier to select the account. Must be a unique string.

<Note>
  `PaymentAccountId` should not contain any spaces. If it contains spaces, it will cause the app to crash when trying to find the correct payment account for the cart's `PaymentOptionId`. The reason for this is that Litium sends it as `"<PaymentAccountId> Checkout"` and the app splits into spaces to retrieve the id. More than one space causes it to split incorrectly.
</Note>

* **MerchantId**: Svea UserName, this is Svea merchant id followed by a string. This value is assigned by Svea.
* **SharedSecret**: Svea Password, this value is assigned by Svea.
* **Environment**: Svea environment. It should be `"Test"` or `"Live"`.
* **IsCompany**: The flag indicates if the account is company or not.
* **Country**: The country of Svea account.
* **UseValidation**: The flag indicates if the account is using validation or not.
* **PaymentOptions**: It must be `"Checkout"`.

## Apple pay

The Svea payment app version 1.9.0 and later supports Apple Pay. To enable Apple Pay, please follow [the guide in Svea's documentation](https://docs.payments.svea.com/docs/preview/apple-pay/getting-started/).

<Note>
  As part of the setup, you will need to verify the domain that is used to serve the storefront. More information on how the domain verification file can be added to the merchant's storefront is available in the guide [How to serve Apple Pay domain verification file](/platform/guides/how-to-serve-apple-pay-domain-verification-file).
</Note>

## Finnish consumer customers

Due to legislation in Finland that prohibits credit providers to share customer details of private individuals that are the result of a lookup in a registry, the billing address might be null for some Litium orders.

## Refund transactions

For some payments methods, e.g. Trustly, there is a limitation that only one refund transaction per payment can be processing at the same time. If you try to create another SRO before the refund transaction has been finalized for the first one, an error will be thrown.

## Callbacks

Svea requires callbacks to be resolved from outside one's own network. Therefore, when running the Svea Payment app locally, you will not be able to complete an order. Please see [Svea documentation here](https://paymentsdocs.svea.com/docs/getting-started/callback).

# Architecture
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/architecture

This section describes the architecture of Litium connect.

## Deployment model

Applications developed to integrate Litium to other external systems have their own life cycle. This means they are independent applications from Litium. These applications communicates with Litium using the API contracts defined in the Litium Connect business domain web APIs.

For example, Litium Connect ERP domain specifies the contracts that are defined in Litium.Connect.Abstractions package that would be deployed together with Litium.

Litium Connect Erp integration application will have its own runtime life cycle and need be a separate application. 

The following image shows how the deployment model for a connector integration application towards Microsoft Dynamics Nav ERP would look like.

<img alt="deployment model erp.png" />

## Component model

* The contracts common to all Litium connect business domains are defined in Litium.Connect.Abstractions package.
* Litium contracts are defined in the Litium.Abstractions package.

<img alt="component model.png" />

Litium connect integration applications should talk to Litium through web APIs. These WebAPI are using the Litium.Connect.Abstractions domain model for the data that is being served through them.

The integration applications are dependent on the WebAPI specification, and not in the Litium application. It is also not dependent on the Litium domain model defined in Litium.Abstractions package.

## Application discovery and registration

The Litium server instance knows about the Litium apps by a registration process as explained below.

The integration applications should register themselves with the intended Litium instance. While registering, they should make it known to Litium, which functionality it is providing, by way of registering to listen to pre-defined webhook events.

Registration is using the [Litium Webhook](/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/architecture/events-handling/webhooks) framework.

For example, one such event, in the ERP domain is OrderConfirmed event. See [API documentation](https://docs.litium.com/api-reference/api?product=Litium\&version=7.4\&xref=Litium.Connect.Erp.Events) for complete list.

### Example

Following is an abstract example to explain how an integration application interacts with Litium. The method names and entities are only for illustration purposes.

In the following sequence diagram, "Dynamics365 App", the integration application registers to listen on the OrderConfirmed event. When an order is confirmed the Litium Connect ERP notify the application of it. The application then decides to respond to the event by exporting the order to Dynamics 365 ERP.

<img alt="app registration sequence.png" />


# Custom endpoint for order return - Litium 8
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/develop-integration-applications/custom-endpoint-litium-8



This is the sample on how to add a custom endpoint to return orders.

1. Download SampleOrderController [here](/storage/ma/b5aa65b87d344a619d54da21a802cc54/742004b01029461ba2cd26c68f08cc48/zip/1E743E356E226A69053798FDD948DEBCE9C57D53/SampleOrdersController.zip "SampleOrdersController.zip") . 
2. Put it in Controllers/Api folder of Litium 8 Accelerator.

<img alt="CustomConnectApi.PNG" />

The sample code will return all orders within the last 24hrs using order API.

```csharp theme={null}
/// <summary>
/// Gets all orders within the last 24hrs.
/// </summary>
[HttpGet]
[Route("Order_Get24hrs")]
public IActionResult Get24Hrs()
{
    if (!ModelState.IsValid)
    {
        return BadRequest();
    }

    using var query = _dataService.CreateQuery<Sales.Order>().Filter(f =>
        {
            f.InDateRange(DateTime.Now.AddDays(-1), null);
        }
    );
    var orderSystemIds = query.ToSystemIdList();
    var result = _orderService.Get<SalesOrder>(orderSystemIds);
    return Ok(result);
}
```

```text theme={null}
https://<Your litium domain name>/Litium/Swagger
```

# Cancel unfulfilled part of a order
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/cancel-unfulfilled-part-of-a-order

This section describes how and when an order can be cancelled.

Orders can be cancelled in full or the remaining part of the partially fulfilled order can be cancelled. 

1. There can be only one cancellation per order. This is reflected in a cancellation shipment created during order finalization (See below).
2. The payment for the cancellation is processed last. Litium will call the payment app to either refund the money or cancel the remaining authorization.

### To cancel unfulfilled part of a order

When the ERP system has finished the order fullfilment process; that is when no more items would be shipped as part of the order, call the following endpoint to finalize the order.

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/action/finalize
```

Litium will create a cancellation shipment, and proceed to cancel or refund the payment due for that shipment.

This cancellation shipment will only contain items that are not yet part of another shipment. That is, if part of the order is already fulfilled, only the items that are not shipped are cancelled.


# Checkout flow
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/checkout-flow

## Business process model

Following is the business process model of the checkout flow.

<img alt="Checkout flow diagram.png" />

### Export order to ERP

Litium Connect ERP API provides webhook events that the Litium Connect Applications can implement to [export the order to the ERP system](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/export-order-to-erp).


# Export order to ERP
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/export-order-to-erp

When an order is ready for processing, it should be exported to the ERP for further processing. This section explains how.

Litium Connect ERP API provides webhook events that the Litium Connect applications can implement.

* OrderReadyForProcessing: when an order is ready for processing, subscribe to this webhook 

* Litium.Connect.Erp.Events.OrderReadyForProcessing is the webhook event raised, that the ERP app should listen to.

<img alt="Seq Order export to ERP with OrderReadyForProcessing.jpg" />After exporting the order to the ERP system, the ERP app should notify Litium that the order is exported to the ERP by calling the following endpoint.

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/notify/exported
```

When Litium receives this call, the order will be set to "Processing" state.

## Litium Connect ERP API 2.2 and earlier

The OrderReadyForProcessing event was added to Litium Connect ERP API 2.3 when the [PendingProcessing order state](/platform/areas/sales/state-transitions) was introduced in Litium 8.20. In earlier versions of Connect ERP API, the OrderConfirmed event can be used for the same purpose.


# Order fulfilment process - Main flow
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/order-fulfilment-process-main-flow

A common order fulfillment flow is for ERP system to pack the items for an order, hand it over to the delivery company, and then capture the money for it. This section describes this main flow.

### Fulfilling an order

When the ERP system has handed over a delivery package to the shipping provider company, call the following endpoint first to register the shipment and capture money for it.

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/shipment
```

When a shipment is created, the following steps are taken in Litium.

1. Create the appropriate delivery with delivery rows (if a partial shipment Litium automatically calculates the shipment value)
2. Litium captures the amount due from the customer. (If the funds are already reserved).\
   Litium Connect is managing the payment capture. The code should be as follows when going to the Delivered state, and should not have any payment captures.

```csharp theme={null}
var delivered = new State<DeliveryCarrier>((short)DeliveryState.Delivered,
DeliveryState.Delivered.ToString(),
(deliveryCarrier, currentState, token) =>
{​​
//_orderUtilities.CompletePayments(ModuleECommerce.Instance.Orders[deliveryCarrier.OrderID, token], token);
}​​,
null);
```

In this flow, the ERP system is not waiting to know whether the capture has succeeded or not. Therefore, after the above call to create the shipment, call the following endpoint, to notify Litium that the order is handed over to the delivery company.

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/notify/delivered
```

Litium will set the delivery status to "Delivered" when the above end-point is called.


# Order fullfilment process - Alternative flow
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/order-fullfilment-process-alternative-flow

An alternative order fulfillment flow is for ERP system to pack the items for an order, and capture the money for the delivery, and then hand it over to the delivery company. This section describes this alternative flow.

This is different from the [Order fulfillment process main flow](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/order-fulfilment-process-main-flow), where ERP system will hand over the delivery package to the delivery company before it knows the payment capture has succeeded.

# Fulfilling an order

When the ERP system has created the delivery package, but before handing it over to the shipping provider company, call the following endpoint first to register the shipment and capture money for it.

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/shipment
```

When a shipment is created, the following steps are taken in Litium.

1. Create the appropriate delivery with delivery rows (if a partial shipment Litium automatically calculates the shipment value)
2. Litium captures the amount due from the customer. (If the funds are already reserved).\
   Litium Connect is managing the payment capture.

There are two alternative ways to proceed now.

1. Attach to the Litium.Connect.Erp.Events.ReadyToShip webhook from your ERP implementation.
2. Listen to the ReadyToShip event in Litium .net api

## Alternative 1: Attach to ReadyToShip webhook

Listen to:

```csharp theme={null}
Litium.Connect.Erp.Events.ReadyToShip
```

This event means, the delivery is ready to ship.

This webhook means the delivery is ready to ship now, and when this event is received, notify the ERP system to hand over the package to the delivery company.

When the package is handed over to the delivery company, call the following endpoint to notify Litium.

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/notify/delivered
```

Litium will set the delivery status to "Delivered" when the above end-point is called.

### Webhooks on payment capture and failures

You may listen additionally to the following endpoints and take appropriate action on payment failures or successful capture.

```csharp theme={null}
Litium.Connect.Erp.Events.PaymentCaptured
Litium.Connect.Erp.Events.PaymentCaptureFailed
```

## Alternative 2: Listen to ReadyToShip .net event

Instead of listening to the webhook, you may listen to the ReadyToShip .net event. Following is a sample code.

This code need to be part of your Litium Accelerator source.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Connect.Erp;
using Litium.Events;
using Litium.Runtime;
using Litium.Sales;
using Litium.Sales.Events;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.SampleCode
{
    [Autostart]
    public class SetShipmentToShipped : IAsyncAutostart
    {
        private readonly IApplicationLifetime _applicationLifetime;
        private readonly EventBroker _eventBroker;
        private readonly Sales.OrderService _orderService;
        private readonly OrderFulfilmentService _orderFulfilmentService;

        public SetShipmentToShipped(Sales.OrderService orderService, OrderFulfilmentService orderFulfilmentService, EventBroker eventBroker, IApplicationLifetime applicationLifetime)
        {
            _eventBroker = eventBroker;
            _applicationLifetime = applicationLifetime;
            _orderService = orderService;
            _orderFulfilmentService = orderFulfilmentService;
        }

        public ValueTask StartAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            var subscription = _eventBroker.Subscribe<ReadyToShip>(async args =>
            {
                var shipment = args.Item;
                if(shipment?.Id !=  null)
                { 
                    var order = _orderService.Get<SalesOrder>(shipment.OrderSystemId);
                    if(order != null)
                    {
                        //Raise the onShipped event.
                        await _orderFulfilmentService.OnShipped(order.Id, shipment.Id);
                    }               
                }
            });

            _applicationLifetime.ApplicationStopping.Register(() =>
            {
                // Application is about to shutdown, unregister the event listener
                subscription.Dispose();
            });
            return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
        }
    }
}
```

# Finalize order

When the ERP is done with the order fullfilment process, call the following endpoint to finalize the order at Litium. 

```
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/action/finalize
```

* If the order is a partially fullfilled order, that is, if all the items in the order is not part of an a shipment yet, those items will be put to a cancellation shipment, and Litium will proceed to refund or cancel authorization for it. See more on "[Cancel unfullfilled part of an order](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/cancel-unfulfilled-part-of-a-order)"
* Litium will notify the payment apps that the order is finalized. Certain payment apps, when this message is received will mark the payment rows as "Shipped".


# Order return management process
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/order-return-management-process

Litium Connect ERP APIs supports order returns and refunding the money for those returns, including partial returns and refunding part of the money back to end customer. This section walks through a complete process of processing an order return.

For Litium 7.4 and later, see the [Sales return management](/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/litium-documentation/sales/return-management_1_1) for more information on Sales Return Management process. 

### Swagger documentation

The web api endpoints in the following sections can be reached by:

`https://<your domain>/Litium/Swagger?urls.primaryName=Litium%20Connect%20Erp%20version%202.0`

## Registering an order return

The order return may be initiated by the customer. Usually it can be by contacting the customer support or going the website to fill a special form.

When an order return is initiated (or warehousing system), notify Litium to create a RMA by sending a POST request to

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/rmas
```

Litium stores the return slips and uses them to create the RMAs.

RMA is the primary document to approve an order return.

## Approving the RMA

The created RMA above, can be set to the following states successively:

When the actual physical package is received by the warehouse, call the following:

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/rmas/{systemId}/notify/packageReceived
```

When the package is inspected change the state to Processing by:

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/rmas/{systemId}/notify/processing
```

Then approve the package by calling:

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/rmas/{systemId}/action/approve
```

At this point, the return is accepted, and the RMA approval process is completed. Litium will automatically create the sales return order

## Refunding the money

Refunding the money to the customer is done through the sales return order. This sales return order is automatically created during the process of RMA approval. The refund amount is automatically calculated by Litium.

Confirm the sales return order, so that the customer will be notified that their return is accepted:

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/salesReturnOrders/{orderId}/action/confirmReturn
```

Then refund the money by using:

```text theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/erp/salesReturnOrders/{orderId}/action/refund
```

# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/overview

This section describes the business processes facilitated by Litium Connect ERP APIs.

There are three main business processes facilitated by Litium Connect ERP APIs

1. Checkout Flow: Exporting the orders into ERP systems
2. Order fulfilment: Facilitating ERP order delivery process, even partial deliveries and partial capture of funds.
3. Order return management: Facilitating return management process, return merchandise authorization (RMA), creating sales return orders and refund of funds. Partial returns with refund of corresponding fund amounts are supported.

See following sections for more details.


# Orders
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/domain-models/orders

Domain model of ERP connect API order contracts

## ERP hub Order Entity Model

Following UML diagram shows the order entity model in the Litium Connect ERP Hub. For clarity and simplicity, it is simplified and not all attributes and relationships are shown. Click here to view the [full-size diagram](/images/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/domain-models/orders/Order-Entity-Model.jpg "Sales module.jpg").

<img alt="Order Entity Model.jpg" />

There are several key differences between Litium 7.x Ecommerce entity model and the above entities, which are described below.

## Order Entity

1. Order entity represents a sales order (SO) or a sales return order (SRO) from Litium. Whether it’s a SO or a SRO is defined by the Order::OrderType property.
2. In case of a SRO, then the Order::OriginalSalesOrderId property refer to the SO for which the current SRO is originating from. The Order:RmaIds contains the list of RMA ids that are associated with this SRO.
3. In case of a SO, and if there exists SROs for this order, their ids are listed in the Order::SalesReturnOrderIds list. The Order:RmaIds contains the list of all RMA ids that are associated with this SO.
4. Order::AdditionalInfo can be used to store any project specific data.
5. Order::BillingAddress contains the billing address.

### Order::VatSummary

If the order contains products that belongs to different VAT bands, a summary of total order amount by VAT band is presented in the VatSummary property.

For example, given an order that contains following info:

<img alt="VatInfoRow.jpg" />

The VatSummary property would contain the following, where key is Vat Rate and value is Total Vat amount.

<img alt="VatRows.jpg" />

## Shipping Info

At the time of placing an order, the end-customer is only selecting a shipping method, and a shipping address.

Other integrations to transport administration systems may generate reference ids to those systems. When the Transport Administration hub is made, those information may be presented in a separate entity, or may be incorporated into the ShippingInfo entity. In the first implementation of the Erp Hub, these information will be available through the ShippingInfo::AdditionalInfo property.

## CustomerInfo

Entity containing information about the end-customer. Since the order contains both the billing address as well as the delivery address, this CustomerInfo object does not refer directly to an address.

## OrderRow

All the financial information of the order is represented by the OrderRow instances associated with the order. These include products bought, fees and shipping costs as well as discounts, promotions and a rounding off adjustment (if there is any). The type of the order row is represented by the OrderRow::Type, which has enumeration values such as Product, Promotion, ShippingCost, Fee, etc.

Sum of financial properties of the set of order row objects gives the total order value for that property. For example, sum of all OrderRow:TotalVat gives the total order VAT amount i.e. Order:TotalVat, and sum of all OrderRow::TotalIncludingVat will be equal to the order grand total, i.e. Order:GrandTotal.

### Promotions in Order Rows

Promotions (campaign discounts) applied to an order may result in one or more separate order rows, as demonstrated in following example.

Example: Product A has a buy 3 pay for 2 promotion. Product B has a 10% discount promotion. A order with 3 of product A and 1 of product B, would result in following order rows.

<img alt="PromotionsOrderLines.jpg" />

The PromotionInfo objects should be used to associate an order row to its promotion order row. For example, OrderLine\_1 is associated with OrderLine\_3 through the PromotionInfo entity which has the Id 3\_for\_2.

This way, a given order line may result in multiple promotion lines, within the same order. It is possible to give a 10% discount, as well as a 20% discount to the same order line. (A limitation in Litium 7 api does not allow creation of such orders as at now though)

## Payment

Payment is at the same level as the order entity in Litium Connect.

This means, a given payment can be associated with several orders. The typical use case is, when there are sales returns. The SRO will be associated with the same Payment as the SO from which the products are returned.

All payment providers in the market are working on lowest monetary unit level. Therefore the payment objects has the financial properties (e.g. Transaction::TotalIncludingVat) are represented in integers in lowest monetary unit, i.e. cents. E.g. a 100 SEK value, in the payment objects would be represented as 10000 cents. This way, the ambiguity of decimal rounding off is eliminated.

### Transaction

A given payment may have several transactions. A typical SO has following transactions.

* Authorization: When the money is reserved in end-customers credit card. Typically this is made at the checkout phase.
* Capture: When money is taken from end-customers account, typically just before order is shipped.

If there are refunds and cancellations, corresponding refund and cancellation transaction entity instances would be recorded into the transaction object.

### TransactionRow

A transaction may consist of several TransactionRows. A TransactionRow is the counter part of the OrderLine, that would be sent to a payment provider. Each TransactionRow corresponds therefore to exactly a single OrderLine.

A given OrderLine may however be part of several transactions. For example, the authorization transaction and capture transaction refer to the same order line.

## Shipments and ShippingInfo

When an order is first placed, the information such as delivery address, information from delivery checkout are contained in the ShippingInfo entity. When the merchants order fulfilment systems process the order and create shipments to be delivered to the buyer, those information is represented by Shipment entity.

In other words, ShippingInfo contains information as collected during the checkout process and is furnished by the buyer (and delivery checkout). In contrast to, Shipments are created during the order fulfilment process, and is furnished by the ERP and Warehouse management and logistics systems.

# How to use
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/erp-app-sdk/how-to-use

How to develop the ERP client project created from  Litium Erp Connector Template.

## Before you start

[Install the template package](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/erp-app-sdk/install-litium-connect-erp-template) before you start.

## Package structure

The host template project is based on `Litium.AppManagement.Application` package to simplify application management and its communication with Litium instance.

Included packages:

### Litium.Connect.Erp.Client

This package provides access to Litium Connect ERP Import API via easy to use and extensible [ASP.NET](http://asp.net/)  Core components.

### Litium.Connect.Erp.ImportJobs

This is very simple yet powerful package that enables scheduling for import jobs using constant time interval or cron expression.

### Litium.Connect.Erp.Store.SqlServer

Provides persistence layer for `Litium.Connect.Erp.ImportClient` using SQL Server database.

## Configuration

After creating a project from the package template, there are some configuration need to be filled before the project can start.

*  Appsettings.json

```json theme={null}
{
  "AppMetadata": {
    "Id": "litium.erp.example",
    "DisplayName": "litium.erp.example",
    "RequestedPermissions": [
      "Function/Products/UI",
      "Function/Products/Content",
      "Function/Products/Settings"
    ],
    "Subscribers": [
      {
        "Url": "/api/webhook/OrderComplete",
        "Event": "Litium.Connect.Erp.Events.OrderConfirmed"
      }
    ],
    "ConfigFiles": [
      {
        "Id": "extendConfig.json",
        "DisplayName": "Extend Config",
        "Description": "This file can be uploaded from Litium Back-office."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

-  RequestedPermissions: contains the list of permision which the App needs.

-  Subscribers: contains the list of event the App wants to subscribe to

-  ConfigFiles: path to the config file, can be uploaded from Litium Back-office.\
 

* In the appsettings.development.json and appsettings.production.json, configure url:s for Litium Api and Erp connector,  together with a database connection string for the batch storage:

```json theme={null}
{
  "ConnectionStrings": {
    ".":  "Database for import batch storage"
    // "ImportBatchStoreDatabase": ""
  },

  "LitiumApi": {
    ".": "Litium installation that we should connect to",
    "ApiUrl": "https://litium.localtest.me:5001/"
  },
  
  "AppMetadata": {
    ".": "Url for this application",
    "AppUrl": "https://erp-app.localtest.me:6001/"
  }
}
```

* Install the App 
  * At the first time running the project, the system will redirect to Litium Back-office to install the App. Click Install button to install.

 <img alt="erp-connector-setup1.jpg" />​

<img alt="erp-connector-setup2.jpg" />

## Subscribe to events via Webhook and import order

* **​**The default ERP connector contains example code to subscribe to events and to schedule products import jobs.\
   

***WebhookController.cs***

```csharp theme={null}
using System.Text.Json;
using Litium.AppManagement;
using Litium.AppManagement.Infrastructure;
using Litium.Connect.Erp.Events;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace litium.erp.example.Controllers;

/// <summary>
///     Sample controller for Litium ERP API webhooks.
/// </summary>
[Route("api/webhook")]
[ApiController]
[Authorize(Policy = LitiumApiConstants.LitiumSystemPolicy)]
public class WebhookController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly ILogger _logger;

    /// <summary>
    ///     Initializes a new instance of the <see cref="WebhookController"/> class.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="logger">
    ///     Diagnostic message logger.
    /// </param>
    /// <exception cref="ArgumentNullException">
    ///     <paramref name="logger"/> is <see langword="null"/>.
    /// </exception>
    public WebhookController(ILogger<WebhookController> logger)
    {
        _logger = logger ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(logger));
    }

    /// <summary>
    ///     Gets called on registered webhook call for OrderCompleted event.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="response">
    ///     Webhook response content.
    /// </param>
    /// <returns>
    ///     <see cref="OkResult"/> instance.
    /// </returns>
    [HttpPost("OrderComplete")]
    public ActionResult OrderComplete([FromBody] Notification<OrderConfirmed> response)
    {
        _logger.LogTrace($"Received notification:{Environment.NewLine}{JsonSerializer.Serialize(response)}");
        return Ok();
    }
}
```

***SampleImportBatchProvider.cs***

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Connect.Erp;
using Litium.Connect.Erp.Api;

namespace litium.erp.example.ImportJobs;

/// <summary>
///     Sample implementation of <see cref="ImportBatch"/> provider used by the scheduled import job.
/// </summary>
public class SampleImportBatchProvider : IImportBatchProvider
{
    /// <inheritdoc/>
    public Task<ImportBatchEntity?> GetImportBatchAsync()
    {
        var batch = new ImportBatch()
        {
            ImportBehavior = ImportBatchImportBehavior.StopOnAnyError,
            Products = new List<Product>()
                {
                    new Product()
                    {
                        ArticleNumber = "Test001",
                        FieldTemplateId = "ProductWithOneVariant",
                    },
                },
            ProductSettings = new ProductImportSettings()
            {
                FieldTemplateId = "ProductWithOneVariant",
            },
        };

        return Task.FromResult<ImportBatchEntity?>(new ImportBatchEntity(batch));
    }
}
```

# Litium Serverless Cloud

To run the app based on the ERP SDK a manifest that contains file storage, mssql database and the dotnet web app need to be created and configured correct. If the app missing some of the configuratuions that app will not function correctly and is usual visible after an new deployment or restart of the app where missing credentials that causing the app to not start correctly.

Example manifest below with all parts already configured, remember to update references between the app if your app id isn't the same.

```text theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: app-storage
spec:
  type: file-storage
  version: 1.0.0
  # properties:
  #   # Storage artifact used for restore when storage is created.
  #   - name: backup_file
  #     value: artifacts/12345678901234567890123456789012

---

kind: app
resource:
  id: app-db
spec:
  type: mssql-database
  version: 1.0.0
  # properties:
  #   # Sql backup artifact used when creating database.
  #   - name: backup_file
  #     value: artifacts/12345678901234567890123456789012

---

kind: app
resource:
  id: app-id
spec:
  plan: s1
  type: dotnet-web
  version: 1.0.0
  configurations:
    - name: app_config
      type: storage
      subPath: config
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: app-storage
          key: storage_volume
    - name: connectionstrings__importbatchstoredatabase
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: app-db
          key: connection_string
    - name: LitiumApi__ApiUrl
      valueFrom:
        resourceRef:
          name: domain-name
          key: public_domain
        transformation:
          regex: (.+)
          replacement: https://$1
    - name: AppMetadata__AppUrl
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: litium
          key: public_domain_name
        transformation:
          regex: (.+)
          replacement: https://$1
    - name: CONFIG_PATH
      value: /app_storage/app_config
  properties:
    - name: artifact
      value: artifacts/<artifact id>
```


# Install
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/erp-app-sdk/install-litium-connect-erp-template

Installation instructions for Litium ERP connector template.

### Before you start

Before installing the Litium Connect ERP template you need to set up the [Litium NuGet feed](/platform/get-started/litium-packages).

Use a [version control system](/accelerators/mvc-accelerator/upgrade-and-maintenance) for easy upgrades of the Litium Connect ERP template.

### Install the template package

The Litium Connect ERP template package is a pre-created package\_.\_ 

Installation of the template package is only needed the first time the version is created. 

Only one version of the template package can exist at the same time.

1. Open Powershell command prompt
2. Install the template pack with

   ```text theme={null}
   dotnet new --install "Litium.Connect.Erp.Templates"
   ```

   After the template is installed, a list of available templates is shown.\
   *Note: To update the template to a later version, you should run the installation command again.*

   If you want to install a specific version of the template, you need to append the version number to the template name separated by two colons (::). For example, a template for the 1.0 version for Erp Contract version 2.1:

   ```text theme={null}
   dotnet new --install "Litium.Connect.Erp.Templates::2.1.100"
   ```

## Create a project with Litium Connect ERP template

1. Open the Powershell command prompt in the folder where the project should be created.
2. Create a project based on the Litium Connect Erp template with the following ​command.
   ```text theme={null}
   dotnet new literpapp [-n Customer.ErpVendor.App]
   ```
   *Note: Use '-n' options to set a custom name for the project.*

The project is created based on the Litium Connect ERP template. Open the project in your IDE and start develop your connector.

See [.Net configuration](http://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/configuration/), where you should put common non secret settings for the project (appSettings.json, appSettings.Development.json, and appSettings.Production.json),  [user-secrets should be used for development configuration and local secrets](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/security/app-secrets?view=aspnetcore-5.0\&tabs=windows).


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/erp-app-sdk/overview

The Litium ERP App SDK provides a boilerplate to develop applications that integrate a ERP system to Litium using the functionality in the Litium Connect ERP API.

The SDK is delivered as a .NET template.

The SDK contains the following features:

* Pre-built functions to build reliable imports of all the data entities supported by the Connect ERP API.
* Support for persisting import reports to a SQL Server database
* Running imports as scheduled jobs
* Communication layer between ERP system and Litium for the checkout, order fulfillment and returns business processes


# Events
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/events



### OrderReadyForProcessing event

OrderReadyForProcessing event will be published when an order has reached the Pending Processing state.

### OrderProcessing event

OrderProcessing event will be published when an order has reached the Processing state.

### OrderCompleted event

OrderCompleted event will be published when an order has reached the Completed state.

### PendingPaymentSucceded event

PendingPaymentSucceded event will be published when a payment authorization changes result from Pending to Success. Some payment methods may have a delay before the final result of the payment arrives, and until then the Pending result will be used on the authorization. When this happens, the payment is guaranteed by the payment provider.

### PendingPaymentFailed event

PendingPaymentFailed event will be published when a payment authorization changes result from Pending to Failed or Denied. Some payment methods may have a delay before the final result of the payment arrives and until then the Pending result will be used on the authorization. When the payment result is Failed or Denied, the payment is not approved and the order should not be fulfilled even if the order is confirmed.

### PaymentRefunded event

PaymentRefunded event will be published when a payment transaction of type refund changes result to Success.

### PaymentRefundFailed event

PaymentRefundFailed event will be published when a payment transaction of type refund changes result to Failed or Denied.

### PaymentCancelled event

PaymentCancelled event will be published when a payment transaction of type cancel changes result to Success.

### PaymentCancelFailed event

PaymentCancelFailed event will be published when a payment transaction of type cancel changes result to Failed or Denied.

### Processing event

The processing event will be published when a shipment has reached the Processing state.

### ReadyToShip event

The ReadyToShip event will be published when a shipment has reached the ReadyToShip state.

### Shipped event

The Shipped event will be published when a shipment has reached the Shipped state.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/imports-to-litium/overview

Litium Connect ERP APIs supports importing Products, Customers and organizations, Prices including customer specific prices and Stock balances to Litium.

Make a Process overview.

1. Connect app registers for ImportFinished webhook
2. Connect app sends import request
3. Connect API sends import to Litium
4. Litium does the import
5. Connect notifies that the import is done via webhook
6. Connect app gets Import-report

<img alt="Import Flow2.PNG" />


# Processing import requests
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/imports-to-litium/processing-import-requests



Imports from the ERP system is done by sending json data to the connect API endpoint. Litium imports the data in batches. It will raise import completed event through a webhook to notify the connect application when the import is finished. Connect will  provide a report with detailed information about what has been imported.

## End point for data import

Action: POST

\{host}/litium/api/connect/erp/imports?api-version=2.0

Returns *ImportReportId*.

## Import Completed event

Web hook for registering *ImportCompleted* event.

Will be sent out when the import is finished:

```csharp theme={null}
[
  {
    "name": "Litium.Connect.Erp.Events.ImportCompleted",
    "description": "Represents an event when a import is completed."
  }
]
```

*\*Full import report will be included in the event argument.*\
 

## How to fetch Import report

Action: Get

End point: \{host}/litium/api/connect/erp/imports/\{importreportid}?api-version=1.1

Overview of data import report:

<img alt="ImportReportModel.PNG" />

**Note!** You must set up all possible values in Litium before doing the import. This applies to:

* Decimal option
* INT option 
* Text option

If one entity with the same Id occurs more than once in the same import, Lithium will import the last value, without throwing an error.

# Update Tracking Informations For Shipment
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/update-tracking-informations-for-shipment

The Litium Connect provides a new API end-point to update tracking  for shipment.

In Litium Connect, There is an API endpoint /Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/\{orderId}/shipments/\{shipmentId}/tracking which is using HTTP PUT method with two parameters. The function requires **orderId** and **shipmentId** parameters from returning of Litium before.

The function has a request body with six parameters.

* **deliveryCarrierId** represents a dellivery carrier id from delivery provider for shipping a package. eg. posten/DHL, etc.
* **trackingReference** represents a tracking reference url to buyers/sellers and support buyers/sellers trace their a package status while it is delivering.
* **trackingUrl r**epresents a tracking url to buyers and support buyers/sellers trace their a package status while it is delivering.
* **returnSlipDeliveryCarrierId** represents a dellivery carrier id from delivery provider for returning a package. eg. posten/DHL, etc.
* **returnSlipTrackingReference** represents a returning tracking reference url to buyers/sellers and support buyers/sellers trace their a package status while it is returning.
* **returnSlipUrl** represents a returning tracking url to buyers/sellers and support buyers/sellers trace their a package status while it is returning.

There are two references here trackingReference and trackingUrl. Some carriers have a common url, to go there and provide a reference in their website. Others have it as part of the url.

There are two references here returnTrackingReference and returnUrl. Some carriers have a common url, to go there and provide a reference in their website. Others have it as part of the url.

When the function executed and will response a updated shipment with six parameters above if it is succeed.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/overview

Litium connect APIs are categorized by business domain area. This section describes the the different domains.



# Checkout
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/checkout

When the buyer makes a checkout in the website, the payment app should contact payment service provider (PSP) to facilitate to handle the funds related to the order.

## Payment session initialization

A payment session with the PSP should be initialized, when Litium requests to do so. This is usually when the buyer enters the checkout page of the ecommerce website.

The payment app should provide the following endpoint, for Litium to initialize the payment session.

```text theme={null}
/api/payments/{paymentSystemId}/initialize
```

The endpoint should accept a *Litium.Connect.Payments.Communications.ConnectPayments.Payment*  that Litium will pass with information to initialize the payment with PSP.

### Urls to PSP

* When the buyer completes the payment, the resulting call from PSP should be received at payment app, and then notified to Litium. Therefore, the payment app should provide the URLs of the payment app to receive these calls.
* The PSP should communicate with the payment app for background calls. Therefore, the urls sent to the PSP should be the URLs of the payment app. 

### PaymentFlowResult

Result of this call returned back to Litium is a *Litium.Connect.Payments.Communications.ConnectPayments.PaymentFlowResult* that contains information to Litium on how to display the payment options to the buyer in the checkout page.

* This should contain an html snippet if the payment integration method is a iframed solution, or a redirect url to PSP if the payment integration method is hosted payment pages.
* *PaymentFlowResult.Payment* entity contains the information about the payment. The *Payment.SupportedActions* should contain operations supported by the payment app.

## Checkout

* Litium uses the PaymentFlowResult to either show the iframe snippet in checkout page, or redirect the browser to the PSP site (in case of hosted integration type)
* The buyer is confirming the payment either in a iframe snippet or a hosted payment page, that is rendered by the PSP. This means, Litium does not collect or pass-through any sensitive payment card data.
* After payment confirmation, the resulting redirect should be received by the payment app., and notify Litium that the payment is confirmed.

### Payment confirmation

To notify Litium of the payment confirmation, the app should call the following endpoint:

```csharp theme={null}
/Litium/api/connect/payments/{paymentSystemId}/action/confirmed
```

Post the PaymentFlowResult to this endpoint. Litium will record the payment transactions to the order upon receiving this call.

## Show receipt

At the end of the checkout session, after the buyer has confirmed the payment at PSP, a receipt need to be shown. To show the receipt to the buyer, the browser should be redirected to Litium from the PSP. 

*Payment.CheckoutFlowInfo.ReceiptPageUrl* has the url to which the browser need to be redirected.

<img alt="payment flow.jpg" />

1.1.1 When the payment is confirmed by the buyer, the PSP notify the payment app, that the payment is confirmed. 

1.1.1.1 Payment app then notify Litium by calling the NotifyPaymentConfirmed endpoint.

```text theme={null}
POST Litium/api/connect/payments/{paymentSystemId}/action/confirmed
```

Litium creates the order and respond back with the payment transaction.

1.1.1.2 The payment app should then let the browser redirect to show the receipt page to the buyer.


# Execute transactions
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/execute-transactions

Execute transactions webhook event is called, when there are multiple transactions to be executed at the same time at the end of order fulfillment process, to notify the payment app that all transactions need to be executed.

When the final shipment enters the Shipped state or Cancelled state, this event will be fired. During this event, the payment app should finalize all the payment operations. For example: marking the shipped rows as "Shipped" if the payment service provider API requires that.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/overview

This section describes the business processes supported by payment apps.

Payment apps facilitate the payment operations of orders, by using a payment service provider. 

1. For the buyer to checkout, a payment session is initialized with the payment service provider, preparing the checkout process. At the end of the checkout process, the receipt for the order is shown to the user. 
2. When funds need to be captured in two phased payments, Litium raises a *capturetransaction* webhook event. PaymentApp should listen to this event to capture money.
3. When funds need to be refunded, Litium raises a *refundtransaction* webhook event. PaymentApp should listen to this event to refund money.
4. If the order is cancelled in full, *canceltransaction* webhook event will be raised by Litium if the payment is a two step payment, and is not yet captured. PaymentApp should listen to this event to cancel the whole authorization. 
5. If the order is only part fulfilled, at the end of the fulfilment process, Litium will raise the executeTransactions webhook event. The payment app should listen to this event to mark the transaction rows as "shipped" if the payment service provider requires to do so.

See the following sections on how to implement various functionality relating to payment operations


# Payment cancellation
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/payment-cancellation

When a order can only be fulfilled partially, the corresponding unfulfilled part of the payment need to be returned back to the buyer.

## Partial order fulfilment

When the order is fulfilled only partially, Litium creates a cancellation shipment for the part that will not be fulfilled. This cancellation shipment has the corresponding value of the funds that need to be returned back to the buyer. 

* If the payment for the order is only authorized at the PSP, then after capturing the part that is fulfilled,  the remaining part of the authorization should be cancelled.
* If the payment for the order is already captured, (for example in a Bank direct transfer or Sale transaction at PSP), then the corrresponding unfulfilled part of the payment need to be refuded to the buyer.

## Cancel transaction

### Webhook registration

* [Register](/platform/architecture/events-handling/webhooks/webhook-registration) to the *canceltransaction* webhook event. This event is only published, only if the cancel is a supported operation in *Payment.SupportedActions*.
* Register to the ExecuteTransactions webhook event, to handle multiple transaction requests at a single call. This webhook event will get fired if the order is going to be only partially fulfilled but partial capture is not supported and other part of the order is going to be cancelled.

## Cancel result

When the cancel operation succeeds, the payment app should notify Litium through following endpoint.

<table><tbody><tr><td><p><code>PUT Litium/api/connect/payments/\{paymentSystemId}/transactions/cancel</code></p></td></tr></tbody></table>


# Payment capture
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/payment-capture

When Litium decides that funds need to be captured for an authorized payment, Litium will publish the capturetransaction webhook event. The payment app should listen to this event to capture funds.

## Webhook registration

* [Register](/platform/architecture/events-handling/webhooks/webhook-registration) to the *capturetransaction* webhook event. If the capture is only part of the order, then this event is only published, when the respective payment supports the partial captures. 
* Register to the ExecuteTransactions webhook event, to handle multiple transaction requests at a single call. This webhook event will get fired if the order is going to be only partially fulfilled, or when partial capture is not supported.

### When partial capture not supported

Certain payments may not support partial capture, depending on the PSP and payment method used. The payment app should update the *Payment.SupportedActions* accordingly to tell Litium that partial capture is not supported.

When Litium see that PartialCapture is not supported for a payment, *ExecuteTransactions* webhook event will trigger, which will contain multiple transactions. 

## Capture result

When the capture operation succeeds, the payment app should notify Litium through following endpoint.

```text theme={null}
PUT Litium/api/connect/payments/{paymentSystemId}/transactions/capture
```


# Payment overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/payment-overview



In case if your payment app does not contain the payment information that is requested, the payment overview endpoint at Litium can be used to fetch the payment information including all transactions.

Payment overview is the endpoint at Litium that can be used to fetch payment information including all transactions. This can be used if the payment app does not have any information about the requested payment and the app want to reconstruct their information to be able to process the request.

Payment overview endpoint will only respond with payment information for payments that are created for the same payment app.

```csharp theme={null}
GET Litium/api/connect/payments/{paymentSystemId}
```


# Payment refund
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/payment-refund

When Litium decides that funds need to be refunded for a captured transaction, Litium will publish the refundtransaction webhook event. The payment app should listen to this event to refund funds.

## Webhook registration

* [Register](/platform/architecture/events-handling/webhooks/webhook-registration) to the *refundtransaction* webhook event. If the refund is only part of the order, then this event is only published, when the respective payment supports the partial refunds. 
* Register to the ExecuteTransactions webhook event, to handle multiple transaction requests at a single call. This webhook event will get fired if the order is going to be only partially fulfilled, or when partial refund is not supported.

### When partial refund not supported

Certain payments may not support partial refunds, depending on the PSP and payment method used. The payment app should update the *Payment.SupportedActions* accordingly to tell Litium that partial refund is not supported.

When Litium see that PartialRefund is not supported for a payment, *ExecuteTransactions* webhook event will trigger, which will contain multiple transactions. 

## Refund result

When the refund operation succeeds, the payment app should notify Litium through following endpoint.

```text theme={null}
PUT Litium/api/connect/payments/{paymentSystemId}/transactions/refund
```


# Payment Tokens
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/payment-tokens

Payment tokens can be used to make the payment for an order using a saved payment token at payment service provider. These are used in saved credit cards and recurring payments.

## Pre-requisites

To save a credit card, payment service provider should usually enable the recurring payment / subscription payments feature for the payment account. 

Also, the payment app implimentation in Litium should support the feature. 

## Saving a payment token

To save a payment token, when creating the order, initialize the checkout flow with setting CheckoutFlowInfo.InitializePaymentToken property to true.

Example:

Following is a code snippet from Litium Accelerator that switches on the above property.

```csharp theme={null}
private CheckoutFlowInfo GetCheckoutFlowInfo()
{
    //Other code...
    return new CheckoutFlowInfo
    {
        //Other code...

        //Initialize to save a paymen token
        InitializePaymentToken = true,
    };
}
```

The payment token is saved in the payment  app.

The payment token is associated with the Payment.SystemId of the payment of the order that is used initialize the payment token. Create the order after setting InitializePaymentToken to true in checkout flow info, and get the Payment.SystemId to pay for a order using payment token as shown below.

## Using Payment Token

To pay for an order using a saved payment token, use a payment method with PaymentIntegrationType.PaymentToken.

Following method should be called to initialize the payment with the saved token. Use the Payment.SystemId of the payment of the order that is used initialize the payment token for this.

```csharp theme={null}
var cartContext = await HttpContext.GetCartContextAsync();
await cartContext.SetPaymentTokenAsync(new SetPaymentTokenArgs() { PaymentToken = token });
```

After that, create the order as usual. 

There is a [detailed example of how to use payment tokens here >>](/platform/guides/use-payment-token-example)


# Shipping information
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/payments-domain/business-processes/shipping-information

Certain Payment Service Providers (PSP) would provide the ability to present shipping options in the payment iframe (or hosted payment page). This section explains how to initialize and fetch shipping information from such PSPs.

### Initializing shipping options

When a payment is initialized, the ShippingOption list is sent using the CheckoutFlowInfo object, connected to the Payment object.

<img alt="shipping Option.PNG" />

The shipping options sent are the ShippingOption entities configured for the current channel (for the current checkout page).

If the PSP is connected to external TA systems (such as nShift), PSP will display the shipping options from the TA system and would ignore this list. However, if the PSP is not connected to a TA system, (or have issues in getting shipping options from existing TA systems), PSP would display the shipping options sent while the payment is initialized.

### Shipping info from Tms systems through Payment Apps:

Information about the shipping details is received if TMS systems are connected at the payment provider side. They are recorded into the ShippingInfo entity.

<img alt="shipping info from tms.jpg" />

# Checkout page
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/shipments-domain/business-processes/checkout-page

During the checkout phase of an order, the buyer is allowed to choose the delivery location and delivery method. The shipping app contacts the Transport Management Service (TMS) system to present with these options and also calculates the relevant shipping cost.

## Using an iframe delivery checkout

The shipping app, when installed to Litium, will provide a shipping option called "Delivery checkout", that should be added to the channel.

It is common practice that this is the only shipping option configured to the channel.

When a buyer enters the checkout page, the delivery checkout iframe will be shown that allows the buyer to specify the shipping address and select a shipping option.

## Shipping discounts

Litium's free shipping discount are only applied to the shipping cost set in Litium backoffice.

It is the TMS system that is showing the shipping cost for the options shown in the iframe. Therefore, those costs are not affected by Litium's discount engine. This means, the shipping costs set by an iframe delivery checkout solution will not come under shipping discounts set from Litium. Instead, the merchant should use the TMS system to configure the shipping campaigns for these shipping options.

## UI Design considerations

When using a iframe delivery checkout, it is recommended not to show the payment iframe at the same time. As the cost of the selected shipping options will affect the cart contents, the payment iframe would need to be updated each time a change is made in the delivery checkout iframe. The cart contents of Litium, the shipping provider and the payment provider run a high risk of becoming out of sync.

Our recommendation is that the buyer should first be selecting his delivery options using the delivery checkout iframe. The UI of the checkout page should then provide a button to continue to payment. When payment iframe is shown, the delivery checkout iframe should be collapsed.

### Changing checkout page for delivery checkout

* Follow the standard pattern introduced with Litium accelerator in showing the delivery checkout iframe.

* Use the Direct shipment app, and select the deliveryCheckout shipping option for testing the checkout page.

## Passing additional information to the shipment app

To pass additional information for a specific checkout session to a shipment app, you can use the `AdditionalInfo` dictionary on the `CheckoutFlowInfo` object in Litium. The `AdditionalInfo` dictionary contains string-based key–value pairs and is intended for optional, app-specific data.

Each shipment app must explicitly declare which `AdditionalInfo` keys it supports. This declaration is made when the app registers itself with Litium by calling the following Connect Shipments API endpoint:

```csharp theme={null}
POST /Litium/api/connect/shipments/providers
```

The supported keys are provided as strings in the `additionalInfoKeys` array as part of the registration request.


# DeliveryCheckout shipping option
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/shipments-domain/business-processes/delivery-checkout-shipping-option



To provide functionality to the checkout page, the shipping app presents a shipping option where the integration type is "DeliveryCheckout". In this option, the shipping app is providing the iframe that should be presented to the buyer to choose his delivery options on the checkout page.

* For the DeliveryCheckout shipping option, it's *ShippingOption.ShippingOptionIntegrationType* should be set to *ShippingOptionIntegrationType.DeliveryCheckout*.
* Shipping app should only provide on one DeliveryCheckout option.

## Initializing delivery checkout

For every order initialized in Litium, the delivery checkout should be initialized with the TMS provider. This section shows how the delivery checkout session is created and initialized.

To initialize the delivery checkout session, Litium calls

```csharp theme={null}
HTTP POST: <appurl>/api/shipments/initializeSession
```

When this call is received, the app contacts the TMS system and creates a new delivery checkout session. The delivery checkout iframe that should be displayed, should be returned in 

*InitializeSessionResponse::ShippingFlowResult::ShippingInfoResultAction.HtmlSnippet* field.

### Updating cart in Litium

When the cart is updated (e.g. a new item is added to cart), Litium calls the above method with the updated cart data. This means, initializeSession call may be called multiple times during a single checkout session depending on how much the cart is updated. 

*InitializeSessionRequest.CartContextSystemId* field can be used by the app to keep track of the cart context session and keep the session created at TMS provider in sync.

## Updating delivery checkout

When the buyer updates information inside the delivery checkout iframe, such as shipping option and delivery address, Litium updates the cart using information received from the app. This section shows the sequence of events that take place during this process.

The following sequence diagram shows a user action on the rendered delivery checkout iframe: Buyer is changing the shipping option selected. Then the frontend raises a window\.parent.postmessage that Litium is listening to. Litium then calls the updateSession method in the shipping app. The shipping app may contact the TMS provider to get necessary data and reply back to Litium with updated shipping cost values.

<img alt="Seq 02 OnShippingOption Update.jpg" />

### window\.parent.postMessage

As shown above, when the customer updates something in the iframe and the cart is affected from that change, Litium need to be notified using a frontend javascript, window\.parent.postMessage as below.

```javascript theme={null}
<script type="text/javascript">
    function shippingOptionChanged(t) {
        //...other code..
        window.parent.postMessage({
            'type': 'litium-connect-shipping',
            'event': 'optionChanging',
            'data': {
                'value': t.value,
                'name': optionName
            }
        }, "*");
    }
</script>
```

Above event is listened to by Litium, and it triggers the following call to the app.

```javascript theme={null}
HTTP POST: api/shipments/updateSession
```

This sequence of events is shown in the above sequence diagram.

You can check out [an example of using a delivery checkout iframe](/accelerators/mvc-accelerator/develop/the-checkout/using-delivery-checkout) in the documentation for the Litium MVC Accelerator.

## Closing checkout session

When the order is placed, a call is made to close the checkout session at TMS provider.

When the payment is completed on the checkout page, the order will be confirmed in Litium. As part of this process, Litium will call the following method:

```csharp theme={null}
HTTP POST: api/shipments/closeSession
```

The shipping app should use this call to update the checkout session in the TMS to a completed state.


# DeliveryOptions shipping option
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/shipments-domain/business-processes/deliveryoptions-shipping-option

In the DeliveryOptions shipping option, the shipping app provides the list HTTP POST: `/api/shipments/initializeSession` of delivery options that should be presented to the buyer. These delivery options has to be rendered in the checkout page by the project.

* For the DeliveryOptions shipping option, it's *ShippingOption.ShippingOptionIntegrationType* should be set to *ShippingOptionIntegrationType.DeliveryOptions*.
* Shipping app should only provide only one DeliveryOptions option.

## Initializing delivery options

For every order initialized in Litium, the delivery options should be initialized with the TMS provider. This section shows how the delivery options session is created and initialized.

To initialize the delivery option session, Litium calls

```csharp theme={null}
HTTP POST: <appurl>/api/shipments/initializeSession
```

When this call is received, the app contacts the TMS system and creates a new delivery options session. The delivery options that should be displayed are grouped into DeliveryOptionGroup entities, and returned in 

*InitializeSessionResponse::ShippingFlowResult::ShippingInfoResultAction.DeliveryOptionGroups* field.

### Updating cart in Litium

When the cart is updated (e.g. a new item is added to cart), Litium calls the above method with the updated cart data. This means, initializeSession call may be called multiple times during a single checkout session depending on how much the cart is updated. 

*InitializeSessionRequest.CartContextSystemId* field can be used by the app to keep track of the cart context session and keep the session created at TMS provider in sync.

## Updating delivery options

To get the resulting delivery cost calculated, Litium calls the shipping app with a UpdateSession call.

```csharp theme={null}
HTTP POST: api/shipments/updateSession
```

When this call is made, the response contains the selected delivery method information in \_UpdateSessionResponse::ShippingFlowResult::ShippingInfoResultAction.\_ShipmentInfos field.

This is a collection of ShipmentInfo, one per each shippingInfo in the order.

### Checkout page implementation

Since it is the checkout page that renders the delivery options, it is the checkout page that should initiate this call, when the buyer has selected a delivery option. The call is initiated by calling *cartContext::UpdateShippingSessionAsync* method.
