# Estimate tax during checkout
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/tax-domain/business-processes/estimate-tax-during-checkout

During the checkout, the tax app is called to find the estimated amount of tax that should be applied to the cart. This section describes the details of this call and its response.

Following endpoint in the tax app is called by Litium during the checkout phase.

```text theme={null}
HTTP POST: <appurl>/api/tax/calculateSalesOrder
```

When this call is received, the app should contact the tax calculation service and get the tax for the items in the cart.

The results should be returned in *CalculateSalesOrderTaxResponse* object.

From following link you can find [guidelines on building a tax app and implementing this endpoint](/platform/guides/how-to-build-a-tax-app).


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/tax-domain/business-processes/overview

This section describes the business processes involving tax apps.



# Shipment tax
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/tax-domain/business-processes/shipment-tax

When shipments are made during the order fulfilment process, actual tax for the shipment need to be calculated. This section describes the request and response for this call.

Following endpoint in the tax app is called by Litium when processing a shipment. Before Litium calls payment apps to capture the money for a shipment, Litium calls the tax app to find the actual tax for the shipment, with a call to following endpoint in the tax app.

```csharp theme={null}
HTTP POST: <appurl>/api/tax/calculateShipment
```

When this call is received, the app should contact the tax calculation service and get the tax for the items in the shipment.

The results should be returned in *CalculateShipmentTaxResponse* object.

From following link you can find [guidelines on building a tax app and implementing this endpoint](/platform/guides/how-to-build-a-tax-app).


# Tax overshoot and undershoot
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/tax-domain/business-processes/tax-overshoot-and-undershoot

Tax estimated during order placement process can be different from the actual tax when shipments are made. This section explains how Litium implements these differences in taxes.

In certain countries, like for example in USA sales tax, the tax depends on the shipments made. In particular, in USA, the tax is calculated as from a source location to a destination location, based on items and services purchased. Which means that US sales tax at the time of placing the order is only an estimated tax amount. The actual tax amount is calculated when the shipments are delivered.

This may lead to the actual tax at the time of shipment deliveries being different from estimated tax at the time of order placement.

## Tax Overshoot

This happens if the estimated tax is more than the actual tax the buyer need to pay. When shipments are made, actual tax is calculated and total of actual tax becomes less than the initial tax estimate. 

In Litium, this excess amount is refunded to the buyer when the [order is finalized](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/cancel-unfulfilled-part-of-a-order). Usually the order enteres automatic finalization when the last shipment is made. In case of partial shipments and order not being fully fulfilled, the Finalize endpoint need be explicitely called to refund any excess taxes. 

To refund the excess taxes, Litium may create a shipment which may only have the excess tax row. This shipment has shipment type "Cancellation" and will be executed during order finalization.

## Tax Undershoot

This happens if the estimated tax is less than the actual tax the buyer need to pay. When shipments are made, actual tax is calculated and total of actual tax becomes more than the initial tax estimate. 

In this scenario, the buyer has paid or authorized less amount of tax than actually needed. 

Litium treats this deficit as a tax deficit, and does not automatically collect this money from the buyer. It is up to the merchant ERP system and accounting system to finally invoice the buyer of uncollected taxes.

In the shipment where actual tax is more than the estimated tax, a shipment row will be created which has a negative value that equals to the tax deficit.


# Domain models
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/tax-domain/domain-models

Following UML diagram shows classes and relationships in Litium.Connect.Tax namespace.

To view a full size diagram, [click here >>.](/images/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/tax-domain/domain-models/TaxDomain.png "TaxDomain.png")

<img alt="TaxDomain.png" />

### CalculateSalesOrderTaxRequest

When tax need to be calculated during the checkout phase, this request is made to the tax app. Tax calculated during checkout should be the estimated tax for the cart, and should be returned from CalculateSalesOrderTaxResponse object.

### CalculateShipmentTaxRequest

When the ERP system notify Litium to create a shipment (see ERP domain), Litium calls the tax app with a webservice call, which has the CalculateShipmentTaxRequest class to determine the actual tax for the shipment. The response is made from CalculateShipmentTaxResponse class.

### CalculateSalesOrderTaxResponse and CalculateShipmentTaxResponse

To return the results of the tax calculation, CalculateSalesOrderTaxResponse and CalculateShipmentTaxResponse is used. 

The response contains a collection of TaxRow entities.

* Each TaxRow would add a new row, of type Tax into the Litium sales order when included in CalculateSalesOrderTaxResponse.
* Each TaxRow would add a new row, of type Tax into the Litium shipment when included in CalculateShipmentTaxResponse.

Each tax row in a order should correspond to the type of tax that it represents, which means for example, USA sales tax would be represented by a single tax order row. This means, that if the tax app is responding with USA sales tax, the response would contain a single tax row in its response object, which represent the USA sales tax.

### TaxDetail Entity

Each TaxRow contains the details about the tax in a collection of TaxDetail entities. In this, how the tax is made up is recorded. For example, USA sales tax may contain state tax and city tax and other special taxes. These taxes all adds up to the final sales tax, and therefore should be recorded in TaxRow\.TaxDetails.

TaxRow\.OrderRowTaxDetails is a `Dictionary<OrderRowId, List<TaxDetails>>` where the dictionary key is the OrderRowId. It records how much tax allocated at order row level. The items in this TaxDetails (in the dictionary values) are recorded into the OrderRow\.TaxDetails collection in Litium.

## CustomerInfo.CustomerSubType

CustomerSubType property in CustomerInfo contains whether the buyer is a non-profit or a government body. This value should be set in Litium, [see example >>](/platform/guides/how-to-build-a-tax-app/customersubtype).

## CustomerInfo.TaxExemptions

This contains the list of tax exemtion certifcates held by the buyer. This is a `IDictionary<string, string>` where key should be the certificate Id and you can use the value for certificate number. This value should be set in Litium.

# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/connect-apis/overview

Connect APIs is a set of business domain-specific web APIs to support integrations to third-party systems such as ERP systems, payment providers, WMS, T&A systems etc.

## ERP API

Use it to connect to enterprice resource planning systems (ERPs) such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP, etc, for order fulfilment and return management.

[API ref](/apis/connect/erp-api)

## Payments API

Use it to connect to payment service providers such as Klarna, Dibs, PayPal, etc, to authorize payments, capture, cancel and refund.

[API ref](/apis/connect/payment-api)

## Shipments API

Use it to connect to transport management systems such as nShift, Ingrid, etc to fetch delivery options for the checkout process.

[API ref](/apis/connect/shipment-api)

## Why use the connect APIs?

### **Easy deployment and upgrade** 

In Litium connect an integration application has its own runtime life cycle, which means the Litium installation does not need to be stopped or taken down for installation or upgrade of the integration applications. This reduces the costs of deployment and upgrade.

### **Easy maintenance** 

Updates of the integration applications would be less frequent as they would be more resilient and can be developed with backward compatibility. This means, as the Litium version is updated, there would be less compatibility issues with existing integration applications that are already in use, and vise-versa. This reduces the maintenance costs.

### **Scaling**

To the advantage of being able to scale independently of Litium server instances. An integration application may need only one application instance while Litium may need to be deployed in multiple servers to improve website performance.

### Standard business domain contracts

Litium connect facilitates "domain-driven design" and "business process-driven development" and exposes standard business domain contracts, like entities, operations, and events (exposed through web API endpoints and webhooks).

# Litium .NET API
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/dot-net-api/overview

An outline of structure and services.

## Structure

The  .NET API is structured into different assemblies to separate the domain entities and service contracts from the application logic.

When you extend and build customer-specific functionality, you only need to include references to the assemblies that contain domain entities and service contracts. This way there will be a minimal number of external dependencies.

A service contract can be either the domain service that will handle the entity or an extension point.

Domain services have an abstract class as a contract and extension points have interfaces as contracts.

Domain entities and service contracts that have breaking changes will be announced in the release notes for each release, with the exception of classes and interfaces in the *Internal* namespace.

Classes and interfaces in the *Internal* namespace should not be used in customer solutions and can be removed by Litium without prior notice.

Naming of the assemblies that contain the domain entities or service contracts:

* *Litium.Abstractions* - contains core domain entities and service contracts.
* *Litium.Web.Abstractions* - contains domain entities and service contracts for web applications.
* *Litium.Web.Mvc.Abstractions* - contains domain entities and service contracts for ASP.NET MVC applications.
* *Litium.Web.WebApi.Abstractions* - contains domain entities and service contracts for ASP.NET WebAPI applications.
* *Litium.Web.Administration.Abstractions* – contains domain entities and service contracts for extending the administration interface.

The namespace in the assembly is the same as the assembly name without “Abstractions”.

### *Litium.Common*

*Litium.Common.KeyLookupService* can be used for high-performance lookup between Id and SystemId of entities. When a value is requested it is cached for future calls making it possible to lookup SystemId for an Id and vice versa.

Example getting SystemId for currency from Id:

```csharp theme={null}
_keyLookupService.TryGetId<Currency>(entity.CurrencySystemId, out id)
```

*Litium.Common.SettingService* is a simple key-value storage that can be used to store serializable objects in the database.

```csharp theme={null}
var lastSyncDate = _settingService.Get<DateTimeOffset>(key);
// Sync stuff...
_settingService.Set(key, DateTimeOffset.Now);
```

## Services

Applications can be designed through

* static instance that contains the services and caches
* dependency injection that holds the state of the services and injects the dependency (constructor parameters) for the service into the instance.

The services in the API are designed to use dependency injection wherever possible. When using dependency injection, services can easily be extended or replaced. Services are used to create/read/update/delete the entity.

### How to find the correct service

If the entity name is "Entity" the service name is "EntityService".

Example:

* entity = BaseProduct
* service = BaseProductService

The service exists in the same namespace as the entity.

## Readonly entities

All entities that implement *Litium.ComponentModel.IReadOnly* can be in read-only mode to prohibit that the entity is changed. To change a read-only entity, you need to invoke the method *MakeWritableClone* to create a clone of the object that can be changed.

## Database manipulation of data

Litium strongly advises against changing the data directly in the database. If you choose to do so anyway:

* you are responsible to ensure business rules are met
* you are responsible to ensure that correct events are fired
* you are responsible to ensure that search indexes are updated.

## API documentation

Complete references to the current and previous versions of the [Litium API can be found here](https://docs.litium.com/api-reference/net-api).


# Extension Management API Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/extension-management-api/overview

Platform extension and app management API

## Extension Management API

The Litium Extension Management API lets you register, update, and remove extensions programmatically — typically from CI/CD pipelines. Base path: `/Litium/api/extension-management`.

<Note>
  This API requires a **service account** (OAuth2 client credentials or bearer token). It is separate from the backoffice admin API at `/Litium/app/api/extension-management/...` used by **Settings > System settings > Extensions**. For manual installation, see [Extension Management UI](/platform/extensions/extension-management-ui).
</Note>

### Endpoints

| Method   | Path               | Description                                                |
| -------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET`    | `/extensions`      | List extensions owned by the authenticated service account |
| `POST`   | `/extensions`      | Register a new extension                                   |
| `GET`    | `/extensions/{id}` | Get one extension by `id`                                  |
| `PUT`    | `/extensions/{id}` | Update an existing extension                               |
| `DELETE` | `/extensions/{id}` | Remove an extension                                        |
| `GET`    | `/targets`         | List supported manifest target types and fields            |

The request and response body for extension operations matches `extension.manifest.json`. See the [manifest reference](/platform/extensions/extension-manifest-reference).

# Changing email with verification
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/storefront/changing-email-with-verification

This page describes how to change email with verification

In this article, you'll learn how to:

* [Sign in user](#sign-in-user)
* [Sign out user](#sign-out-user)
* [Send change email verification](#send-change-email-verification)
* [Use verification code to change user email](#change-email)

## Prerequisites

* GraphQL
* Storefront API knowledge. If you are new, please read this [article](/apis/storefront).
* Storefront API playground. If you are new, please read this [article](/apis/storefront).

## Working with user

### Sign in user

In order to change user email, first the user needs to be signed in. To perform a user sign in mutation, we can use the query below.\
 

```javascript theme={null}
mutation {
  signInUser(input: { password: "password", username: "user@mail.com" }) {
    authentication {
      me {
        person {
          customerNumber
          id
        }
      }
    }
    errors {
      ... on AuthenticationFailure {
        message
        type
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Sign out user

And along with the user sign in mutaion, Litium also provides mutation to sign out a user.\
 

```javascript theme={null}
mutation {
  signOutUser(input: { allSessions: true }) {
    boolean
  }
}
```

## Working with email

### Send change email verification

Before a user can actually change email, Litium need to make sure that the user is allowed to perform that action. Consider the query below

```javascript theme={null}
mutation {
  changeMyEmailVerification(input: { 
    email: "user@email.com", 
    notificationUrl: "https://dummy-domain.com/changeEmailVericationUrl" }) {
    token
    errors {
      ... on ValidationError {
        message
      }
      ... on Forbidden {
        message
      }
      ... on Failure {
        message
        type
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The *notificationUrl* should be an absolute url and the domain need to be registered in Litium backoffice.

Once Litium received the request, a webhook will be sent to *notificationUrl* endpoint, and by that, we can send the verification code to the user, by for example sending an email. 

### Change email

Once token and verification token are provided, we can now change the user email. 

```javascript theme={null}
mutation {
  changeMyEmail(
    input: { 
      notificationUrl: "https://dummy-domain.com/emailChangedUrl", 
      token: "The-token-recived-from-webhook", 
      verificationToken: "the-token-after-perform-changing-email-verification" }
  ) {
    errors {
      ... on Failure {
        message
        type
      }
      ... on Forbidden {
        message
      }
      ... on ValidationError {
        message
      }
    }
    me {
      customerNumber
      id
    }
  }
}
```

The *notificationUrl* in the section above has the same rule - it should be an abosolute url and the domain need to be registered in Litium backoffice.

After the email was changed, the *EmailChanged* webhook will be sent to *notificationUrl* endpoint. and thanks to that we know whether the email was changed successfully or not.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/apis/storefront/overview



## Introduction

The Storefront API provides a GraphQL API interface to the information in Litium specifically composed to serve public websites, portals or mobile applications. The GraphQL schema is based on the information inside each Litium installation and is automatically updated when changes are done inside Litium.

The API can return both published and unpublished information depending on the current user permissions and the requested information.

## Roadmap

The Storefront API is continuously evolving with new features and improvements. For the latest updates and future plans, please check the Litium product roadmap.

## System requirements

Must be hosted on **Litium Serverless Cloud** to operate within the Litium environment.

## Installation

The Storefront API needs to be installed manually into the Litium solution and can be done with the template or with manual steps.

### Automatic

Storefront API can be automatically installed with the [Litium Mvc Accelrator](/accelerators/mvc-accelerator/install-litium-accelerator) or [Litium Empty Web](/platform/get-started/install-empty-litium) template, see their installation pages for instructions.

### Manual

The Storefront API can manually be installed, add the NuGet package *Litium.Storefront.Application* to the web project.

## Access the Storefront API playground

The Storefront API can be accessed with a graphical tool for inspection of the GraphQL schema.

You can use the *[https://.../storefront.graphql](https://.../storefront.graphql)* to access the graphical tool with the schema in your installation. For a demo you can use the [https://demo.litium.com/storefront.graphql](https://demo.litium.com/storefront.graphql) that represents the GraphQL schema for demo site.

## Cross Origin Request Policy (CORS)

When requesting the Storefront API, the browser will use CORS policy to ensure cross domain request if the current domain name and the domain name for the Storefront API is different. Litium has created a CORS policy that allows requests from the domain information that is setup below the globalization settings page.

## Request method

The Storefront API supports POST request with the required http header “Content-Type: application/json”, the payload should be included and formatted into JSON string.

## Authentication

The Storefront API does not require authentication and will only return information that the everyone can access. To access information that is not accessible for everyone the authentication information needs to be included in the request.

The Storefront API supports:

1. Authentication header with a bearer token.
2. Litium authentication cookie

If the authentication that is provided is invalid or has expired the request will be treated as anonymous and using everyone’s permission for the authorization.

## Field permissions

If the provided authentication lacks permission for a field, the field's value will return null during a query.

## Backend domain url

In case the storefront and the backend has different urls, the callback domain to backend can be configured in the [Configuration](/platform/get-started/configuration) file, section Callback domain for Backend.

## Http-headers

Contextual information about the user (see authentication), current requested url (see context) or cart (see cart and checkout) is passed into the Storefront API as http-headers. The http-headers are included in the downstream GraphQL fenderation request that make the information available also for the extension.

### Context

Context is information about the current request, it is used to resolve information about the current page, website, channel, country, language and more. The context information is parsed out from the requested URL and should be passed in the GraphQL request as an header with name "x-litium-storefront-context-url".

#### Example

```json theme={null}
x-litium-storefront-context-url: "https://demo.litium.com"
```

### Cart

### Checkout

### Persisted queries 

[Persisted queries](https://chillicream.com/docs/hotchocolate/v13/performance/automatic-persisted-queries) is supported in the Storefront API, and 265hash with base64 encoded is used as hash function.

Example : 

Check that the data not exists

```csharp theme={null}
curl.exe --insecure -g 'https://localhost:5001/storefront.graphql/?extensions={"persistedQuery":{"version":1,"sha256Hash":"7PTttG20C1EyKVwCkdYvtl1nWanu36TV1hLdXsVKazg="}}'
```

Create a persisted query, this should return persisted=true, otherwise it will return the expected hash/type/format that should be used.

```csharp theme={null}
curl.exe --insecure -g 'https://localhost:5001/storefront.graphql/?query={__typename}&extensions={"persistedQuery":{"version":1,"sha256Hash":"7PTttG20C1EyKVwCkdYvtl1nWanu36TV1hLdXsVKazg="}}'
```

Check that the query now works

```csharp theme={null}
curl.exe --insecure -g 'https://localhost:5001/storefront.graphql/?extensions={"persistedQuery":{"version":1,"sha256Hash":"7PTttG20C1EyKVwCkdYvtl1nWanu36TV1hLdXsVKazg="}}'
```

# .NET web
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/dotnet-web

.NET web lets you deploy your own custom .NET web artifact. Possible to connect your file storage, Redis cache, MS SQL database and other services.

### Pricing

.NET web is priced per hour based on selected app plan. [Read more about prices](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/pricing).

### Installation

**Prerequisites**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new environment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)

### Manifest

Run following command to download dotnet-web manifest:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app dotnet-web -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Example manifest file:

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: dotnet-web
spec:
  type: dotnet-web
  version: 1.0.0
  plan: 
  # properties:
  #    #    - name: artifact
```

### Manifest configuration

**Id**: Choose your own unique-per-environment id of the app. Suggested "dotnet-web".

### Artifact

To deploy your code you need to first [create a dotnet artifact](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/create-dotnet-artifact) and refer the artifact id to the property "artifact".

<Note>
  It is possible to omit an artifact when installing the app, and instead later use the [deploy command](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/deploy-artifact) to deploy your code artifact to your app.
</Note>

### SMTP

If your app should send emails, you should configure SMTP. Read more on the [Install SMTP relay app page](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/smtp-relay-app).

### App plan

To install a .NET web private app you need to provide a plan when creating the app. Pricing is based on which plan you select. Run following command to view available plans for .NET web app:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app dotnet-web
```

Insert the plan-id you want after the "plan:" in the manifest file.

### Apply

Run following command to install the dotnet-web app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

* Fetch Subscription-id: `litium-cloud subscription list`
* Fetch Environment-id: `litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id`

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will create a .NET web app in the given environment.

### Configure logging to Litium Insights

**Prerequisites:**

* [Install Litium Insights and give user(s) permission](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-insights)

**Configure logging**

1. Add nuget package "Litium.Cloud.NLog.Extensions"
2. Add a nlog.config file to your project ([example](https://github.com/NLog/NLog.Web/blob/master/examples/ASP.NET%20Core%206/ASP.NET%20Core%206%20NLog%20Example/nlog.config))
3. In application startup, typically in program.cs, add configuration for Litium NLog to ensure logs are being sent to Litium Insights.

**Example configuration for** [top-level statement syntax](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/program-structure/top-level-statements):

```csharp theme={null}
using NLog.Web;

NLog.Logger logger = NLogBuilder
    .ConfigureNLog("nlog.config")
    .ConfigureLitiumNLog()
    .GetCurrentClassLogger();

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Logging.ClearProviders();
builder.Logging.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Trace);
builder.Logging.AddLitiumNLog();
```

**Example configuration using structured program:**

```csharp theme={null}
using NLog.Web;

namespace MyProject.Mvc
{
    public class Program
    {
        public static void Main(string[] args)
        {
            var logger = NLogBuilder
                .ConfigureNLog("nlog.config")
                .ConfigureLitiumNLog()
                .GetCurrentClassLogger();

            try
            {
                logger.Info("Application starting");
                CreateHostBuilder(args).Build().Run();
            }
            catch (Exception exception)
            {
                logger.Error(exception, "Stopped program because of exception");
                throw;
            }
            finally
            {
                // Ensure to flush and stop internal timers/threads before application-exit (Avoid segmentation fault on Linux)
                NLog.LogManager.Shutdown();
            }
        }

        public static IHostBuilder CreateHostBuilder(string[] args)
        {
            return Host.CreateDefaultBuilder(args)
                .ConfigureLogging(logging =>
                {
                    logging.ClearProviders();
                    logging.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Trace);
                    logging.AddLitiumNLog();
                })
                
                ....
        }
```

4. Use "Microsoft.Extensions.Logging" to write to logs:

```csharp theme={null}
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;

namespace MyProject.Example
{

    internal class MyClass
    {
        private readonly ILogger<MyClass> _logger;
        ...


        public MyClass(
            ILogger<MyClass> logger)
        {
            _logger = logger;
            ...
        }
        
        public void MyMethod()
        {
            _logger.LogTrace("MyMethod was called");
        }
        
        ...
    }
}
```

### Connect MS SQL app

To be able to access your private MS SQL database from the .NET web app you should add configuration in your manifest file.

Example configuration to connect a MS SQL app with id "privatedb" to your .NET web app. Note in this example the environment variable is named "ConnectionStrings\_\_DefaultConnection", this would replace any value in appsettings.json in the section "ConnectionStrings->DefaultConnection":

```yaml theme={null}
configurations:
    - name: ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: privatedb
          key: connection_string
```

### Connect File storage app

To be able to access your file storage app from within your .NET web app (e.g. accessing integration files from the storage app) you need to configure your .NET web app's manifest to access your storage app.

Add the following section to your dotnet app manifest to connect a directory "integration" to a file storage app with id "file-storage" and path integration-directory to your Litium app:

```yaml theme={null}
  configurations:
    - name: integration
      type: storage
      subPath: integration-directory
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: file-storage
          key: storage_volume
```

This will then be available in the folder "app\_storage", so for the above example the files would be accessed through the path "/app\_storage/integration" (and the actual directory on the storage app would be /integration-directory).

### Actions

For a detailed list about which actions are available use the following command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app dotnet-web --details --version add-version-here
```

### Console output

Gets console output from app in container. Normally those logs are sent to Litium Insights, but if your app doesn't start, issues may be printed to the console but never reach Litium Insights because the app hasn't started.

See the guide "[Output console logs](/cloud/serverless/guides/output-console-logs)" for how to perform this action.

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new environment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)

**Manifest**

Run following command to download file-storage manifest:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app file-storage -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Example manifest file:

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: file-storage
spec:
  type: file-storage
  version: 1.0.0
  # properties:
  #   # Storage artifact used for restore when storage is created.
  #   - name: backup_file
  #     value: artifacts/12345678901234567890123456789012
```

**Manifest configuration**

**Id**: Choose your own unique-per-environment id of the app. Suggested "file-storage".

**Properties**: For File storage app it is possible to upload a storage artifact when the app is being created. Note, only possible to upload artifact while creating the app, after the app is created storage should be managed through other interfaces, like connecting the app to Litium or adding an sFTP app. If storage artifact isn't added the storage app will be empty when created.

**Apply**

Run following command to install the file-storage app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

* Fetch Subscription-id: `litium-cloud subscription list`
* Fetch Environment-id: `litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id`

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will create a File storage app in the given environment.

### Connect with Litium app

To be able to access your file storage app from within your Litium app (e.g. accessing integration files from the storage app) you need to configure your Litium app's manifest to access your storage app.

Add the following section to your Litium app's manifest to connect a directory "integration" to a file storage app with id "file-storage" and path integration-directory to your Litium app:

```yaml theme={null}
  configurations:
    - name: integration
      type: storage
      subPath: integration-directory
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: file-storage
          key: storage_volume
```

This will then be available in the folder "app\_storage", so for the above example the files would be accessed through the path "/app\_storage/integration" (and the actual directory on the storage app would be /integration-directory).

### Connect sFTP app with File storage

[Read more on the sFTP app page](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-sftp).


# Headless Chrome
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/headless-chrome

The Headless Chrome app gives you access to a Chrome browser for automation tasks such as generating PDFs from HTML content, capturing screenshots, running automated UI tests, and more. It exposes a WebSocket URL that can be consumed by other applications—such as the Litium platform or a .NET web app.

### Pricing

Headless Chrome is priced **per hour** based on selected app plan. [Read more about prices](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/pricing).

### Installation

**Prerequisites**

Make sure the following are in place:

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new environment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)

### Step 1: Download the Manifest

Use the following command to download the Headless Chrome manifest:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app headless-chrome -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in your current working directory.
</Note>

### Step 2: Configure the manifest file

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: headless-chrome
spec:
  type: headless-chrome
  plan: [insert-plan-id]
  version: 1.0.0
```

* **id**: Choose a unique-per-environment ID, suggested: `headless-chrome`
* **properties**: Headless Chrome does not require any custom properties
* **plan**: Insert plan-id based on which plan best suits your needs

### Step 3: Apply the app to an environment

Run the following command to install the app:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

Helpful commands:

* Get Subscription id: `litium-cloud subscription list`
* Get Environment id: `litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id`

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a **job-id** that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will deploy the Headless Chrome app to the specified environment.

### How to use

To connect to your Headless Chrome instance from another app (e.g., Litium platform or a .NET app), use the WebSocket **URL** exposed by the Headless Chrome app.

<Note>
  The exposed URL is internal and can only be accessed by other apps within **Serverless Cloud**. It is not accessible from outside the Serverless Cloud environment.
</Note>

<Tip>
  View properties that an app exposes: `litium-cloud marketplace show --app headless-chrome --version 1.0.0`
</Tip>

### Example: Configure another app to use Chrome

To use the Chrome socket in another app, configure it to fetch the URL by setting up configurations:

```yaml theme={null}
  configurations:
    - name: CHROME__SOCKET
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: headless-chrome
          key: url
```

This will populate the `CHROME__SOCKET` environment variable with the WebSocket URL from the Headless Chrome app.

Add this configuration section to the YAML file of the app that needs to access Headless Chrome—such as the Litium platform app—then re-apply it using the "apply" command.

### Example: Generate PDF with PuppeteerSharp

Below is a sample C# method using [PuppeteerSharp](https://github.com/hardkoded/puppeteer-sharp) to generate a PDF:

```csharp theme={null}
public async Task<byte[]> GeneratePdf()
{
    string htmlContent = @"<!DOCTYPE html>
                        <html lang=""en"">
                        <head>
                        </head>
                        <body>
                            <h1>Test PDF</h1>
                            <p>This is a test PDF document generated using PuppeteerSharp.</p>
                        </body>
                        </html>
                        ";


    var browserWSEndpoint = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CHROME__SOCKET");

    var connectOptions = new ConnectOptions
    {
        BrowserWSEndpoint = browserWSEndpoint,
        DefaultViewport = null
    };

    var browser = await Puppeteer.ConnectAsync(connectOptions);

    using (var page = await browser.NewPageAsync())
    {
        // Set content of the page
        await page.SetContentAsync(htmlContent);

        // Generate PDF
        return await page.PdfDataAsync(new PdfOptions
        {
            Format = PaperFormat.A4,
            PrintBackground = true,
            MarginOptions = new MarginOptions
            {
                Top = "20mm",
                Bottom = "20mm",
                Left = "15mm",
                Right = "15mm"
            }
        });
    }
}
```


# Execute database migration
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/ms-sql/execute-database-migration

This action handles Entity Framework database migrations through efbundle.

### Prerequisites

* For private MS SQL apps: The role `apps/mssql-db/migration-execution` must be assigned to the app for which you wish to perform this action.

### How to execute

1. Prepare your single-file executable according to [Microsoft's documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/managing-schemas/migrations/applying?tabs=dotnet-core-cli#bundles).
2. [Create an artifact](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/create-dotnet-artifact) of type `db-migration`.
3. Use the `execute-database-migration` action with reference to artifact id:
   * `--property "artifact=[insert-artifact-id]"` (required): This should refer to an artifact of type `db-migration`

### Example - Execute action and view results

1. Execute action:

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud app action --action execute-database-migration --property "artifact=1234567910111213"
   ```

   This will generate a job with a unique job ID.

2. View the status of the job:

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud status show --job INSERT-JOB-ID
   ```

   Example output:

   ```
   Details
   =======
       Status: succeeded
      
   Action: execute-database-migration
       Job id: 1ab2520b-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
       Document id: subscriptions/xxxx/environments/xxxx/apps/mssql-db
       Created: 2024-09-24 19:04:40
       Started: 2024-09-24 19:04:41
       Completed: 2024-09-24 19:05:02

       Properties
       ==========
           Name          Value
           --------------------------------
           artifact      artifacts/bdf78c4xxxxx

       Related items
       =============
           Status: succeeded
           Action: migration
           Job id: 7b3db106-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
           Document id: subscriptions/xxxx/environments/xxxx/apps/mssql-db/resources/database
           Created: 2024-09-24 19:04:41
           Started: 2024-09-24 19:04:52
           Completed: 2024-09-24 19:05:02
   ```

3. View logs of related "migration" item to show results:

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud status logs --job 7b3db106-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx
   ```

   Example output:

   ```
   2024-09-24 19:05:02.1688 | Executing tool from artifacts/bdf78cxxxxx
   2024-09-24 19:05:02.2509 | Applying migration '20210903083845_MyMigration'.
   2024-09-24 19:05:02.2520 | Done.
   2024-09-24 19:05:02.2550 | Executed tool
   2024-09-24 19:05:02.2567 | Completed
   ```


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/ms-sql/overview

Host your MS SQL databases, offering easy integration with the .NET Web app. Pricing is determined by disk usage.

### Pricing

MS SQL is priced per hour based on usage. [Read more about prices](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/pricing).

### Installation

**Prerequisites**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new environment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)

**Manifest**

Run following command to download mssql-db manifest:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app mssql-db -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Example manifest file:

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: mssql-db
spec:
  type: mssql-db
  version: 1.0.0
  # properties:
  #   # Sql backup artifact used when creating database.
  #   - name: backup_file
  #     value: artifacts/12345678901234567890123456789012
```

**Manifest configuration**

**Id**: Choose your own unique-per-environment id of the app. Suggested "mssql-db".

**Properties**: For MS SQL db it is possible to add a database artifact when installing, this backup will then be restored when the database is created. [Read more about uploading a MS SQL backup](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/create-sql-backup-artifact). It is also possible to omit the SQL backup artifact property when creating the app. If no artifact is added the database will be empty once the app is installed, and you may create tables through code with a .NET web application connected to the MS SQL db app.

**Apply**

Run following command to install the mssql-db app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

* Fetch Subscription-id: `litium-cloud subscription list`
* Fetch Environment-id: `litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id`

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will create a MS SQL Db app in the given environment.

### Actions

For a detailed list about which actions are available use the following command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app mssql-db --details --version add-version-here
```

### Backup database

Creates a database backup and stores the backup as an artifact for the current subscription.

See the guide "[Create database backup](/cloud/serverless/guides/create-database-backup)" for how to perform this action.

### Execute SQL Script

Use with care, especially when performing updates, as these may result in outdated cache data. Remember, you are responsible for the scripts you run.

For detailed instructions, see the guide "[Execute SQL script](/cloud/serverless/guides/execute-sql-script)."

### Execute database migration

This action enables Entity Framework migrations with a migration bundle. [Read more about Entity Framework migrations and bundles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/managing-schemas/migrations/applying?tabs=dotnet-core-cli#bundles).

For detailed instructions, see [Execute database migration](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/ms-sql/execute-database-migration).

### Connect with .NET Web app or Litium app

To be able to access your private MS SQL database from a .NET web app or your Litium app you should add configuration in your .NET web or Litium manifest file.

Example configuration to connect a MS SQL app with id "privatedb" to your .NET web app. Note in this example the environment variable is named "ConnectionStrings\_\_DefaultConnection", this would replace any value in appsettings.json in the section "ConnectionStrings->DefaultConnection":

```yaml theme={null}
configurations:
    - name: ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: privatedb
          key: connection_string
```
