# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/overview

Private apps makes it possible to manage other workloads that are related to the e-commerce ecosystem. For instance integration apps, private databases, additional storage and more.

Private apps offer a flexible solution tailored to your specific needs, acting as customizable slots in your environment for various workloads or data. Each app serves a unique purpose, such as storage, database management, or hosting .NET web containers. You can install multiple private apps, selecting an App plan for each that defines its resource allocation. Pricing for private apps is hourly and varies by the chosen App plan. Discover the diverse applications and their pricing in the sections below.

### [.NET web](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/dotnet-web)

Deploy custom .NET web artifacts, integrating services like file storage, Redis cache, and MS SQL databases. Ideal for periodic custom workloads or creating advanced web pages, such as customer review management systems. Select from various App plans to allocate resources appropriately, with costs based on the chosen plan.

### [File storage](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/file-storage)

Use this app for storing files, such as integration documents. It seamlessly integrates with apps like Litium and SFTP for syncing ERP data, with charges based on disk usage.

### [Headless Chrome](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/headless-chrome)

The Headless Chrome app gives you access to a Chrome browser for automation tasks such as generating PDFs from HTML content, capturing screenshots, running automated UI tests, and more. It exposes a WebSocket URL that can be consumed by other applications—such as the Litium platform or a .NET web app.

### [MS SQL database](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/ms-sql/overview)

Host your MS SQL databases, offering easy integration with the .NET Web app. Pricing is determined by disk usage.

### [Next.js web](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/nextjs-web)

Host your private Next.js web app if you for example want additional storefronts connected to your Litium app.

### [Node.js web](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/nodejs-web)

In Litium Serverless Cloud, you can run Node.js applications without the need for a specific framework like Next.js or Nuxt.js. Simply use the common nodejs-web app, which supports any type of Node.js application. The app relies on the build and start commands defined in the package.json file to manage the application's lifecycle.

### [Nuxt.js web](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/nuxtjs-web)

Host your private Nuxt.js web app to host your Vue.js storefronts connected to your Litium app.

### [Redis Cache](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/redis-cache)

Enhance access speed with a private Redis Cache, connectable to .NET Web apps for efficient data retrieval. Costs are App plan-dependent.


# Pricing
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/pricing

This page provides a technical overview of the App Plans available in Litium Serverless Cloud for private apps such as .NET web, Next.js web, Node.js web, Nuxt.js web, and Redis Cache. App Plans define the resource allocation for your private applications, influencing their performance and cost.

### Available App Plans and Resources

To view the available App Plans for a specific private app, you can use the Litium Cloud CLI command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app <app-id>
```

For example, to see the plans available for a .NET web app, you would run:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app dotnet-web
```

This command will output a list of available plan IDs that you can then specify in your app's manifest file.

While resource allocation is dynamically managed by Litium to ensure optimal performance, the table below outlines available plans and their memory allocation. Note that not all plans are supported for all app types. The "a" in the plan ID stands for **autoscaling**, which scales based on CPU usage.

| Plan | RAM    | Autoscaling     | Price                                                          |
| ---- | ------ | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| S1   | 0.5 GB | No              | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S1a  | 0.5 GB | Yes (CPU-based) | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S2   | 1 GB   | No              | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S2a  | 1 GB   | Yes (CPU-based) | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S3   | 2.5 GB | No              | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S3a  | 2.5 GB | Yes (CPU-based) | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S4   | 6 GB   | No              | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S4a  | 6 GB   | Yes (CPU-based) | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S5   | 16 GB  | No              | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |
| S5a  | 16 GB  | Yes (CPU-based) | [See price list](https://docs.litium.com/resources/price-list) |

<Note>
  Some apps, such as SQL Database and File Storage apps, are billed separately based on actual usage (storage in GB) and do not require a plan.
</Note>

<Note>
  The above table is a current example. Always use the CLI to fetch latest information about available plans and their resources.
</Note>

### Pricing Calculation

There are two billing models depending on the type of app:

### RAM usage (for apps using App Plans)

For private apps where an **App Plan** is selected (e.g. .NET Web, Node.js, Nuxt.js, Redis), pricing is based on allocated RAM:

```
[hours running] x [instances running (if autoscaling)] x [hourly price for selected plan]
```

### Disk usage (for storage-based apps without App Plans)

For apps that **do not use App Plans**, such as **SQL Database** or **File Storage apps**, billing is based on actual disk usage:

```
[average disk usage per day] x [price per GB]
```

<Note>
  You do not need to select an App Plan for disk-based apps — they are billed entirely by storage consumption.
</Note>

### How to Select and Specify an App Plan

### For new app installations

1. **View Available Plans**

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud marketplace show --app <app-id>
   ```

2. **Edit manifest file**

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app <app-id>
   ```

3. **Specify Plan**: In the manifest file, locate the `plan:` property under the spec section. Insert the desired plan ID obtained from the previous step.

4. **Apply manifest**:

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud apply
   ```

### For already installed apps

For already installed apps it's also possible to change app plan with the "app plan" command.

1. **View available plans**:

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud marketplace show --app <app-id> 
   ```

2. **Apply a new plan**:

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud app plan --plan [insert-plan-id] --sub [insert-sub-id] --env [insert-env-id]
   ```

<Note>
  This will restart the application and apply the new plan right away (without any downtime).
</Note>


# Redis Cache
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/redis-cache

Enhance access speed with a private Redis Cache, connectable to .NET Web apps for efficient data retrieval. Costs are App plan-dependent.

### Pricing

Redis Cache is priced per hour based on app plan. [Read more about prices](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/pricing).

### Installation

**Prerequisites**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new environment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)

**Manifest**

Run following command to download redis-cache manifest:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app redis-cache -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Example manifest file:

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: redis-cache
spec:
  type: redis-cache
  version: 1.0.0
  plan:
```

**Manifest configuration**

**Id**: Choose your own unique-per-environment id of the app. Suggested "redis-cache".

To install a Redis Cache private app you need to provide a plan when creating the app. Pricing is based on which plan you select. Run following command to view available plans for Redis Cache app:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app redis-cache
```

Insert the plan-id you want after the "plan:" in the manifest file.

**Apply**

Run following command to install the redis-cache app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

* Fetch Subscription-id: `litium-cloud subscription list`
* Fetch Environment-id: `litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id`

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will create a Redis Cache app in the given environment.

### Connect with .NET Web app or Litium app

To be able to access your private Redis Cache app from a .NET web app or your Litium app you should add configuration in your .NET web or Litium manifest file.

Example configuration to connect a Redis Cache app with id "redis-cache" to your .NET web app. Note in this example the environment variables are named "CustomRedis\_\_Connectionstring" and "CustomRedis\_\_Password", this would replace any value in appsettings.json in the section "CustomRedis->Connectionstring" and "CustomRedis->Password":

```yaml theme={null}
configurations:
    - name: CustomRedis__Connectionstring
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: redis-cache
          key: connectionstring

    - name: CustomRedis__Password
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: redis-cache
          key: password
```


# Litium CDN
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-cdn

Litium CDN manages all incoming traffic to your apps. It should be the first app installed in an environment, as it automatically configures domains and access when other apps like Litium platform or Litium storefront are added.

Litium CDN uses Fastly as CDN. Apps that has a public\_domain property, such as Litium platform or Litium storefront, automatically gets an public\_domain assigned when created. If Litium CDN app is installed when apps that has public\_domain property are installed that domain is also configured in Litium CDN automatically. Without Litium CDN you won't be able to access your app through the public domain.

### Install

Maximum one Litium CDN app may be installed per environment. Read more about how to install Litium CDN app in the [getting started section](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-cdn).

### Logs

For logs during deploys/install/update you find those with the [status logs command](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).

### Image Optimizer

Image Optimizer (IO) is automatically activated for LCC. [Read more about IO](https://www.fastly.com/documentation/reference/io/).

### Find system generated public URLs for your apps

Use the "app show" command and look for the property "public\_domain\_name" in the section Exposes -> Value

### Add custom domain

To add your own custom domain to an app, install the app [Litium CDN domain](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-cdn-domain) to add custom domain(s).


# Litium CDN domain
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-cdn-domain

The Litium CDN domain app is used to add custom defined domain name for Litium CDN. One domain per app, so to add multiple domains, install multiple Litium CDN domain apps.

### Install

**Prerequirements**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)
* [Litium CDN app installed](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-cdn)

**Manifest**

Run following command to download litium-cdn-domain manifest:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-cdn-domain -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Example manifest file:

```powershell theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: litium-cdn-domain
spec:
  type: litium-cdn-domain
  version: 1.0.0
  properties:
    # The cluster domain name that public domain should use.
    - name: cluster_domain
    # The public domain name.
    - name: public_domain
```

**Manifest configuration**

Id: Choose your own unique-per-environment id of the app. Suggested "litium-cdn-domain"

Properties:

cluster\_domain: The internal domain that the public domain should point to. This should reference an existing apps exposed property "internal\_domain\_name", for instance, if you have an app with id "nextjs-web" that you want to point to, refer to that like this:

```powershell theme={null}
    - name: cluster_domain
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: nextjs-web
          key: internal_domain_name
    - name: public_domain
      value: mydomain.com
```

**Apply**

Run following command to install the litium-cdn-domain app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

\- Fetch Subscription-id: litium-cloud subscription list\
\- Fetch Environment-id: litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will create a Litium CDN domain app in the given environment, which will add the domain to Litium CDN.

<Note>
  This does not add any certificate for the domain, so if it is a new domain where certificate hasn't already been added by Litium support team, you need to contact support for help with adding certificate. You should also ask Litium support about how to setup DNS for your custom domain.
</Note>

<Note>
  To change properties you have to delete the app and install it again with your updated settings.
</Note>

<Note>
  One domain per app - so to add multiple, install multiple apps (with different id's).
</Note>

### Logs

For logs during deploys/install/update you find those with the [status logs command](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).


# Litium Insights
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-insights

Litium Insights is an essential service that allows you to view application logs, requests, and BI metrics. This tool is invaluable during both development and production workloads.

### Install

Maximum one Litium Insights app may be installed per environment. Read more about how to install Litium Insights app in the [getting started section](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-insights).

For logs during deploys/install/update you find those with the [status logs command](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).

### Login

After installing Litium Insights you access it through your browser at: [https://insights.litium.cloud](https://insights.litium.cloud)

Choose to login with "Serverless account". Use the same credentials you use to login to the CLI. If you dont have an account [you need to create one](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-litium-account).

### App Logs

Litium Insights automatically collects application and request logs from your applications in Serverless cloud. Once logged in to Insights you access your application logs through menu->Analytics->Dashboard->App Logs

<img alt="App logs menu navigation" />

The App Logs view lets you easily filter on different areas of interest, for instance app type, time span, log level and more.

<img alt="App logs filter options" />

### Access

To access **App Logs**, users must have:

* At least the role `subscription/reader` for the relevant subscription.
* At least the role `apps/litium-insights/insights-logs` for the Litium Insights application.

**Assigning Access**

**Give subscription reader access**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud subscription access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role subscription/reader
```

**Example 1** - **Grant access to all Insights apps within a subscription:**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud subscription access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role apps/litium-insights/insights-logs
```

**Example 2** - **Grant access to a specific Insights app:**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud app access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --env <your-environment> \
    --app <app-id> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role apps/litium-insights/insights-logs
```

### Request metrics

Litium Insights automatically collects requests to your applications. The request metrics section is accessed through menu->Analytics->Dashboard->Request metrics and lets you filter on various things like domain, time span, specific URL, etc.

### Access

To access **Request metrics**, users must have:

* At least the role `subscription/reader` for the relevant subscription.
* At least the role `apps/litium-insights/insights-logs` for the Litium Insights application.

**Assigning Access**

**Give subscription reader access**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud subscription access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role subscription/reader
```

**Example 1** - **Grant access to all Insights apps within a subscription:**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud subscription access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role apps/litium-insights/insights-logs
```

**Example 2** - **Grant access to a specific Insights app:**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud app access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --env <your-environment> \
    --app <app-id> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role apps/litium-insights/insights-logs
```

### BI Data

Litium Insights automatically collects BI data from your Litium platform application. The BI data section is accessed through menu->Analytics->Dashboard->Sales details and lets you filter on various things like time span, product, currency, etc.

### Access

To access **BI Data**, users must have:

* At least the role `subscription/reader` for the relevant subscription.
* At least the role `apps/litium-insights/insights-bi` for the Litium Insights application.
* **Insights Plus** must be enabled for the subscription. It is included by default for recent LCC customers. If BI Data is not visible, please contact [cs@litium.com](mailto:cs@litium.com) to update your agreement to the latest version, free of charge.

**Assigning Access**

**Give subscription reader access**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud subscription access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role subscription/reader
```

**Example 1** - **Grant access to all Insights apps within a subscription:**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud subscription access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role apps/litium-insights/insights-bi
```

**Example 2** - **Grant access to a specific Insights app:**

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud app access-control add \
    --subscription <your-subscription> \
    --env <your-environment> \
    --app <app-id> \
    --email <user-or-group-email> \
    --role apps/litium-insights/insights-bi
```

### Alerts (beta)

Depending on agreement type you may also be eligible to set up alerts in Litium Insights. You may set up alerts based on various criteria, such as number of errors of a specific type within a certain timespan, and more. To access and set up alerts, go to menu->Observability->Alerts


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-platform/overview

Litium platform serves as the hub for all applications within a Litium environment, automatically provisioning all the necessary infrastructure including databases, Redis, Litium Search, and more.

### Install

Maximum one Litium platform app may be installed per environment. Read more about how to install Litium platform app in the [getting started section](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-platform).

### Deployments

See [deploy artifact page](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/deploy-artifact) for how to deploy a new version.

Deployments to **production environments** are performed on a rolling scenario, meaning when you deploy the release artifacts the cloud automatically deploys the code to one replica at a time, letting users access the new version without downtime.

See the [automated deployments guide](/cloud/serverless/guides/automated-deployments) on examples how to automate deployments with the help of the CLI.

### Properties

For a detailed list of available properties, use the marketplace manifest command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-platform
```

Properties "artifact", "sql\_backup\_file" and "storage\_backup\_file" are described in more detail in the [install guide](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-platform).

"redis\_prefix" = Prefix all redis keys with this value. When prefix is changed the cache will be cleared.\
"auto\_patch" = auto\_patch is enabled by default and is not advised to turn off.

### Environment variables and secrets

Litium Serverless Cloud always uses appsettings.production.json (or only appsettings.json) for appsettings transformations, regardless of environment. To handle different environment variables you specify those values as configurations in your yaml-file, either in plain text (same value in all environments) or as secrets (to be able to have different values in different environments). [Read more about app configuration and secrets.](/cloud/serverless/guides/app-configuration-and-secrets)

### Actions

For a detailed list about which actions are available use the following command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app litium-platform --version add-version-here
```

### Backup database

Creates a database backup and stores the backup as an artifact for the current subscription.

See the guide "[Create database backup](/cloud/serverless/guides/create-database-backup)" for how to perform this action.

### Backup storage

Creates a storage backup and stores the backup as an artifact for the current subscription.

See the guide "[Create storage backup](/cloud/serverless/guides/create-storage-backup)" for how to perform this action.

### Console output

Gets console output from app in container. Normally those logs are sent to Litium Insights, but if your app doesn't start, issues may be printed to the console but never reach Litium Insights because the app hasn't started.

See the guide "[Output console logs](/cloud/serverless/guides/output-console-logs)" for how to perform this action.

### Execute SQL Script

Use with care, especially when performing updates, as these may result in outdated cache data. Be sure to refresh the cache programmatically or update the Redis prefix to reset all Redis cache. Remember, you are responsible for the scripts you run.

For detailed instructions, see the guide "[Execute SQL script](/cloud/serverless/guides/execute-sql-script)."

### Automate Litium platform setup

Beyond installing apps and environments, configuring the Litium platform often involves setting up domains, configuring payment apps, rebuilding the search index, and more. The following actions make it possible to automate all of this.

<Note>
  All below actions require the role **apps/litium-platform/litium-management** added for the user.
</Note>

**install-app**\
Installs an app, i.e. a payment or delivery app. Requires passing a url as parameter, `--property "url=apps-public-url"`

**uninstall-app**\
Uninstalls an app based on app id. Requires passing the id of the app, `--property "id=id-of-app"`. Additionally pass force flag to force deletion, `--property "force=true"`

**configure-app**\
Configure the app based on the id and path for config file. Requires id (app id) and path to config file, `--property "id=app-id" --property "path=file-path-to-config-file"`

**add-domain**\
Add a domain to Litium. Requires domain name to add, `--property "domain=domain-to-add"`

<Note>
  See app [Litium CDN domain](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-cdn-domain) for how to add custom domain to Litium CDN.
</Note>

**remove-domain**\
Remove a domain from Litium. Requires domain name to remove, `--property "domain=domain-to-remove"`

<Note>
  See app [Litium CDN domain](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-cdn-domain) for how to manage custom domains in Litium CDN.
</Note>

**replace-domain**\
Replace an existing domain with another in Litium. For instance if you have a domain name, mydomain.com, added in Litium connected to a channel, you can use this action to replace that domain with another domain (already added to Litium) to change channel domain mapping. Requires properties 'domain' and 'new\_domain': `--property "domain=domain-to-replace" --property "new_domain=new-domain"`

**rebuild-search-indicies**\
Trigger search indices rebuild. No properties.

### Logs

[Install Litium Insights app](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-insights) to get access to logs, metrics and BI-data.

For logs during deploys/install/update you find those with the [status logs command](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).


# Worker
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-platform/worker

To optimize performance in production environments, Litium background jobs now run automatically on a dedicated Worker Node, reducing the load on public nodes that serve web requests.

This feature is included at **no extra cost** in Litium Serverless Cloud, and is activated by default in environments marked as Production.

<Note>
  This does not replace the benefits of [private apps](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/overview) to integrate your custom workload such as integrations.
</Note>

### Requirements

* Environment is marked as production
* Litium version is 8.16.0 or higher

### What is a background job?

Following workloads will be executed automatically on the worker node:

* Scheduled jobs that have demand set as "worker" or execution restriction set as DisallowConcurrentDistributedExecution. [Read more about job scheduler](/platform/get-started/concepts).
* [ERP connect API](/apis/connect/overview)
* Backoffice background tasks - such as Excel export/import.


# Litium sFTP
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-sftp

With Litium sFTP app you create sFTP users that have access to specific folders in a File storage app.

### Pricing

Free

### Installation

**Prerequisites**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new environment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)
* [Storage app installed](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/file-storage)

**Manifest**

Run following command to download litium-sftp manifest:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-sftp -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Example manifest file:

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: sftp
spec:
  type: litium-sftp
  version: 1.0.0
  properties:
    # IP to whitelist. Possible to add up to 5 ips, separated by comma or line break.
    - name: ip
      value: 192.168.0.1,192.168.0.2
      or
      value: |-
        192.168.0.1
        192.168.0.2
```

**Manifest configuration**

**Id**: Choose your own unique-per-environment id of the app. Suggested "litium-sftp". Possible to install multiple instances of the sFTP app in an environment. Note that every instance needs its unique id.

**Properties**: The sFTP app has one property that needs to be set, that is "ip". Possible to whitelist up to 5 IPs. Either comma separated or new line, see manifest example above. Also possible to add range, but note that only 5 IPs can be whitelisted per sFTP app.

**Configuration section:**

An sFTP needs to be connected to at least one folder in a file storage app. It is possible for an sFTP app to access multiple folders. Below is an example where two folders are given access, with virtual names "integration" and "erp". If sub path doesn't already exist, it will be created.

```yaml theme={null}
  configurations:
    - name: integration
      subPath: integration
      type: storage
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: file-storage
          key: storage_volume
 
    - name: erp
      subPath: erp
      type: storage
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: file-storage
          key: storage_volume
```

**Example of full manifest file:**

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: sftp
spec:
  type: litium-sftp
  version: 1.0.0
  properties:
    # IP to whitelist. Possible to add up to 5 ips, separated by comma or line break.
    - name: ip
      value: 192.168.0.1,192.168.0.2

  configurations:
    - name: integration
      subPath: integration
      type: storage
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: file-storage
          key: storage_volume
 
    - name: erp
      subPath: erp
      type: storage
      valueFrom: 
        appRef:
          name: file-storage
          key: storage_volume
```

**Apply**

Run following command to install the litium-sftp app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

* Fetch Subscription-id: `litium-cloud subscription list`
* Fetch Environment-id: `litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id`

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will create an sFTP app in the given environment.

### Connect to sFTP with client

To view connection settings for the sFTP app after it is created, run the app show command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud app show --app sftp --env your-environment --sub your-subscription
```

This will output a section called "Exposes" where you will find three names of importance:

* **sftp\_hostname**: the hostname to connect to
* **sftp\_password**: the name of the secret, use following command to fetch value: `litium-cloud environment secret value --secret paste-secret-name-here`
* **sftp\_username**: the username to use to connect

Example output:

```powershell theme={null}
Exposes
=======
    Name               Description                                                     Type                  Value

    --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    sftp_hostname      The hostname for sFTP.                                          string                
    sftp_password      The password secret reference for the sFTP authentication.      secret-reference      
    sftp_username      The username for the sFTP authentication.                       string                
```

### Connect with Storage app

See manifest configuration above.


# Litium Storefront
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-storefront

Litium Storefront is a React-based, headless app that serves as the frontend for your site if you're using a headless architecture.

### Install

Maximum one Litium Storefront app may be installed per environment. Read more about how to install Litium Storefront app in the [getting started section](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-nextjs-storefront-app/overview).

Read more about the [React accelerator](/accelerators/react-accelerator/overview).

### Deployments

See [deploy artifact page](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/deploy-artifact) for how to deploy a new version.

Deployments to **production environments** are performed on a rolling scenario, meaning when you deploy the release artifacts the cloud automatically deploys the code to one replica at a time, letting users access the new version without downtime.

See the [automated deployments guide](/cloud/serverless/guides/automated-deployments) on examples how to automate deployments with the help of the CLI.

### Properties

For a detailed list of available properties, use the marketplace manifest command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-nextjs-web
```

Property "artifact" is described in more detail in the [install guide](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-nextjs-storefront-app/overview).

### Actions

For a detailed list about which actions are available use the following command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace show --app litium-nextjs-web --details --version add-version-here
```

### Console output

Gets console output from app in container. Normally those logs are sent to Litium Insights, but if your app doesn't start, issues may be printed to the console but never reach Litium Insights because the app hasn't started.

See the guide "[Output console logs](/cloud/serverless/guides/output-console-logs)" for how to perform this action.

### Logs

For logs during deploys/install/update you find those with the [status logs command](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).


# Litium Storefront Proxy
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-storefront-proxy

The Litium Storefront Proxy is a public app designed to route incoming web traffic efficiently to the appropriate backend services or the storefront application within the Litium Serverless Cloud environment.

### How it Works

The proxy routes traffic by fetching configuration details from a special endpoint provided by the Litium platform app:

```text theme={null}
https://<platform-url>/.well-known/litium/dev-proxy
```

### Example configuration

A sample response from the endpoint looks like:

```json theme={null}
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "items": [
    {"name": "Litium", "path": "litium/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumConnectPaymentsApi", "path": "litium/api/connect/payments/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumTeleport", "path": "litium/dist/teleport/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumWellKnown", "path": ".well-known/litium/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumGraphQL", "path": "storefront.graphql/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumStorage", "path": "storage/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumSitemap", "path": "sitemap.axd/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumPriceAgent", "path": "priceagent.axd/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumPriceAgentForAlternativeChannel", "path": "{path}/priceagent.axd/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumProductFeed", "path": "feed.axd/{**remainder}"},
    {"name": "LitiumRobots", "path": "robots.txt"}
  ]
}
```

Each configuration item specifies:

* **name**: Identifies the internal Litium service.
* **path**: Defines URL patterns that the proxy matches to forward requests correctly.

<Note>
  The proxy intentionally ignores the `Litium` item to avoid publicly exposing the backoffice URL (`/litium`). To access the Litium backoffice, use the public URL pointing directly to the Litium platform application.
</Note>

Requests for entries not found in the configuration will automatically be forwarded to the storefront application.

### Custom entries

The platform automatically sets up default proxy paths, like the example above. For example /storage for images etc.

But it is also possible to add your own paths if you have custom endpoints that should always be redirected to the Litium platform app. You do that by adding array entries to the appsettings.json in your Litium platform project, with the key `Litium:DevProxy:Items`:

**Example appsettings.json:**

```json theme={null}
  "Litium": {
    "DevProxy": {
      "Items": [
        {
          "Name": "CustomAPI",
          "Path": "api/{**remainder}"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
```

<Warning>
  If you add custom items you need to restart your Storefront Proxy app after the Litium platform has been deployed with your changes. Use the restart command to restart your Storefront Proxy app:
</Warning>

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud app restart --app [litium-storefront-proxy] --env [insert-env] --sub [insert-sub]
```

### Install

<Note>
  The Litium Storefront Proxy is automatically included when installing the "Litium nextjs web" public app, thus not requiring manual setup in that scenario. This app is only needed if you choose to use a private app such as next.js web, node.js web, or nuxt.js web as your storefront application.
</Note>

### To install the Litium Storefront Proxy

1. **Download manifest example**

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-storefront-proxy -f enter-any-name.yaml
   ```

   **Example**:

   ```yaml theme={null}
   kind: app
   resource:
     id: litium-storefront-proxy
   spec:
     type: litium-storefront-proxy
     version: 1.0.0
     properties:
       - name: storefront_internal_domain
         valueFrom:
           appRef:
             name: storefront-app
             key: internal_domain_name
   ```

2. **Edit manifest file:** Make sure the property "storefront\_internal\_domain" fetches its value from your storefront app you want to proxy traffic to.

3. **Install app**

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud apply --env [environment-id] --sub [subscription-id] -f [your-yaml-file.yaml]
   ```

### Accessing the storefront app

Once you have installed the Storefront Proxy app you access the storefront app through the public system domain of your storefront proxy app. Use the CLI to view the public system generated domain:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud app show --sub [insert id] --env [insert id] --app [insert storefront proxy app id]
```

### External domain

When configuring your public domain, ensure that it points to the Litium Storefront Proxy app. All incoming requests will automatically be evaluated by the proxy, ensuring correct routing based on the platform configuration.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/overview

Public apps are predefined apps with a specific purpose. Some public apps have no configuration options, and some apps has both configuration options and the possibility to upload artifacts, for instance the public app Litium platform where you upload your own code artifact, as well as storage and database. 
While many of the public apps are included in your subscription, such as Litium platform and Litium Insights, there may be other apps that you need a specific agreement to be able to install. There may also be other restrictions, for instance how many instances of an app you may install per environment. For public apps you don't specify an app plan, this is managed automatically for you by Litium.

### Commerce cloud apps

***

### [Litium CDN](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-cdn)

**Litium CDN** manages all incoming traffic to your apps. It should be the first app installed in an environment, as it automatically configures domains and access when other apps like Litium Platform or Litium Storefront are added. [Learn more about getting started with Litium CDN](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-cdn).

### [Litium insights](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-insights)

**Litium Insights** is an essential service that allows you to view application logs, requests, and BI metrics. This tool is invaluable during both development and production workloads. For more details on usage and setup, [Read more on how to use and get started with Litium insights](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-insights).

### [Litium platform](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-platform/overview)

The **Litium platform app** serves as the hub for all applications within a Litium environment. This app automatically provisions all the necessary infrastructure to run Litium, including databases, Redis, Litium Search, and more. Note that only one Litium Platform App can be installed per environment. To learn more about the installation process, [read more about how to install Litium platform](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-platform).

### [Litium sFTP](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-sftp)

**Litium SFTP** enables external access to your File Storage app via sFTP, supporting user-specific or folder-specific configurations.

### [Litium SMTP relay](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/smtp-relay-app)

To send emails, you need to specify an SMTP relay. You can either use your own host or opt for the Litium serverless cloud SMTP server.

### [Litium storefront](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-storefront)

**Litium Storefront** is a React-based, headless app that serves as the frontend for your site if you're using a headless architecture. Only one Litium Storefront can be installed per environment. To learn more about the installation process, [read more about how to install Litium storefront](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-nextjs-storefront-app/overview).

### Delivery and payment apps

***

# SMTP relay app
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/smtp-relay-app

To send email you need to specify a SMTP relay. You can choose to specify your own host or to use Litium Serverless Cloud SMTP server.

**Prerequisites**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new environment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)
* Customer app created, for example [Litium platform](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-platform)

### Install and configure Litium SMTP relay app

Run following command to download SMTP relay manifest yaml:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-smtp -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

**Use Litium Serverless Cloud SMTP server**

If you want to use Litium Serverless Cloud SMTP server you don't have to configure anything in the manifest yaml-file. The Litium Serverless Cloud SMTP should only be used to send order confirmation emails and similar transaction emails. Should NOT be used to send mass emails. Also note that this is a shared SMTP server that is used by multiple customers therefore the "mail server reputation" may be affected. **We recommend setting up an own external customer specific SMTP** service to avoid this.

If you choose to use Litium Serverless Cloud SMTP, you need to add `"mail3.litiumdrift.se"` to the SPF record **for the domain you're setting as the sender**.

For example, if you're sending emails from `info@yourcompany.com`, you need to update the SPF record for `yourcompany.com` like this:

```
v=spf1 include:mail3.litiumdrift.se
```

If you already have an SPF record, just add the `include:mail3.litiumdrift.se` part to it. For example:

```
v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:mail3.litiumdrift.se
```

<Warning>
  The Litium SMTP is a basic mail service. Litium does not take any responsibility for delivery of mail when using the SMTP service. The service does not have support for TLS or more advanced features like DKIM. If mail is a critical functionality, we recommend configuring Litium to use your own mail service such as Office 365, Gmail suite or Sendgrid.
</Warning>

**Configure an external SMTP server**

To configure an external SMTP server, e.g. Gmail, O365, Sendgrid etc. you should specify that in the properties in the manifest file:

```yaml theme={null}
  # properties:
  #   # Custom smtp host, if not provided Litium Cloud outgoing SMTP will be used.
  #   - name: smtp_host
  #     value: smtp.sendgrid.net:587
  #   # Custom smtp host password.
  #   - name: smtp_password
  #     value: pAsSwOrD
  #   # Custom smtp host username.
  #   - name: smtp_username
  #     value: apikey
```

<Note>
  You may also use secrets instead of plain text for the values. [Read more about secrets.](/cloud/serverless/guides/app-configuration-and-secrets)
</Note>

**Install the app**

Run following command to apply the Litium SMTP relay app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

* Fetch Subscription-id: `litium-cloud subscription list`
* Fetch Environment-id: `litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id`

### Connect Litium SMTP relay app with your Storefront app

When your Litium SMTP relay app is installed you should modify properties for your customer app to use the SMTP relay. Below is an example of how to configure a Litium Storefront app with id "storefront" to your SMTP app with id "smtp":

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: storefront
spec:
  type: litium-nextjs-web # or nextjs-web

  configurations:
    - name: RUNTIME_SMTP_HOST
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_host

    - name: RUNTIME_SMTP_PORT
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_port
  
    - name: RUNTIME_SMTP_SECURE
      value: "false"

    - name: RUNTIME_SMTP_AUTH_USER
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_auth_username

    - name: RUNTIME_SMTP_AUTH_PASS
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_auth_password
```

### Connect Litium SMTP relay app with your Litium Platform MVC app

For the default MVC accelerator the default config names in appsettings.json is:

```json theme={null}
"Accelerator": {  
    "Smtp": {  
        "Host": "",  
        "Port": "",  
        "Password": "",  
        "Username": "",  
        "EnableSecureCommunication": false  
    }  
}
```

To use the default appsettings.json keys your manifest configuration file should look like this, assuming the id of your installed SMTP app is "smtp":

```yaml theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: litium
spec:
  type: litium-platform

  configurations:
    - name: LITIUM__ACCELERATOR__SMTP__HOST
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_host

    - name: LITIUM__ACCELERATOR__SMTP__PORT
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_port
  
    - name: LITIUM__ACCELERATOR__SMTP__ENABLESECURECOMMUNICATION
      value: "false"

    - name: LITIUM__ACCELERATOR__SMTP__USERNAME
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_auth_username

    - name: LITIUM__ACCELERATOR__SMTP__PASSWORD
      valueFrom:
        appRef:
          name: smtp
          key: smtp_auth_password
```


# FAQ
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/faq



### How can I restart my app?

To restart an app you use the "app restart" command. This will trigger a rolling restart of your app.

### Issue when logging in - "Your connection is not private"

If you get SSL errors like "Your connection is not private" when trying to log in it may be because you have a local hsts setup for localhost - this could for instance be caused by running a local aspnet core website with incorrect settings.

The solution is to remove the local hsts rule for localhost. For chrome, do this:

1. Search for chrome://net-internals/#hsts in your address bar.
2. Locate the Query HSTS/PKP domain field and type "localhost".
3. Hit the button "Query"
4. If you see results then it means you need to remove your local security policies for localhost, proceed to step 5
5. Finally, enter the domain name in the Delete domain security policies and simply press the Delete button.
6. Login should now work.

See [https://www.ssl2buy.com/wiki/how-to-clear-hsts-settings-on-chrome-firefox-and-ie-browsers](https://www.ssl2buy.com/wiki/how-to-clear-hsts-settings-on-chrome-firefox-and-ie-browsers) for instructions for other browsers.

### Issue with "File not found" from logs

Litium serverless cloud arhitecture is built on \*nix. Which means that file references is case sensitive. For example if you have a folder structure with capital letters like "Folder/SubFolder/myfile.config" you also need to specify the path in code with the same case.

### Issue with CLI update

If you are getting below error when trying to update/install the CLI it may be because the username and password for the litium nuget feed is incorrect. To resolve that, remove the nuget feed with dotnet nuget remove command and then add it back with `dotnet nuget add source https://nuget.litium.com/nuget/ -n Litium -u username -p password`

error NU1301: Failed to\
retrieve information about 'litium.cloud.cli' from remote source '[https://nuget.litium.com/nuget/FindPackagesById()?id](https://nuget.litium.com/nuget/FindPackagesById\(\)?id)\
\='litium.cloud.cli'\&semVerLevel=2.0.0'.\
Tool 'litium.cloud.cli' failed to update due to the following:\
The tool package could not be restored.

### How to change Redis prefix on my Litium app?

If you want to change Redis prefix on your Litium app you modify your manifest.yaml file for your litium app the property is called "redis\_prefix". The value will serve as the new prefix. To apply the changes you perform the "apply" command that will trigger an update on the app.

<Warning>
  Changing Redis prefix will wipe all current data stored in Redis, including customer current carts. Changing Redis prefix should only be used as a last resort if you have a mismatch between your Redis and database.
</Warning>

<Tip>
  To get your current yaml-file use the command litium-cloud app show -o manifest , and add the redis\_prefix property according to the example below.
</Tip>

Example Yaml:

```powershell theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: ...
spec:
  type: litium-platform
  version: ...
  properties:
    - name: redis_prefix
      value: rev2
... rest of your properties and artifact-references
```

### How to change Elastic prefix on my Litium app?

To generate a new index name go to Settings->Litium Search->Indices in Backoffice and click on "Rebuild index offline", this creates a new index name and the old one is removed. The Elastic prefix is therefore not possible to configure in appsettings.json in Serverless Cloud, since it's not needed.

### What is the limit of upload size (body size)?

Limits of file upload size (body size) is based on best practice to avoid risk of attacks etc. Therefore the current limit of upload size is 100 mb. If you have larger files than that you should split your file to chunks and upload one at the time.


# Create environment
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new

Prerequirements

**Prerequirements**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new enviornment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)

**Create an enviornment**

To create an environment, run following command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud environment create --name enter-name --subscription enter-subscription --location enter-location-id
```

Fetch location-id: `litium-cloud location list`\
Fetch subscription-id: `litium-cloud subscription list`

Tips for environment name could be prod/test/qa/demo/staging etc.

### Production environment

For production environments you should include flag "--production" when creating the environment. This will mark the environment as production environment and make sure the correct production resources are applied to your production Litium apps.

<Warning>
  All non-production environments and system domain *litium.app* will automatically get robots directives set to noindex and nofollow.
</Warning>

It is also possible to set production flag after the environment is created, this is done with the 'litium-cloud environment update --production' command. **Important** if litium app and storefront apps are already installed when setting the production flag, the apps needs to be restarted or redeployed for the changes to take effect.

To unset an environment as production you use the 'litium-cloud environment update --non-production' command


# Create Litium Account
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-litium-account

Serverless Cloud and Litium Insights for Serverless Cloud uses accounts in Litium Account to authenticate and login. Note - this is not the same as the docs-account, so if you haven't logged into Serverless Cloud or Litium Insights for subscriptions in Serverless Cloud before you most likely don't have an account and need to create one. Having a Litium Account is needed to be able to login to Serverless Cloud CLI and to view logs and BI data for Litium Insights for subscriptions in Serverless Cloud.

### Permissions

**Important** - to be able to view subscriptions and/or login and view logs and BI-data in Litium Insights you also need the correct permissions setup. Do this **before** you create your account do avoid error messages like unauthorized.

**Subscriptions** - When a subscription is created Litium Support will give access to the subscription. Then the partner will themselves manage access to additional users. [Read more about access to subscriptions](/cloud/serverless/guides/access/overview).

**Litium Insights** - To give a user permission to Litium insights (logs and/or BI-data) [read more about which access that should be assigned](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-insights). **Important** - access should be added before the user signs up and try to login

### Create account

1. You start the create account flow by either using the CLI authorizing with command litium-cloud auth login (that will open a browser) or by choosing to login with "Litium Account (Serverless)" on the [Litium Insights login page](https://insights.litium.cloud/). Example from Insights\\
   <img alt="" />

2. Choose "Sign up now" at the bottom of the next dialog\\
   <img alt="" />

3. At the next screen, enter your e-mail address and click "Send verification code"\\
   <img alt="" />

4. Check your inbox for an email similar to below, find and copy code\\
   <img alt="" />

5. Paste the code and click "Verify code"\\
   <img alt="" />

6. Above email address it now should state "E-mail address verified. You can now continue."\\
   <img alt="" />

7. Choose a password and click "Create"\\
   <img alt="" />

8. Setup 2f authentication by scanning the QR code by authenticator app of your choice\\
   <img alt="" />

9. On the next screen, verify your authenticator setup by entering your code from your authenticator app anc click "Verify"\\
   <img alt="" />

10. All set - you now have your Litium Account

### Troubleshooting

* Can't log in to Litium Insights - getting "You do not have permission..." error - this means that your account doesnt have permissions setup for any subscription in Litium Serverless Cloud. Fix by adding access according to specifications for the [Insights app](/cloud/serverless/apps/public-apps/litium-insights) or talk to your partner for them to give you access.

# Getting started with Cloud CLI
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli

Prerequirements

### Set up Litium cloud CLI

**Prerequirements**

* Docs account, created via [Docs](/cloud/serverless/overview)
* [NET Core 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/8.0)
* Nuget:

With your Docs account, configure Litium NuGet with following command:

```powershell theme={null}
dotnet nuget add source https://nuget.litium.com/nuget/ -n Litium -u docsusername -p docspassword
```

**Install/update Cloud CLI**\
Cloud CLI tool is named litium-cloud, run following command to install / update the tool:

```powershell theme={null}
dotnet tool update -g litium.cloud.cli --no-cache
```

**Log into Litium cloud CLI**

Run following command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud auth login 
```

A browser will open with a login prompt, login with your Litium Account (serverless) login or choose 'Sign up now' to [create a new account.](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-litium-account)

<Note>
  The Litium Account login is NOT the same as your docs-login. If this is your first time working with Litium Cloud CLI you most probably don't have an account and should select 'Sign up now'.
</Note>

<Note>
  If you get errors like "Your connection is not private" when trying to log in it may be because you have a local hsts setup for localhost - this could for instance be caused by running a local aspnet core website with incorrect settings. [See our FAQ page for how to fix this.](/cloud/serverless/faq)
</Note>

### View subscriptions

Subscriptions are created by Litium. To gain access to a subscription, contact Litium support.\
To see which subscriptions you have access to, run following command:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud subscription list
```

With Litium Serverless Cloud you are in charge of [installing, deleting and updating the payment and delivery apps](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-payment-and-delivery-apps) you need.

### Install private app(s)

Except deploying and running the Litium Platform, Next.Js storefront and other public apps in Litium Serverless Cloud it is also possible to deploy and run private apps. For instance if you have the need of extra storage with an additional Sftp. [See availalable private apps.](/cloud/serverless/apps/private-apps/overview)

### Automate deployments

To use the CLI in a deployment pipeline you should use a [service principal to login and authenticate](/cloud/serverless/guides/service-principal).

### Access control and user management

You should configure [Access control](/cloud/serverless/guides/access/access-control) to manage who should have which access to different resources. [Groups](/cloud/serverless/guides/access/group) is a convenient way to handle access for multiple users.

### Logs and metrics

To view logs and other metrics for your apps, [use Litium Logs & Insights](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-insights).


# Install Litium CDN
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-cdn

Prerequirements

**Prerequirements**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new enviornment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)

**Install Litium CDN**

Run following command to download litium-cdn yaml:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-cdn -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Run following command to apply the litium-cdn to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

\- Fetch Subscription-id: litium-cloud subscription list\
\- Fetch Environment-id: litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

This will create a Fastly CDN service for that environment.

**Additional Fastly configuration**

If you need to do additional fastly configuration you need access to the Fastly service. Reach out to [support@litium.com](mailto:support@litium.com) and include the subscription and environment you want Fastly access for. For instance if you want to add a custom domain.

<Note>
  Fastly Service access is not required to setup Litium and other apps in Serverless Cloud. When you have installed the Litium CDN app system domain names for other apps will be configured automatically for your service in Fastly.
</Note>


# Install Litium Insights
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-insights

Litium Insights is a service where you can view application logs, https requests and BI metrics. What you see is depending on the customer agreement. To access Litium Insights for your environment data the Litium Insights app should be installed.

**Prerequirements**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new enviornment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)

**Install Litium Insights**

Run following command to download litium-insights yaml:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-insights -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

Run following command to apply the litium-insights to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f enter-yaml-filename
```

\- Fetch Subscription-id: litium-cloud subscription list\
\- Fetch Environment-id: litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

**Login to Litium Insight**

Browse to [Insights](https://insights.litium.cloud/login?next=%2F) and choose to login with "Litium Account (serverless)", use same account as you use for Litium Serverless Cloud. Application logs and other metrics for your environment is present after logged in.

**Add access to other users**

For a user to have access to Insight for a particular environment they need to be [granted access control](/cloud/serverless/guides/access/access-control) to the Insights application. To get access to Ingishts a user needs to have at least the role "system/reader" to the subscription and at least the role "system/contributor" to the Insights app.

Best practice is to [add a group](/cloud/serverless/guides/access/group), e.g. "Insights users". And give that group [access](/cloud/serverless/guides/access/access-control) to the subscription with the role "system/reader" and access to the insights app with the role "system/contributor". Then add all members that should have access to that group.


# Install Litium Platform
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-platform

Prerequirements

**Prerequirements**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to install Litium Platform](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)
* [Litium CDN installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-cdn)

### Download and install Litium platform yaml

Run following command to download litium-platform.yaml:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-platform -f enter-any-name.yaml
```

<Note>
  This will generate a yaml-file in the current folder you are in.
</Note>

### (optional) Include release artifact

You can include your own dotnet artifact while installing the Litium platform. To do so follow those steps:

1. [Create release artifact of type "dotnet"](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/create-dotnet-artifact)
2. In the manifest yaml-file downloaded from the marketplace manifest-command, do the following:
   1. Uncomment "properties"
   2. Uncomment the property "artifact"
   3. Add "artifacts/" followed by your artifact-id as "value" for the "artifact" property, e.g. "value: artifacts/d33ae52bb7044adb99d2b4df6fac6216"

<Note>
  It is possible to deploy dotnet-artifacts to the Litium app continiously after the app is installed with the [deploy command](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/deploy-artifact).
</Note>

<Note>
  If you don't reference a sql backup the database will be installed with the same db version as in the dotnet artifact.
</Note>

<Note>
  If you don't reference an artifact or sql backup the latest version of Litium will be installed together with latest database.
</Note>

<Note>
  If you don't reference an artifact and the app is already installed, the current existing artifact will continue to be used.
</Note>

### (optional) Include SQL Backup

You can include your own database while installing the Litium platform. To do so follow those steps:

1. [Create SQL Backup artifact](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/create-sql-backup-artifact)
2. In the manifest yaml-file downloaded from the marketplace manifest-command, do the following
   1. Uncomment "properties"
   2. Uncomment the property "sql\_backup\_file"
   3. Add "artifacts/" followed by your artifact-id as "value" for the "sql\_backup\_file" property, e.g. "value: artifacts/d33ae52bb7044adb99d2b4df6fac6216"

<Warning>
  It's not possible to upload your SQL Backup to your app after the installation is done. In that case you need to remove the Litium App and install it again.
</Warning>

<Note>
  If you don't reference an artifact or sql backup the latest version of Litium will be installed together with latest database.
</Note>

### (optional) Include storage

You can include your own storage whild installing the Litium platform. To do so follow those steps:

1. [Create Storage artifact](/cloud/serverless/guides/artifacts/create-storage-backup-artifact)
2. In the manifest yaml-file downloaded from the marketplace manifest-command, do the following
   1. Uncomment "properties"
   2. Uncomment the property "storage\_backup\_file"
   3. Add "artifacts/" followed by your artifact-id as "value" for the "storage\_backup\_file" property, e.g. "value: artifacts/d33ae52bb7044adb99d2b4df6fac6216"

<Warning>
  It's not possible to upload your storage files to your app after the installation is done. In that case you need to remove the Litium App and install it again.
</Warning>

### Redis and Elastic Search prefix

Read more on the [FAQ page](/cloud/serverless/faq) on how to modify prefix for Redis and Elastic search

### Run following command to install Litium platform:

<Note>
  Before installing Litium Platform, make sure you have [installed Litium CDN app](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-cdn). If you haven't done this your Litium App will not be automatically configured in Litium CDN.
</Note>

litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f name-of-generated-yaml-file

\- Fetch Subscription-id: litium-cloud subscription list\
\- Fetch Environment-id: litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

Optional, view installed app(s) with command: litium-cloud app list --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id

### Find URL to the Litium platform

Run following command to find URL/domain to your Litium platform under Exposes -> Value:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud app show --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id --app litium
```

Copy value from the name "public\_domain\_name"

Open a browser and go to the URL/domain with /Litium at the end to get to Backoffice login prompt.

**Default login (if no custom database was specified during install)**\
Username: Admin\
Password: Password!

# Name change of Litium nextjs web app with GA Release
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-nextjs-storefront-app/name-change-of-litium-nextjs-web-app-with-ga-release

With the General Availability (GA) release of Litium serverless cloud a breaking change was made that changed the type id of this app from nextjs-storefront to litium-nextjs-web. Read more below how to handle this.

### Migrate from old type to new

If you have deployed Nextjs web apps with the old type "nextjs-storefront" you have to install new apps with the new type "litium-nextjs-web".  This can be done without any downtime by following below instructions.

1. Download manifest with command 'litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app litium-nextjs-web -f manifest.yaml'
2. Add same artifact as you use in your old app
3. Apply (install) app with the apply command
4. Change domain in Litium app so that backoffice is communicating with the new app
5. Optional. If you have custom domains configured in fastly those should be changed to point to your new app.
6. Once the new app is working, delete the old app.

# Install Payment and Delivery apps
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-payment-and-delivery-apps

Payment and delivery apps are available as public apps.

**Prerequirements**

* [CLI installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Access to the subscription where you want to create a new enviornment](/cloud/serverless/get-started/getting-started-with-cloud-cli)
* [Environment created](/cloud/serverless/get-started/create-environment-new)
* [Litium Platform installed](/cloud/serverless/get-started/install-litium-platform)

**Install Payment and Delivery apps**

Find available Payment and delivery apps with search command

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace list --filter payment
```

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace list --filter shipment
```

Run 'marketplace manifest' command to download manifest file used for installing the app, example command to download the direct payment app manifest file to the current folder you're in:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace manifest --app direct-payment -f direct-payment.yaml
```

<Note>
  When generating the manifest file you could also specify the option --version to request a specific version to install when you apply the  manifest file with the apply-command below. To view available version for an app, add the --details option to the search command, for example to get all available versions for the direct-payment app:
</Note>

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud marketplace list --filter 'direct payment' --details
```

<Warning>
  If you don't specify version is the manifest file, the default version is selected when installing the app. For payment apps it may be a good routine to always specify which version you want to install so you can control testing and upgrade.
</Warning>

Run following command to install the direct-payment app to environment:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id -f direct-payment.yaml
```

\- Fetch Subscription-id: litium-cloud subscription list\
\- Fetch Environment-id: litium-cloud environment list --subscription enter-subscription-id

<Note>
  After running the apply command, there will be a prompt with a job-id that you can use to [view status and logs of the job](/cloud/serverless/guides/view-status-and-logs).
</Note>

**Install app to Litium app**

Once the payment or delivery app is installed in your environment you may install it to your Litium app.

1. Get the url to your newly installed payment or delivery app by executing the app show command, for example to get url to an installed direct payment app with id direct-payment:

   ```powershell theme={null}
   litium-cloud app show --app direct-payment --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id
   ```

   This will display a table with name "Exposes" that has a row with name "public\_domain\_name" property.

2. Copy the value of "public\_domain\_name" and browse to that url. This will redirect you to your litium app. You may need to login with your litium app credentials. Once logged in the app is created in your Litium app.

3. Press the "install" button at the top of the page to install the app to Litium.

4. Upload your custom configuration-json file to apply your custom solution settings

**Upgrade app**

To upgrade your payment or delivery app to a new version you change your apps manifest to include a later version of your app, and execute the apply command.

For example, let's say you are using the version 1.0.0 in your current installation, the manifest-file you used to installed the app may look like this:

```csharp theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: direct-payment
spec:
  type: direct-payment
  version: 1.0.0
```

Now, you want to upgrade your app to version 1.3.0, then you change the version so the file now looks like this:

```csharp theme={null}
kind: app
resource:
  id: direct-payment
spec:
  type: direct-payment
  version: 1.3.0
```

When you apply the new manifest file the app is upgraded, the command could look like:

```powershell theme={null}
litium-cloud apply -f direct-payment.yaml --subscription enter-subscription-id --environment enter-environment-id
```

**Downgrade app**

To downgrade an app to an earlier version you need to first delete your app and then reinstall with the old version. I.e. it is nott possible to downgrade without first deleting the app and reinstalling.
