# Calculating VAT
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/calculating-vat

In default, implementation VAT is calculated using EU VAT regulations.

Projects may implement other VAT rules for other markets.

## EU VAT regulations

VAT calculation for ECommerce is implemented following EU VAT regulations, for common business scenarios.

1. Default implementation supports items of multiple VAT bands in a single order.
2. Exceptions and special rules are not implemented, and projects will need to implement them if the merchant's business qualifies for special VAT rules and exceptions.

### Vat Calculation

The Vat attributed to a product is taken from the "tax class" of the product, for the country in which the order is originating. That is, the country of the website, and the connected "tax class".

## Implementing VAT rules

To implement VAT rules, override the *IVatRuleFactory* class using the [service decorator pattern](/platform/architecture/dependency-injection/service-decorator), and implement a *IVatRule*.

VAT should be calculated for the whole order. Also, new row totals should be calculated. After implementation, the following conditions should always be true:

1. "unit price including VAT" x Quantity = "Total price including VAT"
2. "Total price including VAT" = "Total excluding VAT" + "Total VAT"

### Example 1

Following is an example, where a different VAT rule is used, if the buyer is from Texas!

```csharp theme={null}
[Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection.ServiceDecorator(typeof(IVatRuleFactory))]
internal class CustomVatRuleFactory : IVatRuleFactory
{
    private IVatRuleFactory _parent;
    private readonly IVatRule _texasSalesTaxRule;

    public CustomVatRuleFactory(IVatRuleFactory parent, TexasSalesTaxRule texasSalesTaxRule)
    {
        _parent = parent; // impl instance of type MyServiceImpl
        _texasSalesTaxRule = texasSalesTaxRule;
    }
    
        public IVatRule Create<T>(Order<T> order) where T : OrderRow
        {
            if(!string.IsNullOrEmpty(order?.BillingAddress?.Country))
            {
                if(order.BillingAddress.Country == "US") 
                {
                // TODO: check customer is from Texas!
                    return _texasSalesTaxRule;
                }               
            }            
            return _parent.Create(order); //Use default rule.
        }
}

/// <summary>
///  Calculates Texas Sales Tax
/// </summary>
[Service(ServiceType = typeof(TexasSalesTaxRule))]
public class TexasSalesTaxRule : IVatRule
{
    public void CalculateVat<T>(Order<T> order)
        where T : OrderRow
    {
        //Calculate sales tax for Texas!

    }
}
```

### Example 2

Sometimes, the default VAT rule should be applied, and then the calculated VAT need to be modified. This is useful, if you would only like to modify certain values.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Sales.Calculator;
using Litium.Sales;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.PriceRules
{

    [Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection.ServiceDecorator(typeof(IVatRuleFactory))]
    public class SalesTaxCalculatorFactory : IVatRuleFactory
    {
        private IVatRuleFactory _parent;
        public SalesTaxCalculatorFactory(IVatRuleFactory parent)
        {
            _parent = parent; 
        }

        public IVatRule Create<T>(Order<T> order) where T : OrderRow
        {
            //Create the default rule.
            var prorataVatRule = _parent.Create(order);

            //we pass the default rule when creating our own rule, so we can use the default rule first.
            var salesTaxRule = new SalesTaxRules(prorataVatRule);          
            return salesTaxRule;
        }         
    }

    public class SalesTaxRules : IVatRule
    {
        private IVatRule _prorataVatRule;
        public SalesTaxRules() { }
        public SalesTaxRules(IVatRule prorataVatRule)
        {
            _prorataVatRule =prorataVatRule;
        }
        public void CalculateVat<T>(Order<T> order) where T : OrderRow
        {
            //Use the default pro-rata calculator to initialize the VAT.
            _prorataVatRule.CalculateVat(order);

            //Apply the additional taxes.
            ApplySalesTax(order);
        }

        private static void ApplySalesTax<T>(Order<T> order) where T : OrderRow
        {
            //Todo: Apply sales tax.
        }
    }
}
```

## Tracking details about VAT calculation

After VAT calculation, orders keep track of VAT, the amount including VAT for each VAT rate.

If the sum of VAT or the amount including VAT is not matching the total VAT or the total including VAT, the rounding off is added in the VAT details.

An example of the VAT details for a row:

```json theme={null}
{
  "description": "Order discount 10% when buying over 4000 SEK",
  "quantity": 1.0,
  "unitPriceIncludingVat": -930.19,
  "unitPriceExcludingVat": -834.03,
  "vatRate": 0.1153,
  "totalIncludingVat": -930.19, 
  "totalExcludingVat": -834.03,
  "totalVat": -96.16,
  "vatDetails": [
      {
          "vatRate": 0.2500,
          "amountIncludingVat": -159.79,
          "vat": -16.51
      },
      {
          "vatRate": 0.1200,
          "amountIncludingVat": -350.60,
          "vat": -36.23
      },
      {
          "vatRate": 0.0600,
          "amountIncludingVat": -419.80,
          "vat": -43.38
      },
      {
          "vatRate": 1.0,
          "amountIncludingVat": 0.00,
          "vat": -0.04
      }
  ]
}
```

***NOTE:*** *The record containing "vatRate: 1.0" is the rounding off. Also the currency's minor unit is used for calculation.*


# Buy X products, get discount on the cheapest
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/discounts/buy-x-products-get-discount-on-the-cheapest

How the discount is applied.

When merchants use this discount type, they first select to which product list the discount should be applied. 

When the buyer uses the discount, the discount amount will be calculated by the system grouping variants by the amount selected in the discount. The most profitable discount for the customer will be chosen by the system. 

### Case study 1

A merchant creates a discount of the type Buy X products, get a discount on the cheapest, by applying it to a product list as buy 2 product items from the list, get one of the items for free. 

1. A customer uses the discount by purchasing 2 items of Product A from the list, and 1 item of Product B from the list:

   * Product A costs 200 SEK.
   * Product A costs 200 SEK.
   * Product B costs 100 SEK.

2. The system then groups the three variants in pairs of 2 items:

   * Group 1 = Product A1 + Product A2, lowest price 200 SEK
   * Group 2 = Product A1 + Product B, lowest price 100 SEK
   * Group 3 = Product A2 + Product B, lowest price 100 SEK

3. The system finds the group which has the most beneficial discount for the customer, resulting in the discount price of Group 1. 

4. The discount given to the customer is 200 SEK. 

### Case study 2

A merchant creates a discount of the type Buy X products, get a discount on the cheapest, by applying it to a product list as buy 3 product items from the list, get one of the items for free. 

1. A customer uses the discount by purchasing 2 items of Product C from the list, and 1 item of Product D from the list:

   * Product C costs 500 SEK.
   * Product C costs 500 SEK.
   * Product D costs 300 SEK.

2. The system then groups the three variants in pairs of 3 items:

Product C1 + Product C2 + Product D, lowest price 300 SEK

3. The discount given to the customer is 300 SEK.


# Buy X products, get discount on the most expensive
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/discounts/buy-x-products-get-discount-on-the-most-expensive

How the discount is applied.

When merchants use this discount type, they first select to which product list the discount should be applied. 

When the buyer uses the discount, the discount amount will be calculated by the system grouping variants by the amount selected in the discount. The most profitable discount for the customer will be chosen by the system. 

### Case study 1

A merchant creates a discount of the type Buy X products, get a discount on the most expensive, by applying it to a product list as buy 2 product items from the list, get one of the items for free. 

1. A customer uses the discount by purchasing 2 items of Product A from the list, and 1 item of Product B from the list:

   * Product A costs 200 SEK.
   * Product A costs 200 SEK.
   * Product B costs 100 SEK.

2. The system then groups the three variants in pairs of 2 items:

   * Group 1 = Product A1 + Product A2, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 200 SEK
   * Group 2 = Product A1 + Product B, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 100 SEK
   * Group 3 = Product A2 + Product B, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 100 SEK

3. The system finds the group which has the most beneficial discount for the customer, resulting in the discount price of Group 2. 

4. The discount given to the customer is 200 SEK. 

### Case study 2

A merchant creates a discount of the type Buy X products, get a discount on the most expensive, by applying it to a product list as buy 2 product items from the list, get one of the items for free. 

1. A customer uses the discount by purchasing 2 items of Product A from the list, and 2 items of Product B from the list. 

   * Product A.1: 200 SEK
   * Product A.2: 200 SEK
   * Product B.1: 100 SEK
   * Product B.2: 100 SEK

2. The system then groups the four variants in a pair of 2 items, because the discount applies when a minimum of 2 items are selected. Item that already used for discount will be exclude out of the next group:

   * Group 1 = Product A.1 + Product A.2, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 200 SEK
   * Group 2 = Product A.1 + Product B.1, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 100 SEK
   * Group 3 = Product A.1 + Product B.2, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 100 SEK
   * Group 4 = Product A.2 + Product B.1, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 100 SEK
   * Group 5 = Product A.2 + Product B.2, highest price 200 SEK, lowest price 100 SEK
   * Group 6 = Product B.1 + Product B.2, highest price 100 SEK, lowest price 100 SEK

3. The system applies the discount to groups that give the most beneficial discount to the customer, which is Group 2 and 5. 

4. The discount given to the customer is (200 x 2) SEK.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/discounts/overview

This section explains how discounts are handled.

Discounts are configured using Litium backoffice. See [more about discounts in the Litium user guide](/help/litium-8/sales/campaigns/discounts). They are represented as order rows with the type Discount. See [more about order rows under Field framework](/platform/guides/data-modelling). Discounts are automatically calculated in Litium API. The calculation can not be overridden.

[Discount types and priority](#discount-types-and-priority)

[Discount codes](#discount-codes)

[Threshold](#threshold)

[Discount limitation](#discount-limitation)

[Historical best price](#historical-best-price)

<h3>
  Discount types and priority
</h3>

Litium supports all discount types below. When more than one discount is active and valid for the cart, the following order of priority is used:

1. External discount (applied as Discounted product price discount type).

2. Product discounts: 

* Discounted product price  
* Product amount discount 
* Product percentage discount 
* Product group discounts, like Mix and match or Buy X and get a discount on the cheapest. 

3. Order level amount discount

4. Order level percentage discount

5. Shipment fee discount and payment fee discount

6. Free gifts

When multiple discounts with the same priority exist, the system will choose the one with the highest value. Only one product discount can be applied per product instance (A product with quantity 4 is calculated as 4 product instances). All product discounts are evaluated together. Discounted product price, product amount and product percentage discount are evaluated together with Buy X discounts. A discount can also be set as not allowed to combine with other discounts or only allowed to combine with one or more specific discounts.

### External discounts

The system supports receiving discounted product prices from external systems and applying them to products during a buyer's session. These discounts are automatically active across all channels and remain hidden from the backoffice interface.

When an external discount is applied to a product instance, it takes precedence and prevents any additional discounts from being applied to that same instance.

To implement external discounts, Litium provides the *AddExternalDiscountAsync* action through the cart context. You simply need to provide the required information for Litium to create an external discount.

Consider the example below for applying an external discount - this can be added to any MVC Accelerator controller:

```csharp theme={null}
[HttpPut]
[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
[Route("setExternalDiscount")]
public async Task<IActionResult> SetExternalDiscount(string variantId)
{
    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(variantId))
    {
        var cartContext = await HttpContext.GetCartContextAsync();

        await cartContext.AddExternalDiscountAsync(new AddExternalDiscountArgs()
        {
            CurrencyCode = "SEK",
            NotAfter = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddDays(1),
            NotBefore = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddDays(-1),
            PriceIncludingVat = 100,
            Source = "Source",
            VariantId = variantId,
            AdditionalInfo = new Dictionary<string, object> { { "key", "value" } }
        });

        return Ok(variantId);
    }

    return BadRequest();
}
```

### Litium allows one product discount per product

Only one discount can be applied per product instance. In an order with quantity 4 of a product A is calculated as 4 product instances.

For example, the order has 4 product A, unit price = 100 SEK and we have these discounts: 

* Discount 1: Buy 3 product A get discount - 50 SEK on one unit.
* Discount 2: 10% discount for each Product A.

The order will look like this : 

1. Product A \* 4 = 400 SEK
2. Discount 1: - 50 SEK (This applied for 3 instance of A)
3. Discount 2: - 10 SEK (This applied for the 4th instance of A)

For each instance of product, we can not have more than one discount applied.

<h3>
  Discount codes
</h3>

All discount types include support for activation by a discount code, and this is configured in the backoffice when creating a discount. 

Single discount codes that are named by the merchant manually can be used for the activation of discounts, one-to-many times. They are case-insensitive.

Generated discount codes that are selected when creating a discount, including the number of codes that should be generated by the system. They will be generated when saving the discount. Codes are generated using random upper case characters and numbers from a list. A generated code will be nine characters long. Generated codes are valid to use once for customers.

The buyer enters the discount code in checkout, and the system validates if the entered discount code corresponds to products in the cart and if an existing discount code has been used fewer times than the defined limit for that code. 

The system will check if the code is connected to an active discount. If it is, it will be stored in the cart. Before calculating the order total in the checkout, the system will check if the discount code is applicable to the items in the customer's cart.  If the discount code is unknown, invalid, or has already been used the allowed number of times, the customer will receive the message "Discount code invalid". If the discount code is valid, the customer will see the name of the discount, and the received amount off on the checkout page. 

Usage is followed and displayed on the discount page. In this view, it is also possible to download an Excel sheet with a list of generated codes. The list also contains information about how many of the generated codes are left to use. 

In certain campaign scenarios, it may not be feasible to generate discount codes at the time the discount is created.

To accommodate this, you can add or delete discount codes for an existing discount later using the API.

* .Net API

```csharp theme={null}
public class DiscountCodeHandler
{
    private readonly Guid _discountCodeSystemId = new Guid("<existing-discount-systemid>");
    private readonly DiscountService _discountService;

    public AddDiscountCodeHandler(DiscountService discountService)
    {
        _discountService = discountService;
    }

    // Add provided codes
    public void AddCodes(IEnumerable<string> codes)
    {
        var normalized = codes
            .Where(x => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(x))
            .Select(x => x.Trim())
            .ToHashSet();

        var discount = _discountService.Get(_discountCodeSystemId);
        var writable = discount.MakeWritableClone();
        foreach (var code in normalized)
        {
            writable.Codes.Add(new DiscountCode { Code = code, MaxUsageCount = 1 });
        }
        _discountService.Update(writable);
    }

    public void DeleteCodes(IEnumerable<string> codes)
    {
        var normalized = codes
            .Where(x => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(x))
            .Select(x => x.Trim())
            .ToHashSet(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

        var discount = _discountService.Get(_discountCodeSystemId);
        var writable = discount.MakeWritableClone();
        var codesToRemoveSet = new HashSet<string>(normalized, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
        var discountCodesToRemove = writable.Codes
            .Where(dc => codesToRemoveSet.Contains(dc.Code))
            .ToList();

        foreach (var discountCode in discountCodesToRemove)
        {
            writable.Codes.Remove(discountCode);
        }
        _discountService.Update(writable);
    }
}
```

* Litium Admin Web API

```powershell theme={null}
# Add codes
curl -X POST https://yourlitiumdomain/Litium/api/admin/sales/discounts/{systemId}/codes \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '["CODE1", "CODE2"]'

# Generate codes
curl -X POST https://yourlitiumdomain/Litium/api/admin/sales/discounts/{systemId}/codes/action/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '10'

# Delete codes
curl -X DELETE https://yourlitiumdomain/Litium/api/admin/sales/discounts/{systemId}/codes \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '["CODE1", "CODE2"]'
```

<h3>
  Threshold
</h3>

All discount types include support for activation by cart threshold, and this is configured in the backoffice when creating a discount. The threshold can be defines as a minimum amount for the products in the cart. You can also limit the cart threshold amount calculation to only consider products from a specific product list as well as a mimimum quantity of products.

The system supports discount combinations when calculating the cart threshold. Threshold amount is evaluated on the total cart amount excluding other discounts that applied on the same cart.

The threshold value for a discount can be set per currency in the backoffice. The threshold value is including VAT.

<h3>
  Discount limitation
</h3>

Product and product group discount types include support for limiting the number of times a discount can be used for an order, and this is configured in the backoffice when creating a discount. The limitation can be set as unlimited or limited to a specific number of uses per order.

The limitation applies to the following discount types:

* Discounted product price
* Product discount in percentage or amount
* Buy X products, get discount on the cheapest
* Buy X products, get discount on the most expensive
* Mix and match

When a discount limit is configured, the system validates the order during the cart calculation. The limit is per order and represents the maximum number of times the discount can be applied to items in that order.

<h3>
  Historical best price
</h3>

The historical best price is the lowest price (including or excluding VAT) for a product variant, channel, country, and currency, within the last 30 days prior to the evaluation date

This calculation includes multiple discount windows, which represent the time periods during when a discount is active for a product (from when the discount starts until it ends).

* A discount window starts when a discount becomes active and ends when it is no longer active. The system records both kinds of events so we can know when discounts started and when they ended.
* While a discount window is open, the evaluation date is the discount start. This ensures the 30-day comparison is anchored to the discount period.
* When a discount ends, the window is closed and its prices are considered as past data in subsequent calculations.

The lowest price is accessible via Storefront API

```json theme={null}
query {
  productSearch(query: { content: { value: "*dress*"}}) 
  {
    nodes {
      articleNumber
      price {
        discountPriceExcludingVat
        discountPriceIncludingVat
        unitPriceExcludingVat
        unitPriceIncludingVat
        vatRate
        history {
          lowestPriceExcludingVat
          lowestPriceIncludingVat
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```


# Initializing payments
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/initializing-payments

Initializing payments are done through CheckoutService.

It gets called through CartContext when a payment option is selected. 

The following example shows, how payment option is selected.

Note the line: *await cartContext.SelectPaymentOptionAsync(selectPaymentArgs);*

```csharp theme={null}
/// <summary>
/// Updates the payment method on the current shopping cart.
/// </summary>
/// <param name="model">Object containing the selected payment method.</param>
[HttpPut]
[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
[Route("setPaymentProvider")]
public async Task<IActionResult> SetPaymentProvider(CheckoutViewModel model)
{
    try
    {
        var selectPaymentArgs = new SelectPaymentOptionArgs
        {
            PaymentOptionId = model.SelectedPaymentMethod
        };
        var cartContext = HttpContext.GetCartContext();
        await cartContext.SelectPaymentOptionAsync(selectPaymentArgs);
        model.PaymentWidget = _paymentOptionViewModelBuilder.BuildWidget(cartContext, model.SelectedPaymentMethod);
        return Ok(model);
    }
    catch (Exception ex)
    {
        _logger.LogError(ex, "Error when changing payment method to {SelectedPaymentMethod}", model.SelectedPaymentMethod);
        ModelState.AddModelError("general", "checkout.setpaymenterror".AsWebsiteText());
        return BadRequest(ModelState);
    }
}
```

During the payment initialization, a Transaction object is created. This has the TransactionType::Init. It contains the transaction rows corresponding to the order rows in the cart. Click here to view the [full-size diagram](/images/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/initializing-payments/Transaction.jpg "Transaction.jpg").

<img alt="Transaction.jpg" />

This Init transaction is not immediately saved to the database. Instead, it is kept in memory, in Cart.PaymentOverview, until there is a guaranteed payment.

This transaction object is sent to payment provider (via payment app) to initialize the payment session.


# Interacting with Cart
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/interacting-with-cart

Interactions with cart should be done using the operations in CartContext.

For example, following method shows how CartContext::AddOrUpdateItemAsync is used to add an item to the cart. Note how the cartContext is obtained from the HttpContext using HttpContext.GetCartContext() method. This provides the cart in the current request.

```csharp theme={null}
[HttpPost]
[Route("add")]
[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
public async Task<IActionResult> Add(AddToCartViewModel model)
{
    var cartContext = HttpContext.GetCartContext();
    await cartContext.AddOrUpdateItemAsync(new AddOrUpdateCartItemArgs
    {
        ArticleNumber = model.ArticleNumber,
        Quantity = model.Quantity,
    });

    return Ok(_cartViewModelBuilder.Build(cartContext));
}
```

### Accessing CartContext

* From UI code: In your controllers and in view model building, you can get the cartContext by using the helper extension HttpContext.GetCartContext()
* To access the cartContext from background code (e.g. integrations), use the HttpContext.SwitchCartContextAsync() method and pass in the SystemId for the cartContext object. This will set the cart context for the current request.

## Calculating order totals

### Rounding off

1. All values are rounded off to the supported decimal unit of the currency. This means, for example, a order in EUR will have amounts rounded off to two decimal places, and a order in Japanese Yen will get rounded off to zero decimal places.
2. Unit price with VAT is rounded off as above. Which means, it is not possible to use unit prices below the decimal precision of a given currency. For example, 0,001 SEK is not a supported Unit price in Litium.
   * Note that, this is the unit price of the SKU (stock keeping unit), and therefore the unit price of item SKU being sold.
   * Example: Item X is sold in packs, each pack contains quantity of 1000 X. A pack costs 1 SEK. This scenario is valid, as the Unit price is 1 SEK (though individually one X only costs 1/1000 SEK)

### Calculating prices

Order row calculations are based on Unit price including VAT, VAT rate and quantity. Following are the formulas used.

1. Order row total including VAT = "Unit price including VAT"  x Quantity
2. Total VAT = "Order row total including VAT" / ( 1 + "VAT\_rate")
3. Order row total excluding VAT = "Order row total including VAT" - "Total VAT"
4. Unit price excluding VAT = "Order row total excluding VAT" / Quantity

### Recalculating cart when user login or change organization.

When working with the site a customer can place products in a cart before signing in. Customer may belong to several organizations and each organization can have it's own prices for products. This means that the price for products in cart can be changed. The new prices can lead to discount changes and the cart must be recalculated. Moreover, some of the products can be deleted from the cart, because they do not belong to the selected organization.

For example, a customer was logged in with selected **Org1** organization and cart has **ProductA**. The **ProductA** has only one price and this price is for **Org1** organization. The user decides to change the organization on **Org2** and the **ProductA** must be removed from the cart, because **Org2** doesn't have the price for this product. In case the **Org2** organization has it's own price for **ProductA** the price must be used in the cart.

To avoid the situation when the cart has products with wrong prices, Litium is automatically recalulating the cart whenever a user login/logout or change organization.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/overview

Placing an order starts with the cart. When a payment for the cart is confirmed, Litium records the order and its transactions, placing the order. This section explains this process in detail.



# Place order
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/place-order

Order is placed from Litium API, when the payment app notify there is at least one guaranteed payment for the given cart.

Therefore, the Litium Accelerator code is not calling a method to record the order to Litium database.

Instead, it will initiate the payment process and when payment app notify that a payment is available, it is the Litium Connect Payments implementation that places the order.

### "Place Order" or "Pay" button in checkout page

When using "hosted payment page" methods, that is, when the buyer need to be redirected to the payment provider to collect payment, it is common to have a button  "Place order" or "Pay", for buyer to click to start making the payment (This is in contrast to iframed checkouts where payment window is loaded in a iframe).

In this scenario, when the buyer click the "place order button", for Litium to initiate the payment process, call the CartContext.ConfirmOrderAsync() method.

```csharp theme={null}
/// <summary>
/// Submits the current shopping cart and places the order.
/// </summary>
/// <param name="model">Object containing all information of the order including delivery info and payment info.</param>
[Route("")]
[HttpPost]
[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]
public async Task<IActionResult> PlaceOrder(CheckoutViewModel model)
{
    //...initiation code

    var cartContext = HttpContext.GetCartContext();

    try
    {
        //..other code

        await cartContext.ConfirmOrderAsync();

        model.RedirectUrl = GetOrderConfirmationPageUrl(cartContext.Cart.Order);
        return Ok(model);
    }
    catch (Exception ex)
    {
      //..exception handling
    }
}
```

## Order placement process flow

The following BPMN diagram shows how the order is recorded and subsequently sent to the ERP system via Litium Connect ERP app. Click here to view the [full-size diagram](/images/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/place-order/BPM-Place-order.jpg).

<img alt="BPM Place order.jpg" />

Litium waits for a guaranteed payment to place the order. After placing the order, buyer is shown the receipt. The sequence of operations at high level is as follows. Click here to view the [full-size diagram](/images/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/place-order/SeqCreateOrderSequence.jpg).

<img alt="SeqCreateOrderSequence.jpg" />

Almost all orders recorded to the database are Confirmed orders. i.e. Order will be put to Confirmed state.

When the order goes to Confirmed, the Litium Connect ERP app listening to the OrderConfimed event will export this order to the ERP system.

Then, when ERP system has accepted the order, Litium put the order to Processing state. i.e. when an order is in the processing state, it is already sent to ERP.

Also see [Litium Connect business processes](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes) in ERP domain.


# Preorder Validation
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/preorder-validation



This section explains how the order is validated by Litium.

## Validation rules for the Litium platform - Non-changeable

* Validating that the cart has any products.
* Validating that the selected shipping option is valid for the country and channel combination.
* Validate that the cart only contains valid discount codes.
* Validating that the selected payment option is valid for the country and channel combination.
* Validating that the field limits of the address entity not is exceeded.

## Validation rules for the Accelerator - Changeable

* ProductIsAvailableForSale - Validating that the product exists and has a price for the selected channel and currency.
* ProductsAreInStock - Validating that the product exists in stock.

## Custom validation rules

You can implement your own validation rules to apply before an order can be placed. Please see the [guide on implementing custom pre-order validation rules](/platform/guides/custom-pre-order-validation-rule).


# Upsell
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/upsell

Upsell enables merchants to offer additional products to buyers within a configurable time window after order confirmation. Rather than initiating a new checkout flow, buyers can add recommended products directly from the order confirmation page — appending them to the already-confirmed order.

## How it works

When a buyer places an order, an upsell window opens for a merchant-defined duration. During this window, the order remains in a mutable state, allowing additional order rows to be appended.

The typical flow is:

```mermaid theme={null}
sequenceDiagram
    actor Buyer
    participant S as Storefront
    participant L as Litium
    participant PA as Payment app
    participant PSP
    PA ->> L: Confirm payment
    L ->> L: Create order
    L ->> S: Redirect to<br/>receipt page
    S ->> S: Display products for upsell
    Buyer ->> S: Select item(s),<br/>click Confirm button
    S ->> L: Create upsell
    L ->> PA: Execute upsell
    PA ->> PSP: Request upsell
    alt Upsell accepted directly
       PSP -->> PA: Upsell created
       PA -->> L: paymentFlowResult.transactionResult = success
       L ->> S: Redirect to<br/>receipt page 
    else SCA required
       PSP -->> PA: Upsell created<br/>with HPP URL
       PA -->> L: paymentFlowResult.paymentFlowAction.redirectURL = [HPP URL]
       L ->> S: Redirect to<br/>HPP URL
       Buyer ->> PSP: Buyer completes purchase in HPP
       PSP ->> S: Redirect to receipt page
    end
    PSP ->> PA: Confirm upsell
    PA ->> L: Confirm upsell
    L ->> L: Update order
```

1. Buyer completes checkout — an order is created in the `Confirmed` state and the upsell window opens.
2. The order confirmation page renders a set of upsell products (curated or algorithmically selected).
3. The customer adds one or more products, and clicks a `Confirm` button.
4. Through the payment app, the Payment Service Provider is asked to add the upsell products to the existing payment. The PSP can either respond directly, or with an redirect to a Hosted Payment Page (HPP) where the buyer can confirm the additional purchase.
5. When the upsell is completed, the order and the connected payment is updated with the additional products.

Use `Litium.Sales.UpsellService` to build and execute upsell flows, and use `Litium.Sales.UpsellOrderService` to read the persisted upsell order state.

## When upsell is available

Litium validates upsell before it creates or updates an upsell order.

* The sales order must be in the `Init` or `Confirmed` state.
* The order must not be locked for another upsell execution.
* The payment must have `AdditionalInfo["_eligibleForUpsell"] = "true"`.

Litium stores the upsell in an `UpsellOrder` that is connected to the original sales order and payment.

## Services

### UpsellService

Use `UpsellService` for the business operations that partner code normally needs:

* `AddItemToUpsellAsync(...)`
* `AddDiscountToUpsellAsync(...)`
* `UpsellAsync(...)`

### UpsellOrderService

Use `UpsellOrderService` when you need to inspect the persisted upsell order:

* `GetBySalesOrderAsync(...)` to find the upsell order for a sales order.
* `GetAsync(...)` to load a specific upsell order.

The service also exposes create, update, and delete methods, but partner integrations should normally let `UpsellService` manage the upsell lifecycle.

## Add an item to upsell

Call `AddItemToUpsellAsync` with the sales order system ID, the article number, and the quantity delta to apply.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Sales;

public async Task<UpsellOrder> AddUpsellItemAsync(
    UpsellService upsellService,
    Guid salesOrderSystemId,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    return await upsellService.AddItemToUpsellAsync(
        new AddOrUpdateUpsellItemArgs
        {
            SalesOrderSystemId = salesOrderSystemId,
            ArticleNumber = "SKU-123",
            Quantity = 1
        },
        cancellationToken);
}
```

Behavior to be aware of:

* If a matching row already exists, Litium updates that row instead of adding a duplicate by default.
* If you set `AlwaysAddItem = true`, Litium always creates a new upsell row.
* If you need custom row matching, set `RowSelector`. For example, if your upsell can contain multiple rows for the same article number, provide a `RowSelector` so that Litium removes the intended row.

## Remove an item from upsell

There is no separate remove method. Remove an item by calling `AddItemToUpsellAsync` with a zero quantity.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Sales;

public async Task<UpsellOrder> RemoveUpsellItemAsync(
    UpsellService upsellService,
    Guid salesOrderSystemId,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    return await upsellService.AddItemToUpsellAsync(
        new AddOrUpdateUpsellItemArgs
        {
            SalesOrderSystemId = salesOrderSystemId,
            ArticleNumber = "SKU-123",
            Quantity = 0
        },
        cancellationToken);
}
```

## Execute the upsell

When the buyer accepts the upsell, call `UpsellAsync`.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Sales;

public async Task<UpsellOrder> ExecuteUpsellAsync(
    UpsellService upsellService,
    Guid salesOrderSystemId,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    return await upsellService.UpsellAsync(
        new UpsellArgs
        {
            SalesOrderSystemId = salesOrderSystemId
        },
        cancellationToken);
}
```

During execution, Litium locks the sales order for upsell processing and updates the stored `UpsellOrder` with the payment flow result from the payment provider.

Certain payment apps like Qliro may require the buyer to be redirected to an HPP flow URL. In this case, `ExecuteUpsellAsync` returns the URL to redirect to.

```csharp theme={null}
private static string GetUpsellRedirectUrl(UpsellOrder upsellOrder)
{
    return upsellOrder?.PaymentFlowResult?.PaymentFlowAction switch
    {
        UpsellFlow upsellFlow when !string.IsNullOrEmpty(upsellFlow.RedirectUrl) => upsellFlow.RedirectUrl,
        _ => null
    };
}
```

## Read the current upsell order

Use `UpsellOrderService` if you need to inspect the current upsell state, for example when you want to display the current rows or inspect the payment flow result.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Sales;

public async Task<UpsellOrder?> GetCurrentUpsellAsync(
    UpsellOrderService upsellOrderService,
    Guid salesOrderSystemId,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    return (await upsellOrderService.GetBySalesOrderAsync(salesOrderSystemId, cancellationToken))
        .FirstOrDefault();
}
```

## What happens after a successful upsell

After a successful execution, Litium applies the upsell to the original order.

* Upsell rows are incorporated into the sales order as order rows.
* Newly added sales order rows get additional info that marks them as upsell rows:
* `_origin = "upsell"`
* `_upsellTransactionReference = <new transaction reference>`
* The payment `PaymentReference2` field is updated with the new transaction reference.
* If the payment already has successful or pending `Init`, `Authorize`, or `Capture` transactions, Litium updates those transactions with the added upsell rows and writes the new reference to `TransactionReference2`.
* The upsell order payment flow result is marked as successful.

Listen to the `UpsellSuccess` event to send notifications to buyers about their upsell status.

During the `UpsellSuccess` event, you can move the order to `PendingProcessing` state.

## Failed and denied upsell outcomes

If the payment provider returns a failed or denied result, Litium updates the upsell order payment flow result with `Success = false`, stores any returned errors, and removes the in-progress tag from the sales order.

Litium publishes different events depending on the outcome:

* `UpsellSuccess` when the upsell is completed successfully.
* `UpsellFailed` when the upsell fails.
* `UpsellDenied` when the payment provider explicitly denies the upsell.

These events carry the `UpsellOrder` as the event item, so subscribers can inspect rows, totals, and `PaymentFlowResult`.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Events;
using Litium.Sales.Events;

public class UpsellEventSubscriber
{
    public UpsellEventSubscriber(EventBroker eventBroker)
    {
        eventBroker.Subscribe<UpsellSuccess>(x => HandleSuccess(x.Item));
        eventBroker.Subscribe<UpsellFailed>(x => HandleFailure(x.Item));
        eventBroker.Subscribe<UpsellDenied>(x => HandleDenied(x.Item));
    }

    private Task HandleSuccess(Litium.Sales.UpsellOrder upsellOrder) => Task.CompletedTask;
    private Task HandleFailure(Litium.Sales.UpsellOrder upsellOrder) => Task.CompletedTask;
    private Task HandleDenied(Litium.Sales.UpsellOrder upsellOrder) => Task.CompletedTask;
}
```

## Cart context handling during upsell

Do not clear the cart context while there is an initialized upsell order that still waits for buyer action.

In the Litium accelerator flow, cart context clearing should be intentionally skipped while an upsell order exists with `PaymentFlowOperation = InitializeUpsell`. The cart context should only be cleared after the upsell has been executed, or when there is no upsell order in progress.

## Abandoned upsell flows and cleanup

Litium uses sales order tags internally during upsell processing:

* `_upsellInProgress`
* `_upsellLock`

In some flows, Litium does not receive a callback after the buyer abandons the upsell. This can happen when the payment provider requires a redirect or an asynchronous confirmation and the buyer never completes that flow.

In those situations, the upsell tags are not always cleared immediately. They are eventually removed by the cleanup job described below.

## How old upsell orders are removed

Litium includes the scheduled job `CleanupUpsellOrders` with the scheduler name `Litium.Sales.CleanupUpsellOrders`.

The job works like this:

* It reads the setting `UpsellOrderExpiryDays`.
* If the setting is missing, `0`, or negative, Litium uses the default value `3` days.
* It deletes upsell orders whose related sales order is older than the expiry days setting.
* For affected sales orders, it removes `_upsellInProgress` and `_upsellLock` if those tags are still present.

This cleanup is the safety net for abandoned upsell flows where no final notification reaches Litium.

## Recommended integration pattern

1. Build the upsell with `AddItemToUpsellAsync` and `AddDiscountToUpsellAsync`.
2. Keep the cart context intact while the buyer can still accept or reject the upsell.
3. Execute the upsell with `UpsellAsync` when the buyer confirms.
4. Use `UpsellOrderService` or the upsell events to inspect the final outcome.

## Related API surface

* `Litium.Sales.UpsellService`
* `Litium.Sales.UpsellOrderService`
* `Litium.Sales.AddOrUpdateUpsellItemArgs`
* `Litium.Sales.AddDiscountToUpsellArgs`
* `Litium.Sales.UpsellArgs`
* `Litium.Sales.UpsellOrder`
* `Litium.Sales.Events.UpsellSuccess`
* `Litium.Sales.Events.UpsellFailed`
* `Litium.Sales.Events.UpsellDenied`


# Cancel or refund of payment
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/cancel-or-refund-of-payment

Cancellation of payment is for payments that have not yet been captured. Refund of payment is for a payment that has been captured.

## Cancellation and refund during order fulfilment process

Litium automatically captures, cancels and refunds payments as part of the order fulfilment process. When a fulfilment shipment is created Litium will automatically create a capture transaction of the corresponding amount for the order's linked payment. In the same way, when a cancellation shipment is created Litium will automatically create a cancellation transaction (in the case of a authorized but not captured payment) OR a refund transaction (in the case of a captured payment).

## Manual canceling or refunding payments

In Litium it is possible to make cancel or refund operations in .NET or through the Admin Web API.

The process of canceling or refunding payments to customers starts with a cancel or refund transaction being initiated. The system then utilizes previously used payment transactions for the cancellation or return to be done to the original payment type for the order. The payment app receives the transaction and executes the refunds with the payment service provider. The payment status will then be updated in the system. 

### How to cancel and refund payments in the Admin Web API

There are methods to cancel or refund a transaction in the Admin API for Sales Transactions.

The CancelAuthorization endpoint can be used for an Authorization transaction and the RefundCapture endpoint applies to a Capture transaction.

<img alt="Transaction.png" />

### How to cancel and refund payments in the .NET Code

PaymentTransactionManager can be used to Cancel or Refund a transaction:

```csharp theme={null}
public class SampleController
{
    private readonly TransactionService _transactionService;
    private readonly PaymentTransactionManager _paymentTransactionManager;
    private readonly ILogger<SampleController> _logger;

    public SampleController(
        TransactionService transactionService,
        PaymentTransactionManager paymentTransactionManager,
        ILogger<SampleController> logger)
    {
        _transactionService = transactionService;
        _paymentTransactionManager = paymentTransactionManager;
        _logger = logger;
    }
    /// <summary>
    /// Creates a cancel transaction for the authorization transaction.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="transactionSystemId">The transaction system identifier.</param>
    [Route("{transactionSystemId}/cancel")]
    [HttpPost]
    public async Task<IHttpActionResult> CancelAuthorizationTransaction(Guid transactionSystemId)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return BadRequest(ModelState);
        }

        var transaction = _transactionService.Get(transactionSystemId);
        if (transaction is null || transaction.TransactionType != TransactionType.Authorize)
        {
            return NotFound();
        }
        else if (transaction.TransactionResult != TransactionResult.Success)
        {
            return BadRequest();
        }

        try
        {
            await _paymentTransactionManager.CancelAuthorizationAsync(transaction, new CancelAuthorizationArgs());
            return Accepted();
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Error when trying to cancel the authorized transaction.");
            ModelState.AddModelError("general", ex.Message);
            return BadRequest(ModelState);
        }
    }
    /// <summary>
    /// Creates a refund transaction for the capture transaction.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="transactionSystemId">The transaction system identifier.</param>
    [Route("{transactionSystemId}/refund")]
    [HttpPost]
    public async Task<IHttpActionResult> RefundCapture(Guid transactionSystemId)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return BadRequest(ModelState);
        }

        var transaction = _transactionService.Get(transactionSystemId);
        if (transaction is null || transaction.TransactionType != TransactionType.Capture)
        {
            return NotFound();
        }
        else if (transaction.TransactionResult != TransactionResult.Success)
        {
            return BadRequest();
        }

        try
        {
            await _paymentTransactionManager.RefundCaptureAsync(transaction, new RefundCaptureArgs());
            return Accepted();
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Error when trying to refund the capture transaction.");
            ModelState.AddModelError("general", ex.Message);
            return BadRequest(ModelState);
        }
    }
}
```


# Cancel the remaining part of an order
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/cancel-remaining-order



This describes the process of cancelling the remaining part of an order, ie cancelling the items that has not yet been included in a shipment. This operation can be done both from the Backoffice UI and by API calls.

## Cancel an order from Backoffice UI

Go to the **Order Details** page, and from the menu. select the **Cancel remaining products** option to execute the process of order cancellation.

<img alt="Order details page with cancel remaining order command displayed" />

If the order has a pending payment, the process of cancellation will be stopped and the error message "**Cannot finalize the order due to payment in pending"** is shown. Otherwise, the system finds all items that are not part of any shipment and adds them to a automatically created shipment of type *Cancellation*.

Then, this shipment is set to *Processing* state, and a cancel or refund transaction is created from it:

* If the payment is already captured, a **refund** transacton is created.
* Otherwise, a **cancel** transaction is created.

Litium calls the payment app with the cancel or refund transaction. The payment app executes the cancel or refund, and notifies Litium of the result at which point the payment status will be updated in the system. In case of success, the cancellation shipment is set to *Cancelled* state, and the order is set to *Completed* state.

## Cancel an order from Connect ERP API

It is a common scenario that it is the ERP system that initiates a cancellation of an order, eg because items have become out of stock during order processing. Since Connect ERP API 2.1, the Finalize action can be called to cancel the remaining part of an order:

```
/Litium/api/connect/erp/orders/{orderId}/action/finalize
```

The call to this endpoint will initiate the same process as the Backoffice UI, ie creating a Cancellation shipment and managing the cancellation or refund of the associated payment.

## How to cancel the remaining part of an order in the .NET Code

ShipmentManager can be used to create a cancellation shipment and use StateTransitionService to set the shipment to Processing:

```csharp theme={null}
public class SampleController
{
    private readonly OrderOverviewService _orderOverviewService;
    private readonly StateTransitionsService _stateTransitionService;
    private readonly PaymentStateService _paymentStateService;
    private readonly ShipmentService _shipmentService;
    private readonly ShipmentManager _shipmentManager;
    private readonly ILogger<SalesOrderController> _logger;

    public SampleController(
        OrderOverviewService orderOverviewService,
        StateTransitionsService stateTransitionService,
        PaymentStateService paymentStateService,
        ShipmentService shipmentService,
        ShipmentManager shipmentManager,
        ILogger<SalesOrderController> logger)
    {
        _orderOverviewService = orderOverviewService;
        _stateTransitionService = stateTransitionService;
        _paymentStateService = paymentStateService;
        _shipmentService = shipmentService;
        _shipmentManager = shipmentManager;
        _logger = logger;
    }

    /// <summary>
    ///  Finalize the order.
    /// </summary>
    /// <param name="systemId">The sales order system identifier.</param>
    [Route("{systemId}/action/finalizeOrder")]
    [HttpPost]
    [ProducesResponseType(202)]
    public async Task<IHttpActionResult> FinalizeOrder(Guid systemId)
    {
        if (!ModelState.IsValid)
        {
            return BadRequest(ModelState);
        }

        var orderOverview = _orderOverviewService.Get(systemId);
        if (orderOverview is null || orderOverview.SalesOrder is null)
        {
            return NotFound();
        }
        else if (_paymentStateService.GetPaymentStatuses(orderOverview).Values.Any(x => x == PaymentState.Pending))
        {
            ModelState.AddModelError("general", "Cannot finalize the order due to payment in pending.");
            return BadRequest(ModelState);
        }

        try
        {
            var shipment = await _shipmentManager.CreateCancelShipment(orderOverview.SalesOrder.SystemId);
            
            _shipmentService.Create(shipment);

            _stateTransitionService.SetState<Shipment>(shipment.SystemId, ShipmentState.Processing);

            return Accepted();
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _logger.LogError(ex, "Error when trying to finalize the order.");
            ModelState.AddModelError("general", ex.Message);
            return BadRequest(ModelState);
        }
    }
}
```

Then, when the shipment state is changed to Processing, TransactionFactory can be used to create transaction, then execute the cancel or refund:

```csharp theme={null}
public async Task ShipmentChangedToProcessingState(Shipment shipment)
{
    var orderOverview = _orderOverviewService.Get(shipment.OrderSystemId);
    if (orderOverview is null || orderOverview.SalesOrder is null)
    {
        throw new ArgumentException($"The order ({shipment.OrderSystemId}) cannot be found.");
    }

    var paymentOverview = orderOverview.PaymentOverviews.FirstOrDefault();
    if (paymentOverview is null || paymentOverview.Payment is null)
    {
        throw new ArgumentException("The payment cannot be found.");
    }

    if (orderOverview.IsFullyCaptured())
    {
        var refundTransaction = await _transactionFactory.CreateRefundTransactions(shipment);
        _transactionService.Create(refundTransaction);
        await _paymentTransactionsProcessor.EnqueueAsysnc(new() { TransactionSystemId = refundTransaction.SystemId });
    }
    else
    {
        var cancelTransaction = await _transactionFactory.CreateCancelTransactions(shipment);
        _transactionService.Create(cancelTransaction);
        await _paymentTransactionsProcessor.EnqueueAsysnc(new() { TransactionSystemId = cancelTransaction.SystemId });
    }
}
```


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/overview

Litium support cancellation of orders as well as order returns. A cancellation means that the order fulfilment is stopped before goods are delivered to the customer. A return means that goods have been delivered and then sent back to the merchant.
