# Best Practices
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/best-practices

When you need to change and extend the business logic.

Projects that may change and extend the business logic for order return management should follow these recommendations:

1. Do not alter or modify an existing order once it has been confirmed. Instead you should create another connected order to handle the situation. This reduces complexity and makes integration with accounting system and existing ERP order delivery systems easy.
2. Before you implement any state transitions, draw them in state diagrams and work out all possible scenarios, preconditions and actions. Keep state transitions as simple as possible, and do not introduce micro-managed states.
3. Do not change the owner object within a state transition. For example, if an order is in confirmed state, within its transition from *Confirmed* to *Processing*, the order shipment state should not be updated. Instead, use the related state transitions in the state transition engine, or schedule all updates to an external thread that will run independent of the state transitions.
4. When there are multiple returns from the same order and exchange items, the business logic for calculating the refund amounts may be complex. To keep it as simple as possible, always consider an item that should be exchanged due to defects etc, as a new sales order with its own life cycle. The exchange orders should not be part of any sales return order calculation. Subsequent implementation of the business logic could give customers an additional advantage when there are campaigns. This, however, is hard to avoid without making the calculations complex.
5. Litium uses IRmaFactory.Create internally to determine whether it's possible to do additional RMAs for the sales order. If it's not possible then the current RMA will be considered as the final RMA and a special rule of rouding off will be applied for the sales return order. 
6. The payment of a sales order should be captured and all shipments should be in *Shipped* state before creating a RMA.


# Entity model
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/entity-model

How the  entities are organized in return management.

Only the key entities and their field subsets are listed in the illustration below.

<img alt="entity model.png" />

The mapping between RMA and *SO*, and between SRO rows and SO rows, is described here:

We have the following relationships between RMA, SO and SRO: 

* One SO can have multiple RMA
* Each RMA could have 0 (when it is not approved and completed) or 1 SRO

SO   ->  RMA1   ->  SRO 1

-"-    ->  RMA2  ->  SRO 2

The relationship between SO and SRO rows looks like this:

| SO 1: | Article | Quantity | Unit price | Row total |
| ----- | ------- | -------: | ---------: | --------: |
| Row 1 | Item A  |        2 |      \$100 |     \$200 |
| Row 2 | Item B  |        3 |      \$150 |     \$450 |

| SRO 1: | Article | Quantity | Unit price | Row total |
| ------ | ------- | -------: | ---------: | --------: |
| Row 1  | Item A  |       -1 |      \$100 |    -\$100 |
| Row 2  | Item B  |       -1 |      \$150 |    -\$150 |

Each SRO row will have a link to link back to the original SO row. In the example above, SRO row 1 will have a link back to SO row 1, which tells us the maximum number of items that can be returned. 

#### Mapping items 

The returned items are mapped to the original order row. This facilitates the calculations and makes it possible to find the unit return price. For cross referencing, each SRO row is matched to the corresponding original SO Row. This could mean that an individual RMA row results in multiple rows in the SRO

#### Sales return processing

Here is a class diagram with classes to manipulate RMA objects:

<img alt="sales return processing.png" />

#### *RmaService*

A Litium API service that handles the RMA entity. This is a service class pattern for all new Litium entities.

#### *IRmaBuilder*

Builds an RMA, from a return slip or using the original order system id. Basic validations of quantities are made, since other returns from same order may have happened. This is to make sure that nothing is over-returned. Only the maximum amount a customer bought in the first place can be returned.

#### *IRmaSroLookupService*

This service returns the mapping between RMA, SO and SRO. It also allows the related entity system id to be fetched, without having to load the source entity.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/overview

Return management allows the system to process cases when customers return items bought on an e-commerce site to the merchant. This section describes how it works and what you need to consider from a developer perspective.

## Terminology

* Return slip: Document that the customer fills in, or that is system generated. It is usually signed and included, physically or electronically, together with the returned package. It has references to the original sales order and states the quantity returned, as well as the reason for the return.
* Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA): Entity that records the items returned and the merchant's decision to approve or deny the return. It has rows with article number, the returned quantity, received quantity, reason for return, customer and admin comments, etc. When a return slip is system generated, the RMA may contain a reference to it.
* Sales Return Order (SRO): Order with *OrderType* property set to *SalesReturnOrder*. This entity records the financial aspects of an RMA, when the customer is entitled to a refund. It can be used to refund money to the customer via payment providers and sent to the ERP system for accounting and other processing.
* Sales Order (SO): Regular sales order.
* Sales Exchange Order: New sales order based on a previous one, to change an item or send a replacement. 
* Transport Administration system (TA): Manages the physical transport of items and typically integrates with carriers, eg PostNord or DHL.
* Package slip: Document that is pasted on the physical package.
* Warehouse Management System (WMS): Manages processes in the physical warehouse of a merchant.

## The return process

<img alt="sales return process.png" />

### Process initiation 

A return process can be initiated in several ways.

* Customer support initiates a return in the ERP system and sends a return slip to the customer. 
* An RMA is initiated through a dedicated web page where a return slip is generated. This can be done via integration to TA delivery checkouts 
* A physical return slip is included with the delivery package. This is filled in by the customer and included in the return package. 
* The customer does not collect the delivery package from the carrier, which results in an automatic return. 

Process initiation is not included in this Litium implementation of return management, but all of the above scenarios can be supported in your solution by building upon the available API.

### Receipt of package at warehouse

When a return package is accepted at the receiving warehouse, an RMA should be initiated in Litium. This can be done automatically in the following ways:

* The return package includes a return slip that was system generated with a scan code linked to a system-created RMA.
* Integration with TAs, using TA-supplied return slips.
* Scan of original order id, which initiates an RMA with possible return quantities.

### RMA approval

As an integrated step in the business process, the RMA should be approved or denied. The RMA processing also includes decision on how to handle the returned items, eg to restock, scrap or return to vendor. The RMA must be approved before any of the following actions can take place

* Create a Sales Return Order (SRO) to refund money.
* Create a new Sales Order (SO) to exchange or replace items.

### Create Sales return order

A Sales return order (SRO) uses the existing order entity in Litium, but has its *OrderType* set to *SalesReturnOrder*. An additional field with a link to one or more RMAs are also added.

Additional order discounts and fees can be applied to an SRO. Since the order rows of an SRO correspond to those of the SO, other fields should not be modified. The cross referencing is kept in a separate table.

### Financial management 

The accounting system of the merchant must be updated with the financial information related to returned items. This information should reflect the actual amounts refunded to the customer. For this reason, an SRO is created when the corresponding RMA has been approved and completed, with links from SRO to the RMA and original SO.

The SRO will trigger the same events (eg Order Confirmed event) as a SO, which can be used to export them to an ERP via the Connect ERP API. 

### RMA approval flag

The RMA approval flag can be set when specific states are reached. Please refer to [the best practice section](/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/best-practices) for details. For automatic setting of this flag, based on the merchant’s business logic, projects may also build a periodic scheduled task that will scan the RMAs by their state and approval status, then check the necessary conditions. 

For merchants that don’t use this field, ie returns are automatically approved, the flag can be made redundant by setting it to true by default when the RMA is created.

## Right to Return

There are a number of possible use cases for return management, depending on the return reason. Litium does not differentiate between various reasons and all returns will be treated as Right to Return according to EU law.

## Multiple returns

A single sales order may result in several returns. Each return will generate a separate RMA connected to the order. A package received at the warehouse will result in one RMA.

## Limitations

* Return slips: The generation of return slips are not built into Litium. Please note that it may not be required to store the return slip in electronic format. In certain situations, however, a signed returned slip may be required for documentation and legal reasons.
* Litium Backoffice includes UI to view and edit RMAs created through API. Backoffice UI to create and edit SROs are on our current roadmap.
* Creation of a new SO for replacement or exchange items is not built into Litium. It is possible to build support in your solution to create a new SO based on an RMA.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/refund-of-payment/overview

An important step of the return process is the ability for the system to correctly calculate the amount to refund to the customer. When doing this calculation the system needs to take into consideration fees and discounts applied to the original Sales order.

The refund of payments are handled by the payment apps via the Connect Payments API.

It is possible to refund part of a captured amount. The refund amount will be limited by the amount captured for a transaction, and other limitations imposed by specific payment providers. If a refund fails, the refund transaction will have the status set to *failed*, and the payment will be tagged with the *Attention* system tag.

It is also possible to capture part of an authorized amount and cancel the remaining part of the authorization. This facilitates B2B scenarios, where the capture may be performed after customer acceptance of the delivery. This allows the return of orders that have not yet been captured, which means that payment has not yet been charged to the customer.

### Gift cards

Litium's [support for gift cards](/platform/areas/sales/gift-cards) does not include refunds of gift cards. Instead, only the amount (if any) covered by the actual payment can be refunded automatically.

## Calculating refund amount

From Litium 8.9, a new business logic is applied to shipping and other fees when calculating the refund amount for a return shipment. For the previous implementation, please see below.

Litium will include the shipping and other fees when calculating the refund amount, only if all items of the order are being returned in the same return shipment.

<img alt="3.png" />

Litium will not refund any part of the fees when doing a partial return. This includes the case where the whole sales order is returned in multiple partial returns.

<img alt="4.png" />

## Changing the business logic on refund value calculation

To change the business logic of refund value calculation, you need to modify the generated Sales return order by overriding the SalesReturnOrderBuilder as follows:

In the following example, we are adding a fee of 100, to demonstrate the concept.

```csharp theme={null}
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using Litium.Sales;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.PriceRules
{
    [Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection.ServiceDecorator(typeof(SalesReturnOrderBuilder))]
    internal class CustomSalesReturnOrderBuilder : SalesReturnOrderBuilder
    {
        private SalesReturnOrderBuilder _parent;
        public CustomSalesReturnOrderBuilder(SalesReturnOrderBuilder parent)
        {
            _parent = parent; // impl instance of type MyServiceImpl
        }

        public override SalesReturnOrder Build(CreateSalesReturnOrderArgs args)
        {
            var sro = _parent.Build(args);
            //TODO: Change the Sales return order here:
            //we are applying a sample fee to demonstrate the concept.
            ApplyFee(sro);

            return sro;
        }

        private static void ApplyFee(SalesReturnOrder sro)
        {
            decimal penaltyFee = 100;
            if ((sro.GrandTotal + penaltyFee) > 0)
                return;

            var orderRow = sro.Rows.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Id == "ReturnFee");

            //following 
            if (orderRow == null)
            {
                orderRow = new SalesReturnOrderRow();
                orderRow.SystemId = Guid.NewGuid();
                orderRow.Id = "ReturnFee";
                orderRow.ArticleNumber = "ReturnFee";
                orderRow.Description = "Return Fee";
                orderRow.OrderRowType = OrderRowType.Fee;

                orderRow.Quantity = 1;
                orderRow.VatRate = 0.25M;
                orderRow.UnitPriceIncludingVat = penaltyFee;
                orderRow.UnitPriceExcludingVat = decimal.Divide(orderRow.UnitPriceIncludingVat, (1 + orderRow.VatRate));

                orderRow.TotalExcludingVat = orderRow.UnitPriceExcludingVat * orderRow.Quantity;
                orderRow.TotalIncludingVat = orderRow.UnitPriceIncludingVat * orderRow.Quantity;
                orderRow.TotalVat = orderRow.TotalIncludingVat - orderRow.TotalExcludingVat;
                orderRow.VatDetails = new List<VatDetail> { new VatDetail { VatRate = orderRow.VatRate, AmountIncludingVat = orderRow.TotalIncludingVat, Vat = orderRow.TotalVat } };
#pragma warning disable CS0618 // VatSummary is obsolete, but it may still be used by Litium connect clients
                orderRow.VatSummary = new Dictionary<decimal, decimal> { { orderRow.VatRate, orderRow.TotalVat } };
#pragma warning restore CS0618 // VatSummary is obsolete,  but it may still be used by Litium connect clients

                sro.Rows.Add(orderRow);
            }
        }
    }
   
}
```

## Litium 8.8 and earlier

To match the sum of the corresponding Sales order, Litium does pro-data calculations of the shipping and others fees applied to the sales order when calculating the value of the refund amount for a return shipment.

Example: The refund amount for a partial order return calculated on a pro-rata basis, including any fee or delivery cost. 

1. The customer buys 3 shirts at \$100 each and pays a \$15 delivery cost, a total of \$315. 
2. The customer returns one of the shirts.
3. The refund is calculated to \$100 for the shirt and (\$100/\$300) × \$15 = \$5 for the delivery cost, a total of \$105.

The same principle applies for any extra cost or fee that was included in the SO. If the entire SO is returned in multiple batches, the original total amount will be equal to the sum of the amounts in the individual SROs. Please see [this spreadsheet](/platform/previous-versions/litium-7/litium-documentation/sales/return-management_1_1/pro-rata-refund_1) for a more detailed example of how refunds are calculated on a pro-rata basis.

### Override Refund Value calculation to not refund the shipping cost

By default, refund value for shipping cost was return by pro-rata basis. Depends on each implementation, delivery cost also be set to zero by adding an override class to Litium.Accelerator.Mvc project like this: 

```csharp theme={null}
public class NewSalesReturnOrderCalculator : SalesReturnOrderCalculator
{
    public NewSalesReturnOrderCalculator(ISalesReturnOrderPaymentInfoBuilder salesReturnPaymentInfoBuilder) : base(salesReturnPaymentInfoBuilder)
    {
    }

    protected override void CalculateDelivery(OrderCarrier sroCarrier, decimal proRataPct, Order saleOrder)
    {
        foreach (var delivery in sroCarrier.Deliveries)
        {
            delivery.DeliveryCost = 0;
            delivery.DeliveryCostWithVAT = 0;
            delivery.TotalVATAmount = 0;
            delivery.TotalDeliveryCost = 0;
        }
        sroCarrier.TotalDeliveryCost = 0;
        sroCarrier.TotalDeliveryCostVAT = 0;
    }
}
```

This override class will set delivery cost to 0 for Sales return order.


# Pro-rata refund calculation (Litium 8.8 and earlier)
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/refund-of-payment/pro-rata-refund

How Litium 8.8 and previous version calculates pro-rata refund amounts for order returns.

This example shows a calculation of the pro-rata refund amount for an order including delivery cost, handling fee and order discount, that is fully returned in one part:

<img alt="Return in one batch.png" />

This example shows a calculation of the pro-rata refund amounts for an order including delivery cost, handling fee and order discount, that is fully returned in multiple parts:

<img alt="Return in multiple batches.png" />

The SRO calculations are based on the following principles:

* Quantities are given negative values. 
* Row discounts keep their positive values.
* Order discounts are given negative values. 
* Delivery costs and fees are given negative values.
* Unit and campaign prices keep their positive values

Payment information rows will remain positive for backward compatibility reasons.


# RMA overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/rma-overview

How an Return Merchandise Authorisation (RMA) is created and used.

The following illustration gives an overview of the order return initiation process:

<img alt="RMA-overview.png" />

1. A customer visits the Litium e-commerce site of a merchant and files a request to return purchased items. 
2. Litium creates a return slip and renders a delivery checkout UI in a TA system or creates a return slip without any rendering. In that case a package slip is sent by e-mail to the customer.
3. The customer downloads a package slip.
4. The customer hands over a package with the items to be returned at a TA service point.
5. The package is received by the merchant’s warehouse and registered in a WMS.
6. A package inspector checks the items and an approval is sent to the Litium API.
7. Litium creates an RMA which can be used to track decision wether to approve or deny the return.
8. Litium notifies the customer that the items has been received by the warehouse.

## RMA states

The following illustration shows how state transitions is implemented by default:

<img alt="RMA states.png" />

The state transitions can be utilised to automate actions, eg to notify the customer when the returned goods have been received by the merchant.

## Managing RMAs in Litium Backoffice

The RMAs connected to an order is displayed on the **Order details** page in Litium Backoffice.

<img alt="Order detail page with RMA.png" />

By clicking on the **Details** link, the RMA will be opened in a dialog where the user is also able to edit the RMA:

<img alt="RMA detail dialog.png" />

By clicking the button at the bottom of the dialog, the RMA can be moved forward to the next state. Different fields of the RMA becomes available for editing depending on the current state of the RMA.

## Managing RMAs in Connect ERP API

RMAs can be created and managed through integration with an ERP system via Connect ERP API. Please see the [Connect ERP API documentation](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/order-return-management-process) for details.


# SRO overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/return-management/sro-overview

How an Sales Return Order (SRO) is created and used.

This illustration shows the process when an RMA has been created and approved.

<img alt="SRO-overview.png" />

1. A RMA has been created and approved in Litium.
2. An administrator or an automation logic initiates the creation of an SRO in Litium. It is based on the information in the RMA and includes an SRO entity, a calculation of the amount to be refunded and a refund transaction.
3. A refund is initiated by an administrator or by an automation logic.
4. Litium sends the calculated amount and refund transaction to the payment app for the original sales order. The payment app requests the refund at the payment provider. 
5. The SRO triggers a Order Confirmed event in the Connect ERP API so that the SRO can be exported to the ERP system, or to any other external system that listens for this event.
6. The customer can be notified that the SRO has been completed and the money refunded. 

There can be several RMAs for one SO, but each RMA will only have one SRO.

## Sales return order states

<img alt="order state machine.png" />

The state transitions can be utilised to enable automations when the state of a SRO changes, eg notifying the customer that a refund has been issued.

## Managing SROs in Litium Backoffice UI

This feature is currently on our product roadmap.

## Managing SROs in Connect ERP API

SROs can be created and managed through integration with an ERP system via Connect ERP API. Please see the [Connect ERP API documentation](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/order-return-management-process) for details.


# Initiating returns from the storefront
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/order-returns-and-cancellation/storefront-return-initialization

How anonymous full-order returns work in the Litium Storefront GraphQL API, what the channel setting controls, and what is created in Sales.

Litium lets buyers start a **full-order return** from a custom storefront **without logging in**, using the Storefront GraphQL API. The feature is **opt-in per channel**, guarded by a channel setting, and limited to **full-order** returns (all eligible lines in one return slip). Partial returns are not supported through this API.

## Channel setting

Returns from the storefront are controlled by **`EnableReturnInitializationInStorefront`** on the sales **channel** tied to the order.

|                           |                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Back office**           | **Return initialization in storefront API**                                                |
| **Location**              | **Channel** → **Settings**                                                                 |
| **Domain property**       | `Channel.EnableReturnInitializationInStorefront`                                           |
| **Default after upgrade** | `false` (added by database migration; existing channels stay off until enabled)            |
| **Scope**                 | Per channel — enable only on channels where the storefront should expose return initiation |

<Warning>
  The setting defaults to **off**. After upgrading, enable it explicitly on each channel that should allow `createOrderToken` and `createReturnSlip`.
</Warning>

### What the setting controls

When the flag is **off** for the order’s channel:

* **`createOrderToken`** responds with error code **`order_not_found`** and message *"The order could not be found."* (same as a missing order, to avoid leaking configuration).
* **`createReturnSlip`** responds with error code **`channel_disabled`** and message *"Returning orders from the storefront is not enabled for this channel."*

When the flag is **on**, the Storefront API may create return slips for orders on that channel, subject to buyer verification, token authorization, and returnability rules below.

### Configuring via Admin Web API

The setting is exposed on the channel settings model used by back office (`Channel.EnableReturnInitializationInStorefront`). Persist changes through the same channel update flows as other channel settings.

## How returns are initiated (storefront)

Storefront return initiation is a **two-step** GraphQL flow:

```mermaid theme={null}
sequenceDiagram
  participant Storefront
  participant API as Storefront GraphQL API
  participant Sales as Sales (Return slip)

  Storefront->>API: createOrderToken(orderNumber, email)
  Note over API: Channel setting on order channel<br/>Rate limit per order number<br/>Email matches order
  API-->>Storefront: JWT (5 min)

  Storefront->>API: createReturnSlip(orderNumber, returnReason, …)<br/>Authorization: Bearer JWT
  Note over API: Token bound to order<br/>Channel setting on order channel<br/>All returnable lines → one slip
  API->>Sales: Persist return slip + rows
  API-->>Storefront: returnSlipId, returnSlipSystemId
  opt notificationUrl provided
    API-->>Storefront: POST webhook (async, non-blocking)
  end
```

| Step | Mutation           | Authentication                            | Purpose                                                          |
| ---- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | `createOrderToken` | None (contextual storefront request only) | Verify **order number** + **buyer email**; issue short-lived JWT |
| 2    | `createReturnSlip` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>`           | Create one **return slip** for all eligible product lines        |

Both mutations require a normal Storefront **contextual** request (website/channel context), like other storefront operations.

### Buyer email verification (step 1)

Email is compared **case-insensitively** after **trimming**:

1. `CustomerInfo.Email` on the order, if set
2. Otherwise `BillingAddress.Email`

**Order number** is the sales order **Id** (external order number), not the internal system id.

### Token and security

* JWT lifetime: **300 seconds** (five minutes).
* Token is scoped to the order (internal claim). Step 2 must use the **same** `orderNumber` as step 1.
* **`createOrderToken`** is rate-limited: **5 attempts per order number per 30 minutes**. The limit applies before order lookup (failed guesses still count).
* Validation failures on step 1 (unknown order, disabled channel, wrong email) share **`order_not_found`** to reduce enumeration; see logs at **Debug** for the actual cause.

For mutation arguments, error codes, webhook payload, and copy-paste GraphQL examples, see [Right of withdrawal — full order return (Storefront API)](/platform/guides/right-of-withdrawal-storefront-full-order-return).

## What gets created

Calling `createReturnSlip` successfully creates a **return slip** in Sales:

* **Id** — `{orderNumber}-return-{n}` where `n` is `1 +` existing slips for that order (e.g. `SO10045-return-1`).
* **Rows** — One row per **returnable** product line; rows with the same **article number** are **grouped** with summed quantity.
* **`returnReason`** — Single reason from the GraphQL `ReturnReason` enum, applied to every line on the slip.
* **`additionalInfo`** — Optional key/value pairs stored on the slip.

The GraphQL response returns **`returnSlipId`** and **`returnSlipSystemId`** only. Further return processing (return authorization, refund, ERP, and so on) follows your existing Sales and integration flows in back office.

## Which order lines are returnable

Eligibility is calculated by **`IReturnableOrderRowService`** (default: `ReturnableOrderRowService`). A product row is included only if:

1. It is a **product** row (`OrderRowType.Product`).
2. It has been **shipped** — quantity is based on **fulfillment** shipments in state **Shipped**.
3. Quantity not already covered by **non-denied** return authorizations on the order is greater than zero.

If no rows qualify, `createReturnSlip` fails with a **validation** error: *"There are no eligible items to return."*

<Note>
  Partners can replace **`IReturnableOrderRowService`** or **`OrderReturnService`** to customize eligibility or slip creation, but the Storefront mutations still expect **full-order** semantics unless you replace the resolvers as well.
</Note>

## Return reasons

Storefront callers pass a **`ReturnReason`** enum value by name. Platform values include:

| Name                 | Typical use                            |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `RightToReturn`      | Statutory / policy right of withdrawal |
| `Exchange`           | Exchange                               |
| `DamagedInShipment`  | Damaged in transit                     |
| `Defective`          | Defective goods                        |
| `NotExpectedQuality` | Quality not as expected                |
| `NotTheItemOrdered`  | Wrong item                             |
| `WarrantyClaim`      | Warranty                               |
| `Unknown`            | Unspecified                            |

Invalid names return **`invalid_reason`**.

## Optional webhook

`createReturnSlip` accepts an optional **`notificationUrl`**. After the slip is committed, Litium sends a **fire-and-forget** `POST` with:

```json theme={null}
{
  "returnSlipId": "ORDER123-return-1",
  "returnSlipSystemId": "guid",
  "orderNumber": "ORDER123",
  "createdAt": "2026-05-24T12:00:00.0000000Z"
}
```

The host must be a **registered Litium domain**. Delivery failures are **logged** only; they do not roll back the mutation.

# Save searches as views
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/save-searches-as-views

This page describes how to save searches of orders as views.

Administrators often need to perform the same order searches with specific conditions repeatedly.

For instance, a user might want to filter orders from yesterday that are still in the "confirmed" state to investigate why they haven't progressed to the "processing" state. These repeated searches are typically associated with recurring tasks that may involve multiple team members.

Administrators can save an order search, including all filters and column settings, as a view. These saved views are accessible to all backoffice users in the Sales area, streamlining the process and ensuring consistency across the team.

## Save a view

To save a search for later use, click the button **Save view.** A popup will be shown to ask for a view name. 

<img alt="popup save views.png" />

## Working with views

Once saved, you find your views in the **Views**  dropdown. If there are many saved views, you can use the search box to find them.

To use a view, simply click on it and all filter conditions and columns will be applied.

Click the **X** icon next to view name to remove a view. 

<img alt="views dropdown.png" />


# State transitions
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/state-transitions

Litium uses a Finite state automata implementation internally to manage state transitions. Order states and Shipment states and how to interact with them are explained below.

## Sales order states

Sales orders goes through following states: 

<img alt="order states.png" />

### Init

This is the initial state of an order, and in Litium backoffice, you would normally not find orders in Init state.

If a order has a valid guaranteed payment, but failed to get confirmed for some reason, the order will remain in Init state.

Orders that are pending approval (B2B order approval flow) would also be in Init state, until they are approved.

### **Confirmed**

Order has a guaranteed payment. The payment can be for part of the order. This condition is configured in accelerator, see below.

### Pending processing

The order is ready to be processed. Usually this means that the order should be exported to the ERP system. This state transition will happen automatically through a cron job run in the platform.

You can configure a delay for the transition from *Confirmed* to *PendingProcessing* state. This can be done through in Backoffice *Settings -> Sales -> System settings -> Maintenance -> Set order state to Pending processing after (minutes)*, or directly through the settings of the cron job in Litium's appsettings.json.

### **Processing**

Order fulfilment has started. Usually this means, the order is exported to ERP and further processed.

### **Completed**

Order fulfilment process is completed.

All shipments are shipped, and payments for those shipments are resolved.

If a order is cancelled (fully or partially), it will still show a "Completed" state, since the order fullfilment process has come to an end. The shipments for the cancelled order will state, that it is cancelled., and payments will have cancelled transactions.

## State transition validation rules

To ensure accurate processing of orders and shipments based on payment status, state transition validations are essential. The MVC accelerator incorporates a built-in state transition validation system that prescribes how order states should adapt to various conditions, such as shipment status.

However, with the adoption of the new headless architecture, the responsibility for these validations has shifted to the Litium platform rather than the accelerator. This transition means that the Litium platform now houses the validation processes.

For those utilizing an MVC accelerator or crafting custom state transition validations, there is an option to disable the platform's newly implemented validation mechanisms by adding configuration settings.

To disable a specific state transition validation rule, the corresponding key must be inserted into the Litium:Sales:DisabledStateTransitionValidations collection. The available keys are:

•  SalesOrder\_\_PaymentIsGuaranteed: Disables the validation ensuring that payment for the sales order is guaranteed.

•  SalesOrder\_\_AllShipmentIsShipped: Disables the validation checking if all shipments have been shipped when the order is transitioning to the completed state.

•  Shipment\_\_OrderNotConfirmed: Disables the validation that verifies the order is confirmed when the shipment status is updated to processing.

Following example shows the condition to consider an order to be in "Confirmed" state.

```csharp theme={null}
using System.Linq;
using Litium.Sales;
using Litium.Validations;

namespace Litium.Application.Sales.StateTransitions
{
    public class InitToConfirmedCondition : StateTransitionValidationRule<SalesOrder>
    {
        private readonly OrderOverviewService _orderOverviewService;

        public InitToConfirmedCondition(OrderOverviewService orderOverviewService)
        {
            _orderOverviewService = orderOverviewService;
        }

        public override string FromState => Sales.OrderState.Init;

        public override string ToState => Sales.OrderState.Confirmed;

        public override ValidationResult Validate(SalesOrder entity)
        {
            var result = new ValidationResult();
            //Administrator is not allowed to Confirm orders, they are automatically confirmed when payment is done.
            // At least one payment is guaranteed. In paymentInfo, there is at least one transaction that has TransactionType = Authorize
            // and TransactionResult = success.
            var isPaymentGuaranteed = _orderOverviewService.Get(entity.SystemId)
                .PaymentOverviews.Any(x => x.Transactions.Any(t => t.TransactionType == TransactionType.Authorize
                                                                    && t.TransactionResult == TransactionResult.Success));
            if (!isPaymentGuaranteed)
            {
                result.AddError("Payment", "Payment was not guaranteed.");
            }

            return result;
        }
    }
}
```

Conditions to enter these states can be configured. If the condition fails, order will stay in its previous state.

StateTransitionValidationRule::FromState and StateTransitionValidationRule::ToState properties identify when the Rule evaluation is triggered. In above example, it is triggered when order goes from Init to Confirmed state.

If there are any errors added to the ValidationResult returned, it is considered as a validation failure, and the order will remain in the current state. In above example, it will remain in Init state.

## Responding to state changes

To respond to state transition events, listen to the event fired when the transition take place. In following example, an order confirmation email is sent, when order enters the Confirmed state.

```csharp theme={null}
using Litium.Events;
using Litium.Runtime;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using System.Threading;
using Litium.Accelerator.Services;
using Litium.Sales.Events;
using Litium.Accelerator.Mailing;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.StateTransitions
{
    [Autostart]
    public class SalesOrderEventListener : IAsyncAutostart
    {
        private readonly EventBroker _eventBroker;
        private readonly MailService _mailService;

        public SalesOrderEventListener(
            EventBroker eventBroker,
            MailService mailService)
        {
            _eventBroker = eventBroker;
            _mailService = mailService;
        }

        ValueTask IAsyncAutostart.StartAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            _eventBroker.Subscribe<SalesOrderConfirmed>(x =>
            {
                _mailService.SendEmail(new OrderConfirmationEmail(x.Item.ChannelSystemId.Value, x.SystemId, x.Item.CustomerInfo.Email), false);
            });

            return ValueTask.CompletedTask;
        }
    }
}
```

*Litium.Sales.Events* namespace contains the list of events that you can listen to in Sales area.

## Shipment states

Following is the main state flow of a shipment in Litium.

<img alt="litium-8-shipment-states.png" />

* When a shipment is first created, it is in the Init state.
* When a shipment is moved to Processing state, payment processing will start. During payment processing, the shipment money is calculated, and if it is needed the relevant amount is captured through payment service provider app.
* When the payments are captured for shipment, the shipment is moved to ReadyToShip state.
  * The ERP system may now handover the package to the shipping company. [See process flow here >>](/apis/connect-apis/domain-areas/erp-domain/business-processes/order-fulfilment-process-main-flow#order-fulfilment-process-main-flow).
* When the ERP system has notified that package is handed over, the shipment is set to Shipped state.

Note: No business logic is included in Litium 8.3 for shipment states canceled and returned, but they are now reflected in the UI and they can set via StateTransitionsService.


# Update historical orders
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/sales/update-historical-orders

This script will update the exchange rate on orders which have already been created.

Orders in the database have an exchange rate column. To calculate and show sales data for orders connected to campaigns and discounts, the system uses data from ExchangeRate and BaseCurrencyCode columns. 

Not all orders in Litium 7, and Litium 8 have base currencies and exchange rates. This script will fill in that data, and update the exchange rate value on historical orders.

Updating the exchange rates on already placed orders may provide improved statistical reports.

```sql theme={null}
--Finds and updates historical Orders that are missing BaseCurrencyCode and ExchangeRate.
--Defines the Base currency code to set for historical Orders
DECLARE @baseCurrencyCode nvarchar(5) = 'SEK'
--Defines the Currency code which Orders were paid with
DECLARE @currencyCode nvarchar(5) = 'USD'
--Defines the exchange rate, to convert from @currencyCode to @baseCurrencyCode
DECLARE @exchangeRate decimal(18,8) = 9.87
--Defines from date, to get orders in the specific date range
DECLARE @fromDate datetimeoffset(7) = '2022/04/25'
--Defines to date, to get orders in the specific date range
DECLARE @toDate datetimeoffset(7) = '2022/05/27'

UPDATE [Sales].[Order]
SET BaseCurrencyCode = @baseCurrencyCode, ExchangeRate = @exchangeRate
WHERE BaseCurrencyCode IS NULL AND CurrencyCode = @currencyCode AND OrderDate >= @fromDate AND OrderDate <= @toDate
```


# Blocks
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/websites-cms/blocks

Blocks are content components that can be reused in many places.

## Introduction

When structuring and working with content, blocks are useful as they are reusable components that can be used in several places. For example a Banner block is typically used in many places, with the same graphical rendering, although with different images in different places depending on the story you are telling. If the case is that the banner should have the same image and texts in multiple places, there are global blocks, which content is centrally managed.

Blocks are nested (version 8.9), meaning that a block can contain another block, increasing flexibility in structuring content for managebility.

**Entities that can have blocks**

* Page
* Campaign
* Website
* Category

## Data model and field templates

The lowest level of data modelling in Litium is a field, which technically is a field definition based on a field type. To set up different types of blocks you define a data model using fields and field templates.

As an example, a banner block can be defined as below and used for pages and campaigns.

**Field template: Banner**

* Field: Image
* Field: Header
* Field: Text
* Field: Link
* Field: Button text

## Nested blocks

Blocks can have nested blocks allowing more flexibility in the data modelling of your content structure. In the field template of a block you define what block types is allowed for a block to have nested.

By allowing only certain block types, we facilitate for administrators managing the content, and minimize the risk of errors in rendering the blocks.

As an example, a footer with columns that have links, can be defined as in the image and table below using nested blocks, and used by the website entity.

**Note** the block container explained in the next section.

<img alt="footer as blocks.png" />

*Conceptual image of nested blocks for a footer.*

<table><tbody><tr><td><p><b>Block container: Footer</b></p></td><td> </td><td> </td></tr><tr><td>Allowed nested blocks: Footer column</td><td> </td><td> </td></tr><tr><td> </td><td><b>Field template: Footer column</b></td><td> </td></tr><tr><td> </td><td>Allowed nested blocks: Footer links</td><td> </td></tr><tr><td> </td><td> </td><td><b>Field template: Footer links</b></td></tr><tr><td> </td><td> </td><td>Allowed nested blocks: None</td></tr><tr><td> </td><td> </td><td>Field: Header</td></tr><tr><td> </td><td> </td><td>Field: Links (array)</td></tr></tbody></table>

*Table with field templates of nested blocks for a footer.*

## Block containers

Block containers are needed to render blocks, and to be able to place a block in an entity, the entity needs at least one block container defined.

Block containers are defined in the field template of entities supporting blocks, and the block container is needed in the code for a view to know how and where to render the block.

#### Best practices

A home page migh have only one block container, and administrators can add and sort the blocks freely insode the whole page.

A website, on the other hand might need several containers to indicate where in the framework content should be placed. For example, a website might have defined one container for the primary navigation and another for a footer.

<img alt="block containers.png" />

*Image showing concept of using block containers.*

## Global and local blocks

Global blocks are updated centrally. This is convenient if the same content is used in several places, for example a banner promoting the same campaign would probably have the same image and text even though it is showed in many different places in the site. 

Local blocks are the opposite of global blocks, and they in use only by an instance of a an entity like a page or a campaign.

A local block can be converted to a global and vice versa.

A block can have both local and global blocks nested.

Global blocks are listed in its own space in the backoffice under Websites > Blocks.

## Draft and published

A draft version of the block will be stored when any changes are made to it. There can only be one draft version of a block at any time. Technically, when the draft is published, the changes are migrated to the corresponding block.

Note: A block and its draft always have the same *SystemId*.

<img alt="Blocks 3.jpg" />

## Settings

All blocks instances share a number of settings.

**Channels**

Use the channels to define the channels where the block should be active and visible to site visitors.

The channel settings are inherited from the block's parent entity.

**Permissions**

You can set permissions on block instance level to restrict which users should be able to read, write or publish the block.

The permission settings are inherited from the parent entity.

**Audience**

Use the audience settings to personalize the experience of site visitors, by defining which target groups or groups that should see the block.

## Creating your own blocks

There is a detailed guide to defining and working with your own custom blocks. The guide is split into two, [one for the MVC Accelerator](/platform/guides/how-to-create-custom-blocks-in-mvc-accelerator) and [one for the React Accelerator](/platform/guides/how-to-create-blocks-in-react-accelerator).
