# Create a website
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/websites-cms/create-a-web

The website represents a page structure and has data modeling that is used for settings.

To create a website, go to back office **Settings** > **Websites** > **Website**. 

1. Click **New**. 
2. Select a website template and a home page field template. When you create a website, a start page will be added automatically.
3. Click **OK**.

<img alt="Websites data modelling 2.jpg" />

When you have created a website, you can add constant strings to it on the **Texts** tab. The values you enter here can be used across the code and are easily edited/translated on this screen.

Here is an example of how to add or update a website text value programmatically, and get it from the text container:

```csharp theme={null}
var website = new Website(_websiteFieldTemplate.SystemId)
{
    Id = this.UniqueString()
};
website.Localizations.CurrentCulture.Name = "WebsiteName";
website.Texts.AddOrUpdateValue("sampleKey", "en-us", "en-value");
website.Texts.AddOrUpdateValue("sampleKey", "sv-se", "se-value");
//Create
_websiteService.Create(website);
var savedWebsite = _websiteService.Get(website.Id);
var usText = savedWebsite.Texts.GetValue("samplekey", "en-us");
var seText = savedWebsite.Texts.GetValue("samplekey", new CultureInfo("sv-se"));
```


# New page editing - beta
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/websites-cms/new-page-editing

This article describes the new "Page editing" feature, which allows content editors to edit and preview page and block content directly.

## Overview

The core of this feature involves displaying a website page within an iframe in the Litium backoffice. To enable live editing, an additional script is added to the website's frontend. This script provides two main functionalities:

1. **Overlays:** When hovering over specific blocks on the page (within the iframe), interactive overlays appear. These overlays contain buttons that trigger editing actions.

2. **Hot Reloading:** When a block is updated, the feature enables the page to "hot reload" the modified block, updating the preview without requiring a full page reload.

## Scripts Integration

The scripts, named as Teleport, needs to be included in your website's frontend. They are automatically integrated into MVC and React Accelerators. For other frameworks, manual script inclusion and hot reload implementation are necessary. The following breakdown details the changes made to MVC and React Accelerators for reference.

### **Example (MVC):**

The script is injected automatically by the system. Only the LiveEditing component needs to be added.

```xml theme={null}
var editMode = (bool?)ViewContext.ViewData["EditMode"] == true;
@if (editMode)
{
    <LiveEditing id="liveEditing" /> 
}
```

### Example (React):

A *preview* query has been implemented in the React Storefront API to load preview-specific scripts and styles. This query utilizes the *`x-litium-storefront-context-url`* header to identify preview pages and avoid loading these resources on live pages. The preview data is queried in *`websiteService.server.ts`*, and Teleport files are included as shown below.

```xml theme={null}
<body className="overflow-x-hidden">
    {website.preview && (
      <>
        {website.preview.scripts.map((value, i) => (
          <Script
            key={'preview-script-' + i}
            src={buildServerUrl(value.src)}
            type={value.attributes?.find((a) => a.name === 'type')?.value}
            strategy="beforeInteractive"
            crossOrigin="anonymous
          ></Script>
        ))}
        {website.preview.styleSheets.map((value, i) => (
          <link
            key={'preview-css-' + i}
            href={buildServerUrl(value.src)}
            rel="stylesheet"
          ></link>
        ))}
        <LiveEditing>{children}</LiveEditing>
      </>
    )}
    {!website.preview && children}
</body>
```

The `<LiveEditing>` component is crucial for hot reloading functionality.

## Components

The script provides two main components:

* **`CoverComponent`:**

  * Scans the page for elements with a specific attribute (e.g., `data-litium-block-id`) that identify editable blocks.
  * Creates an `OverlayComponent` for each identified block.
* **`OverlayComponent`:**

  * Creates an overlay that appears on hover over a block.
  * Contains buttons to trigger editing actions.
  * Sends messages to the Litium backoffice when buttons are clicked.

## Hot Reloading

The `<LiveEditing>` component handles hot reloading of updated blocks.

* **MVC:** Listens for events from Litium and fetches updated block content from a specific controller (`BlockPreviewController`).

* **React:** Listens for events and uses Next.js's [`revalidatePath`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) function to update the page cache.

* **Other Frameworks:** You'll need to implement a similar `<LiveEditing>` component to handle hot reloading based on your framework's capabilities. If no hot reloading is implemented, the iframe will be fully reloaded when a content is updated.

## Communication Flow

Communication between the overlay, the `<LiveEditing>` component, and the Litium backoffice happens through events and messages:

1. **User Interaction:** The user clicks a button in the overlay (e.g., "Edit").

2. **Overlay Action:** The overlay captures the click and sends an event to the backoffice. The event includes the block ID.

3. **Backoffice Processing:** The backoffice receives the message, extracts the block ID, and performs the requested action (e.g., opens the block editor).

4. **Hot Reload Request:** If the backoffice updates a block, it sends an event back to the iframe to trigger a hot reload.

5. **LiveEditing Response:** The `<LiveEditing>` component in the iframe listens for these messages and updates the page content accordingly. Without it, or for unhandled events, the backoffice performs a full iframe reload. To listen for events that signal block updates, use the `litiumBridge` object. This object becomes available after importing the live editing script and provides a method called `.on()` to register event listeners. For example, to listen for the `'blockUpdated'` event, you can use `window.litiumBridge.on('blockUpdated', handleBlockUpdateEvent)`, where `handleBlockUpdateEvent` is your function to handle the update.

The following sequence diagram illustrates the block update process.

<img alt="UpdateBlockDiagram.png" />

## window\.litiumBridge

This is a global object that is made available when you import the live editing script into your web page. It provides an interface for communication between the Accelerator website and the Backoffice.

| Name   | Parameters                                                                                                           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **on** | `eventName` — name of the event to listen.<br />`fn` — callback function to be executed when the event is triggered. | Registers an event listener for content change events. By registering an event, it informs the system that Accelerator can handle the event, enabling seamless updates within the iframe. Without registration, the system performs a full iframe reload for each update. |

## Events

| Name                  | Parameters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                          |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **blockAdded**        | `{ systemId, referenceBlockSystemId, parentBlockSystemId, containerId, index, addBefore, isContainerEmpty }`<br />`systemId` — the system id of the new block.<br />`referenceBlockSystemId` — the system id of the existing block that serves as a reference.<br />`parentBlockSystemId` — the system id of the parent block, if the adding block is a nested block.<br />`containerId` — the id of the container, if the adding block isn't a nested block.<br />`index` — the index to add the block at.<br />`addBefore` — a boolean value. If *true*, the new block is added before the reference block; if *false*, it is added after.<br />`isContainerEmpty` — a boolean value. If *true*, the container to add the block to doesn't have any block; if *false*, it has block(s). | When a block is added, or duplicated |
| **blockUpdated**      | `{ systemId }`<br />`systemId` — the system id of the block.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | When a block is updated              |
| **blockDeleted**      | `{ systemId, parentBlockSystemId }`<br />`systemId` — the system id of the block.<br />`parentBlockSystemId` — the system id of the parent block, if the deleting block is a nested block.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | When a block is deleted              |
| **blockOrderChanged** | `{ systemId, index, previousIndex, containerId, previousContainerId }`<br />`systemId` — the system id of the block.<br />`index` — the new index.<br />`previousIndex` — the old index.<br />`containerId` — the id of the new container.<br />`previousContainerId` — the id of the old container.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | When a block's order is changed      |
| **pageUpdated**       | `{ systemId }`<br />`systemId` — the system id of the page.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | When a page is updated               |

## Upgrade

To leverage the new Page editing feature after upgrading the Litium platform, you must update your existing Accelerator. The necessary file changes are outlined below for MVC and React Accelerators.

Ensure a smooth upgrade by consulting the [upgrade and maintenance guidelines](/accelerators/mvc-accelerator/upgrade-and-maintenance).

### MVC Accelerator

* /Src/Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Client/Scripts/Components/LiveEditing.js (Added)
* /Src/Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Client/Scripts/index.js (Updated)
* /Src/Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Controllers/Api/BlockPreviewController.cs (Added)
* /Src/Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Controllers/ControllerBase.cs (Updated)
* /Src/Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Extensions/BlockContainerHelperExtension.cs (Updated)
* /Src/Litium.Accelerator.Mvc/Views/Shared/\_Layout.cshtml (Updated)

### React Accelerator

* /app/actions/liveEditing/revalidatePage.ts (Added)
* /app/layout.tsx (Updated)
* /components/blocks/LiveEditing.tsx (Added)
* /models/preview\.ts (Added)
* /models/website.ts (Updated)
* /services/imageService.ts (Updated)
* /services/urlService.ts (Updated)
* /services/websiteService.server.ts (Updated)

## Known issues

* Using the same global block multiple times within a page may cause updates to be applied to the wrong global block.
* To add blocks to an empty page, the classic Page editor should be used instead.


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/websites-cms/overview

Websites is Litium's CMS. Here, all websites and web pages are managed.

A website is one of several channels where content can be published.

To read more about the field framework in the websites area, please see [Websites](/platform/areas/data-modelling/websites-data-modeling) [data modeling](/platform/areas/data-modelling/product-data-modeling).


# Pages
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/areas/websites-cms/pages

Pages are shown hierarchically per site in the Websites area.

To access the settings of a page:

1. Browse to the page in the tree structure in the left pane in the **Websites** area.
2. Click the context menu (the three dots) in the upper right corner. 
3. Choose **Edit**.

<img alt="Pages 0a.jpg" />

To remove a page, click **Move to trashcan** on the context menu, or in the upper right corner in edit view. Pages in the trashcan will remain there until they are actively removed.

To restore pages from the trashcan to their original place in the tree structure, click **Trashcan** in the tree structure, select a page and then click **Restore** in the upper right corner.

## Draft pages and publishing

When changes are made to a page, a draft version of the page will be stored. Only one draft version of a page can exist at the same time. Technically, when the draft is published, the changes are migrated to the corresponding page.

Note: A page and its draft always have the same *SystemId*.

<img alt="Pages 1.jpg" />

## Channels

On the **Channels** tab in page edit mode individual pages can be activated and deactivated in different channels. By default, all channels connected to the page will be active when a new page is created. A time interval for when a page should be active in a channel can be set.

## Page service

*PageService* is the main class to use when manipulating the *Page* object. These are the most common methods:

* *Create*/*Get*/*Update*/*Delete*: Basic CRUD actions on the *Page* object.
* *IEnumerable\<Page> GetChildPages(Guid parentPageSystemId, Guid? websiteSystemId = null)*: This method will return all child pages for a given page or website.
  * If *parentPageSystemId* is supplied, then this method will return all child pages of that level.
  * If *parentPageSystemId* is empty (*Guid.Empty*) and *websiteSystemId* is not empty, then the method will return all child pages on the website.
* *void SortChildPages(Guid parentPageSystemId, \[NotNull] IList\<Guid> sortedChildSystemIds)*: Sorting child pages with the order defined in *sortedChildSystemId*.
* *void UnPublish(\[NotNull] Page page)*: Unpublish a given page.


# Add a panel
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/add-panel

Use the SDK add command to generate a web component panel that appears in a Litium backoffice area (Customers, Products, Sales, Media, or Websites).

## What is an area panel?

An area panel is a Custom Element (web component) that the Litium host mounts inside one of the five backoffice area navigation panels. When a user clicks the panel entry in the area nav, your component is rendered directly — no URL routing required.

The five areas you can target are: **Customers**, **Products**, **Sales**, **Media**, and **Websites**.

***

## Generate a panel

From your **extension project root**, run:

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk add panel
```

The CLI will prompt for:

| Prompt             | Example         |
| ------------------ | --------------- |
| Panel display name | `Pricing Rules` |
| Admin area         | `products`      |

You can also pass the type directly and skip the outer type-selection prompt:

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk add panel
```

### What gets generated

Given the name `"Pricing Rules"` in the `products` area on a React project:

```
src/panels/pricing-rules.tsx        ← web component file
extension.manifest.json             ← updated with new target entry
src/index.ts                        ← import injected automatically
```

The manifest entry added:

```json theme={null}
{
  "target": "products.menu.item",
  "name": "Pricing Rules",
  "component": "litium-ext-my-extension-panel-pricing-rules"
}
```

The custom element tag is deterministic: `{customElementTag}-panel-{slug}`, where `{customElementTag}` comes from the `common.web.component` target already in your manifest.

***

## Generated component examples

The CLI generates a framework-appropriate starting template. Each template creates the custom element and registers it with `customElements.define`.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="React">
    ```tsx theme={null}
    // src/panels/pricing-rules.tsx
    import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';

    function PricingRulesPanel() {
      return (
        <div className="panel">
          <h2>Pricing Rules</h2>
          {/* TODO: add your panel content here */}
        </div>
      );
    }

    class PricingRulesPanelElement extends HTMLElement {
      private _root: ReturnType<typeof createRoot> | null = null;

      connectedCallback(): void {
        this._root = createRoot(this);
        this._render();
      }

      disconnectedCallback(): void {
        this._root?.unmount();
        this._root = null;
      }

      private _render(): void {
        this._root?.render(<PricingRulesPanel />);
      }
    }

    customElements.define(
      'litium-ext-my-extension-panel-pricing-rules',
      PricingRulesPanelElement,
    );
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Vue">
    ```vue theme={null}
    <!-- src/panels/pricing-rules.vue -->
    <template>
      <div class="panel">
        <h2>Pricing Rules</h2>
        <!-- TODO: add your panel content here -->
      </div>
    </template>

    <script setup lang="ts">
    // PricingRulesPanel — mounted as custom element
    </script>

    <script lang="ts">
    import { defineCustomElement } from 'vue';
    import PricingRulesPanelComponent from './pricing-rules.vue';

    customElements.define(
      'litium-ext-my-extension-panel-pricing-rules',
      defineCustomElement(PricingRulesPanelComponent),
    );
    </script>
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Angular">
    ```typescript theme={null}
    // src/panels/pricing-rules.ts
    import { Component } from '@angular/core';
    import { createCustomElement } from '@angular/elements';
    import { ApplicationRef } from '@angular/core';

    @Component({
      selector: 'litium-ext-my-extension-panel-pricing-rules',
      standalone: true,
      template: `
        <div class="panel">
          <h2>Pricing Rules</h2>
          <!-- TODO: add your panel content here -->
        </div>
      `,
    })
    export class PricingRulesPanelComponent {}

    export function registerPricingRulesPanel(appRef: ApplicationRef): void {
      const el = createCustomElement(PricingRulesPanelComponent, {
        injector: appRef.injector,
      });
      customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension-panel-pricing-rules', el);
    }
    ```

    Then call `registerPricingRulesPanel(appRef)` during your app's bootstrap.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Vanilla">
    ```typescript theme={null}
    // src/panels/pricing-rules.ts
    class PricingRulesPanelElement extends HTMLElement {
      connectedCallback(): void {
        this.render();
      }

      private render(): void {
        this.innerHTML = `
          <div class="panel">
            <h2>Pricing Rules</h2>
            <!-- TODO: add your panel content here -->
          </div>
        `;
      }
    }

    customElements.define(
      'litium-ext-my-extension-panel-pricing-rules',
      PricingRulesPanelElement,
    );
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

***

## Using the Bridge API inside a panel

Panels have access to `window.litiumExtension` just like any other extension component. Use it to fetch data, show notifications, or get the current user context:

```tsx theme={null}
// Inside your panel component (React example)
function PricingRulesPanel() {
  const [data, setData] = React.useState(null);

  React.useEffect(() => {
    window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/my-extension/pricing-rules')
      .then((res) => res.json())
      .then(setData);
  }, []);

  return <div>{/* render data */}</div>;
}
```

See [Extension Bridge API](/platform/extensions/extension-bridge-api) for the full reference.

***

## Manifest reference

The `{area}.menu.item` target entry written to `extension.manifest.json`:

| Field       | Type                         | Required | Description                                                   |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`    | `"customers.menu.item"` etc. | Yes      | One of: `customers`, `products`, `sales`, `media`, `websites` |
| `name`      | `string`                     | Yes      | Display name shown in the area navigation                     |
| `component` | `string`                     | Yes      | Custom element tag. Must start with `litium-ext-`.            |

See the full [Extension Manifest Reference](/platform/extensions/extension-manifest-reference) for all target types.


# Add a settings page
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/add-settings-page

Use the SDK add command to generate a new page in the Litium backoffice Settings area, complete with a menu entry and a component file wired to your router.

## What is a settings page?

A settings page is a route-enabled page component that appears as an entry in the Settings sidebar. The Litium host navigates to your extension's URL when the user clicks the menu item, and your web component renders the page content.

Settings pages are registered via the `settings.menu.item` manifest target, paired with a `common.web.component` bundle that handles the URL and rendering.

***

## Generate a settings page

From your **extension project root**, run:

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk add settings-page
```

The CLI will prompt for:

| Prompt                | Default                               | Description                              |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Display name          | —                                     | Label shown in the Settings sidebar      |
| Settings group ref ID | `system.settings`                     | The settings group this item is added to |
| URL path              | `/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/{id}` | The full path the menu item activates    |

### What gets generated

Given the name `"Integration Config"` on a React project:

```
src/settings/integration-config.tsx     ← page component
extension.manifest.json                 ← updated with settings.menu.item target
src/index.ts                            ← import injected automatically
```

The manifest entry added:

```json theme={null}
{
  "target": "settings.menu.item",
  "name": "Integration Config",
  "ref_id": "system.settings",
  "url": "/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension/integration-config"
}
```

***

## Wire up the route

The component file is imported automatically into your entry point. The `add` command also injects the route when it finds a router file. If that fails, add a route for the new URL manually:

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="React">
    In your router (`src/App.tsx`):

    ```tsx theme={null}
    import IntegrationConfigPage from './settings/integration-config';

    // Add to your <Routes>:
    <Route path="/integration-config" element={<IntegrationConfigPage />} />
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Vue">
    In your router (`src/router.ts`):

    ```typescript theme={null}
    {
      path: '/integration-config',
      component: () => import('./settings/integration-config.vue'),
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Angular">
    In your routing module:

    ```typescript theme={null}
    import { IntegrationConfigPageComponent } from './settings/integration-config';

    { path: 'integration-config', component: IntegrationConfigPageComponent }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Vanilla">
    Register the route `/integration-config` in your application entry point:

    ```typescript theme={null}
    // In your routing/init logic:
    router.register('/integration-config', renderIntegrationConfigPage);
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

***

## Generated component examples

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="React">
    ```tsx theme={null}
    // src/settings/integration-config.tsx
    export default function IntegrationConfigPage() {
      return (
        <div className="settings-page">
          <h1>Integration Config</h1>
          {/* TODO: add your settings page content here */}
        </div>
      );
    }
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Vue">
    ```vue theme={null}
    <!-- src/settings/integration-config.vue -->
    <template>
      <div class="settings-page">
        <h1>Integration Config</h1>
        <!-- TODO: add your settings page content here -->
      </div>
    </template>

    <script setup lang="ts">
    // IntegrationConfigPage
    </script>
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Angular">
    ```typescript theme={null}
    // src/settings/integration-config.ts
    import { Component } from '@angular/core';

    @Component({
      selector: 'app-integrationconfig-page',
      standalone: true,
      template: `
        <div class="settings-page">
          <h1>Integration Config</h1>
          <!-- TODO: add your settings page content here -->
        </div>
      `,
    })
    export class IntegrationConfigPageComponent {}
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Vanilla">
    ```typescript theme={null}
    // src/settings/integration-config.ts
    export function renderIntegrationConfigPage(container: HTMLElement) {
      container.innerHTML = `
        <div class="settings-page">
          <h1>Integration Config</h1>
          <!-- TODO: add your settings page content here -->
        </div>
      `;
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

***

## How URL routing works

The Settings menu item sets the `sub-path` attribute on your Custom Element when the user navigates to the settings URL. Your router reads this attribute to set the initial route.

The flow is the same as for any other extension page — see [Extension Routing](/platform/extensions/extension-routing) for the full picture.

If your settings extension has multiple pages (e.g. a tabbed settings area), add more routes inside the same component and navigate between them using `window.litiumExtension.navigate()`.

***

## Multiple settings pages in one extension

Each call to `add settings-page` adds one `settings.menu.item` entry. You can have multiple entries pointing to different sub-paths of the same extension:

```json theme={null}
"targets": [
  {
    "target": "common.web.component",
    "name": "my-extension",
    "bundleUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/my-extension/extension.js",
    "customElementTag": "litium-ext-my-extension"
  },
  {
    "target": "settings.menu.item",
    "name": "General Settings",
    "ref_id": "system.settings",
    "url": "/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension/general"
  },
  {
    "target": "settings.menu.item",
    "name": "Integration Config",
    "ref_id": "system.settings",
    "url": "/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension/integration-config"
  }
]
```

Both entries render the same Custom Element (`litium-ext-my-extension`) but pass different `sub-path` values, letting your router display the correct page.

***

## Manifest reference

The `settings.menu.item` target entry written to `extension.manifest.json`:

| Field        | Type                   | Required | Description                                                                       |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`     | `"settings.menu.item"` | Yes      | Target type                                                                       |
| `name`       | `string`               | Yes      | Display label in the Settings sidebar. Supports `t:` prefix for translation keys. |
| `ref_id`     | `string`               | Yes      | Reference ID of the settings group (e.g. `"system.settings"`)                     |
| `url`        | `string`               | Yes      | Full URL path activated when the menu item is clicked                             |
| `permission` | `string`               | No       | Permission key required to see this item                                          |

See the full [Extension Manifest Reference](/platform/extensions/extension-manifest-reference).


# AI-assisted extension development
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/ai-assisted-development

Speed up Litium extension development with AI coding assistants. Install the litium-developer skill to give your AI agent full context about the extension system.

## Overview

AI coding assistants — GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude, and others — can write production-ready Litium extension code if they understand the Custom Element architecture, the `window.litiumExtension` bridge API, and the framework-specific routing patterns. Out of the box, they don't. The **litium-developer skill** solves this by giving your AI agent a compact, accurate reference it can load on demand.

***

## Install the skill

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="npx skills (recommended)">
    Install the skill with one command from your project directory:

    ```bash theme={null}
    npx skills add https://github.com/LitiumAB/agent-skills --skill litium-developer
    ```

    To verify the skill is loaded, ask Copilot:

    ```text theme={null}
    What does window.litiumExtension.navigate() do?
    ```

    If the skill is loaded, Copilot will give an accurate answer about the bridge API rather than a generic response.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

***

## What the skill gives your AI

Once installed, the skill provides your AI agent with:

| Knowledge area     | Details covered                                                                         |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Architecture       | Custom Element + bridge API diagram, host-extension contract                            |
| CLI commands       | `create`, `dev`, `build` with all flags                                                 |
| React patterns     | Custom Element class, `MemoryRouter` with `key`, `routeChanged` subscription            |
| Vue patterns       | `defineCustomElement`, `createMemoryHistory`, `syncRouterFromHost`, `createNavigate`    |
| Angular patterns   | `createApplication`, `@angular/elements`, `InMemoryLocationStrategy`, version isolation |
| Bridge API         | All `window.litiumExtension.*` methods with signatures and examples                     |
| Routing            | `subPath` attribute, `navigate()` vs `replaceUrl()`, event loop prevention              |
| Manifest reference | All `extension.manifest.json` fields and target types                                   |
| Vite config        | IIFE build, `litiumExtension()` plugin, per-framework plugin setup                      |
| Unit testing       | `window.litiumExtension` mock template, Vitest and Jest examples                        |
| Critical rules     | Tag naming, guard patterns, CSRF fetch, cleanup lifecycle                               |
| Common mistakes    | Symptom → root cause → fix table                                                        |

***

## Example prompts

Once the skill is installed, paste these prompts directly into your AI assistant:

### Scaffold and explain

```text theme={null}
I have a new React extension project generated by @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk.
Explain what src/index.tsx does and why MemoryRouter uses key={subPath}.
```

### Add a new page

```text theme={null}
Add a third page called OrderDetailPage to my React extension.
- Route: /orders/:id
- Fetches /Litium/app/api/orders/{id} using window.litiumExtension.fetch
- Shows a success notification when save is clicked
- Has a Back button that calls window.litiumExtension.navigate('/orders')
```

### Fix a routing bug

```text theme={null}
My back button does not work in my Vue extension.
I'm using router.push() to navigate between pages.
What is wrong and how do I fix it?
```

### Write tests

```text theme={null}
Write Vitest unit tests for my React App component.
Include the correct window.litiumExtension mock.
Test that subPath="/pagea" renders PageA and subPath="/pageb" renders PageB.
```

### Migrate from Module Federation

```text theme={null}
I have an Angular Module Federation extension. Show me how to run the migration CLI
and explain what the InMemoryLocationStrategy does in the migrated project.
```

### Manifest and registration

```text theme={null}
Write the extension.manifest.json for my extension with:
- id: order-dashboard
- A common.web.component target with customElementTag litium-ext-order-dashboard
- A settings.menu.item target pointing to /Litium/UI/settings/extensions/order-dashboard
- English and Swedish translations for the name
```

***

## Tips for effective AI-assisted development

**Be specific about the framework.** The skill covers React, Vue, and Angular — always mention which one you are using so the AI generates the correct patterns.

**Reference the bridge API by name.** Saying "use the bridge API to navigate" gives better results than "navigate to the next page". The skill teaches the AI the exact method names.

**Ask for the complete Custom Element class.** Scaffolded projects sometimes get modified. If something breaks, ask the AI to regenerate the full `index.tsx` (or `index.ts`) from scratch using the skill patterns — this is faster than debugging incremental changes.

**Use the testing mock pattern.** The skill includes the exact `beforeEach` mock for `window.litiumExtension`. Ask the AI to add tests first — the mock template is the most error-prone part to write from memory.

**Let the AI check the manifest.** Paste your `extension.manifest.json` and ask the AI to validate it against the manifest reference in the skill. Missing `litium-ext-` prefix and `type: "ui"` are the two most common deployment mistakes.

***

## Keep the skill up to date

When the extension SDK releases breaking changes, update the skill:

```bash theme={null}
npx skills update
```

Or re-run the manual copy command to fetch the latest version from GitHub.

To check the currently installed version:

```bash theme={null}
npx skills check
```


# Create an Angular extension
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/create-angular-extension

Step-by-step guide for building a Litium backoffice extension with Angular and @angular/elements. Your extension version is completely independent of the host.

## Prerequisites

* Node.js 20 or later
* A running Litium instance (local or remote) with backoffice access
* Basic familiarity with Angular and TypeScript
* Registry configured — **complete [SDK Installation](/platform/extensions/sdk-installation) first**

<Note>
  **Any Angular version works.** The Litium host runs Angular 20. Your extension uses its own fully isolated Angular runtime — there are no shared Angular dependencies. The scaffold uses Angular 20 with standalone components, but the same approach applies to other Angular versions.
</Note>

***

## Step 1 — Scaffold the project

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk create my-extension --framework angular
cd my-extension
npm install
```

### What was generated?

| File / folder               | Purpose                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/main.ts`               | Entry point — `createApplication`, `InMemoryLocationStrategy`, and custom element registration |
| `src/app/app.component.ts`  | Root standalone component with `<router-outlet>` and host path sync                            |
| `src/app/app.routes.ts`     | Route definitions                                                                              |
| `src/app/home.component.ts` | Default home page component                                                                    |
| `vite.config.ts`            | IIFE build with `@analogjs/vite-plugin-angular` and the Litium Vite plugin                     |
| `extension.manifest.json`   | Deployment descriptor — includes a settings menu item target                                   |
| `.dev.config.json`          | Dev server port (default `3000`) and Litium backend URL                                        |

The scaffold also includes Jest unit tests and a Playwright e2e smoke test.

***

## Step 2 — Understand version isolation

Open `src/main.ts`. The scaffold uses `createApplication` (not `NgModule`) to bootstrap an isolated Angular platform, registers an in-memory `LocationStrategy`, and defines the custom element:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/main.ts
import 'zone.js';
import { ApplicationConfig, Injectable } from '@angular/core';
import { LocationStrategy } from '@angular/common';
import type { LocationChangeListener } from '@angular/common';
import { createApplication } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { createCustomElement } from '@angular/elements';
import { provideRouter, withDisabledInitialNavigation } from '@angular/router';
import { AppComponent } from './app/app.component.js';
import { routes } from './app/app.routes.js';

@Injectable()
class InMemoryLocationStrategy extends LocationStrategy {
  private _path = '/';
  private _state: unknown = null;

  override path(): string { return this._path; }
  override prepareExternalUrl(internal: string): string { return internal; }
  override getState(): unknown {
    return this._state;
  }
  override pushState(state: unknown, _title: string, url: string): void {
    this._state = state;
    this._path = url || '/';
  }
  override replaceState(state: unknown, _title: string, url: string): void {
    this._state = state;
    this._path = url || '/';
  }
  override forward(): void {}
  override back(): void {}
  override onPopState(_fn: LocationChangeListener): void {}
  override getBaseHref(): string { return ''; }
}

const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    { provide: LocationStrategy, useClass: InMemoryLocationStrategy },
    provideRouter(routes, withDisabledInitialNavigation()),
  ],
};

(async () => {
  const appRef = await createApplication(appConfig);
  const MyExtensionElement = createCustomElement(AppComponent, {
    injector: appRef.injector,
  });
  customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension', MyExtensionElement);
})();
```

`createApplication` creates a **completely new Angular platform** with its own DI injector tree, zone.js instance, and change-detection cycle. The host's Angular platform and yours coexist without conflict because they are entirely separate JavaScript objects.

`InMemoryLocationStrategy` keeps the Angular Router out of the browser history — the host owns the URL bar. `withDisabledInitialNavigation()` defers the first navigation until `AppComponent` applies the host sub-path.

***

## Step 3 — Sync host navigation to the router

Open `src/app/app.component.ts`. The root component receives `subPath` from the host, reads the initial deep-link path with `readInitialSubPath`, and subscribes to `routeChanged`:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/app/app.component.ts
import {
  ChangeDetectionStrategy,
  ChangeDetectorRef,
  Component,
  inject,
  Input,
  OnChanges,
  OnDestroy,
  OnInit,
  SimpleChanges,
} from '@angular/core';
import { Router, RouterOutlet } from '@angular/router';
import { normalizeSubPath, readInitialSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [RouterOutlet],
  template: '<router-outlet />',
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
})
export class AppComponent implements OnInit, OnDestroy, OnChanges {
  private readonly router = inject(Router);
  private readonly cdr = inject(ChangeDetectorRef);

  @Input() subPath = '/';

  private readonly routeChangedHandler = (data: { path?: string }) => {
    this.applyHostSubPath(data?.path);
  };

  ngOnInit(): void {
    const fromInput = normalizeSubPath(this.subPath);
    const initial = fromInput === '/' ? readInitialSubPath() : fromInput;
    this.applyHostSubPath(initial);

    window.litiumExtension?.on('routeChanged', this.routeChangedHandler);
  }

  ngOnDestroy(): void {
    window.litiumExtension?.off('routeChanged', this.routeChangedHandler);
  }

  ngOnChanges(changes: SimpleChanges): void {
    if (!('subPath' in changes)) {
      return;
    }
    this.applyHostSubPath(this.subPath);
  }

  private applyHostSubPath(raw: string | undefined): void {
    const target = normalizeSubPath(raw);
    const pathOnly = this.router.url.split('?')[0];
    const current = pathOnly === '' || pathOnly === undefined ? '/' : pathOnly;
    if (current === target && this.router.navigated) {
      return;
    }
    void this.router.navigateByUrl(target).then(() => this.cdr.markForCheck());
  }
}
```

See [Extension Routing](/platform/extensions/extension-routing) for the full picture.

***

## Step 4 — Define routes

Open `src/app/app.routes.ts`. The scaffold ships with a catch-all route to `HomeComponent`:


Add page routes as your extension grows:

```typescript theme={null}

import { SampleBComponent } from './sample-b.component.js';
```

## Step 5 — Navigate between pages

To navigate **from within your extension**, call `window.litiumExtension.navigate()`. The host updates the browser URL and fires `routeChanged`, which `AppComponent` syncs to the local router:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/app/sample-a.component.ts
goToB(): void {
  window.litiumExtension.navigate('/sampleb');
}
```

<Note>
  Do **not** call `this.router.navigate()` alone for cross-boundary navigation. `InMemoryLocationStrategy` updates only the in-memory router — it does not update the host's browser URL, so the back button and bookmarks will not work correctly.
</Note>

## Step 6 — Access the bridge API

Use `window.litiumExtension` in any component to read host context or show notifications:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/app/sample-a.component.ts
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-sample-a',
  template: `
    <h1>Sample A</h1>
    <p>Language: {{ language }}</p>
    <button (click)="save()">Save</button>
    <button (click)="goToB()">Go to Sample B</button>
  `,

export class SampleAComponent implements OnInit {
  language = '';

  ngOnInit() {
    this.language = window.litiumExtension.getContext().language;
  }

  async save() {
    const res = await window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/my-endpoint', {
      method: 'POST',
    });

      window.litiumExtension.showNotification({ message: 'Saved!', type: 'success' });

  goToB() {
    window.litiumExtension.navigate('/sampleb');
  }
}
```

## Calling the Litium Admin Web API

Use `window.litiumExtension.fetch` for all Admin Web API calls. The host attaches the signed-in user's session credentials to every request — you do not need a service account or OAuth2 setup in your extension bundle.

```typescript theme={null}
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

interface Order { systemId: string; salesOrderNumber: string; }

@Component({
  selector: 'app-sample-a',
  template: `
    <ul>
      <li *ngFor="let o of orders">{{ o.salesOrderNumber }}</li>
    </ul>
  `,
})
export class SampleAComponent implements OnInit {
  orders: Order[] = [];

  async ngOnInit() {
    const res = await window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/sales/order/search', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ take: 20, skip: 0 }),
    });
    const data = await res.json();
    this.orders = data.items ?? [];
  }
}
```

## Troubleshooting

### `platformBrowserDynamic is not a function` or blank screen at startup

The scaffold uses `createApplication` from `@angular/platform-browser`, not `platformBrowserDynamic`. Ensure `zone.js` is imported **before** any Angular import in `src/main.ts`.

### Angular Router navigates but the host URL does not change

You are calling `this.router.navigate()` directly instead of `window.litiumExtension.navigate()`. Use the bridge API so the host browser URL and local router stay in sync.

### Custom Element attribute `sub-path` not updating

Angular Elements maps kebab-case attributes to camelCase inputs. `AppComponent` must declare `@Input() subPath` to receive `sub-path` attribute changes. `ngOnChanges` calls `applyHostSubPath` when the input changes.

### CORS or HTTPS errors during local development

The Vite dev server runs over HTTPS (`@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`). Use `https://localhost:3000` in `bundleUrl`, not `http://`. The Litium Vite plugin adds permissive CORS headers for local development.

Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/create-react-extension

Step-by-step guide for building a Litium backoffice extension with React 19 and react-router-dom. No prior Litium internals knowledge required.

## Prerequisites

* A running Litium instance (local or remote) with backoffice access

## Step 1 — Scaffold the project

```bash theme={null}

```

### What was generated?

| File / folder             | Purpose                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/index.ts`            | Thin registration hub — imports preamble, styles, and registers the custom element |
| `src/element.ts`          | Custom Element class — bridges the DOM and React                                   |

| `src/index.css`           | Tailwind CSS entry                                                                 |

| `extension.manifest.json` | Deployment descriptor — includes a settings menu item target                       |
| `.dev.config.json`        | Dev server port (default `3000`) and Litium backend URL                            |

The scaffold also includes Vitest unit tests and a Playwright e2e smoke test.

***

## Step 2 — Understand the Custom Element entry point

The scaffold splits registration from the element class. Open `src/index.ts`:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/index.ts
export type { LitiumExtensionAPI } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk';

import './preamble.js'; // must be first
import './index.css';
import { MyExtensionElement } from './element.js';

if (!customElements.get('litium-ext-my-extension')) {
  customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension', MyExtensionElement);
}
```

Open `src/element.ts`. This file defines the Custom Element that the Litium host mounts. It uses `readInitialSubPath` for deep links and a `subPath` property setter so host updates re-render React:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/element.ts
import { StrictMode, createElement } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { normalizeSubPath, readInitialSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';
import { App } from './App.js';

export class MyExtensionElement extends HTMLElement {
  private reactRoot?: ReturnType<typeof createRoot>;
  private _subPath: string | undefined;

  get subPath(): string | undefined {
    return this._subPath;
  }

  set subPath(value: string | undefined) {
    const next = normalizeSubPath(value);
    const prev = this._subPath !== undefined ? normalizeSubPath(this._subPath) : undefined;
    if (prev === next && this.reactRoot) {
      return;
    }
    this._subPath = next;
    if (this.reactRoot) {
      this._renderApp();
    }
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this._subPath = readInitialSubPath();
    this.reactRoot = createRoot(this);
    this._renderApp();
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this.reactRoot?.unmount();
    this.reactRoot = undefined;
  }

  private _renderApp(): void {
    if (!this.reactRoot) return;
    this.reactRoot.render(
      createElement(StrictMode, null, createElement(App, { subPath: this._subPath ?? '/' })),
    );
  }
}
```

Key points:

* `element.ts` uses `.ts` (not `.tsx`) so `@vitejs/plugin-react` Fast Refresh does not process the class — mixing JSX with non-component classes breaks HMR
* `readInitialSubPath()` — reads the host-assigned path on first mount for deep links
* `subPath` setter — the host updates this property when the URL changes; React re-renders with the new path
* `disconnectedCallback` — unmounts React to avoid memory leaks

***

## Step 3 — Understand the router setup

Open `src/App.tsx`. React's `MemoryRouter` keeps routing state **inside** the Custom Element. `SubPathRoutes` syncs the host `subPath` prop and `routeChanged` events to the in-memory router:

```tsx theme={null}
// src/App.tsx
import { useEffect } from 'react';
import { MemoryRouter, Route, Routes, useLocation, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';
import type { LitiumExtensionAPI } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk';
import { normalizeSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

export type AppProps = {
  subPath: string;
};

function Home() {
  return (
    <div className="p-4 font-sans text-slate-800">
      <h1 className="text-xl font-semibold">my-extension</h1>
      <p className="mt-2 text-sm text-slate-600">Welcome to your Litium extension</p>
    </div>
  );
}

function SubPathRoutes({ subPath }: { subPath: string }) {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const location = useLocation();

  useEffect(() => {
    const target = normalizeSubPath(subPath);
    if (location.pathname !== target) {
      void navigate(target);
    }
  }, [subPath, navigate, location.pathname]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const api = (window as unknown as { litiumExtension?: LitiumExtensionAPI }).litiumExtension;
    const handler = (data: { path?: string }) => {
      void navigate(normalizeSubPath(data?.path));
    };
    api?.on('routeChanged', handler);
    return () => {
      api?.off('routeChanged', handler);
    };
  }, [navigate]);

  return (
    <Routes>
      <Route path="*" element={<Home />} />
    </Routes>
  );
}

export function App({ subPath }: AppProps) {
  const initial = normalizeSubPath(subPath);
  return (
    <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[initial]}>
      <SubPathRoutes subPath={subPath} />
    </MemoryRouter>
  );
}
```

Add page routes as siblings of the catch-all `Home` route:

```tsx theme={null}
import { PageA } from './pages/PageA.js';
import { PageB } from './pages/PageB.js';

// Inside SubPathRoutes return:
<Routes>
  <Route path="/samplea" element={<PageA />} />
  <Route path="/sampleb" element={<PageB />} />
  <Route path="*" element={<Home />} />
</Routes>
```

See [Extension Routing](/platform/extensions/extension-routing) for the full picture.

***

## Step 4 — Navigate between pages

To navigate **from within your extension**, call `window.litiumExtension.navigate()`. The host updates the browser URL and fires `routeChanged`, which `SubPathRoutes` syncs to the local router:

```tsx theme={null}
// src/pages/PageA.tsx
const goToPageB = () => {
  window.litiumExtension.navigate('/sampleb');
};
```

<Note>
  Do **not** call `useNavigate()` alone for cross-boundary navigation. This updates React Router's memory state but does not update the host's browser URL, so the back button and bookmarks will not work correctly.
</Note>

## Step 5 — Access the bridge API

Use `window.litiumExtension` anywhere in your components to read host context or show notifications:

```tsx theme={null}
// src/pages/PageA.tsx
import type { LitiumExtensionAPI } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk';

declare global {
  interface Window { litiumExtension: LitiumExtensionAPI; }
}

export function PageA() {
  const context = window.litiumExtension.getContext();

  const handleSave = async () => {
    const res = await window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/my-endpoint', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify({ foo: 'bar' }),
    });
    if (res.ok) {
      window.litiumExtension.showNotification({ message: 'Saved!', type: 'success' });
    }
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <h1>Page A</h1>
      <p>Language: {context.language}</p>
      <button onClick={handleSave}>Save</button>
      <button onClick={() => window.litiumExtension.navigate('/sampleb')}>
        Go to Page B
      </button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Calling the Litium Admin Web API

Use `window.litiumExtension.fetch` for all Admin Web API calls. The host attaches the signed-in user's session credentials to every request — you do not need a service account or OAuth2 setup in your extension bundle.

```tsx theme={null}
// src/pages/PageA.tsx
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

export function PageA() {
  const [orders, setOrders] = useState<{ systemId: string; salesOrderNumber: string }[]>([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/sales/order/search', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ take: 20, skip: 0 }),
    })
      .then(res => res.json())
      .then(data => setOrders(data.items ?? []));
  }, []);

  return (
    <ul>
      {orders.map(o => (
        <li key={o.systemId}>{o.salesOrderNumber}</li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

For parameters, return type, and common mistakes, see [`fetch`](/platform/extensions/extension-bridge-api#fetch) in the Extension Bridge API reference.

## Troubleshooting

### CORS or HTTPS errors during local development

The Vite dev server runs over HTTPS (`@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`). Use `https://localhost:3000` in `bundleUrl`, not `http://`. The Litium Vite plugin adds permissive CORS headers for local development.

### Custom Element not defined

Ensure the tag name in `customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension', ...)` in `src/index.ts` matches `customElementTag` in `extension.manifest.json` and starts with `litium-ext-`.

### Navigation broken (page always resets to root)

If clicking a link always shows the default route, the `routeChanged` subscription in `SubPathRoutes` is not wired up. Confirm `api?.on('routeChanged', handler)` is called inside a `useEffect` with a matching `api?.off` cleanup.

### HMR stops working after editing the Custom Element

Keep JSX out of `src/element.ts`. The class must stay in a plain `.ts` file so `@vitejs/plugin-react` Fast Refresh does not treat it as a React component.


# Create a Vue extension
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/create-vue-extension

Step-by-step guide for building a Litium backoffice extension with Vue 3 and vue-router. No prior Litium internals knowledge required.

## Prerequisites

* Node.js 20 or later
* A running Litium instance (local or remote) with backoffice access
* Basic familiarity with Vue 3 and TypeScript
* Registry configured — **complete [SDK Installation](/platform/extensions/sdk-installation) first**

***

## Step 1 — Scaffold the project

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk create my-extension --framework vue
cd my-extension
npm install
```

### What was generated?

| File / folder             | Purpose                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `src/index.ts`            | Custom Element registration via `defineCustomElement`                                              |
| `src/App.vue`             | Root SFC — `<router-view />` and host path sync                                                    |
| `src/router.ts`           | `vue-router` with `createMemoryHistory`                                                            |
| `vite.config.ts`          | IIFE build with `@vitejs/plugin-vue` (`customElement: true`), Tailwind, and the Litium Vite plugin |
| `extension.manifest.json` | Deployment descriptor — includes a settings menu item target                                       |
| `.dev.config.json`        | Dev server port (default `3000`) and Litium backend URL                                            |

The scaffold also includes Vitest unit tests and a Playwright e2e smoke test.

***

## Step 2 — Understand the Custom Element entry point

Open `src/index.ts`. Vue's `defineCustomElement` compiles the root SFC into a Web Component. The router is installed once per element instance via `configureApp`, and `readInitialSubPath` ensures deep links work on first render:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/index.ts
import { defineCustomElement } from 'vue';
import type { LitiumExtensionAPI } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk';
import { readInitialSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';
import App from './App.vue';
import { router } from './router.js';

declare global {
  interface Window { litiumExtension: LitiumExtensionAPI; }
}

const MyExtensionBase = defineCustomElement(App, {
  configureApp(app) {
    app.use(router);
  },
});

class MyExtensionElement extends MyExtensionBase {
  connectedCallback() {
    (this as unknown as { subPath: string }).subPath = readInitialSubPath();
    super.connectedCallback();
  }
}

if (!customElements.get('litium-ext-my-extension')) {
  customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension', MyExtensionElement);
}
```

`defineCustomElement` creates a shadow DOM for the component. Set `customElement: true` on `@vitejs/plugin-vue` in `vite.config.ts` so Tailwind styles from `App.vue` are injected into the shadow root.

***

## Step 3 — Understand the router setup

Open `src/router.ts`. The scaffold exports a shared router with in-memory history — your extension never touches the browser's `history.pushState` directly:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/router.ts
import { h } from 'vue';
import { createMemoryHistory, createRouter } from 'vue-router';

const Home = {
  name: 'ExtensionHome',
  render() {
    return h('div', { class: 'p-4 font-sans text-slate-800' }, [
      h('h1', { class: 'text-xl font-semibold' }, 'my-extension'),
      h('p', { class: 'mt-2 text-sm text-slate-600' }, 'Welcome to the Litium extension scaffold'),
    ]);
  },
};

export const router = createRouter({
  history: createMemoryHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*', name: 'home', component: Home },
  ],
});
```

Replace the inline `Home` component with real page SFCs as your extension grows:

```typescript theme={null}
import PageA from './pages/PageA.vue';
import PageB from './pages/PageB.vue';

export const router = createRouter({
  history: createMemoryHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/samplea', component: PageA },
    { path: '/sampleb', component: PageB },
    { path: '/', redirect: '/samplea' },
    { path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*', redirect: '/samplea' },
  ],
});
```

***

## Step 4 — Sync host navigation to the router

Open `src/App.vue`. The root SFC watches the `subPath` prop (set by the host) and subscribes to `routeChanged` events so browser back/forward and deep links stay in sync:

```vue theme={null}
<!-- src/App.vue -->
<template>
  <router-view />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, onUnmounted, watch } from 'vue';
import { useRouter } from 'vue-router';
import type { LitiumExtensionAPI } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk';
import { normalizeSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{ subPath?: string }>(),
  { subPath: '/' },
);

const router = useRouter();

function applyHostPath(p: string | undefined) {
  const target = normalizeSubPath(p);
  if (router.currentRoute.value.path !== target) {
    void router.push(target);
  }
}

watch(
  () => props.subPath,
  (p) => {
    applyHostPath(p);
  },
  { immediate: true },
);

const routeChangedHandler = (data: { path?: string }) => {
  applyHostPath(data?.path);
};

onMounted(() => {
  const api = (window as unknown as { litiumExtension?: LitiumExtensionAPI }).litiumExtension;
  api?.on('routeChanged', routeChangedHandler);
});

onUnmounted(() => {
  const api = (window as unknown as { litiumExtension?: LitiumExtensionAPI }).litiumExtension;
  api?.off('routeChanged', routeChangedHandler);
});
</script>

<style>
@import "tailwindcss";
</style>
```

`normalizeSubPath` (from `@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router`) ensures paths always start with `/`. See [Extension Routing](/platform/extensions/extension-routing) for the full picture.

***

## Step 5 — Navigate between pages

To navigate **from within your extension**, call `window.litiumExtension.navigate()`. The host updates the browser URL and fires `routeChanged`, which your `App.vue` handler syncs to the local router:

```vue theme={null}
<!-- src/pages/PageA.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
const goToPageB = () => {
  window.litiumExtension.navigate('/sampleb');
};
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <h1>Page A</h1>
    <button @click="goToPageB">Go to Page B</button>
  </div>
</template>
```

<Note>
  Do **not** call `router.push()` alone for cross-boundary navigation. This updates Vue Router's memory state but does not update the host's browser URL, so the back button and bookmarks will not work correctly.
</Note>

<Tip>
  Alternatively, use `createNavigate(router)` from `@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/vue` to update both the host URL and local router in one call.
</Tip>

***

## Step 6 — Access the bridge API

Use `window.litiumExtension` anywhere in your components to read host context or show notifications:

```vue theme={null}
<!-- src/pages/PageA.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import type { LitiumExtensionAPI } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk';

declare global {
  interface Window { litiumExtension: LitiumExtensionAPI; }
}

const context = window.litiumExtension.getContext();

const handleSave = async () => {
  const res = await window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/my-endpoint', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ value: 42 }),
  });
  if (res.ok) {
    window.litiumExtension.showNotification({ message: 'Saved!', type: 'success' });
  }
};
</script>

<template>
  <div>
    <h1>Page A</h1>
    <p>Language: {{ context.language }}</p>
    <button @click="handleSave">Save</button>
  </div>
</template>
```

***

## Calling the Litium Admin Web API

Use `window.litiumExtension.fetch` for all Admin Web API calls. The host attaches the signed-in user's session credentials to every request — you do not need a service account or OAuth2 setup in your extension bundle.

```vue theme={null}
<!-- src/pages/PageA.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, onMounted } from 'vue';

const orders = ref<{ systemId: string; salesOrderNumber: string }[]>([]);

onMounted(async () => {
  const res = await window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/sales/order/search', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ take: 20, skip: 0 }),
  });
  const data = await res.json();
  orders.value = data.items ?? [];
});
</script>

<template>
  <ul>
    <li v-for="o in orders" :key="o.systemId">{{ o.salesOrderNumber }}</li>
  </ul>
</template>
```

For parameters, return type, and common mistakes, see [`fetch`](/platform/extensions/extension-bridge-api#fetch) in the Extension Bridge API reference.

***

## Step 7 — Develop locally

```bash theme={null}
npm run dev
```

This runs `platform-extension-sdk dev`, which starts the Vite dev server on port `3000` (configured in `.dev.config.json`) with HTTPS enabled. Register your extension in the running Litium instance via **Settings > System settings > Extensions** — enter the manifest URL in the install dialog (e.g. `https://localhost:3000/extension.manifest.json` or `https://localhost:3000`):

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "my-extension",
  "name": "My Extension",
  "type": "ui",
  "frameworkType": "web.component",
  "customElementTag": "litium-ext-my-extension",
  "targets": [
    {
      "target": "common.web.component",
      "name": "my-extension",
      "bundleUrl": "https://localhost:3000/src/index.ts",
      "customElementTag": "litium-ext-my-extension"
    },
    {
      "target": "settings.menu.item",
      "name": "my-extension",
      "ref_id": "system.settings",
      "url": "/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension"
    }
  ]
}
```

The host loads your bundle live — every Vite HMR save is reflected immediately.
