## Troubleshooting

### Tailwind styles not applied

`defineCustomElement` creates a shadow DOM. Tailwind CSS must be declared inside the SFC `<style>` block with `@import "tailwindcss"` so styles are inlined into the shadow root. Also confirm `customElement: true` is set on `@vitejs/plugin-vue` in `vite.config.ts`.

### `router.push()` updates the URL but the back button doesn't work

You are calling `router.push()` directly instead of `window.litiumExtension.navigate()`. Use the bridge API so the host browser URL and local router stay in sync.

### Custom Element not defined

Ensure the tag name in `customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension', ...)` matches `customElementTag` in `extension.manifest.json` and starts with `litium-ext-`.

### CORS or HTTPS errors during local development

The Vite dev server runs over HTTPS (`@vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl`). Use `https://localhost:3000` in `bundleUrl`, not `http://`. The Litium Vite plugin adds permissive CORS headers for local development.


# Extension Bridge API
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/extension-bridge-api

Complete reference for window.litiumExtension — the API the Litium admin host injects into every Custom Element extension.

The Litium admin host injects `window.litiumExtension` before any extension bundle is executed. Every Custom Element extension communicates with the host exclusively through this object — no direct Angular dependencies needed.

## TypeScript types

Import types from `@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk` for full autocomplete:

```typescript theme={null}
import type {
  LitiumExtensionAPI,
  ExtensionContext,
  NotificationOptions,
  ExtensionEventType,
} from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk';

declare global {
  interface Window { litiumExtension: LitiumExtensionAPI; }
}
```

***

## Methods

### `navigate(path)`

Navigate within the Litium admin using the host router. Pushes a new browser history entry.

| Parameter | Type     | Required | Description                                                    |
| --------- | -------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`    | `string` | Yes      | Sub-path within the extension, e.g. `/detail` or `/orders/123` |

**Returns:** `void`

```typescript theme={null}
// Navigate to a sub-page — also triggers a 'routeChanged' event back to this extension
window.litiumExtension.navigate('/detail');
```

**Common mistakes:**

* Passing a full host URL when you mean to stay inside the extension. Use a sub-path such as `/detail`, not `/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension/detail` (unless you intend host-level navigation with a `/Litium/` path).
* Calling `navigate()` inside a `routeChanged` handler — this creates an infinite loop. Only call `navigate()` in response to user actions.

***

### `replaceUrl(path)`

Update the browser URL without adding a new browser history entry. Use this when responding to back/forward navigation — it moves the URL pointer without clearing the forward stack.

| Parameter | Type     | Required | Description                                |
| --------- | -------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `path`    | `string` | Yes      | Target path relative to the extension root |

**Returns:** `void`

```typescript theme={null}
// Called inside a routeChanged handler to sync the URL without creating a new history entry
window.litiumExtension.replaceUrl('/detail');
```

**Common mistakes:**

* Using `navigate()` instead of `replaceUrl()` inside a `routeChanged` handler. This pushes a duplicate entry and breaks the back button.

***

### `showNotification(options)`

Display a notification banner in the Litium admin UI.

| Parameter         | Type                                          | Required | Description                        |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `options.message` | `string`                                      | Yes      | The notification text              |
| `options.type`    | `'success' \| 'info' \| 'warning' \| 'error'` | No       | Severity level (default: `'info'`) |

**Returns:** `void`

```typescript theme={null}
window.litiumExtension.showNotification({
  message: 'Order saved successfully.',
  type: 'success',
});

window.litiumExtension.showNotification({
  message: 'Validation failed — check required fields.',
  type: 'error',
});
```

**Common mistakes:**

* Displaying notifications too frequently (e.g. on every key press). Use notifications for significant events only.

***

### `getContext()`

Retrieve the current extension context — language, user, sub-path, and other host-provided data.

**Returns:** [`ExtensionContext`](#extensioncontext-type)

```typescript theme={null}
const context = window.litiumExtension.getContext();
console.log(context.language);           // "en-US"
console.log(context.user.name);          // "Jane Doe"
console.log(context.subPath);            // "/orders/123"
console.log(context.extensionBasePath);  // "/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension"
console.log(context.baseUrl);            // "https://my-litium.example.com"
```

**Common mistakes:**

* Calling `getContext()` once at module level and caching the result forever. `subPath` and other fields can change when the user navigates within the extension. Call `getContext()` when you need the current value.

***

### `fetch(input, init?)`

Call the Litium Admin Web API with the current user's session credentials. The host attaches authentication to every request — extensions do not manage OAuth2 tokens or service account secrets.

| Parameter | Type                       | Required | Description                                                                                                                   |
| --------- | -------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`   | `string \| URL \| Request` | Yes      | Request URL or `Request` object. Use paths relative to the Litium instance root, e.g. `/Litium/app/api/sales/order/search`    |
| `init`    | `RequestInit`              | No       | Standard [`fetch`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/fetch) options (`method`, `headers`, `body`, etc.) |

**Returns:** `Promise<Response>` — same as the browser [`fetch`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/fetch) API.

```typescript theme={null}
const res = await window.litiumExtension.fetch('/Litium/app/api/sales/order/search', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ take: 20, skip: 0 }),
});

if (!res.ok) {
  throw new Error(`Request failed: ${res.status}`);
}

const data = await res.json();
```

**Common mistakes:**

* Embedding service account credentials in the extension bundle. Use `fetch` on `window.litiumExtension` instead — the host handles authentication.
* Calling plain `fetch()` against Admin Web API endpoints. Requests from the extension origin are not authenticated the same way; always use `window.litiumExtension.fetch`.

***

### `on(event, handler)`

Subscribe to a host event.

| Parameter | Type                                        | Required | Description       |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------- |
| `event`   | [`ExtensionEventType`](#extensioneventtype) | Yes      | Event name        |
| `handler` | `(data: T) => void`                         | Yes      | Callback function |

**Returns:** `void`

```typescript theme={null}
const routeChangedHandler = ({ path }: { path: string }) => {
  console.log('New path:', path);
};

window.litiumExtension.on('routeChanged', routeChangedHandler);

// Unsubscribe (call in disconnectedCallback / onUnmounted / ngOnDestroy)
window.litiumExtension.off('routeChanged', routeChangedHandler);
```

**Common mistakes:**

* Not calling `off()` when the element is removed from the DOM. This causes memory leaks and stale handlers firing in unmounted components.

***

### `off(event, handler)`

Unsubscribe a specific handler from a host event. Pass the same function reference you passed to `on()`.

| Parameter | Type                                        | Required | Description                                   |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `event`   | [`ExtensionEventType`](#extensioneventtype) | Yes      | Event name                                    |
| `handler` | `ExtensionEventHandler`                     | Yes      | The exact function reference passed to `on()` |

**Returns:** `void`

***

## Events

### `routeChanged`

Fired by the host when the browser navigates to a URL within your extension's registered path prefix (e.g. triggered by back/forward buttons or a deep link).

**Handler data:** `{ path: string }` — the new sub-path relative to your extension root.

```typescript theme={null}
window.litiumExtension.on<{ path: string }>('routeChanged', ({ path }) => {
  // Sync your in-memory router to the new path
  myRouter.replace(path);
});
```

### `contextChanged`

Not currently emitted by the Litium host. Call `getContext()` when you need fresh context data.

### `languageChanged`

Not currently emitted by the Litium host. Read `getContext().language` when you need the current UI language.

***

## Type reference

### `ExtensionContext`

```typescript theme={null}
interface ExtensionContext {
  /** Current UI language code, e.g. "en-US" */
  language: string;
  /** Authenticated user information */
  user: {
    name: string;
    id: string;
  };
  /** Origin of the Litium instance, e.g. "https://my-litium.example.com" */
  baseUrl: string;
  /** Sub-path within this extension, e.g. "/orders/123" */
  subPath: string;
  /** Base path for this extension, e.g. "/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension" */
  extensionBasePath: string;
}
```

### `ExtensionEventType`

```typescript theme={null}
type ExtensionEventType = 'routeChanged' | 'contextChanged' | 'languageChanged';
```

### `NotificationOptions`

```typescript theme={null}
interface NotificationOptions {
  message: string;
  type?: 'success' | 'info' | 'warning' | 'error';
}
```


# Extension Management UI
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/extension-management-ui

How to install, configure, enable, and disable Litium extensions using the Settings > System settings > Extensions page in the Litium backoffice.

The **Settings > System settings > Extensions** page is the primary interface for managing all registered extensions in your Litium installation. You can install new extensions, view and update existing ones, enable or disable them, and remove them — all without touching configuration files or API endpoints.

<Note>
  You must be logged in with an account that has **System settings** access to use Settings > System settings > Extensions. Contact your system administrator if the option is not visible.
</Note>

***

## Opening the Extensions page

1. Log in to the Litium backoffice
2. Click **Settings** in the left navigation panel
3. Click **Extensions** under **System settings**

You will see a list of all currently registered extensions, their type, and enabled status.

***

## Installing an extension

1. Click the **Add UI extension** button (top right corner of the Extensions list)
2. In the dialog that appears, enter the URL to your manifest — e.g. `https://cdn.example.com/my-extension/extension.manifest.json` or `https://localhost:3000` (the host appends `/extension.manifest.json` when needed). A preview appears when the manifest is valid.
3. Review the extension details in the preview
4. Click **Install**

The extension appears in the list immediately and is enabled by default.

<Note>
  During local development, use `https://localhost:3000/extension.manifest.json` as the manifest URL (or enter `https://localhost:3000` — the host resolves the manifest path). The Litium host will load bundles directly from your Vite dev server, enabling hot-reload. If the browser blocks the fetch due to CORS, the backoffice proxies the request via `/Litium/app/api/extension-management/manifest`.
</Note>

***

## Enabling and disabling an extension

1. Find the extension in the list
2. Use the **enabled** toggle on the right side of the extension row

A disabled extension is not loaded by the backoffice. Users will not see any UI elements registered by that extension.

***

## Updating an extension

To update an extension (e.g. after deploying a new bundle URL or version):

1. Double-click the extension row to open the detail view
2. Click **Reload** to re-fetch and apply the manifest from the bundle's origin URL
3. Alternatively, install again with the same `id` — the system updates the existing registration rather than creating a duplicate

***

## Removing an extension

1. Double-click the extension row to open the detail view
2. Click **Delete**
3. Confirm the deletion in the confirmation dialog

All menu items, bundle registrations, and API proxies registered by that extension are removed immediately.

***

## Viewing extension details

Double-click an extension row to open the detail view. It shows:

* **Name** and manifest URL
* **Version** — as declared in `extension.manifest.json`
* **Targets** — all registered target entries (bundle URLs, menu items, etc.)
* **Enabled** — toggle to enable or disable the extension

***

## API-based management

For automated deployments, register and update extensions through the **Extension Management API** at `/Litium/api/extension-management/extensions`. This is a separate **service account** API — not the backoffice admin API at `/Litium/app/api/extension-management/extensions` used by the Settings UI.

Authenticate with an OAuth2 client-credentials token or bearer token from a Litium service account. The API only returns and modifies extensions owned by that account's client ID.

See the [Extension Management API](/apis/extension-management-api/overview) reference for full endpoint documentation. The request body matches `extension.manifest.json` — see the [manifest reference](/platform/extensions/extension-manifest-reference).

A typical CI/CD deployment step:

```bash theme={null}
# Register a new extension (service account token)
curl -X POST https://my-litium.example.com/Litium/api/extension-management/extensions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @extension.manifest.json

# Update an existing extension (same id in URL and body)
curl -X PUT https://my-litium.example.com/Litium/api/extension-management/extensions/my-extension \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @extension.manifest.json
```


# Extension manifest reference
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/extension-manifest-reference

Complete field-by-field reference for extension.manifest.json — the deployment descriptor that tells Litium how to load and register your extension.

`extension.manifest.json` lives in your extension project root. The Litium host fetches this file when you install an extension via **Settings > System settings > Extensions**, or you can POST its contents directly to the Extension Management API.

## Minimal example

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "my-extension",
  "name": "My Extension",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "ui",
  "targets": [
    {
      "target": "common.web.component",
      "name": "my-extension",
      "bundleUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/my-extension/extension.js",
      "customElementTag": "litium-ext-my-extension"
    }
  ]
}
```

***

## Top-level fields

### `id`

|              |                      |
| ------------ | -------------------- |
| **Type**     | `string`             |
| **Required** | Yes                  |
| **Format**   | Lowercase kebab-case |

The system-unique identifier for your extension. Used as the primary key when registering, updating, or deleting the extension.

```json theme={null}
"id": "my-company-order-widget"
```

<Note>
  Changing `id` after deployment creates a new extension entry rather than updating the existing one.
</Note>

***

### `name`

|              |          |
| ------------ | -------- |
| **Type**     | `string` |
| **Required** | Yes      |

Human-readable display name shown in the Extensions list in the backoffice. Prefix with `t:` to reference a translation key from `texts`:

```json theme={null}
"name": "My Order Widget"
// or
"name": "t:extensions.my-extension.name"
```

***

### `version`

|              |                                   |
| ------------ | --------------------------------- |
| **Type**     | `string`                          |
| **Required** | No                                |
| **Format**   | Semantic version (e.g. `"1.2.3"`) |

Displayed in the Extensions list. Useful for auditing which version is deployed.

***

### `type`

|              |                              |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- |
| **Type**     | `"ui" \| "admission_review"` |
| **Required** | Yes                          |

* `"ui"` — an Admin-panel extension (bundles, menu items, API proxies)
* `"admission_review"` — a server-side webhook that Litium calls during admission review flows (see [Admission review targets](#admission_review-targets))

All new backoffice UI extensions use `"ui"`.

***

### `description`

|              |          |
| ------------ | -------- |
| **Type**     | `string` |
| **Required** | No       |

A short description displayed in the backoffice. Supports `t:` prefix for translation:

```json theme={null}
"description": "Displays a custom order management panel."
```

***

### `targets`

|              |                             |
| ------------ | --------------------------- |
| **Type**     | `ExtensionManifestTarget[]` |
| **Required** | No                          |

An array of target registrations. Each entry wires up one extension point. See [Targets](#targets-reference) below.

***

### `texts`

|              |                                          |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Type**     | `Record<string, Record<string, string>>` |
| **Required** | No                                       |

Translations for `name`, `description`, and any target display text. Keyed by locale:

```json theme={null}
"texts": {
  "en-US": {
    "extensions.my-extension.name": "My Order Widget",
    "extensions.my-extension.description": "Order management panel"
  },
  "sv-SE": {
    "extensions.my-extension.name": "Min orderwidget",
    "extensions.my-extension.description": "Orderhanteringspanel"
  }
}
```

***

## Targets reference

Each object in the `targets` array must include a `target` field that selects the registered target definition. All other fields are target-specific.

### Valid `target` values

| Value                            | Description                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `common.web.component`           | Registers a Web Component (Custom Element) bundle — used for all new extensions                      |
| `settings.menu.item`             | Adds an item to the **Settings** sidebar navigation                                                  |
| `customers.menu.item`            | Adds a panel to the **Customers** area navigation                                                    |
| `products.menu.item`             | Adds a panel to the **Products** area navigation                                                     |
| `sales.menu.item`                | Adds a panel to the **Sales** area navigation                                                        |
| `media.menu.item`                | Adds a panel to the **Media** area navigation                                                        |
| `websites.menu.item`             | Adds a panel to the **Websites** area navigation                                                     |
| `common.api.proxy`               | Registers a transparent API proxy forwarding backoffice requests to your backend                     |
| `common.angular.module`          | *(Deprecated)* webpack Module Federation bundle — migrate to `common.web.component`                  |
| `sales.salesorder.adminaction.*` | Admission review webhook for an order admin action — requires top-level `"type": "admission_review"` |

***

### `common.web.component`

Registers a Web Component (Custom Element) bundle.

| Field              | Type                     | Required | Description                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `target`           | `"common.web.component"` | Yes      | Target type                                                                                                        |
| `name`             | `string`                 | Yes      | Unique name for this target entry                                                                                  |
| `bundleUrl`        | `string`                 | Yes      | Absolute URL to the IIFE JS bundle. Must be HTTPS in production; `http://localhost:...` accepted during local dev. |
| `customElementTag` | `string`                 | Yes      | The custom element tag to mount. Must start with `litium-ext-`.                                                    |

```json theme={null}
{
  "target": "common.web.component",
  "name": "my-extension",
  "bundleUrl": "https://cdn.example.com/my-extension/extension.js",
  "customElementTag": "litium-ext-my-extension"
}
```

***

### `common.angular.module` *(deprecated)*

Registers a webpack Module Federation bundle. Use `common.web.component` for new extensions.

<Note>
  `common.angular.module` is deprecated. Use the [migration guide](/platform/extensions/migrate-from-module-federation) to convert to `common.web.component`.
</Note>

***

### `settings.menu.item`

Adds an item to the Settings sidebar navigation.

| Field        | Type                   | Required | Description                                                                                      |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `target`     | `"settings.menu.item"` | Yes      | Target type                                                                                      |
| `name`       | `string`               | Yes      | Translation key for the menu label                                                               |
| `ref_id`     | `string`               | Yes      | Reference ID of the settings group (e.g. `"system.settings"`)                                    |
| `url`        | `string`               | Yes      | Path to activate when the menu item is clicked (must match the Custom Element's registered path) |
| `permission` | `string`               | No       | Permission key required to see this item                                                         |

```json theme={null}
{
  "target": "settings.menu.item",
  "name": "t:extensions.my-extension.menu",
  "ref_id": "system.settings",
  "url": "/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension",
  "permission": "extensions:my-extension:read"
}
```

***

### `{area}.menu.item`

Registers a web component panel in one of the five backoffice area navigation panels. The panel is rendered directly as a Custom Element — no URL routing is needed.

Replace `{area}` with one of: `customers`, `products`, `sales`, `media`, `websites`.

| Field       | Type                         | Required | Description                                                                    |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `target`    | `"customers.menu.item"` etc. | Yes      | Area-specific target name                                                      |
| `name`      | `string`                     | Yes      | Display name shown in the area navigation panel                                |
| `component` | `string`                     | Yes      | Custom element tag for the panel web component. Must start with `litium-ext-`. |

```json theme={null}
{
  "target": "products.menu.item",
  "name": "Pricing Rules",
  "component": "litium-ext-my-extension-panel-pricing-rules"
}
```

The custom element declared in `component` is mounted inside the area panel when the user selects it. The host does not pass a `sub-path` attribute — panels are single-view.

<Note>
  Use the `npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk add panel` command to generate the component file and add this manifest entry automatically. See [Add a panel](/platform/extensions/add-panel).
</Note>

***

### `common.api.proxy`

Registers a transparent API proxy that forwards authenticated requests from the backoffice to your extension backend.

| Field    | Type                 | Required | Description                        |
| -------- | -------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `target` | `"common.api.proxy"` | Yes      | Target type                        |
| `name`   | `string`             | Yes      | Unique name                        |
| `url`    | `string`             | Yes      | Base URL of your extension backend |

***

### `admission_review` targets

Use these when the extension top-level `"type"` is `"admission_review"`. They register server-side webhooks — not Web Component bundles. Fields such as `bundleUrl` and `customElementTag` do not apply.

#### Sales order admin actions (`sales.salesorder.adminaction.*`)

Litium calls your endpoint when an order **admin action batch** is processed. Set `target` to the admin action identifier, for example:

* `sales.salesorder.adminaction.change_billing_address`
* `sales.salesorder.adminaction.change_shipping_address`
* `sales.salesorder.adminaction.add_order_discount`

| Field       | Type                                 | Required | Description                                                                           |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `target`    | `"sales.salesorder.adminaction.*"`   | Yes      | Admin action target id                                                                |
| `type`      | `"erp" \| "payments" \| "shipments"` | Yes      | How the order is represented in the condition and webhook request body                |
| `url`       | `string`                             | Yes      | Absolute URL Litium calls (relative URLs are accepted when registered from an app)    |
| `condition` | `string`                             | No       | C# expression — when it evaluates to `true`, this extension is included for the order |
| `timeout`   | `number`                             | No       | Seconds before Litium treats the call as timed out                                    |

Valid values for `type`:

| Value         | Request model                                   |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `"erp"`       | `Litium.Connect.Erp.Order`                      |
| `"payments"`  | `Litium.Connect.Payments.Payment`               |
| `"shipments"` | `Litium.Connect.Shipments.UpdateSessionRequest` |

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "directpayment-admission-review",
  "name": "Direct payment",
  "type": "admission_review",
  "targets": [
    {
      "target": "sales.salesorder.adminaction.change_billing_address",
      "type": "payments",
      "condition": "Item.Object.Item.PaymentProviderId.Equals(\"directpayment\")",
      "url": "https://my-app.example.com/api/admission-review/change-billing-address",
      "timeout": 10
    }
  ]
}
```

<Note>
  Do not confuse target `type` (`erp` / `payments` / `shipments`) with the top-level extension `type` (`"admission_review"`). For implementation details, conditions, and endpoint handling, see [How to create admin action extensions for orders](/platform/areas/extending-litium/how-to-create-admin-action-extensions-for-orders).
</Note>

***

## Local dev manifest

During development, change `bundleUrl` to point at your Vite dev server:

```json theme={null}
{
  "id": "my-extension",
  "name": "My Extension",
  "type": "ui",
  "targets": [
    {
      "target": "common.web.component",
      "name": "my-extension",
      "bundleUrl": "https://localhost:3000/src/index.ts",
      "customElementTag": "litium-ext-my-extension"
    }
  ]
}
```

Switch `bundleUrl` back to the production CDN URL before deploying.


# Extension routing
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/extension-routing

How sub-path routing works in Litium extensions — MemoryRouter, subPath, navigate(), routeChanged, and browser back/forward explained for all frameworks.

## How the host delegates sub-paths

The Litium admin host registers your extension against a URL prefix like `/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension`. It uses an Angular `path: '**'` wildcard route, which means **any URL under that prefix is forwarded to your extension**:

```
Host URL: /Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension/orders/123
                                          ^─── your prefix ───^│
                                                               sub-path: /orders/123
```

The host passes the sub-path to your Custom Element via the `sub-path` HTML attribute and fires the `routeChanged` event whenever the sub-path changes.

***

## The `subPath` property

`subPath` (or `sub-path` as an HTML attribute) is set by the host on your Custom Element:

| Situation                                | When it's set                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| First render                             | Set to the URL path at mount time (enables deep links and page refresh) |
| Browser back/forward                     | Attribute is updated **and** `routeChanged` event is fired              |
| `window.litiumExtension.navigate()` call | Attribute is updated **and** `routeChanged` event is fired              |

Your Custom Element must read the initial sub-path on mount and react to both property/attribute changes and `routeChanged` events.

***

## `window.litiumExtension.navigate(path)`

Call this to initiate navigation from **within your extension** to another path. It:

1. Updates the host's browser URL (pushes a new `history` entry)
2. Fires the `routeChanged` event back to all mounted extensions

```typescript theme={null}
// User clicked "Go to detail page"
window.litiumExtension.navigate('/orders/123');
```

Do **not** call this inside a `routeChanged` handler — that creates an infinite loop.

***

## `routeChanged` event

The host fires this event whenever the browser history changes within your extension's path prefix. This includes:

* Back/forward button clicks
* Direct calls to `window.litiumExtension.navigate()`
* Deep links opened in a new tab that was already mounted

**Handler signature:**

```typescript theme={null}
window.litiumExtension.on<{ path: string }>('routeChanged', ({ path }) => {
  // path is the new sub-path, e.g. "/orders/123"
});
```

Always unsubscribe in your cleanup lifecycle hook to prevent memory leaks.

***

## Per-framework setup

### React (MemoryRouter + host path sync)

React's `MemoryRouter` stores routing state in memory. The scaffold reads the initial deep-link path with `readInitialSubPath` in `element.ts`, passes `subPath` into `App`, and syncs subsequent host navigations in `SubPathRoutes`:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/element.ts — Custom Element
import { readInitialSubPath, normalizeSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

export class MyExtensionElement extends HTMLElement {
  private _subPath: string | undefined;

  set subPath(value: string | undefined) {
    const next = normalizeSubPath(value);
    const prev = this._subPath !== undefined ? normalizeSubPath(this._subPath) : undefined;
    if (prev === next && this.reactRoot) return;
    this._subPath = next;
    if (this.reactRoot) this._renderApp();
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this._subPath = readInitialSubPath();
    this.reactRoot = createRoot(this);
    this._renderApp();
  }
}
```

```tsx theme={null}
// src/App.tsx
import { normalizeSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

function SubPathRoutes({ subPath }: { subPath: string }) {
  const navigate = useNavigate();
  const location = useLocation();

  useEffect(() => {
    const target = normalizeSubPath(subPath);
    if (location.pathname !== target) {
      void navigate(target);
    }
  }, [subPath, navigate, location.pathname]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const api = window.litiumExtension;
    const handler = (data: { path?: string }) => {
      void navigate(normalizeSubPath(data?.path));
    };
    api?.on('routeChanged', handler);
    return () => { api?.off('routeChanged', handler); };
  }, [navigate]);

  return (
    <Routes>
      <Route path="/orders" element={<OrderListPage />} />
      <Route path="/orders/:id" element={<OrderDetailPage />} />
      <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/orders" replace />} />
    </Routes>
  );
}

export function App({ subPath }: { subPath: string }) {
  return (
    <MemoryRouter initialEntries={[normalizeSubPath(subPath)]}>
      <SubPathRoutes subPath={subPath} />
    </MemoryRouter>
  );
}
```

To navigate programmatically from page components, call the bridge API — the `routeChanged` handler syncs the local router:

```tsx theme={null}
// Inside a page component — do NOT use useNavigate() alone for cross-boundary nav
const handleViewDetail = (id: string) => {
  window.litiumExtension.navigate(`/orders/${id}`);
};
```

***

### Vue (createMemoryHistory + host path sync)

Vue's `createMemoryHistory` keeps routing state inside the Custom Element. The scaffold installs the router in `defineCustomElement`'s `configureApp`, reads the initial deep-link path with `readInitialSubPath`, and syncs subsequent host navigations in the root SFC:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/index.ts — Custom Element
import { readInitialSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

const MyExtensionBase = defineCustomElement(App, {
  configureApp(app) {
    app.use(router);
  },
});

class MyExtensionElement extends MyExtensionBase {
  connectedCallback() {
    (this as unknown as { subPath: string }).subPath = readInitialSubPath();
    super.connectedCallback();
  }
}
```

```typescript theme={null}
// src/router.ts
import { createMemoryHistory, createRouter } from 'vue-router';

export const router = createRouter({
  history: createMemoryHistory(),
  routes: [
    { path: '/orders', component: OrderListPage },
    { path: '/orders/:id', component: OrderDetailPage },
    { path: '/', redirect: '/orders' },
    { path: '/:pathMatch(.*)*', redirect: '/orders' },
  ],
});
```

```vue theme={null}
<!-- src/App.vue -->
<template>
  <router-view />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onMounted, onUnmounted, watch } from 'vue';
import { useRouter } from 'vue-router';
import { normalizeSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{ subPath?: string }>(),
  { subPath: '/' },
);

const router = useRouter();

function applyHostPath(p: string | undefined) {
  const target = normalizeSubPath(p);
  if (router.currentRoute.value.path !== target) {
    void router.push(target);
  }
}

watch(
  () => props.subPath,
  (p) => {
    applyHostPath(p);
  },
  { immediate: true },
);

const routeChangedHandler = (data: { path?: string }) => {
  applyHostPath(data?.path);
};

onMounted(() => {
  window.litiumExtension?.on('routeChanged', routeChangedHandler);
});

onUnmounted(() => {
  window.litiumExtension?.off('routeChanged', routeChangedHandler);
});
</script>
```

To navigate programmatically from page components, call the bridge API — the `routeChanged` handler syncs the local router:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/pages/OrderList.vue — do NOT call router.push() alone for cross-boundary nav
const handleViewDetail = (id: string) => {
  window.litiumExtension.navigate(`/orders/${id}`);
};
```

Alternatively, `createNavigate(router)` from `@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/vue` updates both the host URL and local router in one call.

***

### Angular (InMemoryLocationStrategy + host path sync)

Angular Router uses a `LocationStrategy` to interact with browser history. The scaffold provides `InMemoryLocationStrategy` in `main.ts` so the router never touches the real URL bar, and `AppComponent` syncs host navigations via `normalizeSubPath` and `routeChanged`:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/main.ts
const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    { provide: LocationStrategy, useClass: InMemoryLocationStrategy },
    provideRouter(routes, withDisabledInitialNavigation()),
  ],
};

(async () => {
  const appRef = await createApplication(appConfig);
  const MyExtensionElement = createCustomElement(AppComponent, {
    injector: appRef.injector,
  });
  customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension', MyExtensionElement);
})();
```

```typescript theme={null}
// src/app/app.component.ts
import { normalizeSubPath, readInitialSubPath } from '@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/router';

@Input() subPath = '/';

ngOnInit(): void {
  const fromInput = normalizeSubPath(this.subPath);
  const initial = fromInput === '/' ? readInitialSubPath() : fromInput;
  this.applyHostSubPath(initial);
  window.litiumExtension?.on('routeChanged', this.routeChangedHandler);
}

private applyHostSubPath(raw: string | undefined): void {
  const target = normalizeSubPath(raw);
  void this.router.navigateByUrl(target);
}
```

To navigate programmatically from page components, call the bridge API — the `routeChanged` handler syncs the local router:

```typescript theme={null}
// Inside a page component — do NOT call this.router.navigate() alone for cross-boundary nav
goToDetail(id: string): void {
  window.litiumExtension.navigate(`/orders/${id}`);
}
```

***

### Vanilla JS (manual)

```javascript theme={null}
// src/index.js
class MyExtension extends HTMLElement {
  #currentPath = '/';

  connectedCallback() {
    this.#currentPath = this.getAttribute('sub-path') ?? '/';
    this.#render();
    this.#unsubscribe = window.litiumExtension?.on('routeChanged', ({ path }) => {
      this.#currentPath = path;
      this.#render();
    });
  }

  disconnectedCallback() { this.#unsubscribe?.(); }

  #render() {
    // Route manually based on this.#currentPath
    if (this.#currentPath.startsWith('/orders/')) {
      const id = this.#currentPath.split('/')[2];
      this.innerHTML = `<order-detail id="${id}"></order-detail>`;
    } else {
      this.innerHTML = `<order-list></order-list>`;
    }
  }
}
customElements.define('litium-ext-vanilla-sample', MyExtension);
```

***

## Browser back/forward behavior

The following sequence describes what happens when a user clicks the browser Back button while inside your extension:

```
User clicks Back button
        │
        ▼
Browser pops history entry
        │
        ▼
Host Angular router receives popstate event
        │
        ▼
Host matches wildcard route for your extension prefix
        │
        ▼
Host fires routeChanged({ path: '/orders' })
        │
        ▼
Your routeChanged handler syncs the in-memory router / re-renders
        │
        ▼
Extension shows the previous page
```

Your extension must **never** call `history.pushState` or `history.replaceState` directly. These calls bypass the host router and break back/forward navigation.

***

## Deep linking and bookmarking

Deep links work because the host passes the current URL sub-path as the `sub-path` attribute on the initial render. For this to work correctly:

1. Your Custom Element must read the initial sub-path on mount (e.g. `readInitialSubPath()` in React, Vue, and Angular, or `this.getAttribute('sub-path')` in vanilla JS)
2. Your in-memory router must initialize to that path (e.g. `MemoryRouter initialEntries` plus `SubPathRoutes` in React, `applyHostSubPath` in Angular, `readInitialSubPath()` plus `applyHostPath` in Vue)
3. Your route definitions must handle all deep-linkable paths (no redirect-all-to-root that loses the path)

Bookmarks work identically — the host rehydrates the URL on page load and passes the sub-path to your extension.


# Migrate from Module Federation
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/migrate-from-module-federation

Guide for migrating an existing Angular Module Federation extension to the new Custom Element (Web Component) approach.

<Warning>
  **`litium-ui` cannot be used in extensions.** The `litium-ui` package is not available to Custom Element extensions. Any imports from `litium-ui` must be removed and replaced with your own components or a UI library of your choice.
</Warning>

## Should you migrate?

Use this checklist to decide:

| Question                                                                                                    | If yes...           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------- |
| Is your extension built with Angular Module Federation (`webpack.config.js` with `ModuleFederationPlugin`)? | You can migrate     |
| Is your extension already built as a Custom Element?                                                        | No migration needed |

<Note>
  **Registry setup is required.** Complete [SDK Installation](/platform/extensions/sdk-installation) before proceeding.
</Note>

***

## Recommended approach — scaffold a new project

The easiest and most reliable migration path is to scaffold a fresh Angular extension project and move your business logic across. This gives you a correct, up-to-date project structure without having to manually update every config file.

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk create my-extension --framework angular
cd my-extension
npm install
```

Then move your existing components, services, and routes from the old Module Federation project into `src/app/`. The scaffold already has:

* `vite.config.ts` — correct IIFE build setup
* `src/main.ts` — Custom Element registration with `@angular/elements` via `createApplication`
* `InMemoryLocationStrategy` — keeps Angular Router out of the browser history
* `extension.manifest.json` — deployment descriptor

Once your components are in place, follow [Step 3](#step-3--replace-host-service-calls) onwards to replace any Module Federation-specific service calls.

***

## Manual migration — step by step

If you prefer to migrate in-place rather than scaffold a new project, follow these steps.

### Step 1 — Back up your extension

```bash theme={null}
git checkout -b migrate/module-federation-to-web-component
```

Always migrate on a feature branch so you can compare the before and after states.

***

### Step 2 — Replace the build tooling

Remove webpack and Module Federation, then add Vite and the extension SDK:

```bash theme={null}
npm uninstall webpack webpack-cli @angular-architects/module-federation
npm install --save-dev vite @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk
```

Create a `vite.config.ts` configured as an IIFE build. Refer to the [Angular extension guide](/platform/extensions/create-angular-extension) for the full Vite configuration.

Archive (do not delete) your old webpack config so you can reference it during migration:

```bash theme={null}
mv webpack.config.js webpack.config.mf-backup.js
```

***

### Step 3 — Replace host service calls

All imports from `litium-ui` or shared host Angular services must be removed and replaced with the `window.litiumExtension` bridge API.

#### Notifications

**Before (Module Federation)**

```typescript theme={null}
import { NotificationActions } from 'litium-ui';
// ...
this.store.dispatch(NotificationActions.showSuccess({ message: 'Saved!' }));
```

**After (Custom Element)**

```typescript theme={null}
window.litiumExtension.showNotification({ message: 'Saved!', type: 'success' });
```

#### Navigation

**Before**

```typescript theme={null}
import { Router } from '@angular/router';
// (shared Angular Router from the host)
this.router.navigate(['/settings/extensions/my-extension/detail']);
```

**After**

```typescript theme={null}
window.litiumExtension.navigate('/detail');
```

#### Translations

Replace `TranslateService.instant()` with one of:

* Your own i18n library (e.g. `ngx-translate`, `i18next`)
* `window.litiumExtension.getContext().language` as a hint with your own translation map

#### Shared state (NgRx / Redux)

Shared store state provided by the host is not accessible in a Custom Element. Refactor to use the bridge API (`getContext()`, `fetch()`) or bundle your own state management (Signals, Zustand, etc.).

#### `litium-ui` components

Visual components from `litium-ui` (tables, buttons, form controls) are part of the host Angular application and **cannot be used** inside a bundled Custom Element. Replace them with your own components or a UI library of your choice (e.g. PrimeNG, Material, Radix UI).

***

### Step 4 — Update the manifest

In `extension.manifest.json`, change the framework type:

```json theme={null}
{
  "frameworkType": "web.component"
}
```

***

### Step 5 — Install dependencies and build

```bash theme={null}
npm install
npm run build
```

Fix any TypeScript compilation errors reported in the output. The most common errors are unresolved imports that referenced host-provided Angular modules.

***

## Testing

1. Start the dev server: `npm run dev`
2. Register the extension in **Settings > System settings > Extensions** with `bundleUrl: 'https://localhost:3000/src/main.ts'`
3. Verify each route loads correctly
4. Click every link and button — confirm bridge API calls (`showNotification`, `navigate`, `fetch`) work as expected
5. Test browser back/forward navigation

***

## Troubleshooting

### `Cannot find module 'litium-ui'`

Remove all `litium-ui` imports. The `litium-ui` package is part of the Litium host and cannot be used in extensions. Replace components with your own UI library.

### Blank screen after migration with no console errors

Check that `zone.js` is imported **before** any Angular import in your entry file (`main.ts`). Vite bundling order differs from webpack and sometimes reorders imports.

### `customElements.define` called twice (hot-reload error)

Wrap your `customElements.define` call with a guard:

```typescript theme={null}
if (!customElements.get('litium-ext-my-extension')) {
  customElements.define('litium-ext-my-extension', MyElement);
}
```


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/overview

Learn what a Litium UI extension is, how the omni-framework architecture works, and which approach is right for your project.

## What is a Litium extension?

A Litium extension is a self-contained JavaScript bundle that adds new UI to the Litium backoffice — a custom settings page, a dashboard widget, an order-action button, and so on. Extensions run **independently** of the platform: you can update, redeploy, or remove them without touching the core Litium installation.

Since Litium 8.24, extensions are built as **Web Components (Custom Elements)**. This approach — called *omni-framework support* — means you can use **any front-end framework** (React, Vue, Angular, Vanilla JS) or any Angular version, completely decoupled from the Angular 20 host application.

***

## Architecture

```mermaid theme={null}
flowchart TD
    subgraph Host["Litium Admin — Angular 20 host"]
        subgraph CE["Custom Element: litium-ext-my-widget"]
            FW["Your framework\nReact · Vue · Angular · Vanilla JS"]
            Bridge["window.litiumExtension\n― Bridge API ―"]
            FW -- "reads context · navigates · subscribes" --> Bridge
        end
        API["navigate()   showNotification()   fetch()   getContext()\non('routeChanged')   on('contextChanged')   off()"]
        Bridge --> API
    end
```

The host injects `window.litiumExtension` **before** any extension bundle is executed. Your extension reads context from it, navigates through it, and subscribes to host events through it. No direct Angular dependency is needed.

***

## Approaches at a glance

| Approach                           | Recommended?            | When to use                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Web Component** (Custom Element) | ✅ **Yes — recommended** | All new extensions. Any framework, any Angular version.                                                                                                                         |
| **iframe**                         | ⚠️ Limited              | Pre-existing external tools that cannot be refactored into a bundle.                                                                                                            |
| **Angular Module Federation**      | ❌ Deprecated            | Only for maintaining extensions built before Litium 8.24. See the [migration guide](/platform/extensions/migrate-from-module-federation) to convert to Web Components manually. |

<Note>
  **Why was Module Federation deprecated?** Angular Module Federation required extensions to share the exact same Angular version as the host. Every Angular host upgrade forced extension upgrades simultaneously. The Web Component approach eliminates this coupling entirely — your extension runs its own isolated copy of React, Vue, Angular, or no framework at all.
</Note>

***

* [Manifest reference](/platform/extensions/extension-manifest-reference) — `extension.manifest.json` fields
* [Testing extensions](/platform/extensions/testing-extensions) — unit tests, mocking, CI
* [Extension Management UI](/platform/extensions/extension-management-ui) — install and configure via Settings


# SDK installation
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/sdk-installation

Install @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk from the public npm registry. This is the mandatory first step before any framework guide.

## What is `@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk`?

`@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk` is the official toolkit for building Litium back office extensions. It provides:

| Feature              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **`create` CLI**     | Scaffold a complete extension project (React, Vue, or Angular)                                                                                                                                          |
| **`add` CLI**        | Add a panel or settings page to an existing extension project                                                                                                                                           |
| **`dev` CLI**        | Run a local Vite dev server for your extension bundle. Register the dev manifest URL in your running Litium admin host so it loads your extension and injects the real `window.litiumExtension` bridge. |
| **TypeScript types** | `LitiumExtensionAPI`, `ExtensionManifest`, `ExtensionContext`, and more                                                                                                                                 |
| **Vite plugin**      | `@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk/vite-plugin` — builds a single-file IIFE bundle the host can load                                                                                                     |
| **Admin Web API**    | `window.litiumExtension.fetch` — host-authenticated fetch for the Admin Web API                                                                                                                         |

***

## Step 1 — Scaffold your first extension

Once the package is available, scaffold a new extension with `npx`:

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk create my-extension --framework react
# Supported frameworks: react | vue | angular
```

***

## Step 2 — Add panels and settings pages

After scaffolding, use the `add` command from your **extension project root** to generate new extension points without touching the project structure manually:

```bash theme={null}
# From inside your extension project directory
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk add
```

Running `add` without arguments launches an interactive prompt. You can also pass the type directly:

```bash theme={null}
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk add panel
npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk add settings-page
```

| Type            | What it creates                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `panel`         | A web component panel in a backoffice area (Customers, Products, Sales, Media, or Websites) |
| `settings-page` | A new page under Settings, with a menu item and a component file wired to the router        |

The command:

1. Detects your framework from `package.json` (React, Vue, or Angular)
2. Generates the component file(s) under `src/`
3. Updates `extension.manifest.json` with the appropriate target entry
4. Prints instructions for wiring up the new component in your entry point

<Note>
  The `add` command must be run from the root of an extension project — a directory that contains both `package.json` and `extension.manifest.json`.
</Note>

See the detailed guides for each type:

<CardGroup>
  <Card title="Add a panel" icon="table-columns" href="/platform/extensions/add-panel">
    Render a web component in an area navigation panel.
  </Card>

  <Card title="Add a settings page" icon="gear" href="/platform/extensions/add-settings-page">
    Add a new page to the Settings sidebar.
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

The scaffolder creates a complete project with:

* `src/` — component source files
* `vite.config.ts` — configured for IIFE bundle output
* `extension.manifest.json` — deployment descriptor
* `.dev.config.json` — dev server port (default `3000`)
* Router setup (framework-specific, using memory history)
* Test setup (Vitest + Playwright, plus framework-specific testing libraries)

***

## Troubleshooting

### `npm ERR! 404 Not Found`

The package name may be misspelled. Confirm the exact name:

```bash theme={null}
npm show @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk
```

### `npx` downloads an old version

npm caches `npx` invocations. Force the latest version:

```bash theme={null}
npx --yes @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk@latest create my-extension --framework react
```


# Testing extensions
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/extensions/testing-extensions

Unit testing strategy, mocking window.litiumExtension, manual testing checklist, and CI configuration for Litium extensions.

## Unit testing strategy

Each generated extension project comes with a pre-configured test setup. The key principle is: **always mock `window.litiumExtension` before any component renders.**

| Framework | Test runner                | Component testing library |
| --------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| React     | Vitest                     | @testing-library/react    |
| Vue       | Vitest                     | @vue/test-utils           |
| Angular   | Jest + jest-preset-angular | Angular TestBed           |

***

## Mocking `window.litiumExtension`

Because your components call `window.litiumExtension.*` during render, you must mock the object in your `beforeEach` block. All three scaffolded projects follow the same pattern:

### React / Vue (Vitest)

```typescript theme={null}
// In each test file (or in a shared setup file like src/setup.ts)
import { vi } from 'vitest';

beforeEach(() => {
  (globalThis as unknown as { litiumExtension: unknown }).litiumExtension = {
    navigate: vi.fn(),
    replaceUrl: vi.fn(),
    showNotification: vi.fn(),
    fetch: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
      ok: true,
      json: async () => ({ items: [] }),
    }),
    getContext: vi.fn(() => ({
      language: 'en-US',
      user: { name: 'Test User', id: 'test-user' },
      subPath: '/',
      extensionBasePath: '/Litium/UI/settings/extensions/my-extension',
      baseUrl: 'http://localhost:5001',
    })),
    on: vi.fn(),
    off: vi.fn(),
  };
});
```

To verify that a bridge API method was called:

```typescript theme={null}
it('calls navigate when the button is clicked', async () => {
  const { getByRole } = render(<App subPath="/samplea" />);
  await userEvent.click(getByRole('button', { name: /go to page b/i }));
  expect(window.litiumExtension.navigate).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
    expect.stringContaining('/sampleb'),
  );
});
```

### Angular (Jest + jest-preset-angular)

```typescript theme={null}
// setup-jest.ts (already present in scaffolded project)
import 'jest-preset-angular/setup-jest';
```

In test files, mock `window.litiumExtension` in `beforeEach`:

```typescript theme={null}
import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { SampleAComponent } from './sample-a.component';

describe('SampleAComponent', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    (window as unknown as { litiumExtension: unknown }).litiumExtension = {
      navigate: jest.fn(),
      showNotification: jest.fn(),
      fetch: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({ ok: true, json: async () => ({}) }),
      getContext: jest.fn(() => ({
        language: 'en-US',
        user: { name: '', id: '' },
        subPath: '/',
        extensionBasePath: '',
        baseUrl: '',
      })),
      on: jest.fn(),
      off: jest.fn(),
    };

    TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      declarations: [SampleAComponent],
    });
  });

  it('displays the language from context', () => {
    const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(SampleAComponent);
    fixture.detectChanges();
    expect(fixture.nativeElement.textContent).toContain('en-US');
  });
});
```

***

## Testing Custom Element registration

Confirm your Custom Element registers correctly by importing the entry point in a test:

```typescript theme={null}
// src/index.test.ts (React example — same pattern for Vue and Angular)
describe('Custom Element', () => {
  it('registers litium-ext-react-sample', async () => {
    await import('./index.js');
    expect(customElements.get('litium-ext-react-sample')).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

***

## Manual testing checklist

Run through this checklist against a real Litium instance before each deployment:

* [ ] Extension loads without console errors
* [ ] Default route renders the expected page
* [ ] All navigation links work (click each link/button that triggers navigation)
* [ ] `window.litiumExtension.navigate()` updates the browser URL bar
* [ ] Browser **Back** button returns to the previous extension page
* [ ] Browser **Forward** button works after navigating back
* [ ] Page refresh with a deep-link URL renders the correct page (not always the root)
* [ ] `showNotification()` displays a banner with the correct message and type
* [ ] `fetch()` calls succeed (check Network tab — requests should include auth headers)
* [ ] `getContext()` returns the correct language and channel after switching them in the backoffice
* [ ] Unmounting the extension (navigating away from the area) logs no memory-leak warnings

***

## Running tests

```bash theme={null}
# Unit tests (single run)
npm test

# Unit tests in watch mode
npm run test:watch

# End-to-end tests (requires a running Litium instance and dev server)
npm run test:e2e
```

The e2e tests use [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) and require:

* `npm run dev` running in one terminal
* A Litium instance configured with the dev extension registered

***

## CI configuration (GitHub Actions)

The Angular 17 sample includes a `.github/workflows/ci.yml` you can copy as a starting point. The key steps for any framework are:

```yaml theme={null}
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: npm test
```

<Note>
  `@litiumab/platform-extension-sdk` is on the public npm registry — no registry configuration or authentication token is needed in CI.
</Note>

***
