# Sales in Litium 8
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/before-upgrading/sales-in-litium-8

Things to consider before an upgrade, regarding discounts, orders, payments, and shipments.

The Sales area has been completely re-written in Litium 8:

* Some things are [not supported or removed](#not-supported-in-litium-8).
* There are differences in [state transition](#state-transitions) functionality.
* Campaigns have become discounts with [some differences in how conditions are applied](#discount-conditions), as well as some [additional changes](#discounts-additional-changes).

For an overview of the upgrade procedure, please see [how to upgrade to Litium 8](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/overview).

***

## Not supported in Litium 8

### Removed and not supported discount types

The exact behavior of most of the [discount types](/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/discounts) has been examined and changed to be improved to better meet customer needs. The only discount type that is planned to be removed entirely is the Free fee discount.

Discount types that are not supported during migration:

* Buy X of the same product Pay for Y
* Reduce order value by a percentage
* Free shipping for delivery methods

### Product from assortment condition is removed

In Litium 8, there is nothing similar to the "Cart contains product from assortment" condition, and it will be skipped during migration.

### Discount and campaign logic extensibility

When campaigns become discounts in Litium, they can no longer be extended to build your own discount logic.

When several active discounts can be applied to a customer's order, [Litium will instead apply these in a pre-determined order](/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/discounts#Discount%20types%20and%20priority), which prioritizes the best discount value for the customer.

### Inactive and archived discounts

Discounts in previous versions of Litium that are not active or are archived will not be migrated to Litium 8.

### No flagging of active/ inactive discounts

The active/inactive flag is not available on discounts in Litium 8. You can inactivate at the channel level, but when you save you will lose the discount start and end date for that channel. Other discount settings that are channel-dependent may be lost as well. If you inactivate all channels in the discount settings in Litium 8, you will not be able to save the discount.

### The number of times a discount has been used is not included

This information regarding the number of times a discount has been used is not saved in previous versions of Litium and it will not be included in the upgrade for discounts.

### The maximum number of times the discount is given is not supported

For the campaign types that applied "maximum number of times the discount is given", this will no longer be supported in Litium 8 and is ignored during migration.

### Carts will not be migrated

Customer carts containing items will not be migrated.

### Multiple payments for the same order are not supported

When you have more than one payment it is not supported to upgrade.

***

## State transitions

How to handle [order states](#fixed-order-states) in Litium 8, and [state transition events and conditions](#state-transition-events-and-conditions).

Please read [more under upgrading state transitions](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/state-mapping) on how to map order states, payments, and shipments.

### Fixed order states

Litium 8.2 includes a framework to mark orders with different tags in order to adapt Litium to custom business logic.

The order states are fixed in Litium 8. Custom states cannot be added.

If your project has custom states and has defined transitions between them, you can use the [tagging feature in Litium 8](/platform/architecture/tagging) to achieve similar functionality as in previous versions of Litium. Custom states cannot be added to state transitions in Litium 8, and existing states cannot be removed.

### State transition events and conditions

Projects can listen to state transition events and take some actions when a state is reached, as well as add or modify state transition conditions in Litium 8. When you [upgrade from previous versions of Litium to Litium 8, you can run scripts to create a state mapping table](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/state-mapping).

***

## Discount conditions

Changes in conditions applied to discounts in Litium 8, compared to campaigns in previous versions of Litium.

### User belongs to conditions

This condition existed in previous versions of Litium and could be added to a campaign. The conditions meant that a customer had to belong to a specific organization, target group, or user group to get a discount.

In Litium 8, these conditions correspond to [target audience settings](/help/litium-8/sales/campaigns/discounts/offer-discount-to-a-selected-group) applicable directly to the discount.

### Order total condition

The order total condition indicated the sum of an order that needed to be exceeded for a discount to be valid in previous versions of Litium.

In Litium 8 a [threshold setting applicable directly to the discount](/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/discounts) is the corresponding concept.

### Target group conditions for discounts

The conditions for discounts are upgraded to include target group conditions when you [upgrade the database with the database tool](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-database).

### Cart contains product conditions

This condition existed in previous versions of Litium and could be added to a campaign. The conditions indicated what products needed to be in the cart for the discount to be valid, for example, a certain product or a product that could be found in a certain category or product list.

In Litium 8, you add the conditions to a [target group](/help/litium-8/customers/organize-platform-users/target-groups) instead, and then [use a connection to that target group for the conditions to apply to a discount](#).

***

## Discounts: Additional changes

Other changes from campaigns in previous versions of Litium to discounts in Litium 8.

### Voucher codes are now discount codes

What were named voucher codes in previous versions of Litium is called discount codes in Litium 8.

In Litium 8, [discount codes are a setting when creating a discount](/platform/areas/sales/order-placement/discounts).

### Generated codes can only be used once

In Litium 8, [generated codes can only be used once](/help/litium-8/sales/campaigns/discounts/use-discount-codes#Generate%20discount%20codes%20to%20activate%20discounts).

In previous versions of Litium, generated codes could be used several times. When discounts using generated codes are upgraded, the old setup can still be used. However, it will not be visible in the UI that multiple uses are allowed for migrated generated codes, only in the Excel file that can be downloaded.

### Currency for discounts is determined by the channel

Litium 8 applies currency from a channel for discounts, and not by setting the currency on an individual campaign.

### The percentage applied to discounts

In previous versions of Litium it was possible to add a decimal. In Litium 8 it will be rounded off to an integer in the UI, although in the API the decimal remains and will be applied.


# Comparing versions 7 and 8
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/comparing-versions-7-and-8

This page covers how features and behaviors have been added, removed or changed between version 7 and 8.

## Campaigns and discounts

What was called campaigns in Litium 7 is called discounts in LItium 8. In Litium 8, a campaign can contain discounts, pages and blocks.

[Read more about discounts in Litium 8](/help/litium-8/sales/campaigns/discounts)

Ther discount type Free fee was removed in Litium 8.

## Order management

In Litium 8.0 there is an improved one page order view in administration with most information needed to be seen for an order.

Administrator abilities like add and edit orders are not released in Litium 8.0, but order management abilities will be added in future versions.

### Order management abilities released in version 8.0

* One page order overview

### Order management released in version 8.1

* Add additional information on the order
* Add additional information on the order info

### Order management released in version 8.2

* Cancel / refund payment API
* Ability as an order approver to approve orders (Litium Accelerator)
* Tags on orders, payments and shipments

### Order management released in version 8.6

* Cancel remaining order rows of an order

### Order management released in version 8.7

* Mange returns coming from ERP API

### Order management released in version 8.10

* Ability to see additional order information in order page
* Ability to see tags for orders, deliveries and payments in order page

## Changed behaviours

### Order states

The order states are fixed in version 8 and custom states cannot be added. The reason for this is to ensure stability and scalability. The order process is a business critical flow and vulnerable to customizations. Instead we've introduced a framework where you can mark orders, payments and deliveries with different tags, which are useful for adapting Litium to custom business logic.

### Discount and campaign logic extensibility

In Litium 8 you can no longer extend the campaigns to build your own discount logic. The reason for this is to ensure stability and scalability. The discount calculations is a business critical area and vulnerable to customizations.

### Discount conditions

In Litium 8 you no longer add conditions the way it was done in Litium 7. The conditions can still be set, but you add them in different ways.

### **Only one product discount price is returned per product (from version 8.6)**

You can set up as many discounts as you wish for a product, but only one discounted price is returned by the API. Litium will return the lowest discount price in the given context.

### **Order total condition moved to discount settings**

The order total condition indicated the sum of an order that needed to be exceeded for a discount to be valid. Instead of as in Litium 7, adding a condition for a campaign, this condition is moved to be a setting directly on the discount.

### "User belongs to..." conditions moved to discount settings

These conditions indicate the organizations (company), user groups or target groups for which the discount is valid. Instead of as in Litium 7, adding conditions for a campaign, these conditions are moved to be settings directly on the discount in a settings group called audience.

### "Has product..." conditions moved to target groups

These conditions indicate what products need to be in the cart for a discount to be valid. Instead of as in Litium 7, adding conditions for a campaign, these conditions are moved to be set using a connection to a target group, which in turn has these conditions.

### Voucher codes becomes discount codes

Voucher codes are renamed to discount codes in Litium 8 and will be a setting available on each discount.

Please contact our support if you have quesions [support@litium.com](mailto:support@litium.com)


# Overview
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/overview

Litium 8 comes with significant changes and major improvements.

Below you will find step-by-step instructions on one way to upgrade to Litium 8 from previous Litium versions, including how to prepare for an upgrade, how to upgrade, and how to go live with an upgraded project. Please also see the documentation on [different upgrade paths](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-alternatives) to take.

### Preparatory information

1. Read through the instructions on this page to get an overview of how to upgrade to Litium 8, and go live.

2. Go through the [before upgrading documentation](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/before-upgrading) to get an idea of the scope of an upgrade to Litium 8, from reference documentation of [changes from version to version of Litium](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/before-upgrading), [changes to consider before migrating sales data](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/before-upgrading/sales-in-litium-8), including discounts and state transitions, and general things to consider [before you upgrade a solution with integrations](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/before-upgrading/integrations).

3. The [before upgrading documentation](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/before-upgrading) should help you determine when an upgrade can be performed.

4. Choose an [upgrade path](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-alternatives).

### Upgrade to Litium 8

1. Run the [Litium independent script](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/independent-script) to check whether there are still payments pending.

2. Back up the database and any other files.

3. Restore the backup to a development environment.

4. When you are upgrading from Litium 5 (read about upgrade to Litium 6 [here](https://docs.litium.com/platform/previous-versions/litium-6/upgrading-to-litium-6)) or from early versions of Litium 6 you have to upgrade first to the latest version of Litium 6 and run the BO a while so that the media files on the disk will be moved to the new folder structure with correct file names.

When the migration of the files is finished a row with Key = "mediamigration-correctblobnames" and ItemJson = "true" will be added to the Common.Setting table in the database.

5. Upgrade the [solution code](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution), including configuring the [Litium app proxy](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/litium-app-proxy), and upgrade the [database](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-database), including running the [scripts for State mapping](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/state-mapping).

### Go live

1. Close the checkout page to prevent new orders from being placed.

2. Close down all integrations to prevent product updates from the ERP, and information such as an order being ready to be shipped, and for monetary transactions to be made.

3. After closing down all integrations, please wait 10-15 minutes to proceed, to prevent pending payments from remaining in the system.

4. Run the [Litium independent script](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/independent-script) to check whether there are still payments pending. Should there be a pending payment captured, the upgrade must be halted until there are no pending payments in the system.

5. Close down the site that will be upgraded, and re-direct customers to a temporary webpage.

6. Restore a new version of the production database to a new production database.

7. Upgrade the new production database to Litium 8.

8. Start the site with the new code.

9. Test functions on the site, as deemed necessary.

10. Allow access to all visitors.


# State mapping
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/state-mapping

If you have defined custom states in a previous version of Litium, and want to upgrade the integrations to Litium 8.

For an overview of the upgrade procedure, please see [how to upgrade to Litium 8](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8).

During the upgrade from Litium 7 to Litium 8, a state mapping table is created. It maps the Litium 7 states to Litium 8 states. The mapping table's general structure:

<img alt="state mapping L7 to L8.jpg" />

When there is no state in Litium 8 that corresponds to the state in Litium 7, a tag will be created for the entity, with the name of the missing state, as shown in the table above.

You may map any custom state to a defined state in Litium 8 using the same script, and create a tag to denote the state in Litium 7. Use the [Tagging feature in Litium 8](/platform/architecture/tagging) to control the flow of the states.

Script to generate State mapping table:

```sql theme={null}
IF NOT OBJECT_ID('dbo.StateMapping') IS NULL BEGIN; DROP TABLE dbo.StateMapping; END;
CREATE TABLE dbo.StateMapping (Area nvarchar(20), SourceStateName nvarchar(100), SourceStateId int, TargetStateName nvarchar(100), Tags nvarchar(max));
INSERT INTO dbo.StateMapping VALUES
('Order', 'Init', 0, 'Init', ''),
('Order', 'WaitingConfirmation', 10, 'Init', '_awaitOrderApproval'),
('Order', 'Confirmed', 1, 'Confirmed', ''),
('Order', 'Processing', 2, 'Processing', ''),
('Order', 'Completed', 3, 'Completed', ''),
('Order', 'Cancelled', 4, 'Completed', '_cancelled'),
('Order', 'Returned', 5, 'Completed', '_returned'),
('Order', 'Attention', 6, 'Processing', '_attention'),
('Order', 'ClosedByAdmin', 7, 'Completed', '_closedByAdmin'),
('Order', 'ReturnConfirmed', 21, 'Confirmed', ''),
('Order', 'ReturnProcessing', 22, 'Processing', ''),
('Order', 'ReturnCompleted', 23, 'Completed', ''),
('Order', 'Invalid', 99, 'Init', '_invalid'),

('Shipment', 'Init', 0, 'Init', ''),
('Shipment', 'Delivered', 1, 'Shipped', ''),
('Shipment', 'Failed', 2, 'Processing', '_failed'),
('Shipment', 'Cancelled', 3, 'Cancelled', ''),
('Shipment', 'Returned', 4, 'Returned', ''),
('Shipment', 'Processing', 5, 'Processing', ''),
('Shipment', 'ReadyToShip', 6, 'ReadyToShip', ''),

('Rma', 'Init', 1, 'Init', ''),
('Rma', 'PackageReceived', 2, 'PackageReceived', ''),
('Rma', 'Processing', 4, 'Processing', ''),
('Rma', 'Completed', 8, 'Completed', '');
```

Script to map shipping and payment options:

```sql theme={null}
IF NOT OBJECT_ID('dbo.OptionMapping') IS NULL BEGIN; DROP TABLE dbo.OptionMapping; END;
CREATE TABLE dbo.OptionMapping(SourceOptionName nvarchar(100), SourceProviderName nvarchar(100), TargetOptionId nvarchar(100), TargetProviderId nvarchar(100));
INSERT INTO dbo.OptionMapping VALUES
('Expresspaket', '', 'expressPackage', 'DirectShipment'),
('Standardpaket', '', 'standardPackage', 'DirectShipment'),
('DirectPayment', 'DirectPay', 'DirectPay', 'DirectPayment'),
('SE KlarnaCheckout', 'KlarnaV3', 'SE Checkout', 'KlarnaPayment')
```


# Upgrade alternatives
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-alternatives

There are three upgrade alternatives to choose from.

Please see [what to consider before upgrading](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/before-upgrading) if you need additional information on ability changes in order to choose an alternative.

For an overview of the upgrade procedure, please see [how to upgrade to Litium 8](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8).

### Alternative A

### Upgrade the platform solution. Use the current database.

All custom functionality that references parts of the Litium API that is no longer available, needs to be re-written.

### Alternative B

### Make a clean install of Litium. Discard the current solution. Keep the current database.

Only code in use will be moved to the new solution, making this a good opportunity to clean an existing solution of all unused code.

Platform solution: The existing layout and functionality in the old solution that you want to keep, need to be migrated and adapted into the new templates.

### Alternative C

### Make a clean install of Litium. Discard the current solution and the current database.

Platform solution: The existing layout and functionality in the old solution that you want to keep, need to be migrated and adapted into the new templates.

Database: You must use the database migration scripts to migrate data from the old database.


# Upgrade the database
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-database

A step-by-step guide to upgrading the database.

Export migration scripts from solution with Litium DB tools.

For an overview of the upgrade procedure, please see [how to upgrade to Litium 8](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8).

❗️ Make sure that you have a backup of your database and any other files.

❗️ Make sure that you have taken all precautions necessary to be able to roll back the upgrade procedure.

1. [System requirements](#1-system-requirements)

2. [Run the Litium State mapping scripts](#2-run-the-litium-state-mapping-scripts)

3. [Upgrade the database](#3-upgrade-the-database)

4. [Update the exchange rates on already placed orders](#4-update-the-exchange-rates-on-already-placed-orders)

### 1. System requirements

Please find the [pre-requisites for Litium 8 here](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/dotnet-upgrade).

### 2. Run the Litium State mapping scripts

Please find the [scripts and the mapping of state transitions here](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/state-mapping).

### 3. Upgrade the database

To manage the upgrade of the Litium platform database the *litium-db* dotnet tool is used.

This is a command-line tool that can migrate the database from the previous version or generate a script that can be executed later.

In the below examples the connection string is in the following format

```bash theme={null}
"Pooling=true;User Id=user;Password=secret;Database=litium;Server=127.0.0.1;TrustServerCertificate=True"
```

### - Manual installation of the db tool

Configure the Litium NuGet feed [Litium packages](/platform/get-started/litium-packages).

Manual installation of the *litium-db* dotnet tool as a local tool:

```bash theme={null}
dotnet new tool-manifest
dotnet tool install Litium.Application.Migrations [--version (Litium version)]
```

The *tool-manifest* need to be created in the folder before a local tool can be installed.

The *--version* can be added to point for a specific version of the *litium-db* tool. We do not recommend installing the *litium-db* tool as a global tool because you can only have one version installed.

### - Execute the database upgrade

With the *update* command, you can execute the database upgrade.

```bash theme={null}
dotnet litium-db update --connection [connectionstring]
```

if you have the connection string in your json-config file you can directly use that for migration

```bash theme={null}
dotnet litium-db update --file [path to the config.json file]
```

### - Manual upgrade: Generate script

With the *pre-script* and *script* command, you can create the database script that is needed for the manual upgrade of the database. For example, if the scripts should be sent to Litium Support for applying to the customer database.

```bash theme={null}
dotnet litium-db pre-script -o prerequisite.sql
dotnet litium-db script -o upgrade.sql
```

The *pre-script* is used to validate the information in the database before starting the migration. If the validation script is failing with an error message the upgrade should be aborted and the database needs to be corrected regarding the instructions in the error.

### 4. Update the exchange rates on already placed orders

Not all orders have base currencies and exchange rates. This script will fill in that data, and update the exchange rate value on historical orders. Updating the exchange rates on already placed orders may provide improved statistical reports.

```sql theme={null}
--Finds and updates historical Orders that are missing BaseCurrencyCode and ExchangeRate.
--Defines the Base currency code to set for historical Orders
DECLARE @baseCurrencyCode nvarchar(5) = 'SEK'
--Defines the Currency code which Orders were paid with
DECLARE @currencyCode nvarchar(5) = 'USD'
--Defines the exchange rate, to convert from @currencyCode to @baseCurrencyCode
DECLARE @exchangeRate decimal(18,8) = 9.87
--Defines from date, to get orders in the specific date range
DECLARE @fromDate datetimeoffset(7) = '2022/04/25'
--Defines to date, to get orders in the specific date range
DECLARE @toDate datetimeoffset(7) = '2022/05/27'

UPDATE [Sales].[Order]
SET BaseCurrencyCode = @baseCurrencyCode, ExchangeRate = @exchangeRate
WHERE BaseCurrencyCode IS NULL AND CurrencyCode = @currencyCode AND OrderDate >= @fromDate AND OrderDate <= @toDate
```


# About the .NET Upgrade Assistant
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/-net-upgrade-assistant

Information about using the .NET tool Upgrade Assistant.

The Microsoft .NET Upgrade Assistant is a migration tool from ASP.NET to ASP.NET Core. It automates tasks related to migrating ASP.NET MVC and WebAPI projects to ASP.NET Core. Please find [more information and the](http://github.com/dotnet/upgrade-assistant) [.NET Upgrade Assistant here](https://github.com/dotnet/upgrade-assistant).

The Upgrade Assistant has an extension system allowing you to customize many of the upgrade steps without having to rebuild the tool. Please see [how to extend the tool here](http://github.com/dotnet/upgrade-assistant/blob/main/docs/extensibility.md).

After running the .NET Upgrade Assistant you will have to carry out additional migration tasks to complete the migration. The project will not build until you complete the migration. Analyzers added to the project will highlight some of the remaining changes needed after the tool runs.

### NuGet packages

A Microsoft .NET tool is a NuGet package that contains a console application. When you use the Microsoft .NET tool Upgrade Assistant, it needs to restore the NuGet packages. It also has to restore the query configured NuGet sources for information on updated packages.

If there are dependencies on authenticated NuGet sources, a v2 .NET Core-compatible NuGet credential provider needs to be installed, and the .NET Upgrade Assistant may need to run in the interactive mode in order to authenticate the NuGet sources.


# Upgrade to .Net 7 or later
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/dotnet-upgrade

These are some important points when upgrading the project to .NET 7 or .NET 8.

## Target framework

Before upgrading the packages for Litium 8.13 or later that using .NET 7, the projects target framework need to be updated to ***NET7.0***, otherwise package installation or upgrade will fail.

Before upgrading the packages for Litium 8.14 or later that using .NET 8, the projects target framework need to be updated to ***NET8.0***, otherwise package installation or upgrade will fail.

## AutoMapper

The AutoMapper in the Litium project has been updated to version 12 in Litium 8.13. There's a breaking change about [AutoMapper no longer creates maps automatically](https://docs.automapper.org/en/latest/9.0-Upgrade-Guide.html) - CreateMissingTypeMaps setting is now no longer supported. You now need to define the mapping rules specifically instead of letting automapper create missing mapping types automatically.

Let's look at an example:

```csharp theme={null}
IQueryable<object> source = _myRepo.GetResult();
List<myObject> dest = mapper.MapTo<myObject>(source).ToList();
```

We have the automapping rule between object and myObject, and we're trying to map a `List<object>` to `List<myObject>`. From Automapper 9 we'll get  the error "Missing type map configuration or unsupported mapping."

A quick work around for this is changing the .ToList() line to something like this:

```csharp theme={null}
List<myObject> dest = source.Select(src => src.MapTo<MyObject>()).ToList();
```

We'll need to do the mapping for each single object, using linq to create a collection and return.

### Read-only collection with AutoMapper

After upgrading to .NET 7 and the new version of AutoMapper, collection can be read-only and should not be assigned directly inside your *AutoMapper.ITypeConverter*'s, instead a new instance should be created. If the source dictionary is read-only, then also the target dictionary will be the same read-only instance and you will not be able to modify the dictionary inside the target object.

To make a clone of the dictionary the easiest way is to use the extension method *ToDictionary(s => s.Key, s => s.Value)*, that will assign *null* or an new dictionary with the same values to the target object. If the dictionary key or values are an complex object a clone of that need to be done as well.

Example in a *AutoMapper.ITypeConverter*

From

```csharp theme={null}
return new Connect.Payments.PaymentInfo
            {
                Id = source.Id,
                AdditionalInfo = source.AdditionalInfo,
            };
```

To

```csharp theme={null}
return new Connect.Payments.PaymentInfo
            {
                Id = source.Id,
                AdditionalInfo = source.AdditionalInfo?.ToDictionary(s => s.Key, s => s.Value),
            };
```


# Litium independent script
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/independent-script

Run the Litium independent script to check whether there are still payments pending.

Should there be a pending payment captured, the upgrade must be halted until there are no payments pending in the system.

For an overview of the upgrade procedure, please see [how to upgrade to Litium 8](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8).

```sql theme={null}
IF EXISTS(SELECT NULL FROM dbo.sysobjects WHERE id = object_id(N'dbo.ECommerce_Order') AND OBJECTPROPERTY(id, N'IsUserTable') = 1)
BEGIN
    EXEC('IF EXISTS( SELECT *  FROM ECommerce_Order ord INNER JOIN ECommerce_PaymentInfo pay on ord.OrderID =  pay.OrderID
        WHERE pay.PaymentStatus in (1,3,4,9) and DATEDIFF(Day,OrderDate,GETDATE()) = 0)
        BEGIN
             SELECT ''Some order payment created in today need to be completed before upgrade'' as Description, ''Error'' as Type
        END
        ELSE
        BEGIN
             SELECT ''All good!'' as Description, ''Info'' as Type
        END');
END
```


# Configure Litium app proxy
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/litium-app-proxy

For payments that are already created through a Payment Service Provider (PSP) before sales data was migrated from earlier Litium versions to Litium 8.

For an overview of the upgrade procedure, please see [how to upgrade to Litium 8](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8).

When a transaction is created through a PSP, that PSP keeps URLs for notification for each transaction created.

When a payment was created before migrating sales data, the URL for notification will be related to a previous version of Litium.

Therefore, you need to configure the Litium App proxy. Litium 8 will then be able to catch the request sent to those URLs and forward the request to the payment app that will operate the notification. The system will be able to forward the response from the payment app back to the caller of the notification (notification acknowledgment).

The list of URLs is configured in Litium.Accelerator.MVC - appsettings.json under Litium node. It is a dictionary where the key is the notification URL and the value is a destination URL on the app.

```json theme={null}
{
    "Litium": {
        "AppProxy": {
            "Url": {
                "/url1": {"AppId": "appId", "DestinationUrl": "/relative-action-url1" },
                "/url2": {"AppId": "appId", "DestinationUrl": "/relative-action-url2" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

In a PSP add-on, the format of the endpoint used to received notification from payment provider is `https://<domain name>/PaymentProviderResult.axd/Report/<PaymentProviderName>`.

#### Example

If you want to create an App proxy for the Klarna Add-on, you will have to define two URLs:

1. The URL of the PSP add-on: /PaymentProviderResult.axd/Report/KlarnaV3.
2. The [push notification URL as defined here](/add-ons/add-ons-as-extensions/payment-extensions/klarna/develop). In the code example below, the URL is /site.axd/KlarnaPayment/PushNotification.

Then, the configuration should be:

```json theme={null}
{
    "Litium": {
        "AppProxy": {
            "Url": {
                "/PaymentProviderResult.axd/Report/KlarnaV3": {"AppId": "KlarnaPayment", "DestinationUrl": "/legacy-callback/PushNotification" },
                "/site.axd/KlarnaPayment/PushNotification": {"AppId": "KlarnaPayment", "DestinationUrl": "/legacy-callback/PushNotification" }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Enable App proxy

In order to enable this feature, insert middleware to use Litium App proxy in Startup.cs.

Please note that App proxy-middleware is already installed per default in the [Litium accelerator](/accelerators/mvc-accelerator).

```csharp theme={null}
public void Configure(IApplicationBuilder app, IHostEnvironment env)
{
    //..
    if (env.IsDevelopment())
    {
        app.UseDeveloperExceptionPage();
    }
    else
    {
        app.UseLitiumExceptionPage();
    }
    
    app.UseLitiumAppProxy();

    app.UseLitiumPageNotFoundPage();
    app.UseLitiumUrlRedirect();
    //..
}
```

# Upgrade the Litium platform solution using Microsoft's .NET Upgrade Assistant
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/upgrade-solution-steps

How to run an upgrade to Litium 8 using the .NET Upgrade Assistant.

1. [Pre-requisites](#1-pre-requisites)

2. [Install](#2-install)

3. [Analyze dependencies](#3-analyze-dependencies)

4. [Run the .NET Upgrade Assistant](#4-run-the-net-upgrade-assistant)

See the [.NET Upgrade Assistant steps](#net-upgrade-assistant-steps)

5. Complete migration to [upgrade the solution](#5-upgrade-the-solution). Note that this is the main and most time-consuming bulk of the work.

6. Configure [Litium app proxy](#6-configure-the-litium-app-proxy)

❗️ Make sure that you have a backup.

The .NET Upgrade Assistant will backup the project in the first step after running. Still, we recommend that you have a backup of your database and any other files before you start.

❗️ Make sure that you have taken all precautions necessary to be able to roll back the upgrade procedure.

### 1. Pre-requisites

[Configure the Litium NuGet feed Litium packages](/platform/get-started/litium-packages).

The .NET Upgrade Assistant requires that your project builds, which may include installing [Visual Studio 2022](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) in order to upgrade to .NET 6.

It also requires a recent version of MS Build to be installed, in order to work with project files. MS Build can be installed by installing Visual Studio 2022.

### 2. Install

Install the [.NET Upgrade tool from NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/upgrade-assistant/) as a .NET CLI tool by running:

```bash theme={null}
dotnet tool install -g upgrade-assistant
```

❗️ Invalid or authenticated sources in [NuGet configuration](https://docs.microsoft.com/nuget/consume-packages/configuring-nuget-behavior) may cause installation problems.

### 3. Analyze dependencies

Analyze your project dependencies by navigating to the directory containing your project or solution, and run the following command:

```bash theme={null}
upgrade-assistant analyze <Path to csproj or sln to upgrade>
```

Change `<Path to csproj or sln to upgrade>` on the commands on this page to the path and name of your solution or project file.

### 4. Run the .NET Upgrade Assistant

Run the following command to start upgrading your project:

```bash theme={null}
upgrade-assistant upgrade <Path to csproj or sln to upgrade>
```

### .NET Upgrade Assistant steps

When you run the .NET upgrade assistant it will show you the following steps:

1. Backup project\
   A backup is created by the .NET Upgrade Assistant. You can choose to skip this step if you have already created the backup.

2. Convert project file to SDK style

3. Update TFM (target framework moniker)

4. Update NuGet packages

5. Add template file

6. Migrate app config files

7. Update C# source

The information about the steps above was last updated upon the release of Litium 8.4 (2022-05-31). Please see the [.NET Upgrade Assistant for more information](https://github.com/dotnet/upgrade-assistant).

### 5. Upgrade the solution

Note that this is the main and most time-consuming bulk of the work.

Most things cannot be upgraded automatically by using the Assistant and must be manually converted.

Analyzers are included in the .NET Upgrade Assistant to help you identify some of the remaining changes needed.

After the analyzers evaluate your code, you can let the Upgrade assistant automatically convert your solution to ASP.NET Core.

Please note, however, that many tasks are not fully automated, and that the analyzer also works on an already-converted solution.

Also, note that the solution will most probably not build until you have manually completed the migration steps.

### 6. Configure the Litium app proxy

[Instructions on how to configure the Litium app proxy](/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-the-platform-solution/litium-app-proxy).


# Upgrade to Angular 20
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-to-angular-20



## Version compatibility

* **Node.js**: `^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || ^24.0.0`
* **Typescript**: `>=5.8.0 <5.9.0`
* **RxJS**: `^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0`

## Migrating an Angular Component to a Standalone Component

Here’s how you can update an existing "classic" component (declared in a module) to a **standalone component**.

**Before**

```javascript theme={null}
// example.component.ts
@Component({
  selector: 'app-example',
  template: ``,
})
export class ExampleComponent { }

// In the module:
@NgModule({
  declarations: [ExampleComponent],
  imports: [CommonModule],
})
export class ExampleModule {}
```

**After**

```javascript theme={null}
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { CommonModule, DatePipe } from '@angular/common';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-example',
  standalone: true, // may be omitted (true by default)
  imports: [CommonModule, DatePipe],
  template: ``
})
export class ExampleComponent {
  value = new Date();
}
```

## Update `litium-ui` version

In your `package.json`, update the `litium-ui` dependency to the latest version. For example:

```javascript theme={null}
"litium-ui": "https://packages.litium.com/Npm/litium-ui?8.24"
```

## Back office extensions: Web Components and Module Federation

If you build or maintain **back office UI extensions**, plan for the **Web Component (Custom Element)** model instead of **Angular Module Federation**.

You previously registered a separate Angular app with the `common.angular.module` target and `ModuleFederationPlugin`. **That pattern is deprecated.** When you ship a Custom Element as a single-file bundle, the Litium platform loads your extension and exposes the **`window.litiumExtension`** bridge API for navigation, notifications, and context. You no longer share Angular with the host bundle.

**Why change?** Each Litium admin Angular upgrade used to force a matching rebuild of federated extensions. With Web Components, you can use React, Vue, Angular (including a different major than the host), or vanilla JavaScript.

**What you should do**

1. If you still use Module Federation, follow the steps in [Migrate from Module Federation](../../extensions/migrate-from-module-federation).
2. If you have not installed the tooling yet, complete [SDK installation](../../extensions/sdk-installation) first (registry access and `npx @litiumab/platform-extension-sdk`).
3. Please find a description of the extension architecture and links to framework guides in [Extensions overview](../../extensions/overview).

## Troubleshoot

### Error: Module not found

If you encounter "Error: Module not found: Error: Can't resolve /node\_modules/@angular-devkit/build-angular/node\_modules/@babel/runtime/helpers/esm/asyncToGenerator.js", then try to install the @babel/runtime on your project:

```bash theme={null}
npm install @babel/runtime --save
```

### "ɵɵdomElementStart is not a function" or "ngDevMode is not defined"

These errors indicate Angular version mismatch between the custom/extension module and the Litium Platform. The solution is to pin the exact version of Angular packages that Litium platform uses:

```json theme={null}
"overrides": {
    "@angular/animations": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/common": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/compiler": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/compiler-cli": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/core": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/forms": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/platform-browser": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/platform-browser-dynamic": "20.0.4",
    "@angular/router": "20.0.4",
    "zone.js": "0.15.0"
  }
```
