# Upgrade to Litium 8.31
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/upgrade-to-litium-8/upgrade-to-litium-8-31

Async migration upgrade guide for partner developers upgrading to Litium 8.31.

This document summarizes all breaking changes introduced as part of the platform-wide async migration (feature #75377). Changes are grouped by migration pattern so you can quickly identify what action is needed in your customer solution.

Three distinct migration patterns are used across the platform:

1. **Async-only** — sync method deleted entirely, compile error expected, must implement async replacement.
2. **New abstract async methods added** — existing sync methods kept as virtual fallbacks, but your custom subclass must add new async overrides to compile.
3. **Async-first with `IAsync*` interface and `*LookupService` / `*ResolverService` orchestrator** — old interface marked `[Obsolete]`, sync path still works, but you should migrate to the new interface and service.

## Pattern 1 — Async-Only: Sync Method Deleted (compile errors expected)

These changes remove sync methods with no backward-compatible fallback. Any code implementing or calling them will get compile errors and must be updated.

### SalesOrderBuilder (Litium.Sales)

Five abstract void methods replaced with Task equivalents. Any custom subclass overriding these must rename and return `Task`:

* `void AddOrUpdateItem(AddOrUpdateCartItemArgs)` → `Task AddOrUpdateItemAsync(...)`
* `void AddOrUpdateFee(AddOrUpdateFeeArgs)` → `Task AddOrUpdateFeeAsync(...)`
* `void AddOrUpdateShippingFee(AddOrUpdateShippingFeeArgs)` → `Task AddOrUpdateShippingFeeAsync(...)`
* `void AddOrUpdateDiscount(AddOrUpdateDiscountArgs)` → `Task AddOrUpdateDiscountAsync(...)`
* `void AddExternalDiscount(AddExternalDiscountArgs)` → `Task AddExternalDiscountAsync(...)`

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
protected override void AddOrUpdateItem(AddOrUpdateCartItemArgs args) { ... }

// After
protected override async Task AddOrUpdateItemAsync(AddOrUpdateCartItemArgs args, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
    await ...
}
```

### ISalesOrderRowFactory (Litium.Sales)

`SalesOrderRow Create(CreateSalesOrderRowArgs args)` has been removed. Replace with:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
public SalesOrderRow Create(CreateSalesOrderRowArgs args) { ... }

// After
public async Task<SalesOrderRow> CreateAsync(CreateSalesOrderRowArgs args, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
    return await ...
}
```

### ISitemapFactory (Litium.Web.Abstractions)

`IEnumerable<SitemapItem> CreateSiteMap(Channel channel)` deleted. Replace with an async streaming implementation:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
public IEnumerable<SitemapItem> CreateSiteMap(Channel channel) { ... }

// After
public async IAsyncEnumerable<SitemapItem> CreateSiteMapAsync(Channel channel,
    [EnumeratorCancellation] CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
    await foreach (var item in ...)
    yield return item;
}
```

### IFeedFieldFactory (Litium.Products.Syndications)

`Func<FeedFieldContext, object?> Create(FeedFieldFactoryContext)` deleted. Both the factory setup and the per-item delegate are now async:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
public Func<FeedFieldContext, object?> Create(FeedFieldFactoryContext ctx) => c => GetValue(c);

// After
public Task<Func<FeedFieldContext, Task<object?>>> CreateAsync(FeedFieldFactoryContext ctx,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    => Task.FromResult<Func<FeedFieldContext, Task<object?>>>(c => Task.FromResult<object?>(GetValue(c)));
```

`FeedEngine.CreateFieldMap` has also been renamed to `CreateFieldMapAsync`. Any code calling it must be updated.

### IPriceAgentItemFactory (Litium.Web.Abstractions)

`PriceAgentItemResult Create(PriceAgentItemArgs)` deleted. Rename to `CreateAsync` and return `Task<PriceAgentItemResult>`.

### IPriceAgent (Litium.Web.Abstractions)

`void Render(TextWriter, IEnumerable<PriceAgentItemResult>)` deleted. Replace with:

```csharp theme={null}
// After — iterate the async stream
public async Task RenderAsync(TextWriter writer,
    IAsyncEnumerable<PriceAgentItemResult> priceAgentItemResults,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
    await foreach (var item in priceAgentItemResults.WithCancellation(cancellationToken))
    {
        await writer.WriteAsync(...);
    }
}
```

The `PriceAgentItemFactoryDependencies.PriceCalculator` property type has also changed from `IPriceCalculator` to `PriceLookupService` — see the section on price calculation below.

### AuditService (Litium.Auditing)

All abstract sync methods deleted — async-only. Existing implementations will get compile errors and must implement:

* `Task CreateReadEntryAsync(..., CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`
* `Task<...> GetAsync(..., CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`
* `Task<...> GetSummaryAsync(..., CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`

The `CreateReadEntry` extension method has been replaced by `CreateReadEntryAsync`.

### IEventOperationValidator (Litium.Security)

`HasAccess` deleted entirely. Any implementation must rename to `HasAccessAsync`:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
public bool HasAccess(TEvent item) => ...;

// After
public Task HasAccessAsync(TEvent item, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    => Task.CompletedTask; // or actual async logic
```

### IReferenceService (Litium.Common) and IMediaReferenceService (Litium.Media)

`FindReferences(Guid systemId)` deleted on both. Replace with:

```csharp theme={null}
public async Task<IEnumerable<ReferenceItem>> FindReferencesAsync(Guid systemId,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
{
    return await ...
}
```

Also affected — custom implementations of `EntityInformationService` and `FieldTemplateInformationService` (administration layer):

* `string GetName(ReferenceItem)` → `Task<string> GetNameAsync(ReferenceItem, CancellationToken)`
* `string GetLink(ReferenceItem)` → `Task<string> GetLinkAsync(ReferenceItem, CancellationToken)`

There is no sync fallback for any of these changes.

### Blob, BlobContainer, BlobService (Litium.Blobs)

All sync public/abstract methods have been replaced. If you have a custom blob provider or call site:

| Removed                                              | Replacement                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blob.Delete()`                                      | `await blob.DeleteAsync()`                                          |
| `blob.OpenRead()`                                    | `await blob.OpenReadAsync()`                                        |
| `blob.OpenWrite()`                                   | `await blob.OpenWriteAsync()`                                       |
| `Blob Get(string name)` on BlobContainer             | `Task<Blob> GetAsync(string name)`                                  |
| `Blob GetDefault()` on BlobContainer                 | `Task<Blob> GetDefaultAsync()`                                      |
| `BlobContainer Create(string, Guid?)` on BlobService | `Task<BlobContainer> CreateAsync(string, Guid?, CancellationToken)` |
| `void Delete(BlobContainer)` on BlobService          | `Task DeleteAsync(BlobContainer, CancellationToken)`                |
| `BlobContainer Get(Uri)` on BlobService              | `Task<BlobContainer> GetAsync(Uri, CancellationToken)`              |

There is no sync fallback for any of these changes.

### IIndexConfiguration and IMultilingualIndexConfiguration (Litium.Elasticsearch)

The sync `BuildIndexState()` / `BuildIndexState(CultureInfo)` and obsolete `BuildIndexDescriptor` methods have been removed. Any class directly implementing these interfaces (not extending the base classes) must now implement the async version:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
public IIndexState BuildIndexState() => ...;

// After
public Task<IIndexState> BuildIndexStateAsync()
    => Task.FromResult<IIndexState>(...);
```

## Pattern 2 — New Abstract Async Methods Added (existing sync kept as virtual fallback)

These abstract classes retain their existing sync methods as virtual delegating defaults, but add new abstract async methods. Your custom subclass will get a compile error until the new async methods are implemented.

### IAccountService (Litium.Account)

Add three new async methods to any custom implementation:

* `Task<ISet<Guid>> GetGroupsSystemIdAsync(Guid personSystemId, Guid? organizationSystemId = default, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`
* `Task<ISet<Guid>> GetOrganizationsSystemIdAsync(Guid personSystemId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`
* `Task<ISet<string>> GetRoleOperationsAsync(Guid personSystemId, Guid organizationSystemId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`

Existing sync methods are retained with delegating defaults.

### Security services (Litium.Security)

Custom subclasses of the following must add the new async overrides:

* **AuthorizationService** — add `HasOperationAsync`, `HasOperationAsync<T>`, `HasAnyOperationAsync`. High impact: \~904 call sites in consuming code.
* **AuthenticationService** — add `PasswordSignInAsync`, `ExternalSignInAsync`, `SignOutAsync`, `RefreshSignInAsync`.
* **DefaultAccessControlService** — add `GetAsync` and `UpdateAsync`.
* **OperationDefinitionService** — add `CreateAsync`, `DeleteAsync`, `GetAsync`, `GetAllAsync`.

Existing sync methods are retained as virtual with delegating defaults decorated with `[LitiumUseAsync]` and `[LitiumAvoidInternal]`.

### KeyLookupService (Litium.Common)

Add three new abstract async methods. Two new public readonly record structs replace the `bool + out` parameter pattern:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
bool TryGetId(..., out string id);
bool TryGetSystemId(string id, ..., out Guid systemId);

// After — implement:
public override Task<KeyIdLookupResult> GetIdAsync(..., CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
public override Task<KeySystemIdLookupResult> GetSystemIdAsync(string id, ..., CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
public override Task<KeySystemIdLookupResult> GetSystemIdAsync(Type areaType, string id, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
```

### UrlValidator (Litium.Web)

New abstract async method added. Override `ValidateAsync` instead of `Validate`:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
protected override UrlValidatorResult Validate(CultureInfo culture, string url) { ... }

// After
protected override Task<UrlValidatorResult> ValidateAsync(CultureInfo culture, string url,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    => Task.FromResult(Validate(culture, url)); // or fully async
```

Please find a description of the updated `UrlValidator` class [here](/platform/architecture/validation/urlvalidator).

### IndexConfigurationBase / MultilingualIndexConfigurationBase (Litium.Elasticsearch)

The obsolete protected methods `BuildIndexDescriptor` and `BuildTypeMapDescriptor` have been removed. If your custom index configuration overrides these, you will get a compile error. Move that logic into the `Configure` method or the new `ConfigureAsync` virtual override:

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
protected override IPromise<IIndexState> BuildIndexDescriptor(IndexConfigurationBuilder<T> descriptor) { ... }

// After
protected override void Configure(IndexConfigurationBuilder<T> builder)
{
    // move your mapping logic here
}
// or optionally for async access in setup:
protected override async Task ConfigureAsync(IndexConfigurationBuilder<T> builder)
{
    await base.ConfigureAsync(builder);
    // async setup here
}
```

Please find a description of how to add a search index [here](/platform/guides/litiumsearch/how-to-add-a-search-index).

### IndexDocumentBuilderBase / MultilingualIndexDocumentBuilderBase (Litium.Elasticsearch)

`BuildIndexDocuments` and `BuildRemoveIndexDocuments` changed from `abstract` to `virtual`. Existing sync implementations continue to work unchanged — no action required. Optionally upgrade to async for better performance:

| Override                                      | When to use                                   |
| --------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `BuildIndexDocuments` (sync)                  | No changes needed — existing code works as-is |
| `BuildIndexDocumentsTaskAsync`                | Single async batch result                     |
| `BuildIndexDocumentsAsync` (IAsyncEnumerable) | True async streaming with `yield return`      |

## Pattern 3 — Async-First with IAsync\* + \*LookupService / \*ResolverService (Obsolete, sync still works)

Old interfaces are marked `[Obsolete]`. Existing implementations and consumers continue to compile and run via sync fallback. Migration is recommended but not immediately required.

### Price Calculation — IPriceCalculator (Litium.Products)

`IPriceCalculator` is `[Obsolete]`. The routing priority is: partner `IPriceCalculator` override (still works) → `IAsyncPriceCalculator` → platform fallback.

* **Consuming prices:** inject `PriceLookupService` (namespace `Litium.Products`) instead of `IPriceCalculator`. Replace `GetListPrices` → `await GetListPricesAsync()` and `GetPriceLists` → `await GetPriceListsAsync()`.
* **Implementing a custom price calculator:** implement `IAsyncPriceCalculator` (namespace `Litium.Products.PriceCalculator`) instead of `IPriceCalculator`.

```csharp theme={null}
// Before — implementing custom price calculator
public class MyPriceCalculator : IPriceCalculator
{
    public IDictionary<Guid, PriceCalculatorResult> GetListPrices(
        PriceCalculatorArgs args, PriceCalculatorItemArgs[] itemArgs) { ... }
}

// After
public class MyPriceCalculator : IAsyncPriceCalculator
{
    public Task<IDictionary<Guid, PriceCalculatorResult>> GetListPricesAsync(
        PriceCalculatorArgs args,
        IReadOnlyList<PriceCalculatorItemArgs> itemArgs,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default) { ... }
}
```

<Note>
  `itemArgs` is `IReadOnlyList<T>` — C# collection expressions (`[item]`) and `List<T>` are directly compatible.
</Note>

The `PriceAgentItemFactoryDependencies.PriceCalculator` property type has changed from `IPriceCalculator` to `PriceLookupService`.

Please find a description of how to obtain list price for a product [here](/platform/guides/how-to-obtain-list-price-for-a-product).

### Stock Status Calculation — IStockStatusCalculator (Litium.Products.StockStatusCalculator)

`IStockStatusCalculator` is `[Obsolete]`. Same migration pattern as price calculation:

* **Consuming:** inject `StockLookupService`, use `await GetStockStatusesAsync()` and `await GetInventoriesAsync()`.
* **Implementing:** implement `IAsyncStockStatusCalculator` with `GetStockStatusesAsync` and `GetInventoriesAsync`. `itemArgs` is `IReadOnlyList<T>`.

Please find a description of stock balance calculation [here](/platform/areas/products-pim/stock-balance-calculation).

### Discount Price Calculation — IDiscountPriceCalculator (Litium.Sales.Discounts)

`IDiscountPriceCalculator` is `[Obsolete]`. Same migration pattern:

* **Consuming:** inject `DiscountPriceLookupService`, use `await GetDiscountPricesAsync()`.
* **Implementing:** implement `IAsyncDiscountPriceCalculator` with `GetDiscountPricesAsync`. `itemArgs` is `IReadOnlyList<T>`.

### Rendering Services — IContentProcessor and IRenderingValidator\<T> (Litium.Web.Rendering)

Both interfaces are `[Obsolete]`. Existing implementations continue to function via sync fallback.

* **Consuming content processing:** replace `IEnumerable<IContentProcessor>` with `ContentProcessorService`, call `await ProcessAsync(content)`.
* **Implementing a custom content processor:** implement `IAsyncContentProcessor` with `Task<string> ProcessAsync(string content, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`.
* **Consuming rendering validation:** replace `IEnumerable<IRenderingValidator<T>>` with `RenderingValidationService`, call `await ValidateAsync<T>(entity)`. `RenderingExtension.Validate` is `[Obsolete]`.
* **Implementing a custom rendering validator:** implement `IAsyncRenderingValidator<T>` with `Task<bool> ValidateAsync(T model, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)`.

```csharp theme={null}
// Before
public class MyValidator : IRenderingValidator<PageModel>
{
    public bool Validate(PageModel model) => model.Fields.HasValue("myField");
}

// After
public class MyValidator : IAsyncRenderingValidator<PageModel>
{
    public Task<bool> ValidateAsync(PageModel model, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        => Task.FromResult(model.Fields.HasValue("myField"));
}
```

### Routing Services (Litium.Web.Routing)

The following routing interfaces are `[Obsolete]` — existing implementations continue to work via sync fallback dispatch:

`IChannelResolver`, `IUrlRedirectResolver`, `IErrorPageResolver`, `ISignInUrlResolver`, `IAccessDeniedUrlResolver`, `IPageNotFoundResolver`

Each has a corresponding `IAsync*` interface and a `*ResolverService` orchestrator. New result record structs replace the `bool + out` pattern:

| Old interface              | New IAsync\* interface          | Orchestrator service             | Result type                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `IChannelResolver`         | `IAsyncChannelResolver`         | `ChannelResolverService`         | `ChannelResolveResult(bool Found, RouteRequestLookupInfo LookupInfo)` |
| `IUrlRedirectResolver`     | `IAsyncUrlRedirectResolver`     | `UrlRedirectResolverService`     | `RouteResolveResult(bool Found, RouteRequestInfo RequestInfo)`        |
| `IErrorPageResolver`       | `IAsyncErrorPageResolver`       | `ErrorPageResolverService`       | `RouteResolveResult`                                                  |
| `ISignInUrlResolver`       | `IAsyncSignInUrlResolver`       | `SignInUrlResolverService`       | `UrlResolveResult(bool Found, string RedirectUrl)`                    |
| `IAccessDeniedUrlResolver` | `IAsyncAccessDeniedUrlResolver` | `AccessDeniedUrlResolverService` | `UrlResolveResult`                                                    |
| `IPageNotFoundResolver`    | `IAsyncPageNotFoundResolver`    | `PageNotFoundResolverService`    | `RouteResolveResult`                                                  |

```csharp theme={null}
// Before — implementing a custom channel resolver
public class MyChannelResolver : IChannelResolver
{
    public bool TryGet(out RouteRequestLookupInfo lookupInfo) { lookupInfo = ...; return true; }
}

// After
public class MyChannelResolver : IAsyncChannelResolver
{
    public ValueTask<ChannelResolveResult> GetAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        => ValueTask.FromResult(new ChannelResolveResult(true, ...));
}
```

<Note>
  `RouteRequestLookup` has changed from a `ref struct` to a `record` to support use across `await` boundaries. Review any code relying on stack-only semantics.

  `IUrlRedirectFactory` is not obsolete — no migration needed.
</Note>

## Analyzer-Assisted Migration (Litium.Analyzers — LITI1006, LITI1007, LITI1008)

The `Litium.Analyzers` NuGet package ships three new Roslyn diagnostic rules that automatically detect async-migration issues at compile time and offer one-click code fixes in Visual Studio. Install the package and the compiler will guide you through most of the migration automatically.

### LITI1006 — Use async method (`[LitiumUseAsync]`)

**Severity:** Warning | **Category:** Usage

Fires when a sync Litium API decorated with `[LitiumUseAsync("AsyncMethodName")]` is called inside an async context (async method, async lambda, or Task-returning method). The warning message names the async replacement:

> Use 'GetAsync' instead in async context

The analyzer understands nested lambda scoping — it only warns when the innermost enclosing function is async, so a sync `Action` lambda inside an async method is intentionally left silent.

Code fix — three modes:

* **Direct** — simple rename + remove `out` argument + add `await`.
* **Tuple** — when the async replacement returns `Task<(bool, T)>`, the fix emits tuple destructuring: `var (found, value) = await ...`.
* **Incompatible** — when the async return type is a named record struct that cannot be automatically mapped from the `out` pattern, the diagnostic fires but no fix is offered; the caller must be restructured manually.

```csharp theme={null}
// LITI1006 — Before (warning in async context)
public async Task MyMethodAsync()
{
    var service = new UseAsyncTestService();
    service.TryGet("key", out var result);   // ⚠ LITI1006: Use 'GetAsync' instead
}

// After — fix applied (Direct mode)
public async Task MyMethodAsync()
{
    var service = new UseAsyncTestService();
    var result = await service.GetAsync("key");
}
```

### LITI1007 — Use await instead of .GetAwaiter().GetResult()

**Severity:** Warning | **Category:** Usage

Fires when `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` is used inside an async context on a `Task` that is not already covered by LITI1006 (which prevents double-reporting). Blocking the thread with `.GetResult()` inside an async method risks deadlocks.

> Use 'await' instead of '.GetAwaiter().GetResult()' in async context

Code fix handles several edge cases:

* **Simple case** — replaces with `await` directly.
* **Member-access chain** — wraps in parentheses: `(await FetchAsync()).TryGetValue(...)`.
* **Null-conditional call** — uses a null-coalescing fallback: `await (_accessor?.GetCartAsync() ?? Task.FromResult<string>(default!))`.
* **Leading comments** — preserved correctly; not duplicated on both the outer paren and the inner await.
* **Sync context** — no diagnostic fires when the call site is inside a sync method or sync lambda; `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` is acceptable there.

```csharp theme={null}
// LITI1007 — Before
public async Task RunAsync()
{
    var result = Task.FromResult("hello").GetAwaiter().GetResult();   // ⚠ LITI1007
}

// After
public async Task RunAsync()
{
    var result = await Task.FromResult("hello");
}
```

### LITI1008 — Unawaited Task passed to result-builder method

**Severity:** Warning | **Category:** Usage

Fires when an unawaited `Task` or `Task<T>` is passed as an argument to an ASP.NET Core result-builder method (`Ok()`, `Created()`, `StatusCode()`, `BadRequest()`, `NotFound()`, `Unauthorized()`, `UnprocessableEntity()`, `Conflict()`, `Accepted()`, or any custom method returning `IActionResult`). Without `await` the response body contains the serialized Task object rather than the resolved value.

> Argument to 'Ok' is an unawaited Task; await it to return the task result instead of the Task object

The code fix adds `await` to the argument. If the containing controller action is not already `async`, the fix also adds the `async` modifier and wraps the return type in `Task<>`.

```csharp theme={null}
// LITI1008 — Before
public IActionResult Get(string id)
{
    return Ok(_service.GetAsync(id));   // ⚠ LITI1008: unawaited Task passed to Ok()
}

// After — fix applied (also makes method async)
public async Task<IActionResult> Get(string id)
{
    return Ok(await _service.GetAsync(id));
}
```

## Quick Reference Summary

| Area                                                      | Change type                          | Action required                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SalesOrderBuilder`                                       | Async-only                           | Rename 5 overrides, return `Task`                                                                                                                            |
| `ISalesOrderRowFactory`                                   | Async-only                           | Rename `Create` → `CreateAsync`, return `Task<SalesOrderRow>`                                                                                                |
| `ISitemapFactory`                                         | Async-only                           | Replace `CreateSiteMap` with `CreateSiteMapAsync` (`IAsyncEnumerable`)                                                                                       |
| `IFeedFieldFactory`                                       | Async-only                           | Rename `Create` → `CreateAsync`, return `Task<Func<..., Task<object?>>>`                                                                                     |
| `IPriceAgentItemFactory` / `IPriceAgent`                  | Async-only                           | Rename `Create`/`Render`; `IPriceAgent.Render` uses `IAsyncEnumerable`                                                                                       |
| `AuditService`                                            | Async-only                           | Implement `CreateReadEntryAsync`, `GetAsync`, `GetSummaryAsync`                                                                                              |
| `IEventOperationValidator`                                | Async-only                           | Rename `HasAccess` → `HasAccessAsync`, return `Task`                                                                                                         |
| `IReferenceService` / `IMediaReferenceService`            | Async-only                           | Rename `FindReferences` → `FindReferencesAsync`, return `Task<IEnumerable<ReferenceItem>>`                                                                   |
| `Blob` / `BlobContainer` / `BlobService`                  | Async-only                           | Update all call sites and subclass implementations to async variants                                                                                         |
| `IIndexConfiguration` / `IMultilingualIndexConfiguration` | Async-only (for direct implementors) | Implement `BuildIndexStateAsync`; base class users: remove `BuildIndexDescriptor`/`BuildTypeMapDescriptor` overrides                                         |
| `IAccountService`                                         | New abstract async                   | Add 3 `GetXxxAsync` overrides                                                                                                                                |
| Security services (`Auth*`, `Access*`, `Operations*`)     | New abstract async                   | Add async overrides per service                                                                                                                              |
| `KeyLookupService`                                        | New abstract async                   | Add 3 `GetXxxAsync` overrides; use `KeyIdLookupResult` / `KeySystemIdLookupResult`                                                                           |
| `UrlValidator`                                            | New abstract async                   | Add `ValidateAsync` override                                                                                                                                 |
| `IndexDocumentBuilderBase` (Elasticsearch)                | Virtual (no action)                  | Existing sync implementations continue to work; optional: migrate to `BuildIndexDocumentsTaskAsync` or `BuildIndexDocumentsAsync`                            |
| `IPriceCalculator`                                        | Obsolete                             | Consumers: inject `PriceLookupService`; implementors: implement `IAsyncPriceCalculator`                                                                      |
| `IStockStatusCalculator`                                  | Obsolete                             | Consumers: inject `StockLookupService`; implementors: implement `IAsyncStockStatusCalculator`                                                                |
| `IDiscountPriceCalculator`                                | Obsolete                             | Consumers: inject `DiscountPriceLookupService`; implementors: implement `IAsyncDiscountPriceCalculator`                                                      |
| `IContentProcessor` / `IRenderingValidator<T>`            | Obsolete                             | Consumers: inject `ContentProcessorService` / `RenderingValidationService`; implementors: implement `IAsyncContentProcessor` / `IAsyncRenderingValidator<T>` |
| Routing interfaces (`IChannelResolver` etc.)              | Obsolete                             | Consumers: inject `*ResolverService`; implementors: implement `IAsync*` interface                                                                            |
| `Litium.Analyzers` (LITI1006–1008)                        | Analyzer tooling                     | Install `Litium.Analyzers` NuGet; fix warnings with one-click code fixes in Visual Studio                                                                    |


# How to use a payment token
Source: https://docs.litium.dev/platform/guides/use-payment-token-example

This example shows how to use a payment token to pay for an order. The order is programmatically created through a Web API call.

This example uses Litium MVC Accelerator 8.17.3 version. It does not assume a particular payment provider app, but the code is tested using the [Qliro payment app](/add-ons/litium-apps/qliro-payment).

Following are the steps in creating an order using a payment token.

1. An order should be created with a payment provider that supports payment tokens, that initializes recurring/subscription payments and returns back the token to the payment app. This order is paid using a credit card or invoice, and the payment token returned will be tied to the credit card or invoice used. Let us call this order as "Init Order".
2. The payment.systemId of the above "Init Order" should be used when creating orders to use the payment token (The actual payment token received from the payment service provider is not available through any API due to security reasons)
3. You can use a web-api endpoint to create an order programatically and use payment token functionality to process its payment.

Following code example demostrates the above steps.

## Initial order to get payment token for recurring payments

When creating the initial order to get a payment token, the payment app should be informed to initialize recurring payments. To initialize recurring payments, an order should be placed with CheckoutFlowInfo.InitializePaymentToken set to "true".

#### Example code using Litium Accelerator:

This method GetCheckoutFlowInfo() is at: *\Src\Litium.Accelerator.Mvc\Controllers\Checkout\CheckoutController.cs*

```csharp theme={null}
private CheckoutFlowInfo GetCheckoutFlowInfo()
    {
        //...other code
            
        return new CheckoutFlowInfo
        {
           //..Other code

           //Enable Recurring payment.
           InitializePaymentToken = true,
        };
    }
```

Once you have created an order with the InitializePaymentToken set, you can use its payment.SystemId to create subsequent orders and pay with the payment token as shown below.

### Creating and paying for order programatically:

Following is code for a Web API method called "subscriptionOrder".

Once it is added, the webapi url will be:

```text theme={null}
https://mysite.localtest.me/api/subscriptionOrder/createFrom/<externalOrderId>
```

You need to replace the mysite.localtest.me and `<externalOrderId>` above.

Code to create the above endpoint is below, and it should be placed in following location:

..\Src\Litium.Accelerator.Mvc\Controllers\Api\SubscriptionOrderController.cs

```csharp theme={null}
using System;
using System.Linq;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Litium.Accelerator.Utilities;
using Litium.Accelerator.ViewModels.Checkout;
using Litium.Common;
using Litium.Customers;
using Litium.Events;
using Litium.GDPR;
using Litium.Globalization;
using Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection;
using Litium.Runtime.DistributedLock;
using Litium.Sales;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.Mvc.Controllers.Api
{
    [Authorize]
    [Route("api/subscriptionOrder")]
    public class SubscriptionOrderController : ApiControllerBase
    {
        private readonly SubscriptionService _subscriptionService;

        public SubscriptionOrderController(SubscriptionService subscriptionService)
        {
            _subscriptionService = subscriptionService;
        }
        /// <summary>
        /// Creates a subscription order.
        /// </summary>
        /// <param name="srcOrderId"> Original order id of the subscription.</param>
        /// <returns></returns>
        [HttpPost]
        [Route("createFrom/{srcOrderId}")]
        public async Task<IActionResult> CreateFrom(string srcOrderId)
        {
            try
            {
                var cartContext = await HttpContext.GetCartContextAsync();
                //await HttpContext.SwitchCartContextAsync(cartContext.Cart.SystemId);

                var subscriptionOrder = await _subscriptionService.CreateSubscriptionOrder(cartContext, srcOrderId);
                return (subscriptionOrder != null)
                    ? Ok(subscriptionOrder)
                    : NotFound($"Order {srcOrderId} not found");
            }
            catch (Exception ex)
            {
                return BadRequest(ex);
            }
        }
    }

    [Service(ServiceType = typeof(SubscriptionService), Lifetime = DependencyLifetime.Singleton)]
    public class SubscriptionService
    {
        private readonly PaymentService _paymentService;
        private readonly PaymentProviderService _paymentProviderService;
        private readonly OrderOverviewService _orderOverviewService;
        private readonly DistributedLockService _distributedLockService;
        private readonly ChannelService _channelService;
        private readonly KeyLookupService _keyLookupService;
        private readonly PersonService _personService;
        private readonly EventBroker _eventBroker;

        public SubscriptionService(PaymentService paymentService,
            PaymentProviderService paymentProviderService,
            OrderOverviewService orderOverviewService,
            DistributedLockService distributedLockService,
            ChannelService channelService,
            KeyLookupService keyLookupService,
            PersonService personService,
            EventBroker eventBroker)
        {
            _paymentService = paymentService;
            _paymentProviderService = paymentProviderService;
            _orderOverviewService = orderOverviewService;
            _distributedLockService = distributedLockService;
            _channelService = channelService;
            _keyLookupService = keyLookupService;
            _personService = personService;
            _eventBroker = eventBroker;
        }
        public async Task<OrderOverview> CreateSubscriptionOrder(CartContext cartContext, string srcOrderId)
        {
            //Note: Following code can be used as a starting point of creating an order and making a payment using a PaymentToken.
            //The code is tested using Qliro payment app.
            //For this to work, your payment account should be enabled to use recurring/subscription payments. Contact payment provider customer service to enable it.
            using (_distributedLockService.AcquireLock(srcOrderId, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)))
            {
                //Makesure we have a totally new cart context.
                await cartContext.ClearCartContextAsync();
                if (await cartContext.TryInitializeCheckoutFlowAsync(() => new CheckoutFlowInfoArgs() { CheckoutFlowInfo = new CheckoutFlowInfo() }))
                {
                    var srcOrderOverview = _orderOverviewService.Get(srcOrderId);
                    if (srcOrderOverview != null)
                    {
                        var srcOrder = srcOrderOverview.SalesOrder;
                        //Following methods sets the channel and country, and internally selects the currency for the order.
                        //These methods need not be called, because the CartContextDefaultFactoryDecorator is setting them. 
                        //await cartContext.SelectChannelAsync(new SelectChannelArgs() { ChannelSystemId = srcOrder.ChannelSystemId.Value });
                        //await cartContext.SelectCountryAsync(new SelectCountryArgs() { CountryCode = srcOrder.CountryCode });

                        //prepare a new order with same items as the src order.
                        foreach (var item in srcOrder.Rows.Where(x => x.OrderRowType == OrderRowType.Product))
                        {
                            var addOrUpdateItemArgs = new AddOrUpdateCartItemArgs()
                            {
                                ArticleNumber = item.ArticleNumber,
                                Quantity = item.Quantity,
                            };
                            await cartContext.AddOrUpdateItemAsync(addOrUpdateItemArgs);
                        }

                        await AddCustomerInfoAsync(cartContext, srcOrder.CustomerInfo);
                        await AddShippingDetailsAsync(cartContext, srcOrder);

                        await cartContext.AddOrUpdateBillingAddressAsync(srcOrder.BillingAddress);
                        await AddPaymentDetails(cartContext, srcOrderOverview);

                        //if a paymentToken is found in the original order, we try to use it with calling SetPaymentTokenAsync method.
                        //Some payment apps (e.g. Qliro) allows to create a order using Invoice method, even without payment tokens for credit accepted buyers.
                        //So, following call is not necessary to create invoice payments in certain payment apps when using invoice methods. Note that, CustomerInfo.NationalIdentificationNumber is required to create invoice payments.
                                                //if (srcOrder.AdditionalInfo.TryGetValue("PaymentToken", out object tokenObj)) //Note: Following code assumes that payment token is saved with the original order additionalInfo.
                        //{
                        //    if (Guid.TryParse(tokenObj as string, out Guid token))
                        //    {
                        //        await cartContext.SetPaymentTokenAsync(new SetPaymentTokenArgs() { PaymentToken = token });
                        //    }
                        //}

                        var paymentToken = srcOrderOverview.PaymentOverviews.FirstOrDefault().Payment.SystemId;
                        await cartContext.SetPaymentTokenAsync(new SetPaymentTokenArgs() { PaymentToken = paymentToken });

                        //await cartContext.ConfirmOrderAsync();

                        //we should get a confirmed order.
                        var result = await _eventBroker.WaitForEventAsync<Sales.Events.SalesOrderConfirmed>(
                           x => Task.FromResult(x.Item.SystemId == cartContext.Cart.Order.SystemId),
                           async () => await cartContext.ConfirmOrderAsync());

                        var subscriptionOrderOverview = _orderOverviewService.Get(cartContext.Cart.Order.SystemId);
                        return subscriptionOrderOverview;
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        throw new Exception($"Order {srcOrderId} not found.");
                    }
                }
                else
                {
                    throw new Exception($"Could not initialize cart context.");
                }
            }
        }

        private async Task AddPaymentDetails(CartContext cartContext, OrderOverview srcOrderOverview)
        {
            var channel = _channelService.Get(srcOrderOverview.SalesOrder.ChannelSystemId.Value);
            _keyLookupService.TryGetSystemId<Country>(srcOrderOverview.SalesOrder.CountryCode, out var countrySystemId);
            var srcPaymentOverview = srcOrderOverview.PaymentOverviews.FirstOrDefault();

            //This is the list of all the options supported by the payment provider service.
            var paymentTokenPaymentOptions = _paymentProviderService.Get(srcPaymentOverview.Payment.PaymentOption.ProviderId)?.Options.Where(x => x.IntegrationType == Sales.Payments.PaymentIntegrationType.PaymentToken);
            if (!paymentTokenPaymentOptions.Any())
            {
                throw new Exception($"Paymentprovider {srcPaymentOverview.Payment.PaymentOption.ProviderId} does not support PaymentTokens");
            }

            //we need to find the PaymentToken option available for the channel.
            var paymentTokenPaymentOption = channel.CountryLinks.FirstOrDefault(x => x.CountrySystemId == countrySystemId)?.PaymentOptions.FirstOrDefault(x => paymentTokenPaymentOptions.Any(k => k.Id == x.Id.OptionId));
            if (paymentTokenPaymentOption == null)
            {
                throw new Exception($"PaymentToken option is not added to the channel {channel.Id}");
            }

            await cartContext.SelectPaymentOptionAsync(new SelectPaymentOptionArgs
            {
                PaymentOptionId = paymentTokenPaymentOption.Id
            });
        }

        private static async Task AddShippingDetailsAsync(CartContext cartContext, SalesOrder srcOrder)
        {
            var srcShippingInfo = srcOrder.ShippingInfo.FirstOrDefault();
            if (srcShippingInfo != null)
            {
                //Note: Here we assume that the shipping option is not using a delivery checkout.
                //Since there will not be end customer input here, you cannot use a delivery checkout.
                await cartContext.SelectShippingOptionAsync(
                    new SelectShippingOptionArgs()
                    {
                        ShippingOptionId = srcShippingInfo.ShippingOption //TODO: It is assumed that the shipping option is still awailable.
                    });
                await cartContext.AddOrUpdateDeliveryAddressAsync(srcShippingInfo.ShippingAddress);
            }
        }

        private async Task AddCustomerInfoAsync(CartContext cartContext, CustomerInfo customerInfoFromOriginalOrder)
        {
            var ssn = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.NationalIdentificationNumber;
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(ssn) && customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.PersonSystemId != null && customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.PersonSystemId != Guid.Empty)
            {
                var person = _personService.Get(customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.PersonSystemId.Value);
                if (person != null)
                {
                    ssn = person.Fields.GetValue<string>("SocialSecurityNumber");
                }
            }

            var addOrUpdateCustomerInfoArgs = new AddOrUpdateCustomerInfoArgs
            {
                CustomerInfo = new CustomerInfo
                {
                    CustomerNumber = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.CustomerNumber,
                    CustomerType = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.CustomerType,
                    PersonSystemId = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.PersonSystemId,
                    OrganizationSystemId = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.OrganizationSystemId,
                    FirstName = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.FirstName,
                    LastName = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.LastName,
                    Email = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.Email,
                    Phone = customerInfoFromOriginalOrder.Phone,
                    NationalIdentificationNumber = ssn,
                }
            };

            await cartContext.AddOrUpdateCustomerInfoAsync(addOrUpdateCustomerInfoArgs);
        }

       
    }

    public static class EventBrokerExtensions
    {
        public static async Task<T?> WaitForEventAsync<T>(this EventBroker eventBroker, Func<T, Task<bool>>? predicate, Func<Task>? action, int maxWaitTimeMilleseconds = 20000, EventScope? eventScope = default)
          where T : class, IMessage
        {
            var evt = default(T);
            using var waiter = new SemaphoreSlim(0, 1);
            using (eventBroker.Subscribe<T>(eventScope ?? EventScope.Local, async x =>
            {
                var task = predicate?.Invoke(x);
                if (task is not null)
                {
                    var result = await task;
                    if (result)
                    {
                        evt = x;
                        waiter.Release();
                    }
                }
            }))
            {
                if (action is not null)
                {
                    await action.Invoke();
                }
                if (!await waiter.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(maxWaitTimeMilleseconds)))
                {
                    //TODO: you may enable the following line to get a error, if the order does not get confirmed withing the specified time limit.
                    //throw new TimeoutException($"Timed out waiting for event of type {typeof(T).FullName} after {maxWaitTimeMilleseconds} milliseconds.");
                }
                return evt;
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Initializing CartContext:

The above method causes the CartContext to be initialized. Since we are calling this from a Web API, the Accelerator as run in a website is not initialized. Therefore, we need to modify the CartContextDefaultFactoryDecorator to match our requirements.

Code is in: ..\Src\Litium.Accelerator\Services\CartContextDefaultFactoryDecorator.cs

```csharp theme={null}
using System;
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Litium.Accelerator.Routing;
using Litium.Accelerator.Utilities;
using Litium.Common;
using Litium.Globalization;
using Litium.Runtime.DependencyInjection;
using Litium.Sales;
using Litium.Security;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;

namespace Litium.Accelerator.Services
{
    [ServiceDecorator(typeof(CartContextDefaultFactory))]
    public class CartContextDefaultFactoryDecorator : CartContextDefaultFactory
    {
        private readonly CartContextDefaultFactory _parent;
        private readonly RequestModelAccessor _requestModelAccessor;
        private readonly PersonStorage _personStorage;
        private readonly KeyLookupService _keyLookupService;
        private readonly SecurityContextService _securityContextService;
        private readonly OrderOverviewService _orderOverviewService;
        private readonly ChannelService _channelService;
        private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;

        public CartContextDefaultFactoryDecorator(
            CartContextDefaultFactory parent,
            RequestModelAccessor requestModelAccessor,
            PersonStorage personStorage,
            KeyLookupService keyLookupService,
            SecurityContextService securityContextService,
            OrderOverviewService orderOverviewService,
            ChannelService channelService,
            IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor)
        {
            _parent = parent;
            _requestModelAccessor = requestModelAccessor;
            _personStorage = personStorage;
            _keyLookupService = keyLookupService;
            _securityContextService = securityContextService;
            _orderOverviewService = orderOverviewService;
            _channelService = channelService;
            _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
        }

        public override Task<CreateCartContextArgs> CreateAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
        {
            var requestModel = _requestModelAccessor.RequestModel;
            if (requestModel != null)
            {
                return Task.FromResult(new CreateCartContextArgs
                {
                    ChannelSystemId = requestModel.ChannelModel.SystemId,
                    MarketSystemId = requestModel.ChannelModel.Channel.MarketSystemId ?? Guid.Empty,
                    CountryCode = requestModel.CountryModel.Country.Id,
                    CurrencyCode = _keyLookupService.TryGetId<Currency>(requestModel.CountryModel.Country.CurrencySystemId, out var currencyCode) ? currencyCode : null,
                    PersonSystemId = _securityContextService.GetIdentityUserSystemId() ?? null,
                    OrganizationSystemId = _personStorage.CurrentSelectedOrganizationSystemId,
                    ClientIp = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString(),
                    ClientBrowser = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Headers["User-Agent"].ToString(),
                    ShowPricesWithVat = requestModel.ChannelModel.Channel.ShowPricesWithVat
                });
            }
            //Start Code added to support PaymentToken example.
            else if (_httpContextAccessor.HttpContext != null && _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext.Request.Path.Value.StartsWith("/api/subscriptionOrder/createFrom/"))
            {
                var orderId = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext.Request.Path.Value.Replace("/api/subscriptionOrder/createFrom/", string.Empty);
                if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(orderId))
                {
                    var orderOverview = _orderOverviewService.Get(orderId);
                    if (orderOverview != null)
                    {
                        var salesOrder = orderOverview.SalesOrder;
                        var channel = _channelService.Get(salesOrder.ChannelSystemId.Value);
                        return Task.FromResult(new CreateCartContextArgs
                        {
                            ChannelSystemId = salesOrder.ChannelSystemId.Value,
                            MarketSystemId = salesOrder.MarketSystemId ?? Guid.Empty,
                            CountryCode = salesOrder.CountryCode,
                            CurrencyCode = salesOrder.CurrencyCode,
                            PersonSystemId = salesOrder.CustomerInfo.PersonSystemId,
                            OrganizationSystemId = salesOrder.CustomerInfo.OrganizationSystemId,
                            ClientIp = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Connection.RemoteIpAddress?.ToString(),
                            ClientBrowser = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Headers["User-Agent"].ToString(),
                            ShowPricesWithVat = channel.ShowPricesWithVat
                        });
                    }
                }
            }
            //End Code added to support PaymentToken example.
            return _parent.CreateAsync(cancellationToken);
        }
    }
}
```

## Using the Web API

To create a order using the payment token, first you need to create a normal order, so that the payment token is initialized from that order. Suppose this order id is LS\_00001

Then, you should call the Web API method: /api/subscriptionOrder/createFrom/\{srcOrderId}, where \{srcOrderId} is the order that is used to initialize the payment token. So, the api call would look like:

`https://mysite.localtest.me/api/subscriptionOrder/createFrom/LS_00001`

Note that, to call a Web API method, you need to create a service account in Backoffice and [use it for authentication as shown here >>](/platform/architecture/web-api/security)
